title: Rams' Alaric Jackson punched Bills' Bradley Chubb after game
summary: Jackson will be facing NFL discipline for approaching Chubb after the game and throwing a punch.
full_text: After his team lost the game, Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson lost his cool and punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. Well after the game was over, while Chubb talked to players on both teams near midfield, Jackson walked over to him and they briefly exchanged words before Jackson threw a right hook to Chubb's jaw. Chubb was unfazed afterward. "It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game, it was a close game," Chubb told the California Post . "They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing, and then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled." Chubb was also seen talking to Rams defensive end Myles Garrett on the field, but when asked whether the two of them had exchanged words, Chubb said there were no issues. "Just the whole team. Like I said, it was an emotional game. Tempers flared," Chubb said. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week." Chubb didn't mention Jackson by name in his postgame interview. "Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb said. "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week." Asked if he was OK, Chubb said he's fine. "I'm just ready for next week," he said. "You see me, I'm smiling, I'm with my team. I'll be ready for next week." Whether Jackson is playing or suspended next week remains to be seen.
author: Michael David Smith

title: With 210 yards passing and 121 rushing, Josh Allen had his fourth career double-triple
summary: Allen reached triple-digit yardage in two statistical categories for the fourth time.
full_text: Bills quarterback Josh Allen's spectacular performance in Monday night's win over the Rams was the fourth double-triple of his NFL career. Allen had 10 carries for 121 yards and a touchdown, and he also completed 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. The Bills won 37-34 in overtime. A double-triple is PFT’s stat recognizing a player who has triple-digit yardage in two different statistical categories. Allen previously had back-to-back double triples in two 2018 games, with 231 passing and 135 rushing in Week 13 against the Dolphins and 206 passing and 101 rushing in Week 14 against the Jets. He also had 308 passing and 109 rushing in Week 14 of 2021 against the Buccaneers. The NFL's all-time leader in double-triples is Lamar Jackson, who has accomplished the feat 17 times — more than twice as many as anyone else in NFL history. Michael Vick, with eight double-triples, is second. The only other double-triple in the NFL this season was accomplished by Jayden Daniels on Sunday, when he had 199 yards passing and 103 yards rushing in the tie against the Giants, when his statistical achievements were overshadowed by his clock management blunder on the last play of the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay: Field goal unit "cost us the game tonight"
summary: The Rams fell to 2-3 on Monday night, due in part to a couple of missed field goals from kicker Harrison Mevis — including a blocked field goal in overtime that, if good, would have won the game.
full_text: '' The Rams fell to 2-3 on Monday night, due in part to a couple of missed field goals from kicker Harrison Mevis — including a blocked field goal in overtime that, if good, would have won the game. After the game, Rams coach Sean McVay pointed a finger directly at the field-goal unit after the 38-35 overtime loss: "It cost us the game tonight," McVay told reporters. McVay then said, "I'm gonna evaluate everything." Last year, McVay fired special-teams coordinator Chase Blackburn after the Thursday night overtime classic in Seattle. This time around, several folks should be getting a little nervous about whether the pink slip could be coming for them. The clock is ticking. The next game is on Sunday, against the Cardinals. After that, the Rams visit the Raiders, followed by a home game against the Chargers. All are winnable, which could boost the Rams to 5-3. Regardless, 2-3 (and 1-3 in prime time) is a far cry from where anyone thought the Rams would be after Week 5.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Allen's 100th win is also his first ever in overtime
summary: On Monday night in L.A., Bills quarterback Josh Allen got his 100th career win.
full_text: ''' On Monday night in L.A., Bills quarterback Josh Allen got his 100th career win. He also got his first in overtime. Allen had been 0-7 in overtime entering the Week 5 game against the Rams. Thanks to a blocked field goal by defensive end Gregory Rousseau and Allen's own legs on the ensuing drive, the Bills moved to 4-1 with a 38-35 victory. Allen, who had 121 rushing yards, becomes the fourth quarterback to win 100 games in his ninth season. The others were Patrick Mahomes (112), Russell Wilson (107), and Tom Brady (101). The victory also keeps the Bills in first place. A loss would have dropped Buffalo to 3-2 and, technically, into second place by virtue of losing last week to the Patriots. On Sunday, the Bills face the 3-2 Raiders in Las Vegas. They're off in Week 7. Next comes a home game against the 4-1 Ravens followed by a Monday night date with the 5-0 Vikings in Minnesota.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in overtime in instant classic
summary: Bills kicker Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining in OT for the win.
full_text: The Bills and Rams were a popular preseason pick to meet in the Super Bowl. If Monday night was a preview, Super Bowl LXI will be a good one. The heavyweights went back-and-forth on Monday night, with eight lead changes and 35 combined fourth-quarter points. The game, appropriately, was decided in overtime. Bills kicker Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining in overtime for a 37-34 victory. The Bills are 4-1 and the Rams 2-3. The first half was all defense as the teams combined for 270 total yards, one play over 20 yards, 20 points, one punt, one turnover and one missed field goal. The second half was all Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford as the quarterbacks took over. The teams ended up combining for 71 points and 890 yards. Both teams had chances to win it late in regulation and again in overtime. James Cook's 5-yard touchdown run with 1:39 remaining in the fourth quarter gave the Bills a brief 34-27 lead, with Buffalo burning 5:35 of the final 7:14. It left plenty of time for Stafford, who led the Rams on an eight-play, 63-yard drive in only 1:34. Rams running back Kyren Williams' 1-yard touchdown run with 5 seconds left tied it 34-34 and sent it to overtime. The Rams won the toss in overtime and chose to kickoff. On their first drive, the Bills faced a second-and-16 after a holding penalty. Khalil Shakir then had a 57-yard catch-and-run to the Los Angeles 22 before Rams safety Kamren Kinchens made the touchdown-saving tackle. On the next play, Cook fumbled for the second time. His teammates saved him on the first one but not on the second. Rams linebacker Nate Landman punched the ball out and defensive lineman Aaron Donald recovered at the 20. Officials missed Landman removing his helmet in the field of play, which should have been a 15-yard penalty. The Rams then drove 50 yards in eight plays to the Buffalo 30 before kicker Harrison Mevis missed for a second time. Greg Rousseau blocked Mevis' 48-yard attempt. Allen directed the game-winning drive, with the Bills going 35 yards in five plays. Allen had runs of 19 and 13 on the game-winning drive, and he finished his night with 10 carries for 121 yards and a touchdown. He was 12-of-19 for 210 yards passing with a touchdown and an interception. Cook ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries. The Rams outgained the Bills 454 to 436, with Puka Nacua setting a career-high and a Monday Night Football record with 17 catches for 138 yards and a touchdown. Nacua had 24 targets. Stafford was 40-of-54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams each had a rushing touchdown, and Davante Adams caught two touchdown passes.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley isn't considering benching QB Malik Willis
summary: The 0-5 Dolphins enter their bye week searching for answers.
full_text: '' The 0-5 Dolphins enter their bye week searching for answers. One of them won't be benching the starting quarterback. Coach Jeff Hafley was asked by reporters on Monday whether he's thinking about flipping from Malik Willis to Kyle McCord in Week 7. "No," Hafley said. He was asked for his thinking in that regard. "We've played five games and Malik is our quarterback," Hafley said. "[A]s far as the Malik questions, again, I totally respect all the questions and I get everybody has a job to do, so good question," Hafley said. "We need to be better. Malik needs to be better, OK? And that's not the headline. The headline is we all need to be better, and I mean that. I thought yesterday for the first time we ran the ball really well and we moved the ball. We ran for 200 yards against a really good team. But everything in the pass game has to be better, right? It's the receivers, it's the tight ends, it's the protection. It all has to tie in and it all has to be better. And that's the quarterback, that's the coaches, that's the offensive line, that's the running backs, that's the tight ends. This is a team game that we all need to be more efficient and we need to be better. And we will work through that. I have confidence in the coaches, I have confidence in the players that we have. We will work through that and we will get better. It's been five weeks." In five games as the Miami starter, Willis has completed 73 of 130 passes for 849 yards, with two touchdowns and four interceptions. His passer rating is 68.4, which puts him last among all 29 qualifiers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Davante Adams' second TD ties it up 27-27
summary: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams loves Monday night.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams loves Monday night. He has touchdowns of 4 and 5 yards tonight against the Bills, with his second score tying the game at 27-27 with 7:14 remaining. He has four touchdowns this season, and all four were on Monday Night Football. Puka Nacua also has had a big night with 14 catches on 19 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is 31-of-42 for 274 yards and three touchdowns. The Rams have outgained the Bills 341 to 264.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Allen scores eighth rushing TD of the season
summary: Josh Allen has his eighth rushing touchdown in five games, and the Bills have the lead again.
full_text: Josh Allen has his eighth rushing touchdown in five games, and the Bills have the lead again. Allen had a 1-yard touchdown run, and the Bills converted the 2-point conversion on Allen's pass to tight end Dalton Kincaid. The Bills are now 1-for-3 on 2-point conversions this season. They lead 27-20, the sixth lead change of the night. Allen is only 8-of-15 for 129 yards with a touchdown and an interception, but he has run for 53 yards on six carries. James Cook has 16 carries for 90 yards and a touchdown. Allen is now the first quarterback in NFL history to record a rushing touchdown in each of his team's first five games of a season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Puka Nacua's touchdown gives Rams a 20-19 lead
summary: After a defensive battle in the first half, Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford have heated up.
full_text: After a defensive battle in the first half, Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford have heated up. The Rams just regained the lead on Stafford's 2-yard throw to Puka Nacua with 14:16 remaining in the game. Los Angeles leads 20-19 after Stafford was sacked on the 2-point conversion. Stafford threw completions of 28 yards to Tyler Higbee and 34 yards to Blake Corum on back-to-back plays to get the drive going. He is 27-of-37 for 228 yards and two touchdowns. Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was injured after making the tackle on Corum on his catch. He appeared to injure his knee. The Bills have ruled out right tackle Spencer Brown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Teams should record and save all headset communications
summary: When a plane crashes, the "black box" preserves all evidence regarding the cockpit conversations.
full_text: '' When a plane crashes, the "black box" preserves all evidence regarding the cockpit conversations. When an NFL team has an inexplicable failure of coaching, is there a way to go back and listen to how it all happened? While some teams may preserve that data, the Commanders do not. Coach Dan Quinn was asked that specific question on Monday, one day after a disastrous failure to manage the final seconds of overtime against the Giants. "We don't do specifically that," Quinn said. "We do a writeup and then go back and review conversations, situations, the film, and the R&D department goes along with that. As far as the communications go, I want to make sure that's up for me, you know, at the top, this is what's happening. This is what we need to get done. And we'll continue to work really hard on that. We have definitely ways to simulate it. That's one way that we have, and we'll continue to do." It would make sense to preserve the headset communications, if only for the benefit of ownership to get to the raw and undeniable facts at a time when folks may be looking for ways to cover their butts. Of course, if owner Josh Harris was on the sideline during games, he'd have first-hand evidence as to what transpired. Which is what Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon does, even though some feel compelled to criticize her for it. For the owners who aren't on the sideline, preserving those communications should be a no-brainer. If they aren't already doing it, adopting that system could be the equivalent of all teams incorporating victory formation after the disastrous Joe Pisarcik moment from 1978.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals will discuss making Carson Beck active on game day
summary: The Cardinals are 2-15 with Jacoby Brissett as their quarterback in the past two seasons, with a point differential of minus-194.
full_text: The Cardinals are 2-15 with Jacoby Brissett as their quarterback in the past two seasons, with a point differential of minus-194. Brissett, though, will remain the starter for the foreseeable future. “When it’s going good, it’s going good , and then it’s a three-and-out machine,” Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told Arizona Sports. “There’s really nowhere in between right now for us. We got to figure out how to do all the good stuff better.” Brissett has played all 351 snaps this season, staying in the game to the finish even in Sunday's 45-21 blowout loss to the Lions. It would have seemed a perfect time to play Carson Beck, but the Cardinals have made the rookie quarterback inactive. As such, Beck can play only if both Brissett and Gardner Minshew are injured. The Raiders got rookie Fernando Mendoza some snaps the past two weeks, and LaFleur was asked whether the Cardinals might think about keeping Beck active on game day for that purpose. “You can only have so many people up [on game day]. . . . It’s hard to put three quarterbacks up," LaFleur said on Arizona Sports. "Right now, Gardner is our backup." During his media availability, LaFleur said the Caridnals will have conversations on Tuesday about whether to make the third-round pick active against the Rams. "If we think that's what is best, [then that's what we'll do]," LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills regain lead, 19-14, on Josh Allen's first TD pass of night
summary: The Bills regained the lead with a nine-play, 61-yard drive.
full_text: The Bills regained the lead with a nine-play, 61-yard drive. Josh Allen threw his first touchdown pass of the night, hitting Keon Coleman for a 7-yard score and a 19-14 lead. It was set up by a defensive holding penalty on Jaylen Watson after the Rams had Allen stopped on a 9-yard scramble on third-and-goal from the 13. The Bills also got a 21-yard defensive pass interference penalty on Quentin Lake, who was covering Coleman, on first-and-20. In addition, James Cook's fumble was originally awarded to the Rams before officials changed the call. They gave the ball back to the Bills. The Bills opted to go for 2 points, but Alec Anderson had a false start. They then decided to kick the extra point, but Tyler Bass missed the 38-yard try. The Bills are 0-for-2 on 2-point conversions this season and 3-for-12 over the past three seasons.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams open second half with a touchdown, lead 14-13
summary: The Rams had not scored on an opening possession of the first half or the second half this season until Monday night.
full_text: The Rams had not scored on an opening possession of the first half or the second half this season until Monday night. Blake Corum's 1-yard touchdown run completed a nine-play, 60-yard drive that returner Alex Bachman set up with a 32-yard kickoff return to the Los Angeles 40. The Rams lead 14-13. The Rams went for it on fourth-and-1 from the Buffalo 35 when Tyler Higbee was called for a false start. Higbee made up for it with a 10-yard catch on fourth-and-6. Higbee also drew a 17-yard pass interference penalty on Cole Bishop in the end zone that set up Corum's touchdown run. Matthew Stafford is 21-of-30 for 144 yards with a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Bills lead Rams 13-7 at halftime
summary: Josh Allen was only 4-of-7 for 60 yards with an interception as the Bills gained 128 yards.
full_text: The Rams have Matthew Stafford. The Bills have Josh Allen. The first half was all defense as the teams combined for 270 total yards, one play over 20 yards, 20 points, one punt, one turnover and one missed field goal. The Bills lead 13-7 at halftime. Buffalo scored on its first three possessions, failing to score a touchdown after a 70-yard opening kickoff return from Ray Davis and after a 10-play, 55-yard drive to the Los Angeles 5. Tyler Bass kicked field goals of 49 and 23 yards. James Cook finally got the Bills in the end zone on a 17-yard run. Allen threw a deep interception on the Bills' final possession of the half. He finished the first half 4-of-7 for 60 yards as the Bills gained 128 yards. Cook rushed for 55 yards on nine carries and caught a pass for 7 yards. Allen rushed for 21 yards on three carries. The Rams gained 143 yards as Stafford went 16-of-23 for 99 yards and a touchdown. Davante Adams caught Stafford's 4-yard touchdown throw. Puka Nacua has five catches for 32 yards and nearly caught up to a 49-yard throw by Stafford to the end zone on the final play of the half. Aaron Donald's first sack of the season was negated by an illegal contact penalty on cornerback Trent McDuffie.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jim Harbaugh blames Justin Herbert's rough start to "desperation time"
summary: A month ago, Jim Harbaugh predicted Justin Herbert will retire as the greatest quarterback ever.
full_text: '' A month ago, Jim Harbaugh predicted Justin Herbert will retire as the greatest quarterback ever . Herbert's play this season, though, has brought questions about the quarterback. The Chargers coach defended Herbert on Monday after the two-time Pro Bowler went 14-of-24 for 121 yards with a touchdown and an interception in a loss to the Broncos. “There are definitely times when he was trying to make a play, and too many times this season, there’s been that desperation time ,” Harbaugh said, via Noah Furtado of TheAthletic.com. “That’s what I’d attribute that to. Doing anything and everything he can.” Herbert has five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. His nine turnovers tie him with Drake Maye for the most in the league this season. Herbert's season high for interceptions is the 15 he threw in 2021, his second season, when he also threw 38 touchdowns. Harbaugh said it is the team's responsibility to put Herbert in better positions to succeed. “I’m not going to tell him anything different,” Harbaugh said. “He’s doing anything and everything that he can to help us win, and I applaud those that do that.”
author: Charean Williams

title: James Cook finds the end zone, giving Bills a 13-7 lead
summary: The Bills have had the ball three times.
full_text: The Bills have had the ball three times. They have three scores. Buffalo scored its first touchdown on James Cook's 17-yard touchdown run, giving the Bills a 13-7 lead with 5:09 remaining until halftime. Cook has eight carries for 53 yards. He has 474 rushing yards and four touchdowns this season. Cook's 474 rushing yards are the fifth-most in team history through five games. Josh Allen has thrown only five passes, completing three for 53 yards. Tyler Bass kicked field goals of 49 and 23 yards on the Bills' first two drives. Kickoff returner Ray Davis set up the first field goal with a 70-yard return on the opening kickoff. The Bills list right tackle Spencer Brown (back) as questionable to return. Brown is in the training room. Tylan Grable has replaced him.
author: Charean Williams

title: Davante Adams' touchdown gives Rams a 7-6 lead
summary: The last time the Rams played on Monday Night Football — in Week 2 against the Giants — Davante Adams caught eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns.
full_text: The last time the Rams played on Monday Night Football — in Week 2 against the Giants — Davante Adams caught eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. He is off to a good start tonight against the Bills. Adams' 4-yard touchdown reception has given the Rams their first lead, 7-6, over the Bills. Bills returner Ray Davis returned the opening kickoff 70 yards to the Los Angeles 26 before punter/kickoff specialist Ethan Evans pushed Davis out of bounds. The Bills, though, lost 5 yards and had to settle for Tyler Bass' 49-yard field goal. Rams kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 50-yard try after his team drove 53 yards in 14 plays. The Bills increased their lead to 6-0 on Bass' 23-yard field goal after the offense stalled at the 5. That allowed the Rams to take the lead on their 14-play, 71-yard touchdown drive. Matthew Stafford is 13-of-16 for 76 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bucs-Cowboys attracts 16.73 million viewers on Thursday night
summary: The numbers for Prime Video's Thursday night broadcasts keep going up.
full_text: ''' The numbers for Prime Video's Thursday night broadcasts keep going up. The most recent game, between the Buccaneers and the Cowboys, averaged 16.73 million viewers. Per Amazon, it was the most-watched Week 5 of the entire Thursday night package. It was also the fourth straight week with a year-over-year gain in comparison to 2025. The Thursday night package averages 17.52 million viewers through its first four games (the package starts in Week 2). It's an 11-percent increase over the 2025 pace. The Cowboys always draw a big audience, and the Week 4 game ended up being far more competitive than anyone could have expected, with the Bucs getting their first win of the season and sending the Cowboys to 2-3.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. passes physical, so trade is official
summary: Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. passed his physical on Monday, according to multiple reports.
full_text: Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. passed his physical on Monday, according to multiple reports. That makes his trade from Arizona to Houston official. The Cardinals will receive a second-round and a seventh-round pick (originally belonging to the 49ers) in 2027 in exchange for Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick. The Texans waived wide receiver Jared Wayne in a corresponding move. Harrison, the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft, reunites with his former Ohio State teammate, C.J. Stroud, in Houston. He finished his Cardinals career with 33 games played, 108 receptions, 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants to sign DL Dawuane Smoot to practice squad
summary: The Giants are signing veteran defensive lineman Dawuane Smoot to the practice squad, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
full_text: ' The Giants are signing veteran defensive lineman Dawuane Smoot to the practice squad, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. The team also worked out Yannick Ngakoue and Julian Owkara on Monday. Smoot, 31, entered the NFL as a third-round pick of the Jaguars in 2017. He spent his first eight seasons there before going to the Bills in 2024. Smoot returned to the Jaguars last season. He appeared in all 17 games last season, totaling 23 tackles, five quarterback hits and two sacks. In his career, Smoot has played 127 games with 21 career starts and has 27 sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Bills WR DJ Moore, CB Dee Alford are inactive
summary: The Bills will not have wide receiver DJ Moore for Monday Night Football.
full_text: The Bills will not have wide receiver DJ Moore for Monday Night Football. Moore is among the team's inactives, sitting out after aggravating an AC sprain in his left shoulder. He has 12 catches for 178 yards and a touchdown this season. Cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) also will not play. Rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell and rookie cornerback Jalon Kilgore are active for the first time. Kilgore could join Damar Hamlin in helping replace Alford in the nickel. The Bills' other inactives are wide receiver Joshua Palmer (shoulder), offensive lineman Jude Bowry, offensive lineman Ar'maj Reed-Adams, defensive lineman Ed Oliver (knee) and defensive lineman Landon Jackson (knee). The Rams will have safety Quentin Lake, who was questionable with a hip injury. Their inactives are wide receiver C.J. Daniels, quarterback Ty Simpson, defensive end Larrell Murchison, offensive lineman Bill Murray and tight end Max Klare.
author: Charean Williams

title: Vikings worked out JuJu Smith-Schuster
summary: The Vikings are continuing to look at veteran wide receivers.
full_text: The Vikings are continuing to look at veteran wide receivers. Today JuJu Smith-Schuster was in Minnesota for a workout, according to Tom Pelissero. The 29-year-old Smith-Schuster signed with the Giants in June and was cut by them in August. The Vikings recently brought in another veteran wide receiver who was cut by the Giants, Odell Beckham Jr., and they're continuing to look for veteran depth at the position. Smith-Schuster was originally a 2017 second-round pick of the Steelers. He has also played for the Patriots and had two stints with the Chiefs.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Monti Ossenfort on Marvin Harrison Jr. trade: These decisions are never easy
summary: At the end of his news conference Sunday, Texans coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed his team acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Cardinals.
full_text: At the end of his news conference Sunday, Texans coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed his team acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Cardinals. The Cardinals announced the trade Monday. The Cardinals will receive a second-round and a seventh-round pick (originally belonging to the 49ers) in 2027 in exchange for Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick. The agreement is still pending Harrison passing a physical. General Manager Monti Ossenfort addressed the trade in a statement. "Decisions like this are never easy," Ossenfort said. "Ultimately, we have to do what is best for our football team and that will always be the driving factor. We are extremely grateful to Marvin for what he has contributed to our organization and wish him the very best as he moves forward in his career." Harrison, the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft, finished his Cardinals career with 33 games played, 108 receptions, 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deebo Samuel to miss time with hamstring injury, Nick Bosa could return this week
summary: The 49ers are going to be down another wide receiver in the coming weeks.
full_text: The 49ers are going to be down another wide receiver in the coming weeks. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Deebo Samuel will be out of the lineup for an indefinite period of time after injuring his hamstring in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks. "Got it pretty good, so he's gonna miss some time ," Shanahan said, via 49ersWebzone.com. Samuel had two catches for 21 yards and two carries for four yards on Sunday. Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing, and Jordan Watkins are the receiver options to join Mike Evans on the field with Samuel out of action. Shanahan had more hopeful news about defensive end Nick Bosa. Bosa has missed the last three games with a calf injury, but Shanahan said that he has "a chance" of being back on the field in Week 6. The 49ers host the Commanders next Monday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL rules DT Zxavian Harris is eligible to sign with teams as a free agent
summary: The NFL has reversed course concerning defensive tackle Zxavian Harris's eligibility to play in the NFL.
full_text: The NFL has reversed course concerning defensive tackle Zxavian Harris's eligibility to play in the NFL. In a memo to teams on Monday, the NFL announced that Harris is eligible to visit, try out for or sign with any team as a free agent. Harris was initially ruled ineligible in September after attempting to join the LSU team after spending part of the offseason with the Saints as an undrafted free agent signing. Per the memo, via Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the NFL determined that Harris did not participate in football activities in college after being waived by the Saints in August. Harris had 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss, three sacks and an interception at Ole Miss last season. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright also attempted to join LSU this summer — he was on the Browns' roster — and was ruled ineligible by the league along with Harris. There's no word on a change to his status.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bucs open WR David Sills 21-day return-to-practice window
summary: When the Buccaneers return to the practice field on Wednesday, they will have wide receiver David Sills.
full_text: '' When the Buccaneers return to the practice field on Wednesday, they will have wide receiver David Sills. The team opened his 21-day return-to-practice window from injured reserve. Sills missed five games due to a hamstring injury. The Buccaneers can activate Sills from IR at any time during the next three weeks. Tampa Bay started the season with six receivers on the active roster, but Jalen McMillan went on injured reserve on Sept. 30 due to a knee injury. Sills joined the Buccaneers as a free agent in May, following the team's new offensive coordinator, Zac Robinson, from Atlanta. Sills played in Robinson's offense with the Falcons in 2025, achieving career-best totals of 18 catches for 191 yards and two touchdowns. He played the 2021-22 seasons with the Giants and the 2023 campaign in Denver before spending 2024 on the Broncos' practice squad. In his career, Sills has appeared in 33 games with 11 starts and has recorded 31 catches for 315 yards and two scores.
author: Charean Williams

title: Nick Sirianni, Jalen Hurts seems to disagree on the management of Philly's final drive
summary: On Sunday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni willingly took blame for the decision to put the kickoff in play with eight seconds left and a one-point lead over Jacksonville.
full_text: On Sunday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni willingly took blame for the decision to put the kickoff in play with eight seconds left and a one-point lead over Jacksonville. He's not willing to take blame for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that would have left the Jaguars with even less time. A 17-yard completion from quarterback Jalen Hurts to tight end Dallas Goedert had given the Eagles a first down at the Jacksonville 34. After the play, the Jaguars took their second timeout. Twenty-five seconds remained. From there, here's what happened. First, Hurts threw an incomplete pass. Twenty-one seconds remained. Then, Hurts threw to receiver Makai Lemon, who failed to go down in bounds and was pushed out of bounds after a seven-yard gain. Seventeen seconds remained. Next, a run on third down resulted in a three-yard loss. The Jaguars called their final timeout. Twelve seconds were on the clock. After the field goal, eight seconds remained. And then it all fell apart for Philly. During his postgame press conference, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts seemed to express disagreement with the management of the clock on Philly's final drive from the moment they earned a first down at the 34 with 25 seconds left. "It's not my place, and we're prepared — I'm prepared as a quarterback to not worry about those things," Hurts told reporters. "So I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game. When I'm up at night, yeah, I think about, 'Man, should I have said something, or should I have took a step back and said, "Wait"?' But ultimately, there's a commitment to that and going out there and executing. And so this was one where it did not work in our favor." On Monday, coach Nick Sirianni seemed to express disagreement with Hurts's belief that he shoul have expressed disagreement while it was happening. "Jalen's playing," Sirianni told reporters. "We're coaching and calling the plays, and Jalen's got to go execute what we call in that moment, 100 percent. We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario. He's already got enough to worry about to go out and execute. That's where we were there in that situation." Sirianni then elaborated on why the Eagles did what they did on their final drive. "Leading up to Jake [Elliott's] kick, we practice that situation every Wednesday," Sirianni said. "Every single Wednesday, we practice what we call two-minute to four-minute. It's a little more complicated than I think people understand. My opinion is that people stop trying — you get to around the 35, you're in range, and people stop trying to advance the ball forward. When you advance the ball forward, you make the kicker's job easier. We are all trying to do our part to help each other be at their best. You guys can look up the percentages when the ball gets in certain spots on the field league-wide. "Because if you don't make the kick, nothing else really matters. So, in that situation, you're trying to move the ball forward. Running it is an option, obviously, but with what Jacksonville was doing in that particular case, it wasn't going to be an option. You saw what happened when we ran it on the third down. I never think that it's something that you can say, 'OK, I'm going to wait 'til third down to pass the ball.' You have no idea how many times it's going to take you to advance the ball a little bit more forward. "We didn't get any yards and got an incomplete pass on the first play. We gained yards on the second play, and then on the third play, we ran it and lost yards there against a full-out pressure. You have to gauge what the defense is doing -- I end up watching those situations each week and any two-minute to four-minute from a -- not only do we practice it, I'll study those situations throughout the week, whatever I deem kind of came up that way in pro football. In my opinion, I think you see a lot of times teams take their foot off the gas there. Now, you'd love for the last play of the game to be your kick, but you'd also say, 'Hey, if I can get that clock under 20 seconds, you're accomplishing that as well.' Leading into that last play, I said what I said yesterday. I stand by that. I did not make the decision that I wanted to make there in that particular case, and it cost us. There's nothing else to be said about that. "But leading up to Jake's kick, to answer your question, that's my thought process there, to bring you inside that a little bit without giving too much information. That's my thought process in that situation. I stand by what I did in that situation, had eight seconds left to go in the game once we gave the ball back to them, and that's where my decision is that I regret what I did then after that. But to give them back the ball with eight seconds left, I think we did what we needed to do as an offense, and you obviously saw the success of Jake's kick in that particular case." If Lemon had simply fallen down in bounds, it wouldn't have been an issue. The Jaguars would have used their final timeout, and the Eagles could have run the ball, called a timeout with three or four seconds left, and kicked a walk-off field goal. Is that on Lemon? Is it on the coaching staff for calling a play that put the ball so close to the sideline? Is it on Hurts for throwing to a player who was near the sideline, when he had a man wide open on the thirty-two at the left hash? Regardless, Sirianni has no regrets as to how things played out before the final kickoff. Hurts apparently does. It'll be interesting to monitor that dynamic if other questions regarding game management, play-calling, etc. emerge as the year moves forward.

title: Jaguars signing LS Jacob Bobenmoyer
summary: There is now a known name for Jacksonville's new long snapper.

title: Bills elevate WR Trent Sherfield, DL Phidarian Mathis for Monday night
summary: The Bills announced a handful of roster moves ahead of Monday night's game against the Rams.
full_text: The Bills announced a handful of roster moves ahead of Monday night's game against the Rams. They have elevated wide receiver Trent Sherfield and defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis from the practice squad on a temporary basis. They also signed cornerback Anthony Kendall to the active roster from the practice squad and released linebacker Mike Danna. author: Josh Alper

title: Who can win Super Bowl 61? Identifying contenders outside of top tier that can hoist Lombardi Trophy
summary: Moving past heavy hitters like the Chiefs and 49ers leaves a dangerous second tier featuring the Jaguars, Bengals and more
full_text:
We are over one-fourth of the way through the 2026 NFL season, and it's going by fast. What have we learned through the first five weeks? Well, the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks are still pretty good, and the Kansas City Chiefs have reinvented themselves offensively with Kenneth Walker III . Those are three obvious Super Bowl favorites, but which teams offer some value?
Let's examine the "second tier" of Super Bowl contenders. For this exercise, we will eliminate the top six favorites to hoist the Lombardi trophy over at DraftKings Sportsbook. That includes the Los Angeles Rams , San Francisco 49ers, Baltimore Ravens , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks. Now, we are left with teams that have odds of at least +1200.
Below, we will examine the Super Bowl odds for seven teams that should make the playoffs, but could also be considered legitimate sleepers.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
The Detroit Lions actually have the second-shortest odds to win the NFC North right now, so do with that what you will. Dan Campbell just registered his first road win of the season on Sunday, as Detroit dominated the Arizona Cardinals , 45-21. However, beating up on a bad team doesn't exactly quell all concerns.
The Lions may lead the NFL in sacks (20), but they still rank dead last in total defense, allowing 404.4 total yards per game. Even with the 21 points allowed on Sunday, Detroit still ranks bottom four in scoring defense with 29.6 points allowed per game. This Lions team is unfortunately reminiscent of recent Lions teams. Jared Goff commands a lethal offense headlined by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown , but it's hard to believe Kelvin Sheppard's defense has the ability to support a legitimate contender. With that said, Sunday's performance against Arizona was good.
It's tough to evaluate the Chicago Bears without Caleb Williams under center. In fact, we got to watch Williams for one game, and then he was injured in a monsoon that made it nearly impossible to move the ball. That one full game was pretty impressive, though. He accounted for four total touchdowns while the offense dropped 552 total yards.
When this Bears team is healthy, they are tough to keep up with offensively. Williams can sling the rock, and D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai make up one of the fiercest rushing duos in the NFL. I do have some concerns about this Bears defense, however. The Green Bay Packers were one of the worst teams in the NFL through four weeks, and then Jordan Love came out and dropped 367 passing yards, two touchdowns and 31 total points on Chicago in a 24-point blowout victory.
Points per game differential
Out of every team on this list, the Denver Broncos are the most frustrating to watch. Take their Week 3 matchup against the Rams, for example. They go down 16-0 at halftime, only to drop 30 points in the second half and win the game. The Rams weren't the Broncos' only impressive victory this season. Don't forget they defeated Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2.
Sean Payton took back play-calling duties from Davis Webb this past week, but it didn't help. Despite the come-from-behind victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers , the Broncos recorded just 224 yards of total offense and went 1 of 12 on third downs. Yikes. Bo Nix threw for just 123 yards and one touchdown.
I feel like all the pieces are in place for the Broncos to eventually become a legitimate contender. Don't forget that they were in the AFC Championship game last year, and probably would have made the Super Bowl if Nix didn't injure his ankle in the divisional round. Nix can make all the throws you want, but he's not seeing the field too well right now and is not quick enough on the trigger. It wouldn't shock me if he starts building some momentum soon. Then, he has some decent weapons around him with Courtland Sutton , Jaylen Waddle and RJ Harvey -- who entered this past week leading the entire NFL in yards after catch. Hey coach Payton, why did you throw the ball to him just once on Sunday?
The Minnesota Vikings have to be one of the most fascinating teams in the NFL. On the one hand, they are undefeated at 5-0 with a defense that ranks first in scoring and third in total defense; on the other, Kevin O'Connell's offense ranks in the bottom six with 283.0 total yards per game. The Vikings have scored the fewest touchdowns (nine) during a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers , per CBS Sports Research.
New quarterback Kyler Murray did have his best game of the season this past Sunday against the New Orleans Saints , completing 80% of his passes for 229 yards and one touchdown while also rushing for 51 yards. Hopefully that's a sign of things to come, because the Vikings can be a legitimate Super Bowl contender if Murray morphs back into his Pro Bowl self. He has legit weaponry around him with Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison T.J. Hockenson and now Odell Beckham Jr . Watch out.
Drake Maye is back after giving the NFL quite the scare to begin the season. He threw for 374 yards, four touchdowns, zero interceptions and also rushed for a touchdown in the 45-17 beatdown of the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday and became the first New England Patriots quarterback to put up that kind of stat line in a single game. He's accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers over the past two contests, after scoring one touchdown with seven turnovers in the first three games of the season.
I also think this Patriots defense is almost being slept on. For them to do what they did to the Raiders without Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III was impressive. Then, I feel as though we've seen this defensive front take over at times. The football world isn't talking enough about the impacts rookie Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder have made. Ponder has 4.5 sacks over the last four games!
It feels like we are still figuring out what the Cincinnati Bengals are. The revamped defense started hot by forcing turnovers on three of their first four possessions of the season, but surprisingly allowed 30 points in a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. What we can't deny is that the Bengals are 3-2, which is their best five-game start since 2021 -- the year they reached the Super Bowl.
Joe Burrow is still one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are still the best receiving duo when healthy. Cincy's defense currently ranks outside the top 20, but there's a real opportunity to make a statement against Lamar Jackson and the Ravens in Week 7 following the bye.
Sunday's thrilling win in London moved the Jaguars to 4-1, but it did reveal some red flags about this team. The Jags probably should have dominated a Philadelphia Eagles squad that was without Lane Johnson , Drew Kendall , Saquon Barkley , DeVonta Smith and Jonathan Greenard, among others, but instead needed a borderline miraculous 53-yard kick return and a last-second 57-yard field goal to win.
The Jaguars' red-zone offense on Sunday was embarrassing. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone vs. Philly, including two trips where Liam Coen's offense couldn't score from the 1-yard line. With that being said, if the Jaguars can clean some of this stuff up, this team could make a serious run. Trevor Lawrence is a legitimate franchise quarterback, and he has a nice supporting cast in Parker Washington , Jakobi Meyers , Josh Cameron and sometimes Brian Thomas Jr. . Bhayshul Tuten is better than I expected as a lead back, and then Anthony Campanile's unit ranks No. 1 against the run and is tied for second in turnover differential.
This is the best team in the AFC South, and no longer some sleeper in the AFC.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: How an initial 2026 NFL Draft embarrassment actually ended up benefitting the Steelers
summary: So far, Pittsburgh has benefited from what transpired back in April
full_text:
Omar Khan's fourth NFL Draft as the Pittsburgh Steelers ' general manager could not have started worse, or at least that's how it initially looked after Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman swooped in and snatched the player Khan and the Steelers were about to select with the 20th overall pick.
Adding insult to injury was the fact that the entire process was recorded and immediately dispersed into the universe. In a matter of minutes, seemingly everyone had seen Makai Lemon chatting on the phone with Khan before Pittsburgh was leapfrogged by Philadelphia, who drafted Lemon after they pulled off a trade with, of all teams, the Dallas Cowboys , their longtime division rival.
The move was viewed as another example of Roseman's excellence at his job. Conversely, it was seen as a complete embarrassment in Pittsburgh.
Inside the Eagles draft room as they’re trying to Makai Lemon on the phone 👀 🎥: Eagles/YouTube pic.twitter.com/E484AsWiKA
#Steelers GM Omar Khan on calling WR Makai Lemon and then getting jumped by the #Eagles : “When the draft happens, there’s a lot of excitement that goes on. There was no ill intent. We made the call… The draft throws curveballs at you in every round, trust me. It happens… https://t.co/qyTNOuoRuo pic.twitter.com/qKIKuEGS6X
That sequence of events looks much different now, however. While it's still too early to say anything definitive, the Steelers are currently benefiting from what transpired six months ago.
The Steelers quickly pivoted to another need. They drafted offensive tackle Max Iheanachor , who was initially described as extremely talented yet extremely raw. Iheanachor, who was born in Nigeria and moved to the United States at 13, did not play football until he joined East Los Angeles College's team in 2021.
Iheanachor quickly developed into one of the top-ranked JUCO players, which led to him joining Arizona State's football team in 2023. He started in five games that season, became a full-time starter in 2024 and was named second-team All-Big 12 in 2025.
Iheanachor was met with early adversity with the Steelers after he sustained an injury during training camp. While the injury temporarily stunted his growth, it didn't stop the Steelers from trading Broderick Jones to the Cowboys in a move that showed how the Steelers felt about their rookie right tackle.
It didn't take long for McCarhty to insert Iheanachor into the starting lineup. In Week 3, Iheanachor came in and helped Pittsburgh rip off 411 yards and 30 points in a win over the Bengals . Since Iheanachor has taken over at starting right tackle, Pittsburgh's offense has averaged 29.3 points, 375 total yards and 119 rushing yards per game after averaging 11.5 points, 249.5 yards and 74.5 rushing yards in its first two games.
"Max is a talented young man. I think that's evident," McCarthy said after Pittsburgh's win over the Bengals. "His injury was a setback in training camp, but he's ready. It was time to give him that opportunity."
After missing out on Lemon and taking a lineman in the first round, everyone in the world knew that the Steelers were going to draft a receiver in the second round. Bernard was projected as the Steelers' best option at receiver entering Day 2 , but the question was whether or not he would actually still be on the board when Pittsburgh was on the clock with the 47th pick.
Fortunately for the Steelers, he was, and Khan was able to draft him without another team swooping in this time.
From a ranking standpoint, there was a considerable drop-off after Bernard (as it turned out, another receiver wouldn't be drafted after him until Antonio Williams went to Washington with the 71st pick). The Steelers, however, remained patient, and their patience was ultimately rewarded after watching two other receivers ( De'Zhaun Stribling and KC Concepcion ) go off the board early in the second round. They would be the last two receivers taken until Bernard was drafted by Pittsburgh.
The 6-foot-1 Bernard didn't put up big numbers in college, which is one of the reasons why seven receivers were drafted ahead of him. What he lacked in numbers, however, he made up for in versatility and reliability, among other things. He was tabbed before the draft as an ideal complementary receiver, which is what the Steelers needed alongside DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman .
Bernard is an excellent route runner, has reliable hands, and can line up on the outside and in the slot. He is also a student of the game, which helped him quickly earn Aaron Rodgers's trust .
The beginning of training camp consisted of Bernard getting limited reps with the first-team offense, while Roman Wilson got the lion's share of the work. He showed his potential in the preseason, however, making a 25-yard catch in his preseason debut and scoring his first career touchdown in Pittsburgh's preseason finale.
Bernard didn't catch a pass in Week 1 and caught just seven passes during Pittsburgh's first four games. On Sunday, though, Bernard stepped up with Pittman inactive and Wilson and Ben Skowronek leaving the game with injuries. He caught six passes for 80 yards while helping the Steelers' record a 34-22 win over the Colts .
Aaron Rodgers showing off the elusiveness @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bUqpkTsr6H
With Pittman, Wilson and Skowronek already ruled out for Pittsburgh's upcoming game, Gernard is expected to continue to get opportunities to shine.
"Football comes easy to him," McCarthy said on Monday when asked about Bernard. "I think there's some young-guy mistakes he made yesterday, but you can see it coming. I think he's acclimated very well to the offense, the ability to play all three positions — he sticks his nose in there in the run game, too. I've been very, very impressed."
The third receiver drafted, Lemon was tasked with helping the Eagles replace AJ Brown , who was traded to New England this offseason. So far, Roseman's rebuild at receiver hasn't worked out.
Through five games, the Eagles' offense is 28th in the NFL in passing. Jalen Hurts is averaging just 187 passing yards per game. In his last two games, Hurts completed 49.3% of his passes, an inexcusable percentage for a high school quarterback, let alone for a former Super Bowl MVP.
Hurts could play better, but the issues go well beyond him. For starters, he's playing for his third offensive coordinator (Sean Mannion) in three years. Philadelphia's offensive line recently saw the retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens . Saquon Barkley , a 2,000-yard rusher two years ago, has missed time due to injury.
Philadelphia's receivers haven't pulled their weight, either. That includes Lemon, who has caught just 15 of 22 targets for 108 yards. He is coming off his most productive game so far, though. He caught five passes for 43 yards in Sunday's loss to the Jaguars .
Excellent hands from Makai Lemon. pic.twitter.com/xNQsFslFk1
From the outside, it appears that Lemon's slow start can at least partly be attributed to Philadelphia's issues around him. In addition to the other issues mentioned above, Lemon isn't getting much help from his fellow receivers in terms of creating space for him. He also faces the burden of being a first-round pick.
The short answer is no. The Steelers ended up drafting two players who are currently making an impact. Iheanachor is a starter, and Bernard currently is too, given Pittsburgh's current injuries at receiver. It's safe to say that the Steelers wouldn't be 3-2 if it wasn't for their two rookies.
Conversely, the Eagles are 2-3 and are in the midst of a disappointing season. Until Lemon and the Eagles turn things around, Roseman, not Khan, will be the one who will have to defend his decisions from Day 1 of the 2026 NFL Draft.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL Week 6 picks and score predictions: Seahawks destroy Broncos, Eagles lose again, Cowboys stun Packers
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I don't think four coaches from the same division have ever been fired on the same day, but if it's ever going to happen, now would be the time, and yes, I am talking about the NFC East.
If the NFC East ceases to exist, it's because the entire division imploded in Week 5 with possibly the most disastrous week for any division ever:
I feel like the play this week is to ride this wave of incompetence and pick against every NFC East team.
So will I actually do that? Let's get to the Week 6 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . If you don't click over, I won't be offended. However, I will be offended if you don't sign up for CBSSports.com's NFL newsletter, which I'm in charge of writing.
If you do sign up, it's like an early Halloween treat for both of us: I get more sign-ups and you get an email from me twice a week. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . I promise that link takes you to the newsletter sign up page and not to the sign up page for the newsletter about small cats that I'm thinking about starting.
Alright, let's get to the picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
If the NFL ever decides to have two head coaches battle each other in a steel cage, I nominate these two. I don't know why the NFL would ever do that, but I just want to get ahead of things in case this happens.
They might not admit it, but there is no bigger coaching beef in the NFL right now than Mike Macdonald vs. Sean Payton and we wouldn't have even known about it if not for a hot mic incident involving Macdonald from earlier this year. During the incident, here's what we found out:
Payton hated everything that happened so much that he essentially banned fans from filming anything at the Broncos' training camp after that.
These signs greet #Broncos fans at training camp. A security official said the great majority of fans are following rules. The official said fans can get a warning initially and nobody is in jeopardy of being evicted unless actions “excessive.” Nobody was said to be tossed Friday pic.twitter.com/cswT91vnvk
Again, this all happened in 2024, and now that you're caught up, that brings us to this week (And if you somehow missed this very real story, we've got all the details here ).
Macdonald apologized for the fact that his comments about the situation leaked out and Payton responded to that by pretending like it wasn't a big deal, but it's definitely a big deal. It's been two years, but I still think Macdonald is mad about the fact that another team was going to accuse him of cheating, especially since it came just before he was about to serve as the head coach in his FIRST NFL GAME ever.
OK, now let's fast forward to this week. Going into this game, Macdonald has one of the best defenses in the NFL and they get to face a Broncos offense that can't get out of its own way this year. One reason the Broncos' offense has been struggling is because they keep getting off to slow starts. They've scored just 23 points in the first half this year (4.6 points per game), which is tied with the Titans -- THE TITANS -- for the fewest in the NFL.
Last week, Macdonald was probably thrilled to see that Payton decided to take over play-calling duties in Denver, because that means he can now take out two years of anger on the Broncos' coach. I was going to predict a blowout here for Seattle, but the game is in Denver, and I don't quite trust Sam Darnold against the Broncos' defense, so I'll say a 10-point Seahawks' win.
PICK: Seahawks (-3) 27-17 over Broncos
The Jaguars loved playing in London in Week 5 so much that they're sticking around for another game. The Jags will actually be making some NFL history Sunday and that's because they're going to become the first team ever to play back-to-back international "home" games. The Jags have played two consecutive games in London before, but in the past, they've played one as the road team and one as the home team. This time, they'll be the home team in both games.
I have no idea why I'm telling you any of this. I think I just needed to stall so I could decide who I actually want to pick to win this game, and now, I'm ready.
Last week, Robert Saleh called the Texans the best 0-4 team in NFL history and I don't think he was kidding.
If there's one thing I've learned about the Texans over the years, it's that there is no team better than them at losing your first few games of the season and then bouncing back to make the playoffs. In 2023, they started the season 0-2 before turning things around just in time to win the division with a 10-7 record. In 2025, they started the season 0-3 and still somehow managed to make the playoffs.
At this point, I'm starting to think the Texans are just seeing how far they can push things. If they can make the playoffs after an 0-3 start, why not 0-4?
One thing you should keep in mind about the Texans is that they're about five plays away from being 4-1.
Basically, if NFL games were only 58 minutes long instead of 60, the Texans would be 4-1. I will definitely talk to Roger Goodell about possibly making that change on the Texans' behalf, but that seems like a long shot, so please don't count on that happening.
The Texans have a chance to completely turn their season around this week. They just traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., DeMeco Ryans just started calling defensive plays again, and if they win here, they'll only be two games out of first place heading into Week 7, which is about all you can ask for when you open a season with four straight losses.
I'm going to say the Texans get their season back on track with a win here.
PICK: Texans (+3) 20-17 over Jaguars
It has been a rough week for the Eagles: They blew a win against the Jaguars, they have no healthy running backs on their roster, and now, they have to fly back from London and face a situation that no team has ever won in.
The Eagles will be going into Week 6 after playing in London and they'll be facing a Panthers team that will be coming off a bye. This will mark just the fifth time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Philadelphia: The team coming off the international game has gone 0-4.
And just when you thought it couldn't get any worse for the Eagles, I have more bad news: The team coming off the international trip has averaged just 15.25 points per game, and the ugly part is that they've been outscored 70-30 over the first three quarters in those four games. I feel like the Eagles should file a protest over this part of their schedule, but I'm not sure who they would even file the protest with.
The problem with this specific situation is that the team coming back from Europe usually needs a small adjustment period. The jet lag after the flight back to the United States usually lasts a day or two, which means it can impact practice for your next game.
On the other hand, the Panthers have been sitting at home since Oct. 5 celebrating their Week 4 win over the Lions in the Cat Bowl. I mean, just think about that: Would you rather be dealing with jet lag or celebrating a win in the Cat Bowl. That's a rhetorical question. You don't have to answer.
Not only do the Panthers have the scheduling advantage here, but they might actually be the better team. Through four weeks, Carolina's biggest weakness is that its defense can't stop the run. The Panthers are surrendering 156.5 yards per game on the ground, which is the second-highest number in the NFL, but if there's one team that might not be able to take advantage of that, it's the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby out, the Eagles were down to their third-string running back (Will Shipley) in Week 5. And well, he's now also injured.
Eagles RB Will Shipley suffered a partial tear of…
author: John Breech

title: Prisco's NFL Week 6 Power Rankings: 49ers are league's best team, Packers climb 10 spots
summary: Pete Prisco shares his latest Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big risers and fallers
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't won a Super Bowl. That doesn't mean he isn't a great coach.
If last season, in which he won 12 games with an injury-ravaged team, didn't prove how good he is at leading the 49ers, this year is doing just that.
The 49ers are 5-0 after going to Seattle and beating the Seahawks Sunday night, doing it with a defense leading the charge, rather than the Shanahan-led offense.
The 49ers limited the Seattle running attack, forced four turnovers, one of which was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown, and had five sacks, the most they've had in a game since 2024. They did it without star pass rusher Nick Bosa.
First-year defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is using a much more aggressive scheme than past Shanahan coordinators, and it's showing up in takeaways and sacks. The coverage is tighter.
Combine that with Shanahan's offensive wizardry and an MVP-type start for quarterback Brock Purdy, and it's easy to understand why the 49ers sit atop my Power Rankings. Going to Seattle and beating the defending champs sends a loud message to the rest of the league.
As for Shanahan, his greatness as a coach might not truly be earned until he wins a Super Bowl. That's just the way it is. He came close when his Jimmy Garoppolo-led 49ers had a lead last against the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII, only to see Patrick Mahomes rally to win it.
This team, provided it stays healthy, has a real shot at getting back there for Shanahan. For now, they are the league's best team with a schedule that might not be as tough as expected before the season. Plus, they already have victories over division rivals in the Rams and Seahawks.
This could be Shanahan's year to win one.
The bottom of my rankings stays the same. The Miami Dolphins remain at No. 32, but the Tennessee Titans at No. 31 will give them a run for their money this season. Neither team has won a game. Who wins first?
author: Pete Prisco

title: Rams left tackle throws punch at Bills' Bradley Chubb following Buffalo's stunning Monday night win
summary: Alaric Jackson hit the Bills' pass-rusher with an apparent sucker-punch following Buffalo's wild Monday night win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills picked up one of the wildest wins of the season on Monday night with an overtime victory over the Rams, and somehow, things actually got even wilder after the game.
Following Buffalo's 37-34 win, several players from both teams stayed on the field to do a jersey exchange and that's when the drama started. Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was trading his jersey with Buffalo's Deone Walker and while that exchange was going on, Bradly Chubb was talking trash to Jackson.
The Rams starting left tackle clearly didn't like what Chubb had to say because he walked straight over to the Bills' pass-rusher and got in his face. Jackson and Chubb then started yelling at each other, and that's when things got ugly. Jackson threw a sucker-punch at Chubb and appeared to make a connection with his face.
At that point, the two players had to be separated by their teammates. You can see a video of the incident below.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
As you can see, Jackson's punch was pretty blatant and it won't be surprising at all if the NFL ends up handing out some sort of punishment here. There is certainly precedent for the league to hand out a suspension.
During the 2025 season, Lions safety Brian Branch got hit with a one-game suspension for instigating a post-game fight following a loss to the Chiefs. That altercation actually took place on Oct. 12, 2025, exactly one year before Jackson's punch.
Jackson was suspended for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, so if he does get punished by the league, it wouldn't be his first time.
Of course, if the NFL does look into the incident, the league will certainly consider both sides of the issue. Based on post-game video, it appears that Chubb was talking trash to anyone and everyone.
Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb had to be restrained by teammates following Monday night’s game against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/f5ltQs1xin
After he left the field, Chubb was asked about the altercation.
"Just emotions. You know what I mean," Chubb said of what happened, via the California Post . "Emotional game. It was a close game. They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back, so I just chilled."
Chubb was also asked if he was quarreling with anyone specifically and it appears that Jackson wasn't the only Rams player he was talking trash to.
"It was just the whole team," Chubb said.
Chubb finished the game with just two tackles, but his team won and that's what matters.
author: John Breech

title: What we learned in NFL Week 5: Mike Evans is perfect fit with Brock Purdy, Josh Allen extends MVP lead
summary: Plus, this NFL Draft class is looking excellent early
full_text:
There are stars on Hollywood Boulevard, so, naturally, when the Rams made not one but two blockbuster trades, acquiring Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie , and the Chargers made the biggest coordinator hire in Mike McDaniel -- both dramatic all-in moves -- plenty of eyes and attention went to Southern California.
The Patriots have run football for much of the 21st century and are coming off a Super Bowl berth, so, naturally, when they traded for A.J. Brown , plenty of eyes and attention went to Beantown.
The Chiefs have run the NFL for much of the last eight years, so, naturally, when they signed Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III to take the burden off a recovering Patrick Mahomes , plenty of eyes and attention went to Kansas City.
We love superlatives: "best" offseason, "worst" offseason, "most interesting" signing, "most surprising" team ... the list goes on.
How about one that just made sense? Mike Evans to the 49ers has been a perfect marriage of talent, tendencies and scheme.
As we sort through who's legit and who's not at this still-early point in the season, we can also group the legit teams into tiers of "playoff legit" and "Super Bowl legit." At 5-0 and coming off a road win at the defending champs, the 49ers are "Super Bowl legit." Evans, who left Tampa Bay after 12 legendary years, is getting exactly what he was looking for: a place where he can contend for a title while being a huge contributor.
As for the 49ers' side of things? Well, after Evans went for seven catches, 113 yards, a touchdown and a two-point conversion against Seattle, Kyle Shanahan put it best:
"That's exactly why he's here."
These are the six lessons we learned in Week 5.
Listen, sometimes you have to toot your own horn: The 49ers signing Mike Evans was one of my favorite moves this offseason . Yes, I understood the injury/age concerns, but the fit was perfect: big, downfield wide receiver for a quarterback ( Brock Purdy ) who's more than willing to give his guys chances downfield.
And in Week 5 against the Seahawks -- a potential NFC Championship matchup -- Evans dominated. On the 49ers' final touchdown drive alone, Purdy and Evans connected four times for 75 yards, plus the two-pointer.
Mike Evans is FEASTING today 💪 @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/plnciLv8D5
MIKE. EVANS. AGAIN. @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7OlyUgWcEV
These two plays, within a minute of each other, are perfect examples of why Evans is so valuable. He can win on big in-breaking routes, and he can win on straight-line shots on the outside. What an absolute stud. He's a future Hall of Famer who's showing he still has a TON left in the tank. Last year, the 49ers scored 26 points combined in three games against Seattle (including playoffs). Sunday, they scored 32.
In Shanahan's system, the ability to attack the intermediate and deep-intermediate areas takes things to the next level. Currently, Evans is catching 2.6 passes per game on throws 10-25 yards downfield. It is extremely early, but that would be the highest rate for any player Purdy has played with, just ahead of Brandon Aiyuk . Evans isn't providing the over-the-top, long-speed prime Aiyuk did, but the fact that he's impacting the offense in a similar way is truly amazing.
That's exactly why he's there, indeed.
This was originally going to just be a lesson learned, but it was so bad that we turned it into an entire story you can read here.
How many NFL wide receivers can make both this play ...
PARKER WASHINGTON, WOW. JAGS TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ubE4xivDcD
51-YARD TOUCHDOWN FOR PARKER WASHINGTON @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Gf38EGe1Qr
You'd probably think of Ja'Marr Chase , Justin Jefferson , Puka Nacua ... players of that ilk. Well, Parker Washington showed that if he doesn't belong in that superstar group, he's up there among the groups right behind them.
Washington doesn't look the part of today's passing-game-revolves-around-me star wideouts, but he plays like one. Last year, he caught 19 of his 29 contested catch opportunities, the best of any player (min. 25 opportunities). Look at the other guys near the top of the leaderboard.
Best contested catch rate, 2025 (min. 25 opps, reg + playoffs)
Washington has now caught four of his five contested catch opportunities this season already, too.
"We consider him an elite wide receiver, so I don't know what everybody else thinks, but we feel like he's pretty freaking good," Trevor Lawrence said after the game.
I am fine waving away the Bears ' poor offensive performance Sunday with Caleb Williams out. I'm not particularly worried about that side of the ball when at full strength.
I am worried about what I saw from the defensive side. Jordan Love lit the Bears up for 367 passing yards -- the most by any player in the rivalry in the history of Lambeau Field -- and connected on five passes of 30+ air yards. The only other quarterback to hit that many in a single game is Ben Roethlisberger back in 2015. My colleague Garrett Podell had a great story on the Packers coming back to life .
But the Bears? They are the worst team in the NFL defending deep passes ... by far.
And that's despite the Bears having played three of the league's worst offensive teams (Carson Wentz-led Vikings in a downpour, Eagles , Jets ).
There are just so many examples of cornerbacks and safeties getting beat in man and in zone. Love was on a heater Sunday, sure, but there were wide-open dudes deep all day.
Jordan Love had 6 big time throws in Week 5 with 228 passing yards on these 6 throws alone These throws are beautiful pic.twitter.com/loZu2Ee3nQ
If we exclude the overmatched middle three teams on Chicago's schedule, the Bears are allowing 453 yards and 33 points per game this season, with opponents completing 70% of their passes for 10.6 yards per attempt. That's simply not good enough to get where the Bears want to go. All the defensive progress it looked like the team had made Weeks 2-4 appears to have been a product of the schedule.
The 2027 draft class has been getting a lot of publicity, even before the 2026 draft was complete. But the top of the 2026 draft, especially on defense, is looking great.
There have been a lot of fun offensive players -- Denzel Boston , First impressions aren't perfect for projecting the future. But it's so far, so good for debut defenders this season.
The Ravens beat the Falcons in a 30-23 "Sunday Night Football" overtime thriller. It's not only an impressive win for Baltimore, which was without Lamar Jackson and got a late touchdown drive plus a two-point conversion to force overtime, but also the latest example to be considered for overtime strategy.
The Ravens won the toss, chose to receive and then went down the field and scored a touchdown. Then Kyle Hamilton picked off Tua Tagovailoa to seal the win. Through two years of having this rule ...
It's a tiny sample size, and we can't draw any overarching conclusions beyond that. It's the one the NFL was hoping for: There's no "right" choice. Jesse Minter cited the win/loss records as part of his reasoning, but also the flow of the game.
"I did feel like our offense was rolling a little bit, and their defense was getting a little bit tired. And if you go out there, and you get Derrick [Henry] rolling again, now you're out of two-minute mode, and you're back into normal offense, that we could punish them with the run game a little bit, and that's what happened."
The Ravens' overtime drive took over seven minutes and forced the Falcons to use both of their timeouts. That's another advantage of taking the ball first: You don't have to worry about the clock on your opening drive. The Falcons, on the other hand, had to be in hurry-up mode after getting the ball with just 2:50 left and no timeouts.
Another advantage of taking the ball first is the idea of the "third possession." If it's still tied after each team…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Sean McVay cannot rely on the Rams' special teams -- and the Rams must fix it before it's too late ... again
summary: The Rams are 32nd in the NFL in special teams expected points added
full_text:
Of all the wild moments in the Bills ' 37-34 win over the Rams , the one that set up Buffalo's win -- and maybe the worst decision of the night -- was Sean McVay deciding to run the ball on a third-and-5 at the Bills' 30-yard line in overtime and settle for a 48-yard field goal attempt.
The attempt got blocked, the Bills scored on their ensuing possession, and the game was over. The preseason Super Bowl favorites -- the dream team that has already had three nightmare losses -- are 2-3.
Now ask yourself, would you rather trust the right arm of 2025 MVP Matthew Stafford , who ran red-hot all of the second half and overtime, to gain 5 yards or the right leg of Harrison Mevis to make a kick from 48 yards?
This was a coaching failure on McVay's part. The Rams have Stafford, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams . Stafford was 24-for-31 for 284 yards and two touchdowns in the second half plus overtime. And you basically give up on offense to bring on your special teams unit? McVay is an excellent coach, but even excellent coaches make mistakes, and this one was truly gross.
"I wish I would've had a better play call and gone for it, gotten it a lot tighter," McVay said. "I'm sick right now with myself. ... I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go for it on third down and go to fourth or whatever it was, and that's on me."
He's right, but those words carry little meaning now. All that matters is that he and the Rams learn a lesson they've been apprehensive to learn (to put it nicely) or damningly ignorant of (to put it harshly): Special teams can and will cost them their Super Bowl dreams ... again.
"It's got to get better,'' McVay added. "We're gonna be able to figure out how to be able to fix this, but it can't continue like this with regards to our kicking operation ... Ultimately, it's my responsibility."
Last year, the Rams finished 31st in special teams expected points added. In a crucial Week 16 matchup against the Seahawks , they gave up a punt return touchdown, and Mevis missed a field goal. The Rams lost by one. In the NFC Championship game, also against the Seahawks, Xavier Smith muffed a punt, leading to a Seattle touchdown one play later. The Rams lost by four.
This year's Rams are dead last in special teams EPA -- somehow worse than last year! In addition to the Mevis miss and the Mevis blocked kick, the Rams gave up a 70-yard return on the opening kickoff. But this runs far deeper than a one-night issue.
The Rams once again failed to address this issue during the offseason and are scrambling. Last year, they fired the special teams coordinator and replaced the kicker midseason. They might have undergone similar changes this year; in fact, they've already released Smith. More changes are surely coming.
The cold, hard truth is that when it comes to the upper echelons of Super Bowl contention, you are only as strong as your weakest link. And the Rams' weakest link is one of the weakest links in the entire NFL. It will be exposed again and again until it changes; it should not matter whether it takes 100 kicker tryouts and 100 special-teamer tryouts, or a trade.
The Rams can collect stars. They can have everything else in place. But continuing to treat special teams as an afterthought is like building a 1,000-piece LEGO set perfectly but forgetting the two pieces that hold it all together, and then it all comes crashing down as soon as you try to display it.
It is said that those who don't learn from the past are doomed to repeat it. If McVay and GM Les Snead cannot learn from the nightmarish past -- and, now, the nightmarish present -- when it comes to special teams, the Rams' Super Bowl dreams will be crushed, and they will have only themselves to blame.
