title: Bill Belichick noticeably absent from Patriots' celebration of 2001 Super Bowl team
summary: Belichick recently attended the Giants' Super Bowl reunion
full_text:
Bill Belichick recently attended the New York Giants ' 40th anniversary of the franchise's first Super Bowl-winning team. Belichick met up with former players from that team during a private dinner. He left before the Giants' win over the Cardinals , which included a halftime ceremony honoring the 1986 Giants.
Two members of the 2021 Patriots were noticeably absent from this weekend's 25th-anniversary celebration: Belichick and former quarterback Tom Brady .
A color commentator, Brady's absence was understandable as he was on assignment in Seattle. Belichick is also busy, given his role as North Carolina's coach. But if he was able to make time to attend the Giants' anniversary, couldn't he have done the same for the '01 Patriots?
There are two possible answers. Belichick may have actually been busy, or it may be because he continues to harbor ill will toward how his time in New England ended.
At the time, Patriots owner Robert Kraft called it a mutual parting, but it's become clear over time that Belichick was forced out after the 2023 season. Belichick didn't appreciate how his exit was handled, and it's impacted his relationship with the franchise in the years since.
Last year, in his first year as the Tar Heels' coach, Belichick acknowledged that Patriots scouts were prohibited from being at North Carolina's facilities.
"It's clear I'm not welcome there at their facility. So they're not welcome at ours," Belichick said at the time.
Both Kraft and Belichick have exchanged public barbs since their split. Kraft initially said that he made a "big risk" by trading for Belichick (who was under contract with the Jets ) to become the Patriots' new coach ahead of the 2000 season. Belichick responded by saying that he was the one who took a risk by coming to New England.
"As I told Robert multiple times through the years, I took a big risk by taking the New England Patriots head coaching job," Belichick told ESPN . "I already had an opportunity to be the Head Coach of the New York Jets, but the ownership situation was unstable."
While the current situation between the two isn't great, Kraft and Belichick enjoyed a historic partnership during their 23 seasons together. Over that span, the Patriots won six Super Bowls, nine AFC titles, and 17 division titles. It was the longest-sustained run of success by a franchise in NFL history.
The 2001 Patriots started the dynasty. After a 0-2 start, the '01 Patriots finished the regular season with an 11-5 record. New England went 11-3 after Brady replaced an injured Drew Bledsoe in the starting lineup. Brady's steady play complemented a defense that allowed an average of just 17 points per game.
The Patriots ran the table in the playoffs, defeating the Raiders , Steelers and Rams to capture the franchise's first Super Bowl title. The 20-17 win over Los Angeles is still one of the biggest upsets in Super Bowl history.
That team's accomplishments were celebrated on Sunday. Patriots fans showered the team with cheers at halftime of New England's eventual win over the Raiders.
Choosing to be introduced as a team... The 2001 New England Patriots 👏 pic.twitter.com/hOsdP20R0d
Belichick wasn't in attendance on Sunday, but he'll have plenty of more opportunities to attend future Patriots' Super Bowl teams. The 2003 team's 25th anniversary, for example, will take place in 2028.
Kraft has also alluded to building a statue for Belichick , a gesture that might compel the team's former coach to return to his old stomping grounds.

title: Rams vs. Bills prediction, odds: Matthew Stafford, Josh Allen clash in Week 5 'MNF' matchup
summary: Here's how to watch Rams vs. Bills, along with the latest odds, key matchups and our Week 5 'Monday Night Football' prediction
full_text:
In the Week 5 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Los Angeles Rams host the Buffalo Bills .
The Rams are coming off a too-close-for-comfort win over the Philadelphia Eagles , having improved to 2-2 on in the process. They have not quite been the super team many expected, though injuries have played their part. They have a chance to get above .500 if they can capture a win against the Bills on Monday night.
The Bills, meanwhile, are coming off their first loss of the season, having dropped a dispiriting game against the division rival New England Patriots . The Bills had started 3-0 behind a pair of explosive offensive performances in Weeks 1 and 2 and then a comeback victory despite turning the ball over five times in Week 3. Their defense hasn't been up to snuff, and the Rams present a tremendous challenge.
Will the Rams leave the stadium with a winning record, or will the Bills bounce back from last week's defeat? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
You can follow along live here on our blog.
The Bills gained more than 400 yards and scored at least 36 points in each of their first two games of the season, playing pristine football as they secured wins against the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions . They did not turn the ball over at all and they looked like an absolute machine as they worked their way through those two defenses with relative ease.
Over the last two weeks, things have been a bit choppier, as the Bills didn't top 350 yards in either game and turned the ball over multiple times against both the Los Angeles Chargers (five) and New England Patriots (two), scoring 24 and 26 points, respectively. They were fortunate to escape with a win against L.A., but didn't get quite so lucky against New England and suffered their first loss of the season.
The Rams, meanwhile, were torn asunder by the division rival San Francisco 49ers back in Week 1, but have since been incredibly stingy on defense. They've held each of their last three opponents under 260 yards, and two of them under 185. Their pass defense, in particular, has been remarkable, but the run defense has also been quite good since that first game. And they've done it without Myles Garrett (who got knee surgery following the Week 1 game) and, last week, without Aaron Donald (who is set to return on Monday after a one-game absence).
Buffalo is without wide receiver Josh Palmer on Monday night, and could be without No. 1 target DJ Moore as well. Moore is questionable after missing two of his last three practices. That could mean Josh Allen is down to Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid as his passing-game options, leaving the Bills shorthanded against what has been an excellent pass defense over the last three weeks and that gets Jaylen Watson back after he missed most of the last two games.
Allen, of course, is capable of turning any group of skill-position players into a functional one, as we saw over most of the last two years before the Bills traded for Moore. It's worth noting, though, that the Rams have entirely shut down the tight end position so far this year, allowing 12 catches for a league-low 85 yards to players at the position. Kincaid could therefore have a tough time getting going here, meaning the passing game would have to run through Coleman (who could see a lot of Trent McDuffie , who is playing at an extraordinarily high level) and Shakir. Allen can obviously make that work; it would just be more difficult than if he had Moore in addition to the other weapons.
James Cook — who led the NFL in rushing last season — is averaging an incredible and career-best 6.0 yards per carry so far this year, and has tagged two of four opponents for at least 135 yards on the ground. The Rams were run all over by San Francisco back in Week 1, but have since limited opposing backs in a big way. They haven't exactly faced a murderer's row of running games ( Giants , Broncos , Eagles) during that span, though, so they could find it tougher to contain Cook here. Cook getting going would obviously take some of the pressure off of Allen and the potentially weapons-depleted passing game.
After sputtering to just 290 total yards back in their Week 1 game in Australia, the Rams have put up at least 415 yards in each of their last three games stateside. The only thing that's kept them from truly exploding offensively has been turnovers, as they've given the ball away two times in each of their games so far this season — including those last three where they piled up all the yardage.
After throwing 46 touchdowns against just eight interceptions on his way to an MVP season a year ago, Matthew Stafford has already been picked off six times. Stafford only completed 61% of his passes, and he's down from 7.9 to 7.3 yards per attempt. Stafford, of course, didn't have Puka Nacua for two of those games, but even with Nacua back last week, he was at just 62.7% completions and 6.2 yards per attempt while being held scoreless and intercepted twice. He just has not played up to last year's standard yet.
Buffalo's defense, though, has been vulnerable through the air early on in the Jim Leonhard era. The Bills have gotten excellent pass rush from Greg Rousseau (who leads the league with six sacks and ranks third with 29 total pressures) and great play inside from Deone Walker (19 pressures and three batted passes) but the back end has been leaky, with opponents totaling the sixth-most passing yards in the league through four weeks, along with 10 touchdown passes against just two interceptions.
Christian Benford returning to the lineup after he missed last week's loss against New England will help, but the Bills could still have their hands full with Nacua and Davante Adams — the latter of whom looks reinvigorated (career-best 10.3 yards per target) after repeated red-zone touchdown connections overshadowed a significant drop in efficiency last year. (He averaged just 6.9 yards per target, the fourth-worst mark of his 13-year career.) Adams was quiet last week against Philly (four catches for 32 yards on nine targets), but during the previous two games, he caught 15 passes for 332 yards and two touchdowns in Nacua's absence.
It's worth noting that the Bills have given up the sixth-most catches, seventh-most yards and second-most touchdowns to running backs as pass-catchers so far this season. The Rams typically rarely target their running backs with the pass, but that has changed with Kyren Williams . Watch out for him on underneath routes.
Williams and Blake Corum have also been highly efficient on the ground, combining for 87 carries for 456 yards and three touchdowns. That's an average of 5.2 yards per carry, and they each have success rates over 50% while Williams leads the league with a 64.8% rate on his runs. The Bills have given up only 0.98 yards before contact per carry so far this year, per Tru Media, but they've allowed 3.05 after contact thanks to one of the highest missed-tackle rates in the league. They can't allow Williams and Corum to slip out of their grasp here.
So far this season, the Rams have alternated between looking like the Rams team we expected and a much different version than that. That's largely due to injuries that have led to inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. The pass defense has been largely excellent, though, and the return of Aaron Donald should help the run defense. I don't think Buffalo has anyone that can deal with the Puka Nacua-Davante Adams-Kyren Williams trio, so the Rams should put some points on the board here. Pick: Rams 28, Bills 24

title: Is DJ Moore playing on 'Monday Night Football?' A look at the Bills WR's status vs. Rams
summary: Moore was initially listed as questionable with a shoulder injury
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills will help conclude Week 5 in the NFL when they roll into SoFi Stadium for a "Monday Night Football" heavyweight matchup with the Los Angeles Rams . This could very well be a Super Bowl preview between two of the league's elite clubs, but  Buffalo won't be firing on all cylinders offensively as top wideout DJ Moore is officially inactive for the contest as he continues to deal with a nagging shoulder injury.
After not practicing on Thursday or Friday because of the ailment, Moore returned to the practice field on Saturday in a limited capacity, which held out hope and led to his questionable designation.
On Monday afternoon, the Bills elevated wide receiver Trent Sherfield Sr. from the practice squad, indicating that Moore was truly a game-time decision.
Roster moves: - Signed CB Anthony Kendall from the practice squad - Released OLB Mike Danna - Elevated DL Phidarian Mathis and WR Trent Sherfield Sr. from the practice squad
Moore, who was acquired by the Bills this offseason in a trade with the Chicago Bears , initially suffered the injury in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions . He has yet to miss a game due to the injury, but it has lingered, and he re-aggravated it in the second quarter of last week's loss to the New England Patriots .
When Moore has been on the field, he's been the type of top target that the Bills were hoping to give Josh Allen when they struck the deal with Chicago. Through four games, Moore has caught 12 balls for 178 yards and a touchdown. While those are modest numbers, the injury has helped keep the production deflated. That said, in the two games he did not leave with an injury, Moore was a go-to resource for Allen in the passing game.

Former second-round pick Keon Coleman will need to carry more of the receiving workload. Those six catches were tied for the second-most in a game in his career, while his receiving yards were also second-best of his career.
In Week 4, five of Coleman's six catches went for first downs, and he averaged 12.8 air yards per target. That quantifies just how much of an explosive weapon he was in that contest, and he finished the game with four of his catches going for 16-plus yards.

title: Cowboys hire former NFL head coach, Packers' DC to help fix struggling defense
summary: Brian Schottenheimer is calling in reinforcements after Thursday night's loss against the Bucs
full_text:
Brian Schottenheimer is turning to a familiar face in an effort to improve his struggling defense. On Monday, Schottenheimer announced the hiring of Mike Pettine as the Cowboys' new senior defensive assistant. It was one of the upcoming changes Schottenheimer alluded to amid the Cowboys' 2-3 start to the season.
Pettine, 60, worked alongside Schottenheimer when they were both coordinators under Rex Ryan with the New York Jets . In both 2009 and 2010, Pettine's defense helped the Jets get within a game of the Super Bowl . During those playoff runs, Pettine's defense defeated offenses led by quarterbacks such as Carson Palmer , Philip Rivers , Peyton Manning and Tom Brady .
Pettine also has experience working with Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Pettine actually gave Parker his first NFL job in 2019 when Pettine was entering his second season as the Green Bay Packers ' defensive coordinator. (On a related note, the Cowboys face the Packers this weekend at Lambeau Field.)
"He's gonna be here in a role to support everything that CP is leading and guiding," Schottenheimer said of the hire .
Pettine's NFL background also includes two years as the Cleveland Browns ' head coach during the 2014 and 2015 seasons. He most recently served as the Minnesota Vikings ' assistant head coach/outside linebackers coach.
Schottenheimer shared that the idea of a senior defensive assistant was initially raised when Parker was tabbed as defensive coordinator. They had two potential coaches in mind to fill that role, but they decided not to immediately fill the position when those situations dissolved.
That position will now be filled by Pettine, a former high school head coach who broke into the NFL in 2002 with the Baltimore Ravens . Pettine has coached and worked alongside a slew of notable defensive players in the NFL, including Hall of Famers Ray Lewis, Ed Reed and Darrelle Revis .
"I think Pett's experience, not only in football, but his experience in this system of what we do," Schottheimer said. "His understanding of the 3-4 family. He has the awareness of some of our players: Kenny Clark , Rashan Gary . He was the coordinator when CP was there. So, I think it's just a great fit and just a guy who certainly brings a bunch of experience to the staff, myself included."
Pettine's addition obviously can't hurt what has statistically been one of the NFL's worst defensive units through the season's first five weeks. The unit is 26th in the NFL in points allowed, 25th in passing touchdowns allowed, 29th in average yards-per-carry allowed, 32nd in third-down efficiency and 25th in red zone efficiency. Dallas' defense has allowed at least 20 points in each of its first five games and has allowed at least 30 points twice.
It's safe to say that Dallas' 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay last Thursday night compelled Schottenheimer to fill his senior defensive assistant vacancy.   The Cowboys' defense struggled against an undrafted rookie ( Jalon Daniels ) making his second career start and first road start. They also allowed running back Bucky Irving to run for a career-high 165 yards.
Cowboys fans should look at this move favorably, as it shows Schottenheimer's eagerness to improve his defense. In Pettine, Parker will now have a trusted face to go to moving forward. Parker can bounce ideas off of him, and Pettine can offer suggestions and insight whenever he deems it necessary.
Coaching staff aside, there is another reason why Cowboys fans should feel a little better about the defense moving forward: Joey Porter Jr. , who likely would have made a difference against Tampa Bay. Porter was unable to play, however, after experiencing symptoms of an illness prior to kickoff.
Porter practiced on Monday ahead of Sunday night's big game against the Packers, who are coming off their most impressive win of the season, a 31-7 pummeling of the Chicago Bears .
Another potential positive was a players-only meeting held earlier in the day. Afterward, the players said that the unit's issues so far are on them, not Parker and the rest of the coaching staff.
"It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation," DeMarvion Overshown said of the meeting . "It was more so what can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays or even Monday walkthroughs?
"We got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. So as long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're gonna be great."

title: Michael Penix Jr. injury: Falcons QB's injury not considered serious but Week 6 status unclear, per report
summary: Penix might be available for Sunday's game against the Bears
full_text:
The latest injury in Michael Penix Jr.'s snakebitten career was particularly cruel not only for him but for his team, too. Penix took a hard hit to his ribs late in regulation, knocking him out for overtime of the Falcons ' eventual 30-23 loss to the Ravens on "Sunday Night Football."
Penix's injury is not considered serious, according to ESPN , who added that he could potentially play in Sunday's game against the Bears . Atlanta plans to exercise caution, however, and will monitor his practice this week before making a decision on his status for Week 6.
Here's the hit from Tavius Robinson that caused Penix's injury:
MICHAEL PENIX TAKEN DOWN HARD HE IS IN PAIN pic.twitter.com/Ref6DhrROW
Initially, Penix missed just one play — the one immediately following the hit — when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game and found Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain on second-and-20. Penix returned and threw a ball away under pressure, and the Falcons punted to end regulation.
The Ravens took the ball to start overtime and produced a touchdown drive that lasted over seven minutes. Cameras panned multiple times to the sideline, where Atlanta's medical staff was working on/examining Penix's right ribs. When Atlanta came out on offense, Tagovailoa entered while Penix had a towel over his head, distraught as he could only watch from the sideline. After the game, Penix said he was emotional because he wants to finish games and is frustrated by how many times he hasn't been able to do so.
"I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt, and I did not feel like I was gonna be able to give our team what we needed to help us win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling, so that's all that happened," Penix said. "I was trying to get out there. [I] feel like if we had the ball first in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as we were sitting, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold."
Tagovailoa found Drake London for 20 yards on Atlanta's first offensive play of overtime, but got picked off by Kyle Hamilton on the next snap.
KYLE HAMILTON PICKS IT OFF! @RAVENS WIN! pic.twitter.com/CbkK3CiuUN
Though Kevin Stefanski said the team will need to conduct more imaging and testing before establishing a timeline for Penix's return, Penix speaking to the media is a good sign.
"Knowing me, I'mma be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough my career," Penix said. "... I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field."
Penix, who missed the first two games of the season, had been a huge reason Atlanta turned its season around from 0-2 to 2-2 and is still afloat now at 2-3. The Falcons have now had four different quarterbacks play this season already: Penix, Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (who started the first two games) and Jack Strand (who relieved a struggling Rush in a 34-3 loss in Week 2).
Penix's ability to push the ball downfield helped free up the running game and make the passing game, mainly through London, come to life. The Falcons would very much like Penix's self-diagnosed availability for Week 6 to be accurate, given how much the team has struggled without him.
Sunday's game is a big one for both teams. Atlanta is sitting at 2-3 after dropping Sunday night's game. Chicago is 3-2 after also coming up short in Week 5 against the Packers .

title: NFL suspends Dre Greenlaw one game after head-butting incident in 49ers' win over Seahawks
summary: The discipline stems from a second-quarter incident where the linebacker drew a late-hit flag on Sam Darnold and headbutted a helmetless Ernest Jones IV
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw has been suspended for one game without pay after he was ejected during the 49ers' 32-29 victory over the Seattle Seahawks , per the NFL . Greenlaw is scheduled to miss the 49ers' Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders , but he is allowed to appeal the NFL's decision.
During the second quarter, Greenlaw drew a flag for a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold on the Seattle sideline and was confronted by several Seahawks players, including linebacker Ernest Jones . As the two players met face-to-face, Greenlaw head-butted the helmetless Jones, leading to his ejection.
Greenlaw was ejected after headbutting Jones on the sideline pic.twitter.com/N8M1ucPWfD
"During the second quarter, Greenlaw used his helmet to headbutt Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who was not wearing a helmet, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the league said in its statement.
Greenlaw has been suspended before, receiving a one-game ban last year during his stint with the Denver Broncos . That came after he aggressively ran after an official while yelling at them following a game-winning field goal. Greenlaw has also been ejected multiple times before, including in 2022 following a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert , and later that same year in the playoffs, when he threw a jab at Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro.
In five games played this season, Greenlaw has recorded 37 tackles and one forced fumble.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Javon Hargrave out for season with torn Achilles: Three trade targets for Packers
summary: Green Bay is running short on healthy defensive linemen after losing Hargrave and Edgerrin Cooper to season-ending Achilles injuries
full_text:
The Packers ' 31-7 win over the Bears was Green Bay's best and most important victory this season , a sign the team could be headed in the right direction after a rocky first few weeks. Headed in the wrong direction, though, is the team's health on defense. One week after the team lost standout linebacker Edgerrin Cooper for the season with a torn Achilles, defensive lineman Javon Hargrave suffered the same injury and is also done for the year, per ESPN .
"That kind of takes the air out of the room a little bit, when you lose ... not only a great player but a great guy, a key piece to this team, and it kind of puts a little bit of a cloud on the day," coach Matt LaFleur said.
The timing adds to that cloudiness; the injury occurred late in the blowout win, and he had to be carted off the field.
Hargrave, a Pro Bowler in 2021 and 2023, signed a two-year, $23 million deal this offseason and was expected to bolster a Green Bay interior that struggled down the stretch of last year. Hargrave has played just a hair under the Packers' defensive snaps this year, and his injury is the third to the position group. Warren Brinson (calf/groin) is on IR, and Jordon Riley (Achilles recovery) remains on the PUP list. Anthony Campbell (ankle) missed Week 5 as well.
The Packers' healthy defensive linemen (not including edge rushers) are Karl Brooks , Chris McClellan , Jonathan Ford and Devonte Wyatt .
The injury is also unfortunate as it comes just as Micah Parsons was nearing a return from his torn ACL. He's still officially on the PUP list but could be back in the coming weeks.
With so many injuries up front, Green Bay could look for outside help with the Nov. 10 trade deadline less than a month away. The Packers are down a 2027 first-round pick due to the Parsons trade but own all of their other picks in next year's draft as well as the Cowboys ' fourth-rounder from the Rashan Gary trade this offseason.
The Packers may slow-play the exploration of trade options. They're 3-2, but Sunday's win over the Caleb Williams-less Bears shouldn't make them rash buyers. If they do want to buy, though, three interior defensive linemen stand out.
Daron Payne has been the subject of trade rumors a few times, yet he's spent all nine seasons of his career with Washington. Could this be the year he gets moved? The Commanders are 1-3-1 and reeling after an embarrassing clock management debacle against the Giants . He is in the final year of a four-year, $90 million deal.
Payne, 29, is coming off his best game of the year, which included a sack. He has generally been a dependable, available (two games missed over the last seven years) starter in the middle, and he's a significant part of what's been a solid run defense this year.
The Commanders' decision makers, though, are in a precarious position. Coach Dan Quinn should be on the hottest of hot seats, and GM Adam Peters' tenure has produced mixed-at-best results of late. If Peters knows he'll be back for next year, he might be more willing to deal Payne and recoup draft assets.
The Dolphins spent all offseason getting rid of many of their most important, older players from their last regime. Zach Sieler was one of a few exceptions. He has been a steady presence -- and a very good, under-recognized player in general -- in the middle of Miami's defensive line. If he played on a better team or in a bigger football market, he'd probably have been a multi-time Pro Bowler; he had 10 sacks in both 2023 and 2024.
Sieler can still get it done at 31. He had two sacks in Week 4 against the Vikings and has five tackles for loss this season. He has consistently been solid against both the run and the pass. The Dolphins needed to keep some veterans around early as they transitioned to a new regime, but it might be worth exploring the next step, especially if Sieler prioritizes playing for a competitive team.
Through five weeks, the top interior defensive lineman in Pro Football Focus' ranks is ... A'Shawn Robinson . Yes, the well-traveled veteran, now 31, is dominating against the run and also has a sack. He has a tackle on nearly 20% of the snaps he's played against the run, a terrific number, and is a huge reason the Buccaneers are allowing the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL this year.
Robinson's on a one-year deal. Like the Commanders, the Buccaneers might be holding out hope they don't have to sell -- at least not yet. But if the trade deadline approaches closer and the 1-4 Bucs aren't getting more competitive, Robinson, on a one-year deal, could become an attractive option for playoff contenders.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Should winless Titans bench Cam Ward? Why abandoning the former No. 1 pick will not fix Tennessee's turmoil
summary: Turning to Mitch Trubisky will not fix an offense averaging just 11.6 points or an expensive, revamped defense that has disappointed
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans fell to 0-5 on Sunday after being handily defeated by their rival, the Houston Texans , 26-3. The Texans were also winless heading into this matchup, but they used the hapless Titans as a get-right game.
Tennessee is a disaster, in more ways than one. This was the top team in the AFC just five years ago. Now, the Titans are unrecognizable. No, literally — they are unrecognizable. The Titans debuted new uniforms, created a new logo, and found new ways to disappoint everyone in Nashville.
Reporters who have covered this franchise since the move to the Volunteer State in 1997 claim this is as bad as it's ever been, and it's hard to disagree with that assessment. The Titans are now 6-33 over the past three seasons and 2-18 at home. Both rank worst in the NFL . You read that correctly, by the way. The Titans have won two home games over the last three years. The last victory in front of their home fans came against a Chris Oladokun-led Kansas City Chiefs team last season.
Titans players and coaches have talked about "owning the (AFC) south." Tennessee is 2-20 in its past 22 divisional games, the worst record over that span since the 2008-2012 Cleveland Browns .
A major talking point when it comes to this "Titanic" disaster is the play of the quarterback. Former No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward has not looked like a legitimate starter through five games, and he's entering some pretty dangerous historical territory as the losses mount. Ward is now 3-19 as an NFL starter. It's the second-worst QB record through 22 starts all-time, behind Steve DeBerg (2-20).
Maybe wins aren't a legitimate QB stat, but through five games, Ward ranks 28th in both passer rating (77.2) and passing yards per game (179.2). He's thrown just three touchdowns. Jaxson Dart had three passing touchdowns in his one full game played this season.
The "bench Cam Ward" movement has picked up steam over the past 24 hours, but head coach Robert Saleh quickly dismissed the idea of sitting his second-year signal-caller .
"Cam's our starting quarterback," Saleh told reporters on Sunday. "We're gonna give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're gonna continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better."
Should the Titans bench Ward after five games? No. I don't think they should, and here's why:
As we exit Week 5, the Titans rank dead last in total offense (246.4 yards per game), dead last in scoring offense (11.6 points per game), and second-worst in passing offense (163.8 yards per game). No, your eyes aren't lying to you, the Titans stink. However, it's not just their quarterback.
This isn't a 2025 Minnesota Vikings situation, where Kevin O'Connell was forced to make a change under center because it was the one thing holding his team back. The Vikings had a top-three defense and a talented supporting cast ready to take off. The Titans don't have a Brian Flores defense or a Justin Jefferson . Benching Ward for Mitch Trubisky doesn't turn you into a playoff team.
Against the Texans, Ward completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards and one interception. He was bad, but his offensive line got absolutely WORKED. It was upsetting because the play of the offensive line through four weeks was one of the few bright spots for the Titans. Not on Sunday. That bright spot was blotted out by one of the best defensive lines in the NFL, which took over this game.
Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter combined for four sacks and five QB hits. Left tackle Dan Moore Jr . had maybe the worst game of his Titans career, right tackle JC Latham lost reps against his former Alabama teammate, and paying Peter Skoronski all that money in the offseason didn't make any difference.
pic.twitter.com/thDGXM0TiE
The Titans' entire offensive operation on Sunday was abysmal, from passing to blocking to running to even catching. Putting Trubisky in is not fixing all of this.
Then what about the defense? Saleh is regarded as one of the best defensive minds in football, and the Titans celebrated his arrival by completely revamping that side of the ball. Tennessee paired Jeffery Simmons with new running mates on the interior, such as John Franklin-Myers , Jordan Elliott and Solomon Thomas . At pass rusher, the Titans traded for another former Saleh player in Jermaine Johnson II and drafted Keldric Faulk late in the first round. The Titans also added two new starters at cornerback in Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott. I'm not sure any of these additions have panned out just yet.
Through five weeks, the Titans rank No. 19 in total defense (331.8 yards allowed per game), tied for 10th-worst in sacks (10), eighth-worst in EPA per play (.03), tied for last in takeaways and rank dead last in total defensive pressures (44). The defense has been disappointing all year.
During the Week 1 loss to the New York Jets , there was a second-quarter drive in which the Jets rushed 15 times on their way to a field goal. They picked up 74 yards on 19 plays and took up 11:48 of game time. That's called imposing your will. In Week 2 against the Philadelphia Eagles , Jalen Hurts and Co. converted on 12 of their 19 combined third and fourth downs. That same Eagles team went 0-12 on third downs vs. the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Then, during the Titans' matchup against the Baltimore Ravens last week, Lamar Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first two quarters. He didn't need to take the field in the second half because the 24-7 lead he built was enough to win the game.
Spotrac claims the Titans spent the most money in free agency this offseason ($319,877,500). You would never be able to tell by the play on the field.
I'm not defending Ward's play, which, again, has been bad, sad, disappointing — whatever descriptor you want to use. What I contend is that he's not the only problem on a very bad team.
The Titans have registered four losing seasons in a row, including two straight 3-14 campaigns. What was the goal for the franchise this year with a new head coach in Saleh and a new offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll? To me, the answer to that question was easy: Find out what you have in Cam Ward.
This season was all about figuring out what you have at quarterback. You can't do that with him on the bench. There are fans out there totally ready to give up on Ward and punt on their former No. 1 overall pick after 22 games. That would be an emotional decision. I actually thought Ward put together his best game of the season just eight days ago in Baltimore, throwing for 222 yards, one touchdown and an interception that wasn't his fault, while rookie Carnell Tate enjoyed a breakout performance with 145 yards receiving.
Maybe there was a disconnect with some people about the expectations for the Titans this season? You had Kyle Brandt on national television riling up the fan base by picking them to make the playoffs for some reason. I was expecting a "6-11"- type season from the Titans this year, so I can agree it's looked worse than I thought it would. But do you really want to pull the plug on the Ward experiment right now? Why not accumulate all the data you can before banishing him from Music City?
CBS Sports senior NFL writer Pete Prisco said on Sunday that Ward deserves the rest of the season to prove what he can do. But if he continues to play like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL, then yes, Tennessee will once again hop on the QB carousel.
Should the Titans draft a quarterback next year? 🤔 @PriscoCBS weighs in. #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/mGkqEpbuAt
Ward should not be benched after a 0-5 start, but I can admit that a benching could be coming.
It's easy for me to sit back and act like this is my "Madden" video game. "Let's sim to next year and draft Jeremiah Smith." The fact of the matter is, people's jobs are on the line. Being an employee of the Titans is an incredibly scary thought. It feels like those people don't have any job security. Seriously,…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline candidates: Khalil Mack leads five Pro Bowl players who could be moved next
summary: The winless Chargers have little reason to retain Mack, an aging pass rusher on an expiring contract who could help a playoff contender
full_text:
There have been four in-season trades since the 2026 NFL campaign kicked off five weeks ago, and each of them involved a big-name player. Former Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . is the most recent mover with the NFC West's last-place team sending him to the Houston Texans , and he joined Cam Jurgens , Joey Porter Jr . and J.J. McCarthy as those to be dealt ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
More transactions are on the way, with less than a month to go until the deadline. The time of year has arrived at which teams have to decide whether to spend on impact players who can help them win right now or to sell off their best assets and look ahead to the future. Veterans on expiring contracts playing for bad teams are always the likeliest to be dealt in-season, and there are a number of them who come to mind after the first quarter of the 2026 season.
Some trades may not move the needle all that much. Others will feature star players or prospects like Harrison who may deliver breakout seasons with new teams.
Here are five players with at least one career Pro Bowl selection who could be next in line to be traded.
The Chargers ' season went down the drain before it ever really started. They were supposed to open the year at 2-0 before embarking on a gauntlet of a schedule, but they dropped both of those games as favorites and still have not won a game in five tries. Since things are clearly not working in Los Angeles, it might be time for a complete reboot . And even if they do not tear everything down, Khalil Mack still makes loads of sense as a trade candidate.
Mack is 35 years old but on pace for his most sacks since 2023, when he finished ninth in Defensive Player of the Year voting. This might be one of the Chargers' last chances to trade him for something meaningful, especially since he is on a one-year contract. There is no guarantee he returns in 2026, and if he does, the Chargers cannot bank on him playing like this again. A playoff team would be better suited to benefit from Mack's late-career efforts than one still searching for its first victory.
Surprisingly, with three wins in five games, the Browns are not in a position to move their veterans for more draft picks. All of the youth they acquired in the last few drafts is beginning to pay off. But what if there was a way for them to secure even more draft capital without losing any meaningful production from a lineup that has been better than expected? That would be a reality if they put Jerry Jeudy on the trade block.
At 27 years old and two years removed from a 1,229-yard Pro Bowl season, Jeudry still has value. He would be a starting-caliber wide receiver on a number of teams. The Browns are simply no longer a fit for him as they commit more to their younger options like rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion , who are tied for the team lead in targets. Jeudy has just two starts on the year, and his eight receptions are only the sixth-most on the roster. It looks as though Cleveland is phasing out a player it signed to a $52.5 million deal in 2024. He should have a market among teams in search of receiving depth.
The offense in Tennessee is a mess. There are only a couple of obvious building blocks on that unit in quarterback Cam Ward and wide receiver Carnell Tate , while just about everyone else faces an uncertain future. Tony Pollard , at 29, is significantly older than those two foundational pieces, is in the last year of an affordable contract and is not quite as productive as he was in his first two seasons with the Titans . That profile makes him a potential mover as the franchise all but certainly looks to stockpile more draft picks in the slog of a rebuild.
The Titans can turn to Tyjae Spears and rookie Nicholas Singleton if they part ways with Pollard. Neither might give the offense the same kind of rushing ability that Pollard would, but that is not the point. The Titans are still in "play the long game" mode rather than in a position to flesh out a high-powered offense. A playoff-bound team could give up a draft pick to acquire Pollard as a No. 2 running back.
The Cardinals already made one trade, so they are clearly keen to sell. They are still a ways out from their contention window in the loaded NFC West and need to keep stacking young difference-makers like Trey McBride and Jeremiyah Love . Moving Josh Sweat gives them an opportunity to add to their stash of draft picks, which just got even more robust with the acquisition of a second-rounder and sixth-rounder in the Harrison trade.
There was some buzz in the offseason that Sweat wanted out of Arizona. General manager Monti Ossenfort said in August that the team had no intention of trading him, and Sweat dispelled this month the narrative that he wanted a new contract. Where there is smoke, there is usually fire, so there might be something brewing behind the scenes even though all parties involved are publicly on the same page about Sweat remaining a Cardinal.
Following their botched overtime execution in Week 5, the Commanders stand in sole possession of last place in the NFC East. This has the makings of another potential lost season, rather than another step towards Super Bowl contention, with Jayden Daniels as the franchise quarterback. And while teams with standout quarterbacks on rookie contracts typically seek to add veterans rather than part with them, if Washington deems this year a lost cause, it might try and get whatever it can in return for players who are not part of the long-term future. Daron Payne could be in that group.
Payne's four-year, $90 million contract voids at the end of the season, so the Commanders have a decision to make on whether to re-sign him for a second time. In the years since they paid up to keep a then-Pro Bowler, Payne has not replicated the production of his breakout, 11.5-sack 2022 season. Me might have overstayed his welcome but could be an impactful addition to another team who would not have to pay as much to retain him in 2027 as the Commanders did four years ago.
Who becomes the next player to hit the trade market largely depends on which team pulls the plug on its season first. The Chargers might be that team, considering they are off to an 0-5 start and face a brutal schedule between now and the trade deadline with road games against the Chiefs and Rams and a home date with the Texans. Things will probably get worse before they get better in Los Angeles, so it is only a matter of time before they put their roster in motion.
Mack is about as clear-cut a trade option as any player in the league, not just because of the Chargers' struggles, but also due to his status as a high-performing, aging veteran on an expiring contract. Teams will likely call about him, if they have not already. One to monitor would be the Bears , who need edge rusher help as they work toward a return to the playoffs, and who are quite familiar with Mack, considering he spent four years of his prime in Chicago.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Eagles RB Will Shipley could miss weeks, per report: What's next with Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby also hurt
summary: The Eagles are down to two healthy RBs on their active roster
full_text:
Eagles running back Will Shipley could miss multiple weeks with a partial tear of his plantar fascia, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports , the latest blow to a reeling team dealing with a long list of injuries at running back and across the roster.
Shipley started Sunday's eventual 19-16 loss to the Jaguars in London in place of both Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (core muscle). Both Barkley and Bigsby suffered their injuries in Week 4 against the Rams ; Barkley was considered "week-to-week" after the injury and has not been placed on IR; Bigsby underwent surgery for his injury and landed on IR, meaning he's out at least three more games.
Currently, the Eagles have two running backs — Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele — on their active roster, with former Cowboys fifth-round pick Jaydon Blue on the practice squad. Both Pierce and Steele were signed from the practice squad just last week; now, they could be in line for big roles.
It's looking like a dire situation regardless of who's running, though.
Shipley, in his second career start, had five carries for 6 yards and a touchdown before exiting. Pierce didn't fare much better, running 11 times for 14 yards. Jalen Hurts rushed twice for 2 yards.
Overall, the Eagles had 18 rushes for 22 yards, the 1.2 yards per carry was their second-worst of the 21st century.
All of this came during a tumultuous week in which Lane Johnson retired and the Eagles traded Cam Jurgens to the Ravens . On Sunday, the only Week 1 starter remaining along the offensive line was left tackle Jordan Mailata .
And that was before the Eagles blew a lead in the final eight seconds, with Nick Sirianni's poor decision to give the Jaguars a returnable kick looming large . After Jake Elliott gave Philadelphia the lead, Ameer Abdullah returned the ensuing kickoff 53 yards. With one second remaining, Cam Little drilled a 57-yard field goal.
"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game," Sirianni said. "I put that fully on me."
Philadelphia (2-3) currently ranks 30th in yards per play this year and has the highest three-and-out rate in the league. Injuries have played a huge role.
Notable Eagles offensive injuries this season
If Barkley continues to miss time — hamstrings can be notoriously fickle injuries — Pierce will be first in line. A fourth-round pick for the Texans in 2022, Pierce ran for 939 yards and finished with 1,104 yards from scrimmage as a rookie. But he struggled in his second year (2023) and basically disappeared from the Texans' offense by 2024. In 2025, he disappeared from the Texans completely: Houston waived him mid-season. He landed with the Chiefs near the end of what was by then a lost season in Kansas City. He did not make the Eagles' initial 53-man roster but stuck around on the practice squad until being brought up to the active roster last week.
Steele, undrafted in 2024, gained a bit of a cult following for his long hair and physical running style as a rookie with the Chiefs. He spent all of last season on Kansas City's practice squad before being cut. The Eagles signed him to a futures contract in January 2026. Like Pierce, he didn't make Philadelphia's initial roster but stuck around on the practice squad before being added to the active roster last week. He has only played special teams for the Eagles so far this year.
There was considerable hype around Blue, a talented back out of Texas, but he had only a small role in his rookie year in Dallas, and the team waived him as part of its roster cuts this year. Philadelphia signed him to its practice squad days later. He is yet to appear in a game this season.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL ball-spotting technology explained: Why tracking chips and Hawk-Eye have limitations
summary: A controversial spot involving Cooper Kupp in the Seahawks' loss to the 49ers highlighted the limitations of the NFL's RFID chips
full_text:
The mantra that football is "a game of inches" rang true in Week 5 when the Seattle Seahawks fell just short of an opportunity to tie or take a late lead against the San Francisco 49ers . A close call on the game's decisive play gave new life to the question of why the NFL cannot use technology to spot the ball, because human error might have been the difference between the Seahawks staying alive or falling to their NFC West rival in the 32-29 defeat.
Seattle, trailing by three points, faced a fourth-and-10 from midfield with 54 seconds to play in the game. Sam Darnold completed a pass to Cooper Kupp , who ran towards the 40-yard line and lunged toward the first-down marker as he flew out of bounds.
The officials marked Kupp short of the line to gain. The play went to a booth review and stood as called on the field. Seattle had only one timeout remaining, so the 49ers knelt with the ball to drain the clock for their fifth consecutive victory to open the season. The Seahawks were left frustrated with the result of their do-or-die play, as they would have had time to seek a go-ahead touchdown or game-tying field goal had the officials granted Kupp a first down.
What should the ruling on this play be? 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/YzuDyGXn0S
If the ruling on the field was a first down, the call likely would have stood due to a lack of concrete evidence that Kupp was short. It went the other way, which emphasized both how crucial it is to get the call right in real time and how there is still a gray area in spotting the ball.
As the league embraces the use of technology to track player data, deliver countless camera angles, complete video reviews and implement virtual measurements, it is reasonable to wonder why it does not have the ability to spot the ball digitally.
The answer is that the technology is not yet reliable enough.
The NFL began placing RFID microchips in footballs at the start of the 2017 season. The chips capture data, including speed, distance and rotation, that are collected for Next Gen Stats. They weigh three grams and are embedded in the balls during production. While they act as accelerometers, these chips are not precise enough for use in the spotting process. The 6-inch margin of error makes any argument to use this technology for spotting a non-starter.
"In some cases, those 6 inches might be good enough [to spot the ball]," Zebra Technologies' Jill Stelfox said in 2017 when her company partnered with the NFL to create the chips. "But in all cases, it's probably not good enough at this point with the technology being where it is. It also depends on where your feet are, and your knees are, and we don't have those tagged with chips. They're only in the shoulder pads. So the NFL is still going to need referees to do that."
Making up for potential inaccuracies is not as simple as stitching together videos of the play, determining when the ball carrier went down or out of bounds, and syncing that timestamp with the location determined by the chip. There will always be the chance that the measured distance is up to 6 inches off from reality. It is no different from officials incorrectly interpreting where the ball is at a given time with their own eyes.
Assume, for instance, that the replay officials found the ball in Kupp's hand broke the plane of the sideline. While they could sync the chip with that video and determine the ball's position, if it is within a half-foot of the first-down line, they cannot say with certainty that it actually reached the marker.
And then there is the problem of camera angles. Even with all of the cameras in use during NFL games today, there is not always an angle that shows the exact moment a player hits the ground or the ball crosses a line. Over-the-top cameras positioned directly above the ball and down-the-line cameras positioned directly on each yard marker, sideline, goal line and end line are required for precision. That does not even cover situations in which the ball is not clearly visible, either.
The NFL's replay system received a major upgrade with the introduction of Sony's Hawk-Eye technology in 2021, which allows the league to process live video in real time and sync camera angles with timestamps. In 2025, use of the Hawk-Eye system expanded to the virtual measurement process, wherein the NFL uses six 8K optical-tracking cameras in each stadium to mark the exact position of the ball relative to the line to gain. This is more accurate than the in-ball RFID chips but comes with its own limitations.
Most prohibitive is the fact that the cameras require a clear line of sight to determine the ball's position. For measurements, officials manually spot the ball and move out of the way so the cameras can detect its position. In the flow of play, there are far too many instances in which the view of the ball is blocked.
This is why Hawk-Eye is far more useful for real-time decisions in tennis and soccer than it would be for spotting the ball after each play. In tennis, the cameras can see clearly whether the ball landed inside, outside or on the line. In soccer, the cameras can generally determine whether the ball crossed the plane of the goal or whether players are offside. There is too much congestion on the football field to consistently track the ball.
Considering the NFL's willingness to adopt technology and its commitment to making the correct call on every play, if the opportunity arises to relieve officials of spotting duties, one has to imagine the league would jump on it. The fact that RFID chips and Hawk-Eye can accurately capture so much additional data suggests that it is only a matter of time until a breakthrough makes digital spotting a reality. There is no telling when this capability will come to fruition, though.
author: Carter Bahns

title: What's next for Chargers? Why Khalil Mack should be traded, plus what to do about Jim Harbaugh, Mike McDaniel
summary: Los Angeles must now determine whether to change offensive coordinators, retain its general manager and move veterans before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
full_text:
Five teams entered Week 5 with an 0-4 record, no two more surprising than the Texans and the Chargers . Both playoff staples of the past few years, they were trying to take the first step in joining the 1992 Chargers as the only teams to start 0-4 and make the postseason.
One succeeded. The Texans thumped the inept Titans 26-3. The other failed. The Chargers fell 23-17 to the Broncos in an eyesore of a game. Neither Bo Nix nor Justin Herbert reached 125 yards passing. The Broncos' 224 yards of offense were the second-fewest in a win this season.
The difference was turnovers. The Broncos forced three -- awful fumbles by Herbert and Charlie Kolar and a terrible pick by Herbert -- and turned that into 13 points. A fourth "turnover," a turnover on downs early in the fourth quarter, set the stage for the collapse. The Chargers had actually scored two touchdowns in the third quarter to take a 17-10 lead. Their possessions after that? Three and out, turnover on downs, fumble, interception, end of game.
The Chargers lead the NFL with 13 turnovers this season, and they've come in all shapes and sizes.
Simply put, it's over. It might have been over for a while, but this absolutely drives the point home in more ways than one. Not only is it over in terms of competitive football, but, with the trade deadline less than a month away, it's over in terms of what the next big goals should be for this organization. The Chargers started four rookies on the offensive line, three of whom were drafted in the fourth round or later. Herbert took five sacks, including one, fittingly, on the final play, setting up for a Hail Mary.
BRONCOS DEFENSE CALLS GAME ‼️ pic.twitter.com/uHv9ChQAmx
Los Angeles was also without its top two wide receivers, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston . But guess what? The Broncos were without their top two corners -- superstar Patrick Surtain II as well as Riley Moss -- and figured out a way to defend effectively. Bad teams find ways to lose games, and the Chargers are a bad team.
Technically speaking, the Chargers have the Chiefs next week as their brutal schedule continues. But in the grander scheme, up next are big questions about the roster, the coaching staff and the front office. Those questions must be answered, maybe sooner rather than later.
Jim Harbaugh got two pointed questions to end his press conference on Sunday. First: Do things have to change -- particularly with the offense -- given the struggles, or is it to continue doing what they've been doing?
"Just keep digging deep and moving forward," Harbaugh said. "That's what staying the course looks like, and coach being right about the decisions, these critical decisions. That's as important as anything."
Second question: Why stay the course when the course has led you here?
"Keep working harder, keep working smarter," Harbaugh said. "That's just the truth. That's the answer."
Harbaugh has to say that then, but it's clear it's not the answer. In fact, earlier in the press conference when asked about what message can get through to an 0-5 team, Harbaugh said, "I don't know what that message is."
There is no message for a team like this, no magic potion. The marriage between Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has gone completely bust. There were always going to be differences between the two stylistically -- Herbert hangs in the pocket and delivers downfield, McDaniel wants a quick, on-time passing attack -- but Herbert looks like he needs a complete reboot.
I know the Herbert discourse is treading on thin ice, but this is a quarterback who threw three interceptions in 2024 and seven in 2023. He threw 13 last year, but his 2.5% interception rate was hardly worrying. This year, he has seven picks already, many of the jaw-dropping-bad variety. His 4.9% interception rate is second-worst in the NFL and on par with J.J. McCarthy last year. Yikes!
It's also not indicative of who he is as a player. He entered this season with a 1.7% interception rate. There's been no physical decline. He's 28 years old. A complete fall off like this would be unprecedented. Herbert has been awful, but it's clear he's in a tough spot, too: the wrong fit, a bad ecosystem around him, etc.
The Chargers have to keep playing Herbert 1.) to hope he improves, 2.) to see what works and what doesn't and 3.) because turning to DJ Uiagalelei doesn't help anything or anyone (except for maybe Herbert).
So that leads us to McDaniel. Harbaugh said McDaniel's job was safe last week, but that was before the worst offensive performance this season (3.8 yards per play, 36% success rate, -0.30 EPA per play). In fact, the Chargers now rank dead last in offensive EPA per play, largely due to turnovers.
There is a world where the product improves, but the Chargers are already so far out of it that it doesn't matter. The goal should be to get Herbert to play —if not good football, at least viable football—by cutting down on turnovers and sacks, improving consistency on completions, etc. Replacing McDaniel right now doesn't make sense. The entire offense was just overhauled to McDaniel's very specific system, and you can't just replace a system and build a new one in a week. McDaniel will likely be a late-season or post-season fire.
And then there's Harbaugh, who has taken a lot of hits this season. The McDaniel hire didn't work. Even the defense has regressed. Harbaugh blamed himself for Sunday's loss after the fourth-and-1 decision, though ESPN's model actually agreed with going for it , and Herbert defended the decision as well.
Harbaugh shouldn't be fired this season, and he shouldn't be fired after the season. He clearly missed on his offensive coordinator hire, and it's not his fault he lost last year's ace defensive coordinator, Jesse Minter, to the Ravens job. The Chargers haven't quit on Harbaugh, which would be a sign that they're moving on.
Harbaugh went 11-6 each of his first two seasons in Los Angeles, lifting a franchise that had been stuck in mediocrity. Harbaugh's exit from his other NFL coaching spot -- the 49ers from 2011-14 -- ended in a quick downfall, but that was due to a reported front-office/coach rift . As long as that's not the case, Harbaugh deserves a chance to get the operation back on track.
GM Joe Hortiz's name is one to watch. He was previously with the Ravens and Jim's brother, John. The Ravens have a long history of stability and patience. Their GM, Eric DeCosta, has been with the team since its inaugural 1996 season and GM since 2019, through ups, downs and disappointments. Hortiz might not be afforded that leash, and a season from hell like this is much worse than anything DeCosta's produced in Baltimore, but it's worth acknowledging.
Long story short, if I had to guess, the Chargers will keep Herbert and Harbaugh and fire McDaniel at season's end or at least sometime in November or December. Hortiz is truly on the fence, and how the team's youngsters look could go a long way. This is only his third year as GM, and he had built a winner in 2024 and 2025. Seasons like this, though, often come with major change.
With the Nov. 10 trade deadline rapidly approaching, the Chargers should be active sellers. They might be able to fetch a better return if they trade away pieces sooner rather than later, and at 0-5, now is very much the time to sell.
The most obvious trade candidate here, Khalil Mack is still playing excellent football at 35 years old. He has three sacks, five tackles for loss and 14 pressures this year. He is on a one-year deal, so moving him makes all the sense in the world, and there should be plenty of suitors. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones pitched a Bears reunion as an idea, and said one GM and one assistant GM both agreed a fifth-round price tag makes sense.
Donte Jackson played well for the Chargers in both 2024 and 2025 under Minter and has taken a slight step back in his tiny 2026 sample size. Like Mack, Jackson is only signed through the end of this season. Trying to…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Pick Six: NFL Week 5 winners and losers, plus Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades and Bills-Rams picks
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Oct. 12
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
If the NFC East ceases to exist this week, it's because the entire division imploded in Week 5. The implosion started on Thursday with the Cowboys ' loss to a 0-4 Buccaneers team, and then things only got uglier from there.
On Sunday, the Eagles somehow managed to lose even though they kicked a field goal that gave them a 16-14 lead with just eight seconds left against the Jaguars . And let's not forget about the other two teams. The Commanders and Giants went to overtime and somehow tied, even though both teams had the ball inside their opponent's 25-yard line in OT. The Commanders actually had the ball in field goal range at the end of overtime, but they simply let the clock run out before they could try a kick.
Basically, the NFC East gave us a coaching clinic on what not to do in late-game situations. I could probably spend the entire day talking about everything the NFC East did wrong in Week 5, but we've got a newsletter to get to, so let's get to it.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here .
It appears that Josh McDaniels was still kind of bitter about being fired by the Raiders . The Patriots scored 45 points against the Raiders on Sunday, and that happened because McDaniels refused to take his foot off the gas. With New England up 38-17 late in the fourth quarter, the Patriots had an eight-play TD drive where they threw four passes. At that point, you should be running out the clock, but McDaniels clearly wanted to BURY the Raiders.
Sorry, Tom Brady . Your old team destroyed the team you now own.
Anyway, we're starting our grades section off with the Patriots' big win.
Patriots 45-17 over Raiders
As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 5, you can check those out here .
You can't have a week of NFL action without having winners and losers, so here are some winners and losers. In a twist, we had one game where there wasn't a winner or a loser since it ended in a tie. When that happens, both teams usually end up in our loser column.
Carter Bahns came up with this week's list of winners and losers, and we're going to check out his losers below.
If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here .
Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Personally, I overreact to everything. With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look at several things that happened during Week 5 to decide for yourself if we're all overreacting.
Statement: The Vikings are legit Super Bowl contenders. Overreaction or reality: Reality. Flores is the best coordinator in the NFL. We already knew this defense was excellent, but it was encouraging to see Kyler Murray play his best game with the Vikings yet. He completed 24 of 30 passes (80%) for 229 yards and a touchdown to Justin Jefferson , and he ran the ball seven times for another 54 yards, excluding three kneeldowns. Murray doesn't have to be great. But if he can take care of the ball, find Jefferson — who made some spectacular catches — and make a few timely plays, this is a legitimate Super Bowl contender.
Statement: The NFC East winner will have a losing record. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. The NFC East did not have a banner week. The Cowboys dropped a home game to the previously winless Buccaneers on Thursday. Sunday morning, the Eagles lost after taking a two-point lead with eight seconds and inexplicably giving the Jaguars a returnable kickoff. All of that paled in comparison to the utter disaster that was the end of the Commanders-Giants game. That means the 3-1-1 Giants are still in first place in the division, the Cowboys and Eagles are 2-3, and the Commanders are 1-3-1 and reeling.  It becomes really, really difficult to see any team in this division reaching 10 wins, simply because each team has major issues. Only once has the NFC East (as currently constructed) had a champion with a losing record. I won't go that far yet, but no team reaching double-digit wins is very much on the table.
Statement: The Commanders should fire Dan Quinn , but they really can't right now. Overreaction or reality: Reality. I hate advocating for anyone to be fired, but the NFL is a results-driven business, and the results just aren't good enough for the Commanders. As Quinn said , Sunday's tie feels like a loss, and it feels like another lost season in the nation's capital. Quinn put all the blame for the debacle on his shoulders, as he should have. But the idea that it's time for him to be fired goes deeper than Sunday. A week earlier, a poor fourth-and-1 decision using a third-string quarterback turned a winnable game against the Colts into a blowout loss. Quinn's performance has been fire-worthy. The thing is, the Commanders have two first-time coordinators. There is one former head coach on staff — running backs coach Anthony Lynn — but upending the staff would be a tough development in a season that's quickly slipping from returning to the playoffs to simply hoping Daniels can stay healthy and continue to progress.
There are plenty more overreactions, and you can check them out here .
Going into the weekend, there was some speculation that the Cardinals might look to trade Marvin Harrison Jr ., and a deal actually went down on Sunday. Harrison is now headed to Houston , where he'll be reunited with his former college quarterback, C.J. Stroud .
Here are the details of the deal:
Harrison, who was in his third season with the Cardinals, had just five catches through Arizona 's first four games. Going into training camp, it seemed like a split between the two sides was almost inevitable. The relationship between Harrison and the Cardinals got off to an ugly start almost immediately after Arizona made him the fourth overall pick in 2024. During his rookie year, Harrison asked the team to purchase him a $50,000 jugs machine that he wanted to use at home, but the team declined, according to AZ Central . It's a small thing, but it shows that some franchises just aren't doing everything in their power to win.

The Rams are expected to have Aaron Donald back in the lineup after missing him for their past three games. As for the Bills, DL Ed Oliver and WR Josh Palmer have both been ruled out.
