title: Has the David Bailey breakout arrived? Jets' No. 2 overall pick shines in three-sack day vs. Browns
summary: Bailey quieted the critics with the best game of his young career
full_text:
When the New York Jets selected edge rusher David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , the hope was that he would not only develop into a premier havoc-wreaker but that he would also deliver an immediate impact for a struggling defense. Bailey fell short in the first month of his career in providing that spark, but he flipped a switch in Week 5 as the Jets logged their most dominant defensive performance of the year.
Sunday's 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns was the "I have arrived" kind of statement that eluded Bailey in his first four games. He provided three sacks to lead a Jets pass rush that got home on Deshaun Watson eight times — good for the most sacks by any team in a single game this season.
It was not just those three instances in which Bailey rattled Watson, either. He also forced the Browns quarterback to throw the ball into the turf on third down on the game's final series, and he flushed him out of the pocket on the next snap, which led to a game-ending strip sack for Will McDonald IV .
Bailey finished the day with seven tackles, nine quarterback pressures and three sacks. That was good for a 32.1% pressure rate on his 28 pass rush snaps.
THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN
The skepticism about Bailey's worthiness of an early first-round draft pick, which circulated among fans and the media, aged poorly. A week ago, some tepidness about his rookie-year stardom would have been warranted, but after Game 5, there is hardly room for pessimism anymore. All of a sudden, Bailey leads all rookie pass rushers with 26 total pressures and nine quick pressures, per Next Gen Stats.
"I've said all along that his time is going to come," Jets coach Aaron Glenn said after the win . "I have all the confidence in him in the world. He did a good job today. He did a good job. There were some things that he's gotta work on, but for him to come out and get three sacks, that's who David is, and we expected that."
The disruptive effort was easily the best of Bailey's young career. The production went well beyond personal-best levels, too. The nine pressures he logged on Watson were tied for the most in a single game by a rookie since Jared Verse matched that total against the Las Vegas Raiders in the 2024 season. What's more, his three sacks tied the most by a Jets rookie since individual sacks first became a tracked statistic in 1982. Only Hugh Douglas in 1995 recorded as many in a single game.
"We had a big focus on working on our four-man rush games this week," Bailey said . "Kind of rushing with some chemistry, working together. We [were] working with each other throughout the whole week, going after practice, spending a little extra time in the film room. I think, honestly, the d-line as a whole just came together, and we just kind of stuck with the plan that we created, and then I just started having so much success over the board."
The Jets' upcoming schedule over the next month is a mixed bag of Super Bowl contenders and less-challenging opponents, which offers Bailey opportunities to both tee off on matchup advantages and test himself against the NFL's best. It would be understandable as an inexperienced rookie if he were to only replicate his Week 5 production in those contests against weaker foes. Where Bailey can truly establish himself as a difference-maker is in the Week 6 trip to face the New England Patriots and in the back-to-back tests against the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills in Weeks 9 and 10.
New York deployed Bailey on the left side of the defense for 87.1% of his snaps through five games. He will match up against right tackles far more than left tackles if that usage rate continues, which means he will see a heavy dose of the following blockers in the next five games.
Two of Bailey's most favorable individual matchups come against the Chiefs and Bills. If the Jets are to upset either one of those division leaders, he will need to win his one-on-one battles and disrupt Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen . That is a tall ask, but one that can cement Bailey as a star if he delivers on it.
The gripes about Bailey's tepid start were arguably less about his own impact and more framed in the sense that other first-year players made greater contributions in the season's opening month. Bailey himself was actually quite effective in Weeks 1-4, even if the sack numbers were modest. For instance, he entered the game against the Browns ranked in a tie for eighth among all edge rushers in pressures. He was not as visibly disruptive as a trio of linebackers drafted behind him, though, with Arvell Reese , Sonny Styles and Jacob Rodriguez all dazzling across their first four games.
It did not help Bailey's public perception that Reese, whom the New York Giants picked at No. 5, outpaced him in the Rookie of the Year race. He said he paid no mind to the comparisons and criticism that came with his relatively more humble four-game sample size.
"All that I feel like matters is what my coaches are telling me, what my teammates are telling me," Bailey said . "That's kind of been my focus on that."
On Sunday, Bailey delivered a reminder that four games are far too few to draw conclusions. It took just one more contest for him to leap in front of everyone else in the rookie pecking order.
The insinuation when the Jets took Bailey with the second pick in the draft was that they viewed him as the best defensive player in his class. Only quarterback Fernando Mendoza went higher on the board. If he strings together more outings like the one he just enjoyed, he will live up to that billing as the most productive defender right out of the gate. And that is not to mention how much greater heights he could achieve as he develops over the years to come. He might be in the early stages of a tremendous career.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFC East makes dubious NFL history with winless Week 5 as Giants hold unlikely division lead
summary: The NFC East's Week 5 is something that has happened just four times since 2002 divisional realignment
full_text:
The NFC East just had an all-time week to remember, or if you're a fan of the Dallas Cowboys , Philadelphia Eagles , New York Giants or Washington Commanders , an all-time week to forget.
Dallas lost 24-16 at home to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers with Jalon Daniels , an undrafted rookie making his second career start, at quarterback. Philadelphia lost 19-17 in regulation against the Jacksonville Jaguars despite kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Last and ugliest, the New York Giants and Washington Commanders tied despite both teams reaching field-goal range in the last two minutes of overtime.
With all four NFC East teams going winless in Week 5, they have now become just the fourth occurrence of an entire division going winless despite having a divisional matchup in the 418 NFL regular-season weeks since the 2002 divisional realignment, per CBS Sports Research. That means the 2026 NFC East did something that has only happened in less than one percent of the 418 weeks of NFL regular season action, 0.96%, to be exact, since 2002.
In the case of the Giants and Commanders, they now own two of the last three ties in the NFL, with these two NFC East teams tying each other in 2022. The Cowboys account for the other tie in this span, a 40-40 home tie against the Green Bay Packers last season. Another unfathomable stat for the Giants is that they are now winless in their last six overtime games, with four losses and two ties.
Week 5's events have now created a tightly-contested NFC East division race through five weeks. The Giants are in first place at 3-1-1, but both the Eagles and the Cowboys are right behind them at 2-3. The Commanders are bringing up the rear at 1-3-1.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Nick Sirianni, Dan Quinn fail their teams in pivotal moments during dismal NFC East weekend
summary: The Eagles and Commanders squandered chances to win Sunday, and both coaches are feeling the heat
full_text:
Clock mismanagement and a pair of coaches overthinking late-game situations doomed the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders . Both teams are fighting for air in the NFC East after five weeks, and both coaches are feeling the heat.
The Eagles led the Jacksonville Jaguars with eight seconds left in London following Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal before giving one of the NFL's most dangerous return threats, Ameer Abdullah , a shot at a big return. Abdullah answered with a 53-yard burst to set up Cam Little's game-winning 57-yard field goal as time expired, dropping the Eagles to 2-3 overall.
"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. "What hurts there is the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game, and I put that one on me."
The Commanders were in game-winning field goal range against the New York Giants in overtime before the clock expired at the 25-yard line during a 27-all tie . Now 1-3-1, Washington would've moved one game back of the division leaders with a victory.
Dan Quinn said, "It falls on me," when asked about his team's failure to stop the clock and attempt the game-tying field goal without any timeouts.
Quarterback Jayden Daniels assumed responsibility after going down in the middle of the field with the final seconds ticking off the clock, but Quinn pointed fingers at himself.
"At the end, I can make life easy there," Quinn said . "We didn't need to gain more yards."
These weren't two situations that required genius decisions on the headset. In fact, both were elementary-level calls that most of us could've made from the couch.
Both coaches failed their respective franchises in a big spot, including one in a divisional game. Ironically, Sirianni nixed the idea of having his quarterback run around and burn time off the clock before attempting the go-ahead field goal, the inverse of a decision that backfired on Quinn and the Commanders.
"It hurts in the sense of the guys fought their ass off and had a chance to win the game. And then for me to not make the right decision in that, you feel like you let everyone down," Sirianni said. "That will stick with me for a long time. All I know is I'll work my butt off to get better from it."
Quinn's error was the more notable blunder, ending with the coach slamming his headset to the ground after a game that ended in a tie felt more like a loss in Washington.
Those coaching mistakes came a couple of days after Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was considering staff changes following his team's humiliating loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Is there any team interested in winning the division this season?
Tampa Bay's decisive 17-point third quarter behind undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving's first 100-yard outing on the ground in two years put the spotlight on the Cowboys' second-year coach and his 2-3 start this fall.
"I'm going to look at everything," Schottenheimer said. "I'll spend countless hours trying to figure it out and getting a chance to step back, look at these five games, and see what we need to improve. ... Yeah, I think we evaluate everything, but at the end of the day, we're five games in. I am disappointed in the way we performed this evening as a football team, and that's just going to be one part of the process."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Head-scratching decisions by Commanders, Eagles; Georgia new No. 1 in college football, CFP shake-up
summary: Plus, Brewers eke out NLCS opener over Dodgers
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Lost in a sea of close finishes and general wackiness, you might have missed the Vikings handing the Saints a 23-13 loss in New Orleans. Minnesota is a relatively quiet 5-0, and that begs the question: Should the Vikings be considered a legitimate Super Bowl contender?
That's one of the topics our Zach Pereles explored in his Week 5 overreactions , and his conclusion was clear. Whatever reservations you have about Kyler Murray as a championship quarterback, put them aside. The defense is good enough that Murray won't have to be Superman every week.
Another team that impressed in Week 5 was the Packers . Green Bay thumped the Bears and improved to 3-2 on the season. Jordan Love threw for 367 yards, and the Packers defense allowed just 3.6 yards per play. It seems like the Pack may very well be back after a shaky start .
Of course, in the words of the great Sturgill Simpson , "It ain't all flowers, sometimes you gotta feel the thorns."
There were some teams that would rather forget Week 5 happened altogether. The Commanders are certainly on that list of losers after bungling what looked like a sure win over a division rival. The Raiders are another team who failed a big test as reality finally hit , although Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action .
Another No. 1 overall quarterback -- Cam Ward -- is going through hard times. Just don't expect the Titans to bench him anytime soon .
College football is always good for a little chaos, but Week 6 provided something extra. A number of highly ranked teams, included former No. 1 Texas went down over the weekend.
The Longhorns blew a lead to rival Oklahoma in the Cotton Bowl as their obvious flaws finally caught up to them . As a result, Texas has given itself a little less wiggle room in the race for a College Football Playoff berth.
As Tom Fornelli points out in his CFP Vibe Check , have the Horns inspired enough confidence for anyone to believe they won't drop a couple more games along the way?
If it's any consolation, Texas was not alone in its sadness. They had the company of a few more top-25 squads.
If you thought Week 6 was fun, just wait until you see what's in store for Week 7. There is one banger after another on the slate ( Ohio State vs. Indiana ; BYU vs. Notre Dame ; Alabama vs. Tennessee ), and you can see the odds for the biggest games right here .

title: Cover 32: Look out NFL, Drake Maye has his swagger back; plus games balls, biggest gaffes from Week 5
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 5 in the NFL, including the bizarre tie in Giants-Commanders and David Bailey's breakout
full_text:
Call it the yips, a slump, or just being downright bad, whatever had been plaguing Drake Maye through the early part of the season appears to be a thing of the past. The Patriots quarterback emphatically announced the return of his swagger with a dominant five-touchdown performance in New England's 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5.
Maye looked like the MVP runner-up he was a year ago in this contest, completing 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns. He added 25 yards and another score on the ground to his day as well. That helped Maye become the first quarterback in team history to have at least 300 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and one rushing touchdown in a game. Of course, the most important element of Maye's day was the zero he posted in the turnover column.
Outside of keeping it clean in the turnover margin, Maye's eruption against the Raiders was particularly notable when it comes to his deep ball. Last year, Maye was regarded as the most efficient deep ball passer in the NFL , but that was noticeably absent in his game during the early struggles this season. On Sunday, Maye completed 72.7% of his passes (8 of 11) that went for 10-plus air yards for 206 yards and three touchdowns, giving him a 154.4 passer rating. Those passing yards and passing touchdowns were season highs for the former first-round pick.
THIS IS A DIME. @DrakeMaye2 | @EliRaridon 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/SJByiCW5zY
Really, Maye's resurgence began to sprout last week in New England's win over Buffalo. Over these last two games, Maye has completed 19 of 29 passes of 10-plus air yards for 390 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. When making the same throws over his first three games, Maye was 13 of 31 for 340 yards and four interceptions.
What has helped Maye not only stabilize his season but also return to elite form has been his ability to better handle pressure. Over the past two games, Maye's been pressured on 30 dropbacks. In that span, he has completed 12 of 26 throws for 136 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, while being sacked just twice. Conversely, on the 42 dropbacks he was pressured over the first three weeks, Maye was 12-of-28 for 183 yards and three interceptions, while being sacked eight times. A night and day difference, particularly in the turnover department.
It's funny how quickly the narrative can change in the NFL. After that 1-2 start, where Maye and the Patriots looked absolutely lost, the sky felt like it was falling in Foxborough. They've since ripped off two key wins in the AFC (including a head-to-head against the Bills in Buffalo) to move over .500 for the first time this season.
Not only that, but Maye looks like the MVP contender he was a year ago, which completely changes the complexion of this team and the overall season outlook. There's also a case to be made that his high-level play could continue or even improve with the return of A.J. Brown looming. If that proves to be the case, New England is firmly back in the Super Bowl conversation, which is something nobody thought coming off that 3-point dud they produced in Jacksonville in Week 3.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft had his coming-out party in Week 5 as the Jets outlasted the Browns to move to 2-3 on the year. David Bailey generated 9 pressures, including 5 quick pressures and 3 sacks, against the Browns. His 9 pressures are tied for the most by a rookie in a game since Jared Verse in Week 7, 2024. title: NFL Week 6 early odds: Eagles favored despite massive disadvantage, Packers-Cowboys line flips
summary: The statuses of Lamar Jackson, Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams could dramatically reshape several Week 6 betting lines
full_text:
In lockstep with feeling even more of that fall chill in the air these days is the ramp-up in competitiveness throughout the NFL .
The league is coming out of a Week 5 slate that truly felt like teams had shaken off the rust and thrown haymakers. Specifically, we saw several underdogs bite back. That included the Green Bay Packers , who took down the Chicago Bears as a home underdog, and the San Francisco 49ers , who went into Lumen Field and took down the Seattle Seahawks . Even going back to Thursday's action, the Bucs went into Dallas and beat the Cowboys with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels under center.
What does Week 6 have in store for us? How about six divisional matchups, which include an international showdown between the Texans and Jaguars ? That should keep the momentum rolling for what has been a wildly entertaining season so far. As we turn our attention to next week's slate, let's take our first glimpse at the betting lines and see who the oddsmakers project coming out on top.
Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami, and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Seahawks at Broncos (Thursday)
Seahawks -155, Broncos +130
Texans at Jaguars (in London)
Panthers +105, Eagles -125
Steelers -155, Buccaneers +130
Chargers +295, Chiefs -375
Cowboys -105, Packers -115
Commanders at 49ers (Monday)
Commanders +340, 49ers -441
Seattle is coming off a grueling home loss to the 49ers and will now have to travel to face the Broncos, who outlasted the Chargers in Week 5. The Seahawks opened as a 1.5-point favorite, and that has jumped to a full field goal at -3. Denver is 2-0 ATS at home this season, and this will be the first time they're a home underdog in 2026. Last season, the Broncos were 3-0 ATS as a home dog. As for Seattle, it is 1-1 ATS this season as a road favorite.
Jacksonville played in London in Week 5 and will remain in England, while Houston will need to make the international trek later this week. The Jags pulled out a last-second win over the Eagles on Sunday, but failed the cover, dropping them to 3-2 ATS on the year. They'll welcome in a Texans team that notched its first win of the season as they took down the Titans in Nashville. That also gave Houston its first ATS win of the year. The Under of 43.5 could be a lean in this game as it's 6-3 between these two division rivals this season.
Cleveland dropped a Week 5 road matchup to the Jets and is 3-2 (SU and ATS) on the year. They're 2-0 ATS at home, but they'll head into Week 6 as a home underdog, laying 3.5 points to the Ravens, who are coming off a road win in Atlanta. This line could see some movement throughout the week once it becomes clear whether Lamar Jackson (who did not play in Week 5) will suit up.
Chicago opened as a 1.5-point favorite on the road over the Falcons, but that has since been turned on its head. Now, the Falcons are laying 1.5 points as they host the Bears. This comes after the Bears lost as a road favorite to the Packers, and Tyson Bagent was benched for Case Keenum . If Caleb Williams is able to play in Week 6, however, it wouldn't be too surprising to see the odds swing back toward Chicago. The Bears are 3-2 ATS this season and 1-1 ATS on the road. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr . didn't finish Sunday's loss to the Ravens due to a rib injury. If he cannot go for Week 6, that'd also shift the lines dramatically, as Tua Tagovailoa finished the overtime period with an interception last night.
Carolina is going to have quite the rest advantage over Philadelphia. The Panthers were on the bye in Week 5, while the Eagles were just playing an international game in London. That's, in part, why this line is so slim, with Philly laying just 1.5 points in this NFC matchup. Of course, given the uncertainty surrounding an array of key players for the Eagles ( DeVonta Smith , Saquon Barkley , etc.) that has helped keep this line effectively a coin flip. Under coach Dave Canales, the Panthers are 3-3 ATS when they have the rest advantage. Under Nick Sirianni, the Eagles are 9-11 ATS when at a rest disadvantage.
New Orleans was initially a 1.5 -point road favorite, but that has since flipped, and it's now the Giants laying 1.5 points. New York is coming off a tie against the Commanders, but it covered in Week 5. Meanwhile, the Saints are reeling a bit after dropping three straight home games, including a Week 5 loss to Minnesota. The Giants are 3-0 ATS at home this season, while New Orleans is 2-0 ATS on the road, so something will need to give here.
New England is a full touchdown favorite over the Jets after stabilizing its season with two statement wins over the past couple of weeks. Most recently, the Patriots dropped 45 points in a win over the Raiders, pushing them to 3-2 on the season and 3-1-1 ATS. That includes a perfect 2-0 ATS mark at Gillette Stadium. As for the Jets, they pulled out a win against the Browns, which helped them cover and improve to 3-1-1 ATS. New York is 1-1-1 ATS on the road.
Indy is up to a full touchdown favorite over the Titans after the line initially opened at Colts -6.5. Both of these AFC South clubs are coming off losses in Week 5, with the Colts falling to the Steelers in Pittsburgh while the Texans went into Nashville to beat the Titans. The Titans are 1-1 ATS on the road this season, and the Colts are 1-1 ATS at home.
The Bucs will have a rest advantage over the Steelers after coming off their mini-bye following their Week 5 matchup with the Cowboys last Thursday. Despite that, Tampa Bay is a home-field underdog, with the Steelers laying 3 points in this matchup. The Bucs are 1-4 ATS this season and are 0-3 ATS at home (0-1 ATS as a home underdog). Pittsburgh has yet to record an ATS road win this season (0-2 ATS) and is 0-1 ATS as a road favorite.
The Rams still have their Week 5 matchup to play on Monday night as we write this, but they've opened Week 6 as the biggest favorite on the board. They are laying 12.5 points at home to the Cardinals, who are coming off a 45-21 loss to the Lions at home. Arizona is 2-3 ATS this season and has been a solid bet on the road (2-1 ATS). Before Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, the Rams are 1-1 ATS at home and 2-2 ATS on the season.
The Chargers are 0-5 on the season and 0-4-1 ATS. Now, they'll have to travel to Kansas City as a 8.5-point underdog to face a Chiefs team that is coming off its bye week. That's up from the 7.5 points the Chiefs were laying at the open. Since Patrick Mahomes became the full-time starter in 2018, the Chiefs are 5-8 ATS after the bye and 18-22 ATS with the rest advantage. This season, Kansas City is 2-2 ATS and 1-1 ATS at Arrowhead Stadium. The total for this game has dipped noticeably, falling to 43.5 after opening at 45.5.
Buffalo still has its Week 5 matchup with the Rams on Monday night, but is a 6-point road favorite over the Raiders in Week 6. That's up from the 5.5 point spread at the open. Las Vegas is coming off a blowout loss to the Patriots on the road, giving them their second loss in as many weeks. The Raiders are 2-0 ATS at home this season, while the Bills are 1-0 ATS on the road (before taking on the Rams in Week 5).
The Cowboys will have a bit of a rest advantage over the Packers after playing last Thursday, but they're reeling from their loss to the Buccaneers. That, along with Green Bay's dominant win over the Bears, has seen the odds in this game flip. Now, the Packers are laying 1.5 points after Dallas initially was the 1.5-point road favorite. The Cowboys are 1-1 ATS on the road this season, while the Packers are 1-1 ATS at home.
San Francisco is coming off a statement win in Seattle, which has helped see this line jump up and cross several key numbers. Initially, the 49ers opened as a 5.5-point favorite, but that has since ballooned to -7.5. The Niners are 2-1 ATS at home this season, with an average margin of victory of 12.7 points. While Washington got Jayden Daniels back this week, it was…

title: Marvin Harrison trade: A look at other top-5 picks who were traded ahead of Year 4 in the last decade
summary: Harrison is one of five players in the last 10 years to be traded in before year four as a top-5 pick
full_text:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . is joining an exclusive club that he may not want to be part of. The Arizona Cardinals have traded Harrison , who they drafted at No. 4 overall just a few years ago, to the Texans, Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Sunday.
Arizona is trading the 24-year-old and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN .
When the Cardinals drafted Harrison in the 2024 overall draft, like any team that picks a player in the top 10, they thought they had found a long-term star. Flash forward 33 games later, and things haven't worked out as expected for either party.
Other than Harrison, in the last 10 years, only four other top-5 picks have been traded before their fourth season. The majority of the players haven't fared too well in their careers after that initial trade. Harrison will be looking to rewrite history and turn the move into a success.
Let's take a look at the other players with similar stories and how they played before and after the trade.
Team drafted (Year/Draft No.)
Team traded to/Year traded
108 receptions, 1,578 yards in 33 games
12-21 record, 23 TDs, 25 INT
Didn't appear in a game for DEN
12-21 record, 23 TDs, 25 INTs
2-2 record, 5 touchdowns, 3 interceptions
Didn't appear in a game in the first year with DAL
22 starts over 3 years, 124 combined tackles, 2 INTs, 1 forced fumbles
44 combined tackles, 3 passes defended with ATL
31 starts, 191 combined tackles, 1 forced fumble, 2 INTs
13-25 record, 45 TDs, 39 INTs
4-7 record, 9 TDs, 13 INTs
Two-time Pro Bowler, Super Bowl champion
Harrison has just five receptions for 85 yards so far this season. He has yet to record a 1,000-yard receiving season in his first two years in the league, dropping from 885 yards in his rookie season to 608 yards last year. The wide receiver's success at Ohio State made most people believe he would be an instant star in the league, but the stat line has fallen flat.
Harrison will now have a new start with the Texans, who won their first game this week, defeating the now 0-5 Tennessee Titans 26-3. Houston will face the 4-1 Jaguars , who are coming off a last-minute thrilling victory against the Philadelphia Eagles , next week.
Quarterback Zach Wilson went from the No. 2 overall pick to a bust very quickly. In his rookie year, he went 3-10 with nine touchdowns and 11 interceptions. The next season, he started nine games at 5-4, had a slew of bad performances, and cycled between the bench and the field all season.
Since being traded by the Jets, Wilson hasn't started a single game and has made just four game appearances, all with the Miami Dolphins . Wilson's trade did not equate to a new start for the QB, and he became a career backup after his failed experiment in NY.
Trey Lance is such an interesting study, as injuries and changing depth charts left him on the outskirts of the 49ers QB situation.
He was the backup to Jimmy Garoppolo to start his career, then named the starter over Jimmy G in his sophomore season, but an injury changed his career significantly. Ahead of the 2023 season, Sam Darnold, who we'll discuss more below, and Mr. Irrelevant (aka Brock Purdy ) were listed ahead of Lance on the depth chart. The Niners no longer felt the need for Lance, with two other quarterbacks they trusted, and he was dealt to the Cowboys ahead of the 2023 season.
Lance was the Cowboys' third-string QB and didn't play all season. He made four appearances for the Cowboys during the 2024 season, most notably after Dak Prescott got hurt and backup Cooper Rush was struggling. He started one game in 2024, which was a loss.
He then signed with the Chargers ahead of the 2025 season and played one game for them, losing that start as well. Lance has only started six games in the league, going 2-4, and in his career has a 54 completion percentage, 1,289 yards, five touchdowns and five total interceptions over four years.
Cornerback Jeff Okudah was selected at No. 3 overall by the Lions in 2020. Injuries have impacted his career, including time on IR in his rookie year in 2024 with the Houston Texans and in 2025 with the Minnesota Vikings.
In 2022, he was eventually benched after starting the season as the starter. During the next offseason, he was traded to the Falcons in exchange for a fifth-round pick. He spent one year with Atlanta before going to Houston ahead of the 2024 season. He spent a year there as well before joining the Vikings for a year, his final stop in the league.
Quarterback Sam Darnold has seen the most success of anyone on this list, though it was far from immediate. He bounced around to four teams before he found his fit with the Seattle Seahawks, where he helped lead the team to a Super Bowl win. But let's start from the beginning.
Darnold was the No. 3 overall draft pick in 2018 and was with the Jets until 2020, recording a 13-25 starting record, with 45 touchdowns and 39 interceptions.
He was traded to the Panthers ahead of the 2021 season, and he went 4-7 with nine touchdowns and 13 interceptions. The next season, he lost the starter job to Baker Mayfield and would end up starting six games, going 4-2, with seven touchdowns and two interceptions.
Free agency left Darnold on the 49ers ahead of the 2023 season, after the Panthers decided not to renew his contract. He started just one game, the season finale, for San Fran.
His time with the Niners was short, joining the Vikings the next season, where he would be named the starter after J.J. McCarthy got hurt. Darnold went 14-3 in his one year with Minnesota, with 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.
Darnold also went 14-3 in his first season with the Seahawks. He put together an impressive playoff run that culminated in Seattle being crowned champs.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: What's wrong with Matthew Stafford? Why 2025 MVP is struggling this season, could bounce back vs. Bills
summary: Stafford has as many touchdown passes as interceptions
full_text:
The Rams ' Super-Bowl-or-bust season has started, for the most part, bust, given their great expectations.
Everything went wrong in a Week 1 blowout loss to the 49ers , from the travel plan to the on-field product to the health problems that emerged from it: Myles Garrett underwent knee surgery, and Puka Nacua missed several weeks with a hip/groin issue. Los Angeles blew out the Giants in Week 2 after Jaxson Dart left early, but collapsed in Week 3 against the Broncos and needed a late comeback to overcome a sloppy first 50 minutes against the struggling Eagles .
The Rams are 2-2 -- hardly the end of the world, but not looking close to a championship winner. One of the biggest reasons is that Matthew Stafford doesn't look close to what he was during his MVP-winning 2025. If the Rams want to live up to their superteam reputation, it starts with him.
Stafford was at the peak of his powers last season in several facets, but perhaps the most impressive was his lack of turnovers. He threw just eight interceptions, and his 1.3% interception rate was the lowest of his career.
He's already up to six interceptions this season -- only Drake Maye has more -- and his 3.7% interception rate would be his highest since his 2009 rookie season. It's been a combination of bad throws and bad decisions.
The crushing pick-six he threw to Talanoa Hufanga in Week 3? "Yeah, that was forced ... Hufanga did a really nice job of kind of fighting through the Y, and [I threw] just a little bit back behind [my target]."
The two picks against the Eagles? "Obviously, I don't ever want to turn the ball over like the first one. It was a physical mistake; the ball kind of sailed on me. On the second one, I just got too aggressive. ... I put that ball in a bad spot ..."
jumped the pass, ran a lot, took the lead What an effort by Talanoa Hufanga 🙌 pic.twitter.com/9xvvAC6uoF
The aggressive mindset is ingrained in Stafford. He wants to and can make the big-time throws. The big issues arise when you combine that mindset with inaccuracy. Stafford's off-target rate so far this season is 14.8%, on pace for by far his highest rate since PFF started tracking the stat in 2017. He's only been above 13% once, and he was at 10.9% last year.
Five of his six interceptions this year have been overthrows, underthrows or behind his target, per PFF.
Five of his six interceptions have also been on throws 10+ yards downfield, and that's arguably a more concerning issue. Stafford has a 28.3% off-target rate on throws at least 10 yards downfield this year. That's also on pace for his worst mark, and it's nearly double his rate from last year (15.5).
So was last year just an absolute heater? It's a little bit of both. From 2017-25, Stafford's off-target rate on throws 10+ yards downfield was 20.7%. He should regress toward that mean this season, even if he doesn't absolutely light it up like last year.
There have been several close misses, too. In Week 4, Stafford almost had the touchdown throw of the year to Davante Adams , but the normally sure-handed wide receiver dropped it in the back of the end zone. He also just missed Adams on another deep ball (the ball glanced off an outstretched Adams' hands) and missed Konata Mumpfield by a couple of yards on another deep ball. These are the types of throws that littered his MVP-season highlight reel last year.
Matthew Stafford almost had the touchdown throw of the year Sunday. pic.twitter.com/uNq4UDXS1u
Stafford's downfield accuracy and turnover issues should improve. For him to perform at a career-worst or near-career-worst level this season would be a stunner. It would eliminate the Rams as a Super Bowl team, and the offense will struggle all season if it's the case. Stafford has had some stretches where he turns it over a lot. Normally, it balances out.
Nacua will really help this offense; it doesn't take a football genius to know this. He had nine catches for 125 yards and a rushing touchdown against the Eagles. Since Nacua entered the NFL , Stafford has a significantly higher EPA per play, yards per attempt and explosive pass rate with Nacua on the field compared to with Nacua off it.
Another return that could help Stafford? The play-action dropback game. Last year, 37% of Stafford's dropbacks used play action. This year? It's 23%, on pace for his second-lowest mark as a Ram. Similarly, Stafford has only been under center on 44% of his snaps this season, down from 60% last year. His rollouts are also down, something ESPN's Ben Solak pointed out earlier this week.
There doesn't appear to be any reason for the lack of under-center and/or play-action plays. McVay hasn't addressed it, nor has he been asked about it, according to the team's press conference transcripts this season. Stafford doesn't appear to be any less mobile than he has been recently. Furthermore, the Rams lead the NFL in rushing success rate, which, one would think, would make play action even more effective.
Maybe McVay gets back to arguably the best weapon in his and Stafford's arsenal. It simply doesn't make much sense that he hasn't leaned on it heavily this year.
The win over the Eagles was more important than impressive. There's the major difference between a 1-3 record and 2-2, obviously, but the Rams also overcame themselves -- turnovers, drops, penalties -- and the rain, and Stafford got his first win over a Vic Fangio-coached defense. Sometimes there are just matchups great quarterbacks can't solve; Fangio has been that for Stafford.
It was also important for the Rams to see that when they needed it most, they could have it. Here were the Rams' final two non-kneeldown drives:
Across those two drives, Stafford was 12-for-15 for 140 yards. He hit Nacua on a deep ball and had two beautiful back-shoulder throws to Tyler Higbee .
"There's no style points in this league, but I do think a lot of growth can come from this," McVay said.
Stafford will need to be closer to that end-of-game level in Week 5 against the Bills , who have a high-powered offense of their own. There's a good chance for Stafford to have his best game yet. The Bills ...
Christian Benford is dealing with a toe injury and missed last week's loss to the Patriots . In that game, the previously struggling Maye threw for 269 yards and three scores, and New England's previously struggling offense scored 29 points. Maxwell Hairston gave up two touchdowns and left the locker room early without speaking to reporters . Slot cornerback Dee Alford suffered an ankle injury and did not return.
Stafford should have a great chance to exploit this defense and build on his finish to Week 4. If he can, the Rams will start to look like the powerhouse they were expected to be entering the season.

title: Deep dive into the Cardinals’ trade of Marv Harrison
summary: The Arizona Cardinals just traded WR Marvin Harrison, Jr. to the Houston Texans this past weekend. As part of the Cardinals fanbase, we have already heard this news. Harrison was taken with the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Name a receiver accolade, and Harrison won that award while at Ohio State, which […]
full_text: Marvin Harrison Jr. could be set for a breakout performance as the Cardinals host the Lions in Week 5. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Arizona Cardinals just traded WR Marvin Harrison, Jr. to the Houston Texans this past weekend. As part of the Cardinals fanbase, we have already heard this news. Harrison was taken with the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Name a receiver accolade, and Harrison won that award while at Ohio State, which is known as “Receiver U.” RELATED: IS THE HARRISON TRADE THE NAIL IN THE COFFIN FOR OSSENFORT? Harrison was viewed as a can’t-miss gold jacket recipient. He was the next Larry Fitzgerald. At the top of the 2024 draft, three quarterbacks were taken: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Drake Maye. Next up, Arizona selected Harrison. They could have gotten WR Malik Nabers instead, or TE Brock Bowers, CB Cooper DeJean, or OT Joe Alt. All of these players already have Pro Bowl hardware. Harrison’s rookie season was decent, but not eye-opening. He had 116 targets, which is a lot for a rookie. His 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdown catches were acceptable. He also converted 43 first downs. Again, acceptable numbers for a rookie. But not OMG numbers from the #4 overall draft pick who had won the Biletnikoff Award as the nation’s best receiver, was a two-time All-American, and had been named the Big 10 “Most Valuable Player.” His eight receiving TDs tied the franchise rookie record with Fitzgerald and Anquan Boldin. Again, encouraging. But he was not named to the NFL All-Rookie Team, which was a telling sign. Then last year was a series of unfortunate events. First, in Week 6, he suffered a concussion. Then he underwent an appendectomy and missed the next two games. In Week 13, Harrison suffered a heel injury, which caused him to be gone for another two games. And finally, he had a foot injury in the Week 17 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. This placed him on IR. He only started 10 games with 608 yards, four TDs, but had a very good average per reception of 14.8. All during training camp, the buzz was that Harrison was all new and would have a productive 2026 season. Three things decided Maserati Marv’s future with the Cardinals: can’t get separation, drops, and lack of focus. The issues For weeks, numerous media articles were written about not whether Harrison would be traded, but to which team and for how much equity. On the field, it had become very apparent that QB Jacoby Brissett had lost confidence in Harrison and rarely looked his way. The main reason is that Harrison just wasn’t getting open. He had issues separating himself from his defender, and Brissett threw the ball in a different direction. Why the separation issue? College cornerbacks are not on the same level as NFL cornerbacks. Here at ROTB , we went back and researched all the corners Harrison faced in his final two years at Ohio State. That is 26 opponents, times two cornerbacks per game. Of those 52 defenders, only six are in the NFL; five played in the UFL, and one is in the CFL. 12. Out of 52. That tells us that Harrison dominated lesser talent on the rosters of Rutgers, Toledo, Maryland, Arkansas State, Purdue, and Northwestern. He had 160 yards against Youngstown State, 163 versus Maryland, 184 in the Arkansas State win, and 149 in the Michigan State game, a 38-3 Ohio State victory. But against Notre Dame in 2023, Harrison had 32 yards, while the year before it was only 56 yards. Versus Indiana, just 18. 118 yards in the 30-24 loss to Michigan. 45 yards against Wisconsin. Harrison has had issues with NFL cornerbacks. This is no longer college football with college football cornerbacks. And it does not help that the Cardinals are in the notorious NFC West Division, where every team’s defense is exceptional. This INT is on Marvin Harrison Jr but will go in the stat sheet against Kyler Murray That’s why we track turnover-worthy plays pic.twitter.com/CgR0IrleMA — PFF (@PFF) September 26, 2025 And then the drops. Every Cardinals fan has a memory of their most vivid Harrison drop. Ours is the sure touchdown in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 3 last year, which would have propelled Arizona to a nifty 3-0-0 record. Against the Lions, Harrison was listed on the inactive list, when in reality, he had already been traded to Houston. Being completely healthy this year, he started four of four games with 13 targets, five receptions for 85 yards, five first-down conversions, a 17.0 yards-per-catch average, one touchdown, and one drop. In contrast, TE Trey McBride has 56 targets. 51 for WR Michael Wilson. WR Kendrick Bourne had eight targets in the loss to the Lions alone, and 22 for the year. Brissett is simply looking elsewhere. Last year, after QB Kyler Murray went down and Brissett took over, he connected with Wilson routinely, and Wilson had a breakout season. After the 2025 season was completed, it was apparent that Wilson had moved to the WR1 position. The trade According to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk , the trade was finalized on Saturday. The Texans wanted to keep it a secret until after their game with the Tennessee Titans so that it would not become a distraction. The Texans were able to get their first win of the season with a 26-3 decision over the hapless Titans. In his postgame presser, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans was asked if they had traded for Harrison. He looked a bit perplexed, stalled for a second, then spewed: “You guys want to know, huh? Yes, all right. We traded for Marvin Harrison.” On the other side, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was also asked about the trade in his postgame presser versus the Lions. His response: “I just thought it was in the best interest of the club.” Both GMs for Houston and Arizona have a history of working together. So, the fact that Harrison ended up with the Texans isn’t that surprising. Ossenfort used to work for Nick Caserio while the two were in New England for 14 years. But this was not an Ossenfort decision; the coaching staff orchestrated this trade. Ossenfort then put the plan in motion. Trade: the Arizona Cardinals have agreed to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and 2027 7th-round pick to the Houston Texans in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and 2027 6th-round pick, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/ziepfRIPr4 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 11, 2026 Financially, it is a good deal for the Texans. Harrison is due $4 million this year and $5.62 million in 2027. He also has a fifth-year option coming up this offseason. His $22.5 million signing bonus was already paid by the Cardinals. Harrison has been known as a dynamic receiver, just not in Arizona. In fact, out of all the productive receivers that have come out of Ohio State, Harrison has shown he is the worst of them all. Harrison does join his former Ohio State signalcaller, C.J. Stroud. With Houston, they aren’t gambling on a rookie who hasn’t played yet in the NFL. Harrison has two-plus seasons already as a small sample. He isn’t a bad receiver; however, he has hardly been distinguished. Nobody in the league considers Harrison to be one of the best pass catchers in the league. Hell, he isn’t even the best pass catcher on his own team. Since 2024, Harrison ranks 70th out of 130 wideouts in yards per route run (1.54) and 44th in receiving yards per game (47.8). Maybe Houston can rekindle his talent. Maybe Harrison needs to be lined up against some lesser talent on defense, eh? That was on Harrison 100% you gotta catch that the pass was perfect — Rob Gotcher (@GotcherRob13984) September 26, 2025 Harrison just couldn’t get himself open. That is the bottom line. Yes, he had 10 drops in the 30 games he started, but while playing for Arizona, Harrison ranked dead last in the league among all receivers (with 50 targets or more over the past three years) in separation, averaging just 2.1 yards of separation when targeted, per NFL Next Gen Stats . That is a huge stat, and very telling. Brissett…

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Lions Winners & Losers: Arizona tanks big time
summary: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win against a mediocre Detroit Lions ballclub. The Lions finished last in the NFC North Division last year, as the Cardinals finished last in the NFC West. Both clubs are involved in the “last place finish” schedule. RELATED: PETZING’S OFFENSE GETS ITS REVENGE The 1-3-0 Cardinals would end up being […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win against a mediocre Detroit Lions ballclub. The Lions finished last in the NFC North Division last year, as the Cardinals finished last in the NFC West. Both clubs are involved in the “last place finish” schedule. RELATED: PETZING’S OFFENSE GETS ITS REVENGE The 1-3-0 Cardinals would end up being at the bottom of the league if they lost to the Lions. As it was, Detroit took Arizona to the woodshed in a 45-21 bloodbath. The game began really good as the Cardinals went down on their first drive of the game, and scored after a 14-play drive. But in the second quarter, the Lions scored 24 unanswered points and took control of the contest with a full half to go. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS The opening drive – The Cardinals defense got Detroit to go three-and-out on their first possession, and then the offense took over on their own 27-yard line. Right off, an 11-yard catch by TE Trey McBride, followed by short receptions by TE Elijah Higgins and WR Michael Wilson. Then, a 22-yard reception and several plays later a nine-yard grab by WR Kendrick Bourne. Suddenly, Arizona was on Detroit’s 18-yard line with a third-and-10. Seven yards to Wilson set up a fourth-and-short on the Lions’ nine-yard line. The offense went for it, and QB Jacoby Brissett then found TE Teagan Quitoriano for the two-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead. 14 plays, 73 yards, 7:54 of clock, and a temporary feeling that today would be the day. WR Kendrick Bourne – This is a guy who should have been given more reps all season long. Several good grabs to move the sticks. The 22-yard grab on the opening drive was just a preview. In the second quarter, Bourne caught an eight-yard pass that got them from being deep to manageable. Then on the next possession, Bourne corralled the Brissett pass and went 23 yards to Detroit’s 49-yard line. Led all receivers with 70 yards on five receptions. oh my McBride 😳 #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/014MXVJnXd — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 TE Trey McBride – Yes, the game was out of reach when McBride snagged that bobbled touchdown with 2:11 left in the game. What a spectacular catch on a poor throw. The most amazing aspect was McBride’s feet awareness, much-less his focus on the football at all times. Had the most targets with 10, but most of those were when the game was already out of reach. What gives? Two targets and one reception at the half. Nine catches for 66 yards is a travesty. Throw him the ball! S Budda Baker – If you want someone to tackle a defender, just tell Budda. Time and time again, he took down an offensive player that his teammates had whiffed on, or let go. Led all tacklers with 11. TQ's second TD of the day 🙂‍↕️ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/xyZ8b0q9Er — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 TE Teagan Quitoriano – Two targets, two receptions, two touchdowns? Why isn’t this offense getting him more involved with stats like this? ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Non-tight end coverage – All game long, the Lions’ tight ends were wide-ass open. Why? Starting TE Sam LaPorta was open on all five of his catches, and scored on a 38-yard catch and run. The play before was 11-yards to LaPorta and a 12-yard reception on the series before. There goes Sam pic.twitter.com/jWOW1mJVFT — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Backup TE Brock Wright snared an 11-yard reception that converted a first down. It was so bad that LaPorta led all Detroit receivers with 88 yards, and caught all five targets. We tried to see DC Nick Rallis’ defensive game plan, and are certain it states, “No need to cover the Lions’ tight ends since they are all blockers.” Offense after the opening points – As great as the opening drive was, it became a scoring desert after that: punt, punt, punt, punt, punt, INT, missed FG, until the Cardinals scored a touchdown with 5:20 remaining in the third quarter, and then it no longer mattered. Tackling – All game long, name a Cardinals defensive player, and he missed a tackle or three. Arizona’s tackling consisted of grabbing waists or jumping on shoulder pads. Remember the wild ride by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs where a pile of players went for 12 yards? The replay was from the end zone, the pile was headed in the direction of. In the bottom of the pile, you can see Gibbs’ legs still churning. Do they no longer teach players at this level to take out legs? Or is Budda Baker the only Cardinals defender who knows this? CB Garrett Williams had three missed tackles, while LB Mack Wilson had a pair. All game long, players who bounce off Detroit ballcarriers, including two that were third-and-long that became a first down. Pathetic display of how to bring down the other team’s ballcarriers. Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 11, 2026 Offensive line – Brissett rarely had a clean pocket when he dropped back, and forget about running the ball. There were simply no lanes created all game. Brissett was sacked five times and that could have been double digits if Brissett had not gotten out of the stronghold of yet another defender. This group is in trouble now that Paris Johnson is gone for the season. 56 yards on the ground is a mess. Most passing downs were two words: Jail break. Defense, beginning with Quarter 2 – In the beginning, the defense was pretty stiff. Detroit’s first three possessions were all three-and-out followed by a punt. After the Cardinals had a three-and-out to begin the second quarter, the flood gates opened for the Lions: TD, TD, TD, FG, TD, TD, TD, punt. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – It starts with “hold my beer” QB Jacoby Brissett – To be fair, his pocket was in shambles for most of the game. He tried his best to get out into the flats and attempt to find an open guy, but the Lions defenders were just too much for this pieced-together offensive line. 38 yards for 8⃣4⃣ moves the chains ⛓️ #DETvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/1RfcajfkGy — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 11, 2026 Brissett had his moments, but on passing downs, unless he rolled out, he was harassed and flushed. He went 29 for 47 for 292 yards, three TD passes against one INT, sacked five times with a QB rating of 91.8. Fourth downs – The Lions went 4 for 4 on fourth downs. Ouch. But they were a dismal 4 for 13 on third-down efficiency. RB Jeremiyah Love – At no time was this young guy a threat. Finished with 12 carries for 22 yards with a long of eight yards. This Cardinals team needs premier offensive linemen and pass rushers, and yet passed on both for another running back. DT Roy Lopez – Had a productive day and was a good anchor to stop the run up the gut. Finished with six total tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one QB hit. His sack of QB Jared Goff in their second possession forced a punt. In the second quarter, Gibbs caught a short pass in the flats, and Lopez tracked him down after a 23-yard gain.

title: Reports: Michael Penix Jr. rib injury does not seem to be serious, status for Week 6 still up in the air
summary: Michael Penix Jr. couldn’t finish the Sunday Night Football loss to the Baltimore Ravens after getting drilled in the ribs late; he actually returned briefly after Tua Tagoviloa took the field for a single play but was in too much pain to return for overtime. The worry was that Penix, who despite some very real […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA- OCTOBER 11: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons throws a pass during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta,Georgia. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Michael Penix Jr. couldn’t finish the Sunday Night Football loss to the Baltimore Ravens after getting drilled in the ribs late; he actually returned briefly after Tua Tagoviloa took the field for a single play but was in too much pain to return for overtime. The worry was that Penix, who despite some very real hiccups against Baltimore has given this passing game a massive boost over the past three weeks, might miss a game or multiple games owing to his injury. The team hasn’t confirmed this yet, but Adam Schefter reports that it’s a relatively minor rib injury—as minor as those get, given that they’re not particularly fun to go through—and Penix may actually be able to start in Week 6. The days ahead will tell the tale. Michael Penix’s rib injury is not considered serious, per sources. Penix might be able to return for Sunday’s game vs. the Bears, but the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week before it knows whether he will be able to play in Week 6. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 12, 2026 This is a relief for multiple reasons. The first is that you could tell when he took the hit that Penix was hurt, and the fact that Tagovailoa had to finish the game meant we were bracing for Atlanta’s starter to be out a while. Ideally he would not miss the Chicago game given that the Bears have a very gettable pass defense, but even if he does, the fact that this doesn’t seem likely to stretch out multiple weeks is a major relief. The second is that not having Penix on the field opens the door to a horror show of backup quarterback options headlined by Tua, who has as many interceptions in three passes (1) as Penix has in three weeks and 77 attempts. Perhaps Tagovailoa will look a lot better not having to come into the game cold, but I’m not particularly eager to find out. Kevin Stefanski said he’ll likely have an update on Wednesday, but it sounds like the Falcons and Penix may have dodged a more serious, long-term outcome here. We’ll learn more as the week rolls on.

title: Falcons snap counts from a tough overtime loss to the Ravens
summary: I’m still dragging something fierce after three straight primetime games, but the snap counts must roll on, and so they shall. Offense LG Matthew Bergeron: 64 C Ryan Neuzil: 64 RG Chris Lindstrom: 64 RT Jawaan Taylor: 64 WR Drake London: 63 LT Jake Matthews: 63 QB Michael Penix Jr.: 61 RB Bijan Robinson: 52 […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Bralen Trice #48, Avieon Terrell #12, and Xavier Watts #31 of the Atlanta Falcons tackle Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens after a catch in overtime of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m still dragging something fierce after three straight primetime games, but the snap counts must roll on, and so they shall. Offense LG Matthew Bergeron: 64 C Ryan Neuzil: 64 RG Chris Lindstrom: 64 RT Jawaan Taylor: 64 WR Drake London: 63 LT Jake Matthews: 63 QB Michael Penix Jr.: 61 RB Bijan Robinson: 52 TE Kyle Pitts: 43 WR Jahan Dotson: 42 TE Charlie Woerner: 42 WR Olamide Zaccheaus: 21 RB Brian Robinson Jr: 14 WR Chris Blair: 13 WR Zachariah Branch: 12 TE Austin Hooper: 10 TE Nick Muse: 5 T Mike Jerrell: 3 QB Tua Tagovailoa: 3 C Corey Levin: 1 Several things did not go according to plan in this one. Matthews played after there was some question of that this week, but he and Lindstrom had their worst games of the season against a tough Baltimore front. That led to a faltering ground game and more pressure than Penix was comfortable with. Every offensive lineman allowed at least one pressure, but those were heavily concentrated with Matthews (3) and Lindstrom (4), who allowed seven of the 12 pressures Penix faced on the day. When the line is struggling, the offense is going to splutter, as it did for long stretches Sunday night. Otherwise, the usage shouldn’t look unfamiliar here. The Falcons run a lot of two tight end looks, Dotson is heavily favored as the team’s #2 receiver, and Zaccheaus is running ahead of Branch as WR3. The lack of production from Zaccheaus and Branch’s explosiveness in his limited looks may change that in the weeks ahead, however. Defense S Xavier Watts: 76 S Jessie Bates: 76 ILB Divine Deablo: 76 CB Mike Hughes: 69 OLB Samson Ebukam: 58 ILB Kendal Daniels: 50 OLB Cameron Thomas: 49 CB Avieon Terrell: 43 DL Maason Smith: 43 DL Gervon Dexter: 43 CB CJ Henderson: 39 DL LaCale London: 37 DL Brandon Dorlus: 36 ILB Harold Perkins Jr.: 25 CB Billy Bowman Jr.: 25 DL Zach Harrison: 24 S Sydney Brown: 24 OLB Bralen Trice: 20 DL Jared Ivey: 18 S DeMarcco Hellams: 2 OLB Drake Jackson: 2 CB Mike Ford: 1 Several things went awry here, too. The first was simple wear and tear, as the Falcons had to lean very heavily on Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas in this one and taxed their defensive front, leading to a late collapse. The second is that an injury to CJ Henderson, who has playing quite well, put an enormous strain on this cornerback group, where Mike Hughes was already struggling to the tune of 5/8 for 63 yards (a significant portion of the 24/30 for 201 yards Tyler Huntley put up). When Hughes briefly exited the game, the Falcons had to put Mike Ford on the field, and the Ravens immediately went after him for a seven yard touchdown. Hughes’ struggles have been well-documented at this point—he’s allowed a team-high 288 yards and two touchdowns with zero pass breakups and zero interceptions on 20 receptions and 29 targets—but Henderson had been a bright spot filling in for Terrell. If he’s out, the Falcons are heavily relying on rookie Aveion Terrell, Billy Bowman Jr., and some combination of Ford and practice squad elevations along with Hughes, which is a recipe for a tough week against the Bears. The other note of note is that Daniels was once again in the driver’s seat for major snaps next to Divine Deablo, and it’s purely a situational timeshare with Harold Perkins Jr. The more a team runs, the more playing time Daniels receives, while Perkins gets more run against teams that pass heavily. It’s mostly working quite well. Special teams DeMarcco Hellams: 25 Mike Ford: 25 Josh Woods: 25 Nick Muse: 23 Jammie Robinson: 22 Sydney Brown: 21 Harold Perkins Jr.: 19 Charlie Woerner: 15 Chris Blair: 14 Kendal Daniels: 13 Jake Bailey: 11 Nick Folk: 10 Liam McCullough: 9 Maason Smith: 7 Billy Bowman Jr.: 7 Gervon Dexter: 7 Xavier Watts: 7 LaCale London: 7 Zachariah Branch: 6 Mike Jerrell: 5 Matthew Bergeron: 5 Zach Harrison: 5 Kyle Hinton: 5 Brian Robinson Jr.: 5 Olamide Zaccheaus: 5 Jake Matthews: 5 Avieon Terrell: 4 Divine Deablo: 4 Mike Hughes: 2 CJ Henderson: 1 The good news: The Falcons only missed one special teams tackle on Sunday night and Nick Folk and Jake Bailey were quite good. The bad news: The Falcons were penalized three separate times on Sunday, each one costing them field position in a game where drives frequently sputtered out. The lack of discipline is showing up week after week on teams, and it’s proving costly week after week.
