full_text: The Carolina Panthers, fresh of their division-leading early bye week have been set up as 1.5 point road underdogs to the Philadelphia Eagles. This now qualifies as a lack of respect from our friends at FanDuel . The Eagles are coming off of a three week losing streak that featured losses to the Chicago Bears, the Los Angeles Rams, the Jacksonville Jaguars (in London), questionable decision making by the Eagles coaching staff, and some of the least inspired quarterback play of Jalen Hurts’ career. The Panthers, if you need to be reminded, are fresh off of a rest week, a primetime win against the Detroit Lions, and are set to return several injured starters that missed at least the Lions win, with some missing the whole season to date. Week 6 Spread Panthers: +1.5 (-1010) Eagless: -1.5 (-110) O/U 41.5 (-115/-105) Moneyline Panthers: +108 Eagles: -126 Remember that home-field advantage is traditionally accounted for by spotting the home team—theEagles, in this case—three points on the spread. That would actually see the Panthers favored by less than a safety on a neutral field. It is clear that FanDuel doesn’t trust Bryce Young yet. Honestly, that’s kind of fair, but this still feels like a betting line weighted more on performance from past seasons for both teams than it is on the last four to five games of the 2026 season. summary: The Carolina Panthers entered their Week 5 bye exhilarated and exhausted. A thrilling and convincing win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football in Week 4 put the team atop the NFC South. Injuries have mounted for the Panthers, but an early bye has the team set to return players who were injured both […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after defeating the Detroit Lions 32-26 at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers entered their Week 5 bye exhilarated and exhausted. A thrilling and convincing win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football in Week 4 put the team atop the NFC South. Injuries have mounted for the Panthers, but an early bye has the team set to return players who were injured both during and before the season. How did the rest of the NFC South fare this week? Week 5 NFC South results Tampa Bay Buccaneers 24, Dallas Cowboys 16 The 1-4 Bucs notched their first win of the season against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football thanks to the efforts of undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels. Daniels was playing in relief of an injured Baker Mayfield and may have, albeit briefly, saved head coach Todd Bowles’ job. Put one way, chaos is afoot in Tampa. Put another, grab your popcorn and let’s watch this dumpster burn. Minnesota Vikings 23, New Orleans Saints 13 The now 1-4 New Orleans Saints have come along way since being crowned the 2026 NFC South champs by most of the national media in the offseason. Tyler Shough, expected to be the division MVP if that were a thing, completed 16 of 25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions. They will still be a tough out for the Panthers, because that’s how the NFC South works, but they seem less like the ascendant team who lucked into a talented quarterback and more like Uncle Rico and his imaginary friends trying to throw a ball over that mountain. Baltimore Ravens 30, Atlanta Falcons 23 (OT) The 2-3 Falcons are the closest competition the Panthers have in the South. Michael Penix has been a revelation at quarterback compared to Cooper Rush and their defense has been taking major strides forward in recent weeks, sort of They took the momentum of a two-week winning streak against the Packers and the Saints and snapped it against a Ravens team without Lamar Jackson. Their defense, despite giving up 30 points to Tyler Huntley & co., played alright. This loss largely comes down to their offense. Penix’s crew didn’t score until late in the second quarter and then couldn’t finish a drive in the fourth. Settling for two field goals despite holding the ball for 12:58 in the fourth quarter doomed the Falcons as much as Penix’s game sealing interception in overtime. NFC South Standings Carolina Panthers (2-2) Atlanta Falcons (2-3) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) New Orleans Saints (1-4)

Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That was a thorough whistle-to-whistle butt-kicking, and the Chicago Bears need to regroup and turn the page after the stink bomb they dropped in Green Bay yesterday. The Bears fell behind 14 to 0, made it interesting heading into the half at 14 to 7, but did nothing coming out of the break and lost 31 to 7. Even with the halftime score so close, head coach Ben Johnson felt like most fans when he dropped a few f-bombs to ESPN 1000 on his way into the locker room. Staying with the bomb theme, the Bears had no answer for Jordan Love’s right arm. He had one of the best games of his career, and his four pass plays of over 40 yards were the most the Bears have allowed in a game since at least 2000 ( per The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbein via TruMedia ). His second touchdown to Christian Watson traveled 66.9 yards in the air, the third-longest completed air-yard pass in the NFL since NextGenStats started tracking it (2016). The Bears need to figure out how to pressure the quarterback or cover better, and I don’t think a couple of defensive players returning from the PUP list is enough. Could we see another trade? Starter Caleb Williams hasn’t logged a full practice since injuring his hamstring, and backups Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum combined for four turnovers and four sacks in yesterday’s loss. Even though Caleb had a solid workout Sunday morning, Johnson still isn’t sure his QB1 will be cleared for Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. “He’s doing a great job progressing, and we’ll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games,” Johnson said about Williams via ESPN’s Courtney Cronin. “But he’s itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we’ll move forward from there.” When he was asked who’ll get the first team reps at quarterback on Wednesday if Williams is limited, Johnson said via WGN’s Eli Ong, “Yeah, we’re still working through that. No determination has been made in terms of what direction we’re going. There’s a lot of things that we’re assessing right now.” And when asked if Bagent would get those QB1 reps, he said, “We have three guys that can win games in this league.”

title: 10 Bears Takes: Packers Week was a disaster, a Caleb Williams return, and more
summary: Week 5 was Packers week, and despite being favored for the first time in two decades heading into Lambeau Field, the wheels came off the backup quarterback experience in the form of a 31-7 beatdown on Sunday afternoon. In a game that the Bears never led, and frankly, never felt like they were in, it […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears embraces head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers after the Packers defeated the Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 5 was Packers week, and despite being favored for the first time in two decades heading into Lambeau Field, the wheels came off the backup quarterback experience in the form of a 31-7 beatdown on Sunday afternoon. In a game that the Bears never led, and frankly, never felt like they were in, it was a stark reminder that although they’ve had their fair share of impressive performances, this team is far from a finished product. More on Sunday’s blowout loss, and where they go from here in Week 5’s installment of 10 Bears Takes. 1. On Friday, news broke that former Super Bowl-winning head coach Mike Ditka died at age 86—more on how his football legacy will live on in Chicago for eternity. In many ways, Mike Ditka was larger than life, especially in the city of Chicago. Because of the Bears’ lack of success over the last three decades, the ‘85 Bears have remained the pride of Chicago sports, no matter the sport. Not only did that team have plenty of likable players, but they were also dominant on the field for a good stretch. Their head coach, though, always caught headlines for his unique, hard-nosed personality. For those around to watch Ditka’s 12-year playing career, they’d all agree that his personality and coaching style were reflective of how he played the game. He’s one of three tight ends taken in the first round in franchise history, and as Greg Olson pointed out on the broadcast, he was always a presence around the franchise once his coaching career ended. His immediate success at the position as a rookie was almost unheard of, and even after he left the Bears organization, he remained a legendary figure in Chicago sports. Many will remember him as a gruff personality not afraid of conflict, while others will remember him for his years on different NFL-related shows. He was always one to stick up for the Bears, and there wasn’t a time that I can remember when he didn’t pick them to win a game. In many ways, Ditka’s persona was larger than life, and you don’t think of the Chicago Bears without thinking of the coach himself. As Ben Johnson said, he is the gold standard around Halas Hall, and even in death, that will never change. While 86 years on this earth is a long time to live, life is never long enough, and it’s a great reminder to love those in your life and not take a day for granted. 2. Packers week couldn’t have gone much worse, and now Ben Johnson and company must swallow their pride, get back to the drawing board, and find a way to get back in the win column next weekend in Atlanta. There’s little better in the sports world than your favorite team getting the “last word” in a rivalry game like the Bears did in the Wild Card Round in January. In Johnson’s first season as the team’s head coach, he didn’t shy away from the rivalry, and dare I say, he fueled the fire in ways that not many head coaches have done in franchise history. Coming into Week 5, it felt like the two organizations were headed in separate directions. Despite being separated by just one game in the standings, the Packers struggled to win, while the Bears had multiple convincing wins over their first four weeks. As usual, none of that mattered, especially with the game being played at Lambeau Field. Justifiably so, the Bears were loud all offseason about their ability to get the better of the Packers in two of the three games from last season. There was confidence from both the organization and the fans that their fortunes had finally turned, and this was about to be as lopsided in the Bears’ favor as it had been for Green Bay over the last three decades. While that might still be the case as the years go on, Sunday served as a sobering reminder that the Packers still have Chicago’s number, at least to a certain extent. The 31-7 final score at Lambeau was a good snapshot into just how lopsided the majority of Sunday’s contest truly was. Frankly, the game started on the wrong foot with the opening offensive drive and never really equaled out. Not only did the Bears never lead, but for the most part, it never felt like they were fully “in” the game. The offense sputtered, and the defense only gained their footing for a quarter or so. Simply put, if you were judging both teams based on that one game, it would feel like the clock had been turned back a few years and Bears fans were back living in the nightmare that quarterback Aaron Rodgers had them in. The good news is that, for the majority of the season, the Bears have looked like the much better team. Maybe Sunday’s game will serve as an indicator of future success for both teams, but as we’ve learned so far this season, the NFL is very much a week-to-week league at this juncture in the calendar. That said, Johnson, his staff, and this team must reassess their approach moving forward. With any luck, they won’t start a backup quarterback in Week 6, but even if Caleb Williams comes back against Atlanta, plenty went wrong on Sunday and needs to be corrected. It’s time for this team to address the issues, get their starting quarterback back under center, and get back into the win column next Sunday. After all, the last thing this team can afford to do is throw away a 3-1 start, especially considering half of those games were played with backup quarterbacks. 3. Going 2-1 with a pair of backup quarterbacks is no easy feat. That said, things went up in flames at Lambeau Field with Bagent leading the charge in a disastrous second start. First, we’ll start with the good. When Williams originally went down with his hamstring injury, everyone’s mind immediately went to a season-ending injury. Once it was confirmed as a hamstring injury, the initial prognosis was much better than expected. Honestly, if they can get Williams back in Week 6, missing three games over a 17-game season is about as “best-case scenario” as you could hope for when the season happened. When most teams lose their starting quarterback, no matter how long, the immediate concern is staying afloat. I believe that I was far from alone in that mindset, even with Williams’ injury. Case Keenum had an impressive showing on Monday Night Football, and some wondered why they would “go back” to Bagent after that type of performance. In the moment, I understood both arguments. On one hand, yeah, it’s hard to bench a player who had a storybook-like performance against a good Eagles defense. On the other hand, matching that outing was going to be next to an impossible feat. Trusting that Johnson had his roster evaluated correctly and leaning on the depth chart (with Bagent being the primary backup) made plenty of sense. In Bagent’s first start, there was some good, even if there were some concerning signs. In the end, they left some points on the board, but a few of his “should have been” interceptions were wiped away by penalties. As I wrote last week, there should have at least been a conversation about who was starting this weekend. Even if they believed that Keenum’s Monday night performance wasn’t repeatable, Bagent’s body of work against the Jets was less than stellar. Simply put, going 2-1 with two different backup quarterbacks is an impressive feat that should not be overlooked. If that number is flipped or if they go winless, there’s a good chance that Williams is rushed back before he was ready. A winning record without Williams was not only unexpected, but it has also allowed them to stay true to Williams’ recovery timeline. That said, a conversation needs to be had when it comes to Bagent’s standing on the depth chart. If Week 4 was a questionable performance, Week 5 was a flat-out disaster. Not only did he throw two interceptions, but he also missed wide-open…
author: Aaron Leming

title: Bears vs. Packers: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and Jordan Love’s Explosives
summary: All that offensive ball control dominance the Chicago Bears have had so far this season didn’t help them against Jordan Love and the explosive Green Bay Packers offense yesterday. In Chicago’s 31-7 loss, Love was 25 of 31 (80.6%) for 367 yards, with 2 touchdowns and a passer rating of 137.5. His 367 passing yards […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a touchdown pass against the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images All that offensive ball control dominance the Chicago Bears have had so far this season didn’t help them against Jordan Love and the explosive Green Bay Packers offense yesterday. In Chicago’s 31-7 loss, Love was 25 of 31 (80.6%) for 367 yards, with 2 touchdowns and a passer rating of 137.5. His 367 passing yards are the most ever against the Bears at Lambeau Field, and it wasn’t a bunch of YAC (yards after catch), as Love was finding open receivers downfield. On passes over 20+ air yards, Love was 6 of 8 for 258 yards, which is the second-most deep passing yards in a game in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). His five passes of 30+ air yards are tied for the most in a single game since ESPN started tracking that stat 20 years ago. Chicago’s defense had no answer for Love, who just kept looking deep. The Bears sacked Love twice, but his 2.54-second time to throw was his longest this season. What stings so much is that the Packers used Chicago’s defense to get their offense back on track. Before yesterday’s game, the Packers’ offense struggled to find consistency, but the Bears offered no resistance. Green Bay had more yards (428 to 246), more first downs (18 to 17), a better time of possession (30:24 to 29:36), and was better on third downs (33.3% to 28.6%) and fourth downs (1-1 to 2-5). The Bears ran more plays (68 to 59) and had fewer penalties (3 for 20 yards to 4 for 25), but the turnover margin (5 for Chicago, 0 for Green Bay) was impossible to overcome. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing-time breakdown and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE Tyson Bagent, who was making just his sixth career start, performed like we should have expected a backup quarterback to perform on the road. He’d never been in an environment as loud and hostile as Lambeau Field, and his inexperience showed all day. He wasn’t decisive. He wasn’t confident. He was late in his progressions. He seemed to be aiming the ball instead of letting it rip, and with below-average arm strength, he can’t afford to take anything off his passes. Case Keenum came in and wasn’t much better, but it was too little, too late, and the Packers were in full pass-rush mode at that point. The Bears are now 2-1 in games started by their backup quarterbacks, and most NFL teams would be happy with that. DEFENSE In case you missed it, the Bears lost three defenders to injury during the game: linebacker TJ Edwards (hamstring), cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring), and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quad). Chicago’s secondary either busted coverages or simply couldn’t keep up with Green Bay’s Christian Watson (6 receptions, 143 yards, 2 TDs), Marcus Golden (6 for 123), or Tucker Kraft (5 for 64). SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was wide left on a 43-yard field goal and hit his only extra point try. Tory Taylor had 4 punts with a 53.0 average (46.3 net) with 1 punt inside the twenty. Zavion Thomas returned 6 kickoffs for a 32.0 average, with a long of 61. Kalif Raymond had a 9-yard punt return. To check out the complete Bears vs. Packers box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Bears falter on both sides of ball in blowout loss to Packers
summary: The Chicago Bears have had a rough history with the Green Bay Packers throughout the last decade or so, and that bad luck continued on Sunday. Their 31-7 loss to Green Bay dropped them to a 3-2 record for the 2026 season, and it saw them dominated on both sides of the ball. Though the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears passes against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have had a rough history with the Green Bay Packers throughout the last decade or so, and that bad luck continued on Sunday. Their 31-7 loss to Green Bay dropped them to a 3-2 record for the 2026 season, and it saw them dominated on both sides of the ball. Though the absence of Caleb Williams at quarterback significantly impacted the Bears’ ability to generate explosive plays on offense, the defense gave up plenty of those through the air at Lambeau Field. Green Bay’s dynamic passing attack helped its offense get out to an insurmountable lead in the second half, and bad play from both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum made it impossible for the Bears to catch up. If you watched the game, you know it wasn’t pretty, and you likely don’t want to think too much about it. For those of you who do, however, and for the ones who didn’t get to watch the game, here are some of my key takeaways from the Bears’ loss so you don’t have to. It’s time to be realistic about Tyson Bagent There’s no other way around it; Bagent was bad on Sunday. He finished the game 12-for-21 (57.1%) with just 87 passing yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions. He made several throws into tight coverage or outright double-team situations, making baffling decisions that one wouldn’t expect from a quarterback who has been touted for his intelligence. Eventually, the Bears chose to put Keenum into the game, though his results weren’t much better. Let’s be realistic about Bagent. He’s not one of the best 32 quarterbacks in the NFL. He is not a starting-caliber player. In four years in the NFL, he has three passing touchdowns and nine interceptions. The Bears would not be better off with him than they are with Caleb Williams. The hyperbole around Bagent, a tremendous success story from the Division II level as an undrafted free agent, has built his hype into something much greater than he actually is. He’s not a terrible football player, and even after this performance, I’d argue he’s still a solid backup quarterback (there are a lot of really bad NFL quarterbacks out there), but Sunday showed what he really is. Deep coverage struggles vs. Packers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden each surpassed 120 receiving yards on Sunday against the Bears. Tucker Kraft had a 48-yard gain in the game. Jordan Love finished the matchup with 367 passing yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, a 137.5 passer rating, and an initial PFN QB Impact grade of 84.6, which ranks second in the NFL in Week 5, as of this writing. Simply put, Chicago struggled to stop the Packers’ vertical passing game this week. Xavier Woods had some instances where he looked out of position as the deep safety help. Dillon Thieneman appeared to have a play or two of poor processing and positioning, as well. Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, and Jaylon Johnson all seemed to have lapses in coverage over the course of the afternoon, pending further All-22 review. The Bears’ secondary simply isn’t fast enough right now. They don’t have the raw speed at cornerback to make up for the lapses in judgment along the perimeter that Stevenson and Johnson make, and Coby Bryant’s presence at safety is sorely missed. It’s not the end of the world The Bears went 2-1 in the three games that Caleb Williams missed due to injury. In the grand scheme of things, it could’ve been a lot worse. Sure, they were utterly outclassed on both sides of the ball against the Packers. Their lapses in coverage will need to be addressed in the remaining 12 games of the season. But a calling card of this Bears team has been their offense, which has looked dynamic when Williams is throwing the ball more often than not. In most cases, having a backup in at quarterback significantly limits how much an NFL offense can operate to its full potential, both from an execution and a play-calling perspective. There’s a chance that Williams returns for the Bears’ game against the Falcons next week. With how Atlanta has looked in recent weeks, the Bears will need all the help they can get. But they’re still 3-2, and there’s plenty of football left to be played. Sunday’s result is nothing to panic over.

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: 5 Bye Week Overreactions
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did what they needed to do on Sunday to beat the lowly Miami Dolphins. In doing so, they head into their bye week with a winning record. At 3-2, they’re technically in last place in the AFC North, but they’re very much in the thick of things. That’s not to say things […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals did what they needed to do on Sunday to beat the lowly Miami Dolphins. In doing so, they head into their bye week with a winning record. At 3-2, they’re technically in last place in the AFC North, but they’re very much in the thick of things. That’s not to say things are perfect in Cincinnati, because they’re not. After the first two games showcasing a dominant defense, Al Golden’s crew has struggled over the last three weeks. The offense, despite all their star power, looks mediocre at times. Before we get into some overreactions heading into the bye week, here are some random thoughts on the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins : Congratulations to Evan McPherson, whose 22nd consecutive made field goal established a new franchise record, surpassing the previous mark held by Shayne Graham. Joe Burrow completed more than 70% of his passes and threw four touchdowns, but averaged just 5.1 yards per completion. Much of his afternoon was spent dinking and dunking underneath, taking what the defense gave him rather than pushing the ball downfield. On the rare occasions he did take a shot deep, though, he reminded everyone what he’s capable of: JA'MARR CHASE ARE YOU SERIOUS @CINvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k4RKY5bLbY — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Jordan Battle took plenty of heat for his performances in Weeks 3 and 4, and deservedly so. He responded with two interceptions against Miami, but what impressed me most was his tackling. Battle was much more reliable in the open field on Sunday, and this tackle may very well have saved a touchdown: More than the interceptions, these are the plays I want to see more of from Jordan Battle. Make the sound tackle and keep a moderate gain a moderate gain on the play. pic.twitter.com/VTDWyJKmCH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 The Bengals, largely thanks to their rebuilt defensive line, have been pretty successful at stopping the run between the tackles. When opposing running backs get to the outside, though, it’s a different story. After shutting down Houston’s rushing attack in Week 2, Cincinnati has struggled to contain the ground games of the Steelers, Jaguars, and Dolphins. It’s becoming a troubling trend. I know the Bengals only won by a touchdown, but the game wasn’t nearly as close as the final score suggests. Miami’s late touchdown was the very definition of garbage-time scoring. Still, I don’t love the fact that the Bengals are the only team the Dolphins have managed to score more than 13 points against this season. Bye Week Overreactions With the bye week upon us, here are a few overreactions based on what we’ve seen from the Bengals through the first five weeks of the season. Samaje Perine should be RB1 Zac Taylor decided to ride the hot hand on Sunday in Miami, giving Perine 13 carries compared to Chase Brown’s 11. Perine was the more effective runner against the Dolphins, just as he was in Week 4, although neither back had much success against Jacksonville. That doesn’t mean Brown should be relegated to the bench. Brown has been far more involved in the passing game, hauling in 24 receptions compared to Perine’s seven. Considering the Bengals have Joe Burrow under center and operate a pass-first offense, Brown isn’t going anywhere. Dexter Lawrence wasn’t worth the No. 10 pick After back-to-back losses in Weeks 3 and 4, followed by a game in which the Dolphins nearly doubled their combined scoring output from the previous four weeks, it’s clear the Bengals should have used their top-10 pick on someone who could actually transform their defense. Right? Wrong. Lawrence has earned the second-highest defensive grade among defensive linemen who have played at least 50% of their team’s snaps, according to PFF, with an 82.5 grade. He also ranks third among defensive tackles in quarterback hurries. And don’t overlook the improved play of linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. Much of their development can be attributed to Lawrence occupying blockers in front of them, allowing them to make plays they might not have made a year ago. Lawrence isn’t the problem. He’s a big part of the solution. Tee Higgins is WR1 Both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have caught 27 passes through five games, but Higgins has racked up 423 receiving yards compared to Chase’s 289. And that doesn’t mean a damn thing. On almost any other team in the NFL, Higgins would unquestionably be WR1. Unfortunately for him, he shares the field with the best wide receiver in football. Chase can do things that almost no other receiver in the league can replicate. Higgins is a phenomenal player, and there’s no denying that, but Chase is on another level. Darrin Simmons is on the hot seat Special teams haven’t exactly been a bright spot for the Bengals this season. Outside of Evan McPherson and the kicking game, the unit has been responsible for several costly mistakes. In Week 3, a muffed punt and a roughing-the-kicker penalty cost Cincinnati 10 points. Against Miami, Lawrence was flagged for roughing the snapper on a field goal attempt, extending a drive that ultimately ended in a Dolphins touchdown. And that wasn’t the only special teams mistake on Sunday. Here’s the thing, though: Simmons has been Cincinnati’s special teams coordinator since 2003 and has held the title of assistant head coach since 2020. If there’s one thing Mike Brown and the Bengals’ front office are known for, it’s loyalty. Simmons has been with the organization for more than two decades, and despite the recent mistakes, it’s hard to imagine him going anywhere. He’ll probably be in Cincinnati until he decides to retire. Tanner Hudson > Erick All Erick All returned to the Bengals after an injury that kept him off the field for much of the last two seasons. Through the first four weeks, Cincinnati made a concerted effort to establish an offense that operated more frequently from under center. Unfortunately, the results were mixed at best. Against Miami, the Bengals moved away from that approach, potentially signaling a shift in offensive philosophy coming out of the bye. If that’s the case, Hudson could see his role expand at All’s expense. That doesn’t necessarily mean Hudson is the better tight end. He’s simply more familiar with the shotgun-heavy offense the Bengals have relied on over the last two seasons, while All spent much of that time recovering from injury. If Cincinnati continues to lean into what Burrow does best, Hudson could find himself playing a much bigger role moving forward. What are some of your Bengals overreactions as the team heads into their bye week? Relevant Song Lyrics? And we’re winning (winning), winning (winning) ugly And we’re winning (winning), winning (winning) ugly And we’re headed for the heartbreak Headed for the blues, yeah

title: Officials miss horrible late hit on Joe Burrow in win vs. Dolphins
summary: Late in the Cincinnati Bengals’ 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was seen throwing his helmet when he came off the field after failing to score a touchdown in the red zone. Some thought the frustration came from failing to finish the drive, but it appears it was more related to officiating. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Late in the Cincinnati Bengals ’ 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was seen throwing his helmet when he came off the field after failing to score a touchdown in the red zone. Some thought the frustration came from failing to finish the drive, but it appears it was more related to officiating. Somehow, the officials missed a blatant roughing the passer call on Burrow’s third-down throw. This is the play that made Joe threw his helmet on the sidelines. That should have been a flag for a late hit so obvious. pic.twitter.com/6eySZ9NWKI — Depressed Cincy Fan (@depressedcincy) October 12, 2026 In the video, you can see two defenders hit Burrow well after he releases the ball. Furthermore, it appears both players land on top of Burrow with their full body weight, something the NFL has tried to take out of the game via roughing the passer penalties. This seems to be a problem Burrow has dealt with for his entire NFL career. We see flags for hits on quarterbacks much less obvious than this every week, but for some reason, Burrow doesn’t seem to get those calls. Burrow was surely frustrated to not get the call, as it would have extended the drive, but you have to wonder if this is also a result of all of the other missed calls that have built up over time. If the NFL really wants to protect quarterbacks, they could start by enforcing the rules when it comes to one of the more popular quarterbacks in the game.
author: Drew Garrison

title: Bengals News: Amarius Mims calls for help with his cleats problem
summary: Cincinnati Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims is playing like arguably the best right tackle in the NFL right now. title: Joe Burrow gives stern warning to Bengals following mistake-filled win vs. Dolphins
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals were able to snap their two-game losing streak on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins by a score of 31-24. It was nice to get back in the win column, but it doesn’t feel like anyone was particularly happy with the Bengals’ performance. Quarterback Joe Burrow didn’t seem especially pleased when speaking to […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals were able to snap their two-game losing streak on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins by a score of 31-24. It was nice to get back in the win column, but it doesn’t feel like anyone was particularly happy with the Bengals’ performance. Quarterback Joe Burrow didn’t seem especially pleased when speaking to the media, offering what could be taken as a warning to the Bengals about playing complete games. Burrow noted red-zone turnovers, personal-foul penalties, and field position as areas where the Bengals fell short on Sunday. Joe Burrow with some stern words toward the team as a whole after a 31–24 went over winless Miami. “We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, gave them points on the board. Yeah, we got to be smarter…. We… pic.twitter.com/ZHX0cP1Z1n — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) October 11, 2026 “We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, gave them points on the board,” Burrow said. Beating the Dolphins, who entered the matchup at 0-4, isn’t anything other than what is expected of a team with Super Bowl aspirations. The game never really felt like it was in danger, but Burrow clearly wanted to put the game away far sooner and in a cleaner fashion. “We had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those fixed if we want to be a great team,” Burrow continued. There are a lot of good things to take away from the Bengals’ first five games of the season, but there are also plenty of things to be concerned about as the team heads into their bye week. As the team looks to get healthy and prepare for the rest of their season, one thing is clear — the franchise quarterback is not happy with their 3-2 record, or how they got there.
author: Drew Garrison

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ bounce back win over the Dolphins
summary: Don’t look at the final score. The Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) were in control against the Miami Dolphins (0-5) from start to finish, despite giving up some garbage time points. Here’s what we learned from the 31-24 win. The running game has hope The loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a heartbreaker in a lot of […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Samaje Perine #34 of the Cincinnati Bengals rushes the ball in the second quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look at the final score. The Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) were in control against the Miami Dolphins (0-5) from start to finish, despite giving up some garbage time points. Here’s what we learned from the 31-24 win. The running game has hope The loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a heartbreaker in a lot of ways, but one of the biggest issues was the complete absence of a running game. Against the Dolphins, though, the Bengals rushed for a season-high 117 yards. A big reason was the performance of Samaje Perine, the ultimate team player, always ready to step in when called upon. Perine got 68 yards on 14 carries and also had a receiving touchdown. What’s really encouraging is that the run game was pretty consistent, as those 117 yards came on 31 carries, with neither Perine nor Chase Brown nor Joe Burrow having a run longer than 11 yards. The Bengals just steadily wore down Miami’s front seven. Jordan Battle has a lot of pride Say what you want about his tackling or revealing Malik Willis’ tells before the game, but Battle backed it up with interceptions on back-to-back drives, the first such performance since Dre Kirkpatrick back in 2014. Battle also had a couple of big open-field stops in the run game. He’s showing what he can do in spurts. Now he just needs to be more consistent. Yes, the run defense against Miami was very bad (allowing 217 yards on 34 carries), but, to be fair, they were playing in brutal weather conditions- the hottest road game in Bengals franchise history. Players were reportedly getting IVs on the sidelines. So there’s hope that Battle and the rest of the run defense will be even better after the bye. Special teams are going to be the focus of the bye This is not acceptable anymore. The muffed punt and roughing-the-punter penalty in Week 3, then a roughing call that turned a Miami field goal into a touchdown on Sunday. Special teams mistakes are really hurting this team. These are simple fixes, so expect Darrin Simmons, the longest-tenured coach on the Bengals, to get his unit in order over the bye week.

title: Bengals kicker Evan McPherson continues to rewrite Bengals franchise history
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ 2020 NFL Draft class may have more notoriety because of Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins being their first two picks of that class, but their 2021 haul can’t be overlooked, either. Sure, they drafted Ja’Marr Chase at No. 6 overall that year, but it’s a 5th-round selection that is also continuing to […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals ’ 2020 NFL Draft class may have more notoriety because of Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins being their first two picks of that class, but their 2021 haul can’t be overlooked, either. Sure, they drafted Ja’Marr Chase at No. 6 overall that year, but it’s a 5th-round selection that is also continuing to rewrite the team’s record books. Kicker Evan McPherson is quietly cementing himself as the best at his position in team history. After going 14-of-14 as a rookie on field goal attempts in the 2021 postseason (an NFL rookie record), McPherson has continued to up his game for the team. Late in the Week 5 contest against the Dolphins, Cincinnati was deep in Miami territory after Jonathan Allen recovered a fumble from Malik Willis. That Bengals’ offensive drive stalled, but with just two minutes remaining, head coach Zac Taylor sent McPherson out for a field goal to ice the game, but more was at stake. McPherson predictably hit the 26-yard field goal, placing him above former Cincinnati kicker Shayne Graham for most consecutive field goals made by a Bengals kicker. His 22 straight, dating back to last season, pushes him ahead of Graham (also his mentor and fellow Florida Gator) for the most in team history. As noted in the tweet above, McPherson was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September after a perfect three games. He has continued that streak in October, despite the team being 1-1, and has been 5-of-5 on 50-plus-yard field-goal attempts. Oddly enough, the record-breaker was a walk in the park compared to what McPherson was asked in prior games. That was his only attempt against the Dolphins (save for extra points), compared with five 50-plus attempts in the first three contests. After a tough 2024 season that ended prematurely with an injury, McPherson quietly put together a great season last year. He continued that progress with an amazing preseason, and has hit kicks from 50, 57, and 58 yards so far this year, while also being perfect on extra points. Understandably, much of both the national and local attention goes to Burrow, Chase, Higgins, and the (somewhat) previously-maligned defense performances. But McPherson is absolutely “feeling it” right now, and is a key to the Bengals’ march to the postseason. Kudos to McPherson, and another tip of the cap to Graham, who was a good kicker for the Bengals for many years.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Jordan Battle backs up talk with two interceptions vs. Malik Willis in Bengals’ win over Dolphins
summary: Jordan Battle had a pretty good idea of what he wanted to accomplish against the Miami Dolphins. By the time halftime rolled around Sunday, the Cincinnati Bengals safety had made his presence felt in a big way. After discussing a potential tell in quarterback Malik Willis’ throwing motion earlier in the week, Battle intercepted the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle (27) celebrates an interception in the second quarter of the NFL Week 5 game between the Miami Dolphins and the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jordan Battle had a pretty good idea of what he wanted to accomplish against the Miami Dolphins. By the time halftime rolled around Sunday, the Cincinnati Bengals safety had made his presence felt in a big way. After discussing a potential tell in quarterback Malik Willis’ throwing motion earlier in the week, Battle intercepted the Miami signal-caller twice in the second quarter of Cincinnati’s 31-24 victory. The back-to-back takeaways helped the Bengals establish control of a game they needed to win after consecutive losses. Battle’s performance was particularly timely. Cincinnati’s defense has faced plenty of scrutiny during the early portion of the 2026 season, and Sunday presented an opportunity to turn preparation into production. Battle did exactly that, putting himself in position to make two enormous plays and helping the Bengals head into their bye week with a winning record. "Very meaningful, especially do it at home." – Jordan Battle Jordan said he grew up a couple blocks from the stadium. Here's Jordan Battle postgame with @FOX19Jeremy after 2 interceptions in the Bengals 31-24 win. @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/s9L66brK27 — Cole McIntire (@ColemcintireTV) October 11, 2026 If you’re wondering, Battle’s reference to “home” in the above tweet is because he is a South Beach native. The veteran safety said he grew up just a few blocks away from Hard Rock Stadium. Battle turns his film study into production The storyline began before the teams ever took the field. Battle revealed during the week that he had noticed a subtle habit in Willis’ throwing motion that Cincinnati might be able to exploit. As reported by the Associated Press, Battle explained his observation this way: “He has a slight little tap before every throw,” Battle said, describing what he had noticed while studying Miami’s quarterback. Battle believed the movement could provide a useful clue for the defense when anticipating Willis’ passes. It was an interesting revelation to make publicly, giving Miami an opportunity to account for the observation before kickoff. Whether that particular tell directly influenced either interception is debatable. What isn’t debatable is that Battle and the Bengals made Willis pay for his mistakes. The first interception came when defensive end Boye Mafe got a hand on Willis’ pass, disrupting its flight and allowing Battle to come away with the football. It was a good example of the secondary benefiting from pressure up front, with Mafe creating the opportunity and Battle finishing the play. The second takeaway was an even bigger statement from the Cincinnati safety. On Miami’s next possession, Willis attempted a throw across his body toward the middle of the field. Battle read the play, broke on the pass, and intercepted it, giving Cincinnati another possession and putting the Bengals in excellent position to extend their lead. Two interceptions on consecutive opponent drives is an impressive feat under any circumstances. Doing it in the first half of a road game, against a quarterback whose tendencies had become a talking point throughout the week, made Battle’s performance that much more noteworthy. A difference-maker in a much-needed victory Battle’s second interception helped set up another Cincinnati touchdown, with Joe Burrow connecting with tight end Tanner Hudson to give the Bengals a 21-7 advantage before halftime. The Bengals ultimately held on for a 31-24 win, improving to 3-2 and putting an end to their two-game skid. Burrow threw four touchdown passes, while the defense generated critical turnovers to keep Miami from taking control of the contest. Battle’s two interceptions were the headline-grabbing plays, but his overall contribution went beyond the box score. The safety also recorded pass breakups, and his ability to recognize what was developing in front of him was a significant part of Cincinnati’s defensive effort. After the game, Battle was quick to give credit to the preparation and execution that made the plays possible. “You study players and see things,” Battle said, “but it’s just trusting the game plan and putting me in position to make plays.” That response is worth noting. Battle had identified something during film study, but recognizing a tendency and actually making a play are two different things. The Bengals still needed pressure, sound coverage, and a safety capable of reacting when the opportunity arrived. On Sunday, Battle delivered. The interceptions also gave the Bengals a timely reminder of what their defense can accomplish when its different levels work together. Mafe’s pressure helped create the first takeaway, while Battle’s instincts and anticipation produced the second. Those are precisely the kinds of complementary plays Cincinnati needs to see more consistently as the season progresses. There is still plenty of football left to play, and one strong performance doesn’t erase every concern about the defense. However, Battle’s afternoon against Miami was an encouraging development for a unit looking for momentum. While Battle’s career has been a bit “feast-or-famine”, he showed up Sunday against Miami. And, as Cincinnati’s defensive line goes (four quarterback hits, three sacks), the secondary feasts. The Bengals will now have their Week 6 bye before returning to action against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7. If Battle can continue turning his preparation into splash plays, while also breeding more consistency, Cincinnati will have another valuable defensive weapon in its effort to climb the AFC standings. For one Sunday in Miami, the safety’s film study paid off big time, and the Bengals walked away with a win they badly needed.

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor knows his team has plenty to clean up
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals may have beaten the Miami Dolphins on Sunday to improve to 3-2 on the season. However, it was far from the best this team has or could have looked so far this year. Head coach Zac Taylor listed the grocery list of self inflicted wounds from Sunday to reporters as he talked […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor looks on during the first quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals may have beaten the Miami Dolphins on Sunday to improve to 3-2 on the season. However, it was far from the best this team has or could have looked so far this year. Head coach Zac Taylor listed the grocery list of self inflicted wounds from Sunday to reporters as he talked about how the team needs to improve: “There’s a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown. Gave them four points. Give up over 200 yards rushing. So, plenty, plenty to clean up. The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We’ve had some down to the wire games last three weeks. I know how hot this one was today. So the bye week comes at a great time for us. To be 3-2, these guys will regroup. We know who we are today. There’s a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks.” This team definitely felt like they needed a bye week in the worst way. The past few weeks have been riddled with these issues, and special teams especially has been atrocious. When you’d be better off if your punt return or field goal blocking unit had just stood around and done nothing, it is a major issue. Yet, that is where the unit is currently at. Who Dey! Bad beat in South Beach: Dolphins’ last-minute touchdown sets up painful bad beat It is truly insane sometimes to look back at the lines that Vegas has made for these games and how close they end up being. The 50-50 ball to Ja’Marr Chase will make most highlight reels, but the other three were either perfectly placed or timed balls that show why Burrow is considered on of the best in the NFL. NFL News Commanders QB Jayden Daniels says team’s botched final play vs. Giants ‘on me’ In one of the more peculiar finishes you will ever see to an NFL game, the Washington Commanders seemed to forget either the game would end in a tie at the end of the overtime period or that they didn’t have a timeout. They were inside the New York Giant’s 30-yard line with 57 seconds. After they ran the ball, they huddled up, walked to the line of scrimmage with no sense of urgency, snapped the ball without enough time to be able to get a spike off if needed and Daniels just ran into defenders. Even after he was tackled with under 10 seconds left, no one really moved with any urgency until time was nearly out. Just baffling that no one seemed to know the situation on the offense. NFL Network: Cardinals to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans Well the mystery is over after head coach DeMeco Ryan revealed at his press conference after the team’s first win of the season on Sunday they traded for Harrison. This reunites CJ Stroud with Harrison who both played at Ohio State University through the 21-22 season. A second round pick next year is also a big price to pay. A fairly big gamble considering both player’s struggles as of recent and Stroud being in a contract year. ‘It’s Even More Disrespectful’ — Ex-NFL LB Reacts to Mike Evans Addressing Viral Exchange With Trevon Diggs During 49ers-Seahawks Evans truly pulled off the coldest trash talk moves of All-Time Sunday when he had to turn Diggs around to read the name on the back of his jersey to tell who he was. It is certainly something we will see repeated going forward, but there is truly no rebuttal for that.

title: Browns HC: Plenty of blame when the offense struggles
summary: The Cleveland Browns had one of their ugliest offensive showings of the season on Sunday against the New York Jets.  How bad was it?  The Browns: In a lot of ways, it was reminiscent of the Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, except that the Jaguars are now 4-1 while the Jets came into […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns had one of their ugliest offensive showings of the season on Sunday against the New York Jets. How bad was it? The Browns: could not sustain drives (a combined 4-of-18 on third/fourth downs and five consecutive possessions between the second and third quarters that ended with a punt); averaged just three yards per play; had their leading rusher (Quinshon Judkins) average just 3.1 yards per carry; and saw quarterback Deshaun Watson complete just 45 percent of his passes, get sacked a career-high eight times, and take numerous hits. In a lot of ways, it was reminiscent of the Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, except that the Jaguars are now 4-1 while the Jets came into the game with just one win and fresh off being slapped around by the Chicago Bears. So what went wrong? Was this the beginning of Watson turning back into the quarterback that filled the Browns with regret from 2022 to 2024? Is Judkins turning into Trent Richardson 2.0? Maybe the offensive line needs to up its game? Should we just blame it on the rain that was falling at MetLife Stadium? Head coach Todd Monken was asked about it during his media availability on Monday , and he essentially channeled the spirit of the wise Lester Freamon from The Wire and pointed out that all the pieces matter: “I think that’s always the case. (The sacks are all) not a Deshaun issue. That’s an athletic quarterback issue and trying to make plays. They’re so used to being able to escape and make plays, and you do see it, you see it weekly. So that is the hardest part: when you’ve got to get the ball out. You’ve got to mitigate the loss, because for every big play that you make, it can’t be offset with a sack, because one’s a drive extender and one’s a drive killer. “We have to do a better job coaching-wise with our protection schemes, our communication up front, and our attention to detail as a group. And then we’ll give ourselves a chance. It’s not all him. There’s a piece of it that is, there’s a piece of it I have to own, and our offensive staff has to own, and there’s a piece that all of our players have to own. That’s part of the pie. The pie that is winning and losing, which is coaching and scheme. (It is there) in terms of attention to detail, in terms of how we do it, how we practice it. “And then the other part of it is the opponent, what impact they have on it. And they’re all a piece of it, and we all own it. Just like we’re going to all own the wins, we’re going to all own this. And that’s part of what we do. And we’re going to come back and fight like hell to fix everything that we know that we’re capable of. Because I’ve seen our best, and our best is good enough. And now we just got to be able to stack plays, starting with us as coaches and then players. That’s just what you do every week.” Sounds like the Browns have a lot to work on this week in practice as they prepare to host the first-place Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. What do you think, Browns fans? Just a bad day from the offense, or is this an omen of what the rest of the season will be like? Have your say in the comments! On Monday, Browns HC Todd Monken noted that Judkins was day-to-day, along with LB Carson Schwesinger, but wouldn’t […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns rushing attack has struggled most of the 2026 NFL season and saw RB Quinshon Judkins depart Week 5 in a walking boot , adding to more concerns heading into Week 6 versus the Baltimore Ravens . On Monday, Browns HC Todd Monken noted that Judkins was day-to-day, along with LB Carson Schwesinger , but wouldn’t rule anyone out for the AFC North showdown in Cleveland on Sunday. So far this season, Judkins has 73 rushing attempts, with Raheim Sanders (9) and Jaleel McLaughlin (2) the only two other running backs to carry the ball for Monken’s crew. The head coach reported that Dylan Sampson could be brought back from injured reserve soon but, according to multiple reports , the Browns are signing RB Audric Estime to their active roster as well: Sources: The #Browns are signing RB Audric Estime off the #Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster. The 23-year-old Estime brings 508 career rushing yards, 130 receiving yards and 3 TDs to Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/cN57eboBz3 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 12, 2026 Estime was a big play back for Notre Dame and was expected to be a Day 2 pick before falling to the Denver Broncos in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL draft. title: Rain game halts Browns momentum, reveals flaws: 4 downs to review Week 5’s loss
summary: It was fun while it lasted. The Cleveland Browns winning streak, that is. In a game in which the Meadowlands was dealing with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, the Browns saw their winning streak come to an end at the hands of the New York Jets. It was a weird game, but it’s the NFL; […]
full_text: It was fun while it lasted. The Cleveland Browns winning streak, that is. In a game in which the Meadowlands was dealing with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, the Browns saw their winning streak come to an end at the hands of the New York Jets . It was a weird game, but it’s the NFL; you’ll have a weird game every now and again. For Cleveland, those weird games usually happen in the Meadowlands. 1st Down: This wasn’t a trap game Let’s get this out of the way. Many fans believed that this game against the Jets was a trap game and it couldn’t be farther from the truth. New York were favored to win this game. The Browns weren’t. Despite what people will say, the Jets aren’t a bad football team. Are they good? Not necessarily, but they are in the same boat that Cleveland is in. The only difference is that the Jets have looked like a poorly coached team more times than not this season. Leading up to Sunday’s game, safety Grant Delpit said this: Full quote from Grant Delpit on if this weekend is a trap game. "Nah, listen, we're not in any position to be calling games trap games. This is the fifth game of the year. So we still got a lot to figure out. As you can see, it's been pretty sloppy for us. So glad that we've… https://t.co/oCtRNPz2DZ pic.twitter.com/aNIu7Yh3EN — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) October 9, 2026 As he said, this is a team that is trying to figure things out, and they haven’t played their best football as of yet. In terms of the game, it was an uneven performance from both teams. Offensively, both units were bad, but the defenses did enough to keep their team in the game. The Jets were finding ways to give the game away, but the Browns failed to capitalize on those mistakes. I don’t believe this game was as winnable as many believed, but that’s fandom in a nutshell. You might believe that this was a trap game, but in reality it wasn’t; it was just a weird game with a result that the fans aren’t going to like. 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the running game, offense I am not at DEFCON 1 with this Browns running game. As stated before the season started, the running game will be a work in progress. It’s week 5, and the running game is still a work in progress. The running back isn’t the problem; the same can be said for the offensive line. What’s the issue behind the running game struggles? The lack of consistent push is making it harder for the running game to materialize. The lack of a blocking tight end is also missed. It’s not hard to find a blocking tight end (TE2 for that reason); you can trade for one or just sign one off the street. Cleveland should consider either at this point. Staying on the offense, the entire unit was bad. From an operational standpoint, quarterback Deshaun Watson was abysmal. Watson did make plays with his legs and had a decent throw here and there, but it’s about finding consistency, which has eluded him. Wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin were barely involved, and the offensive line had their issues. Overall, not a great day offensively. 3rd Down: Team is still searching for a complete game Five games in, the Cleveland Browns have yet to play a complete game in all 3 phases. Defensively, the unit held up their end of the bargain (despite a few missed tackles), but it was the offense and special teams costing the team at the worst possible time. The mistakes were eventually going to catch up to them; it just happened against a team that is in the same situation that they are in (in terms of expectations for the year). The Browns are searching for that consistency that has been eluding them since the start of the season. 4th Down: Team is ahead of schedule; everything is in front as of now Losing stinks, I know. However, it could be a lot worse. Yes, the quarterback play has been inconsistent, and the running game has been nonexistent. Yet, the team is 3-2. It’s hard to win in the NFL week in and week out, and Cleveland is still trying to figure that out. It’s too early to say that this team is a playoff team, but they aren’t as bad as people say they are. The Browns will still be playing for 1st place in the AFC North next Sunday. Next Sunday’s game against the Baltimore Ravens shouldn’t be considered a must-win in any capacity. Controversial to some, but it shouldn’t be. Progress is being made, but the team has to figure out how to play complementary football on a consistent basis. Extra Points Not completely out on wide receiver Isaiah Bond, but we see why his snaps are limited. He didn’t do himself any favors today with his performance. Outside of his speed, his route running isn’t great, and too often he jumps trying to catch the ball when he doesn’t have to. New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick isn’t beating the “dirty player” allegations. Committing two personal fouls on wide receiver KC Concepcion. Whether it was the facemask or the helmet-to-helmet hit that knocked Concepcion out of the game, it is enough evidence to prove it. He might be public enemy #1 in Cleveland after his hit on RB Nick Chubb’s knee a few years ago. Re-shuffling the offensive line will not fix the running game; it just creates more instability and more problems. Didn’t think right tackle Dawand Jones would reach unplayable, but it’s looking that way. The injuries might have something to do with it. 3-2 is better than 0-5. title: Biggest contributors to Browns loss in Week 5 to the Jets
summary: The Cleveland Browns had a chance to improve their record to 4-1 against the New York Jets, but a 17-12 loss dropped them to 3-2. It was an unfortunate loss, as the Jets were one of the more winnable games on their schedule. This loss could come back to haunt them later in the season. Looking at […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns had a chance to improve their record to 4-1 against the New York Jets, but a 17-12 loss dropped them to 3-2. It was an unfortunate loss, as the Jets were one of the more winnable games on their schedule. This loss could come back to haunt them later in the season. Looking at the bigger picture, what aspects of the Browns’ performance contributed most to their loss? Special teams errors were a big factor in this matchup. From mishandled punts to missed extra points, this was a messy game for this group. Field position mattered a lot, and Cleveland giving the Jets good field position certainly contributed to the loss. Offensive inconsistency was the real nail in the coffin in this matchup. It is difficult to win a game when you score only 12 points. Going into this game, it was clear that the Browns wanted to establish the run, but they never really found their footing. Quinshon Judkins , Cleveland’s leading rusher, finished the game with just 44 rushing yards. Given the rainy conditions, there were concerns about the Browns’ ability to catch the ball heading into the game, and they certainly struggled with this at times. Isaiah Bond , in particular, struggled with drops, including a wide-open touchdown pass and another late in the game that bounced off his hands. Small moments like that really add up in a close game. title: Cowboys news: Team adds defensive help to coaching staff
summary: The Dallas Cowboys losing on Thursday night at home to the previously winless Buccaneers was somehow not the most embarrassing thing to happen throughout the NFC East in week five. The Philadelphia Eagles had their own international meltdown involving a late field goal to lose, in London to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Commanders ran the […]
full_text: Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys losing on Thursday night at home to the previously winless Buccaneers was somehow not the most embarrassing thing to happen throughout the NFC East in week five. The Philadelphia Eagles had their own international meltdown involving a late field goal to lose, in London to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Commanders ran the clock out on themselves with a chance to beat the first place New York Giants in overtime. The 2-3 Cowboys are still in the playoff race as a result, but they need to avoid further coaching mistakes like the rest of their rivals. The organization hired Mike Pettine to help first year defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday to help with this. Cowboys add Mike Pettine to defensive coaching staff – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys had visions of Christian Parker working with veteran coach Mike Pettine for some time, and hired the former Packers coach ahead of a primetime game in Green Bay. Mike Pettine has been added as senior defensive assistant — a former defensive coordinator of the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and the Green Bay Packers, and he most recently worked with the Minnesota Vikings to help Brian Flores form one of the more formidable defenses in the league. “Had a chance to work with Pettine for a number of years, along with the Jets, and he’s gonna be here in a role to support everything that [Christian Parker] is leading and guiding, and we are really, really excited,” Schottenheimer said on Monday. “They worked together in Green Bay, and this is actually something the C.P. and I talked about when we first hired him.” What a horrific NFL week 5 for the NFC East – Shane Tayl0r, Inside The Star Kickoff strategy in late-game situations will be a real discussion point between the Cowboys and Eagles, who play each other in Week 7. A 48-yard field goal for Philly gave them a 19-17 lead with eight seconds remaining. However, Jags returner Ameer Abdullah returned the ensuing kickoff 53 yards to set up Cam Little with a 57-yard field goal. So, instead of kicking the ball into the end zone, forcing the Jags to have to run a play on offense with no timeouts, head coach of the Eagles, Nick Sirianni, kept it in play and allowed legit the only thing that could have beat you happen. NFL Week 5 Sunday aftermath: Commanders melt down in tie; Eagles rue costly last-second gaffe – Kevin Patra, NFL.com Nick Sirianni took the blame for the Eagles late loss the same way Brian Schottenheimer did after Thursday night. Sirianni likely had the Week 3 Ravens-Cowboys ending in his brain at the time, wherein Dallas kicked to the end zone, which allowed Baltimore to run a play and get into field goal range in six seconds for a stunning game-winner . The difference here was that Jacksonville didn’t have a timeout. That detail is massive. Without a timeout, even starting at the 35-yard line, Jacksonville would have had to throw at a presumably well-guarded boundary to stop the clock. Not impossible, but harder than the helter-skelter kick returns can create. That Philly allowed a big return that was called back to start the game — and was missing a key special teams player in Jeremiah Trotter Jr. , who earlier was ejected for fighting — should also have played a role in Sirianni’s thinking. After slow growth, Cowboys defense struggles vs lowly Bucs – Dyllan Rivers, Blogging The Boys The way the Cowboys allowed explosive plays against the Bucs in the second half was highly concerning. On the first play of the second half, Bucky Irving broke free on a run that seemed to take an eternity to cross the line of scrimmage, finally taken down by Caleb Downs after a 72-yard scamper. The very next play resulted in a Tampa Bay touchdown. Two plays, 86 yards, seven points. The next drive, coming after a Ryan Flournoy tipped ball interception, blew open on a Tez Johnson 64-yard catch and run. DaRon Bland tripped over his own feet, allowing Johnson to run free deep into Cowboys territory. After three back-to-back run plays, the Buccaneers would go on to score another touchdown. Enough time has passed for us to point out the 3 silver linings from the Dallas Cowboys’ loss to the Bucs in Week 5 – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports CeeDee Lamb was quiet in the Thursday night home game, but it meant George Pickens finally got going. Is Dallas closer to having both receivers go off in the same game? No one should have been overly concerned. This is the way the Cowboys offense will operate as long as it has two elite wide receivers. Still, a strong performance from Pickens is good for everyone in Dallas, and mostly for his confidence. He finished with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. The Cowboys went to him on the slant a lot once again. He probably wants a few of those targets back, but beyond the numbers, Pickens kept showing up when the Cowboys needed him the most.

title: History says this Cowboys team is doomed
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have played five games so far this season and unfortunately won only a pair of them. 40% success is hardly worth bragging about. In more specific terms, a 2-3 record is a tough scene. To be clear, the first five weeks of the season were arguably the most difficult in terms of […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have played five games so far this season and unfortunately won only a pair of them. 40% success is hardly worth bragging about. In more specific terms, a 2-3 record is a tough scene. To be clear, the first five weeks of the season were arguably the most difficult in terms of any five-week stretch. This was the case because of the travel to Brazil, the road game after, and the short week that followed that. This is for context only and in no way to excuse what the Cowboys have done during the span in question. If the Cowboys held four wins through this stretch, they would likely be a playoff team this season. Obviously they came nowhere close to that. More practically speaking, emerging from this stretch 3-2 would be a huge win, again relative to the unique quirks of the schedule. They didn’t even get there. Unfortunately with a 2-3 record at their backs, they are also now facing an uphill battle from a historical perspective. History says this team won’t make the playoffs With five weeks now in the books we can search certain things at Stathead and Pro Football Reference that weren’t as easily accessible before. Their system doesn’t allow for searches that include spans to start a season short of five games. Here is a list of every team in franchise history that has started their season with a 2-3 (or worse) record. This year’s team is number 24 in that capacity. Of the previous 2-3 instances where a Cowboys team was 2-3 or worse through the first five games, they have only made the playoffs twice. If we round up that is 9%. You’ll note that each of those two teams (1996 and 2018) saw the Cowboys reach the postseason as the NFC East winner. Some years it pays to be in a crummy division, and that certainly seems to be the case this year for Dallas. On the heels of what we saw in Week 5, 10 wins probably earns some hats and t-shirts for whoever gets there. Maybe it will be the Cowboys. But this does not bode well! If you look at the list of teams on this list and reference them against what you remember about each of them, you will realize that we are talking about some Cowboys teams that were not very good and who were actually particularly maddening. On the latter note, part of what is frustrating about this is that the Cowboys are here in consecutive seasons (they were actually 2-2-1 last year to be clear) despite an offense that, on paper, is one of the best in franchise history. That they are not able to capitalize on that through over a full season now is an endless mystery. Do you think the Cowboys will be part of the 9% when this season is over? Or will they fall among the rest? Let us know in the comments below.
