title: How does Kenneth Walker’s start compare to the Chiefs’ all-time greats?
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs‘ newest offensive weapon has delivered a remarkable opening month. With 621 yards from scrimmage, six total touchdowns, and an impressive 6.2 yards per carry, Walker has become a driving force behind Kansas City’s undefeated start. A look at the Chiefs’ legendary running backs puts his early success into perspective. It’s a […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ‘ newest offensive weapon has delivered a remarkable opening month. With 621 yards from scrimmage, six total touchdowns, and an impressive 6.2 yards per carry, Walker has become a driving force behind Kansas City’s undefeated start. A look at the Chiefs’ legendary running backs puts his early success into perspective. It’s a conversation that takes us through different eras of Kansas City football, from Christian Okoye and Priest Holmes to Larry Johnson, Jamaal Charles, Kareem Hunt and Isiah Pacheco. While their journeys to becoming featured backs differed, each offers perspective on how impressive Walker’s arrival has been. Different paths to becoming the featured back Not every great Chiefs running back began his career with the same opportunity. Walker arrived in Kansas City with the expectation that he would immediately become the team’s primary rushing option. Kareem Hunt found himself in a similar position as a rookie in 2017 after Spencer Ware suffered a season-ending knee injury. Others had to wait. Larry Johnson spent the early portion of his career playing behind Priest Holmes. Jamaal Charles gradually earned more opportunities before becoming one of the franchise’s most explosive running backs. Isiah Pacheco began his rookie season sharing the backfield before eventually taking over a larger role. Even Christian Okoye’s rise to becoming the centerpiece of Kansas City’s rushing attack took time. How Walker stacks up against Chiefs history How Walker stacks up against Chiefs history Running back Comparison stretch Carries Rush yards Yards per carry Rush TDs Larry Johnson 2005, Weeks 9–12 116 569 4.9 6 Kenneth Walker III 2026, Weeks 1–4 87 537 6.2 4 Kareem Hunt 2017, Weeks 1–4 68 502 7.4 4 Christian Okoye 1989, Weeks 2–5 98 464 4.7 4 Jamaal Charles 2009, Weeks 10–13 67 310 4.6 3 Isiah Pacheco 2022, Weeks 10–13 67 324 4.8 2 Priest Holmes 2001, Weeks 1–4 55 240 4.4 2 These are representative four-game stretches from each player’s emergence as a primary rushing option, rather than a ranking of their first four official starts. The historical periods differ because their opportunities developed differently. The numbers tell an interesting story. Walker has produced the second-most rushing yards among these selected stretches, trailing only Johnson’s remarkable 2005 breakout. But perhaps more impressive is how efficiently Walker has produced those yards. Johnson needed 116 carries to reach 569 yards. Walker has accumulated 537 yards on just 87 attempts, averaging more than a full yard per carry, better than Johnson during that stretch. While Johnson’s production was extraordinary, Walker’s workload and explosive-play ability make his start stand out. Larry Johnson: When opportunity met dominance If one player’s emergence deserves mention alongside Walker’s, it’s Larry Johnson. Johnson spent his early career waiting behind Holmes, one of the most productive offensive players in franchise history. But when Holmes suffered a season-ending injury in 2005, Johnson finally received the opportunity to become Kansas City’s featured running back. What followed was one of the franchise’s most dominant stretches of rushing production. Beginning in Week 9, Johnson rushed for 107 yards against the Oakland Raiders , 132 against the Buffalo Bills , an incredible 211 against the Houston Texans , and another 119 against New England Patriots . That’s 569 yards in four games, and Johnson was only getting started. He eventually finished the season with 1,750 rushing yards and 20 rushing touchdowns despite not becoming the full-time starter until midway through the year. Kareem Hunt: The closest comparison Of all the running backs on this list, Kareem Hunt might be the closest comparison to Walker. Both entered their respective seasons with high expectations, and both delivered immediately. Hunt’s NFL debut against the Patriots in 2017 remains one of the most memorable performances by a Chiefs rookie. He rushed for 148 yards, added 98 receiving yards and scored three touchdowns in Kansas City’s 42-27 victory. Over four games, Hunt rushed for 502 yards on 68 carries, an astonishing 7.4 yards per attempt. He also added 157 receiving yards, for 659 yards from scrimmage. Walker has surpassed Hunt’s early rushing total, but Hunt was more efficient per carry and produced more total yards from scrimmage. The different roads of Charles, Okoye, Holmes and Pacheco Not every Chiefs great announced himself with an explosive opening month. Priest Holmes is perhaps the best example. When Holmes arrived from Baltimore in 2001, the NFL didn’t view him as one of its premier running backs. Through his first four games in Kansas City, Holmes rushed for just 240 yards. But by the end of the season, he had led the NFL with 1,555 rushing yards. And over the next several years, Holmes became one of the most productive all-around running backs in league history. Jamaal Charles followed a different path. His opportunity grew during the 2009 season, and by Week 10 he began to show the explosiveness that would define his career. Charles rushed for 310 yards over the next four games, but his most memorable performance came later that season when he erupted for 259 yards against Denver. Christian Okoye brought an entirely different style to Kansas City’s offense. Nicknamed the “Nigerian Nightmare,” Okoye became known for his physicality and ability to wear down opposing defenses. Early in his league-leading 1989 season, Okoye rushed for 464 yards across Weeks 2 through 5, offering a glimpse of the bruising running style that would help him finish with 1,480 rushing yards. And then there’s Isiah Pacheco. Pacheco didn’t enter the league with the expectations that surrounded Walker, Hunt or some of the franchise’s earlier stars. A seventh-round pick in 2022, Pacheco earned his opportunities through a physical running style and relentless effort. His production during his first extended stretch as Kansas City’s primary rushing option wasn’t nearly as explosive as Walker’s, but he contributed to Kansas City’s championship success, demonstrating that a running back’s impact isn’t always measured by eye-popping statistics. Different players. Different circumstances. Different styles. But each eventually became an important part of the Chiefs’ offensive identity. The bottom line Four games don’t make a legendary career. Holmes, Johnson, Charles and Okoye built their reputations through sustained production. Hunt’s remarkable rookie season demonstrated how quickly a running back can make an impact, while Pacheco showed that championship contributions aren’t always reflected in individual statistics. Walker still has plenty to prove. But there’s something significant about a running back arriving in Kansas City and immediately putting together a four-game stretch that compares favorably with some of the best to ever wear a Chiefs uniform. Through four games, Walker has already established himself as one of the most important additions to Kansas City’s offense. And perhaps the most exciting part for Chiefs fans is that this could be just the beginning. The Chiefs have had great running backs before. What makes Walker’s arrival so exciting is that he isn’t simply reminding fans of those players. He’s starting to write his own story.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Andy Reid says Chiefs left guard Kingsley Suamataia will ‘be back in’
summary: After the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed a change to the team’s offensive lineup: Mike Caliendo started left guard for the entire contest instead of Kingsley Suamataia. Reid said the details behind the decision would stay between him and Suamataia. After the Week 5 […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed a change to the team’s offensive lineup: Mike Caliendo started left guard for the entire contest instead of Kingsley Suamataia. Reid said the details behind the decision would stay between him and Suamataia. After the Week 5 bye, Reid spoke to local media via video call and updated them on Suamataia’s status, who had started every game at left guard since the start of the 2025 season, before the trip to Las Vegas. “Yeah, he’ll be back in,” Reid said to reporters. Will Suamataia return to the lineup with a new teammate aside him? Second-year left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) has missed the entire season recovering from a bulging disc in his lower back. Ahead of Wednesday’s practice, Reid didn’t give much of an update on the preseason starter. “Josh was here all week and doing his rehab and stuff, so we’ll see,” Reid shared. “They’ll be back in tomorrow and have a better idea of what’s going on.” . @ByNateTaylor “I’ll be surprised if Josh Simmons practices next week.” Via @TheFan965 — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) October 6, 2026 For what it’s worth, ESPN’s Nate Taylor shared that he would be surprised if Simmons practices this week when he appeared on “Cody & Gold” on 96.5 The Fan last Tuesday. Rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson has filled in admirably so far this season, so there is a big question to answer once Simmons is healthy: does Benson go to the bench as a sixth-man backup for both the guard and tackle spots — or does he take right tackle Jaylon Moore’s place in the front five? If Benson stays in the starting lineup on the right side, it keeps the interior depth where it is now; Moore practiced at guard during training camp but has exclusively played offensive tackle during his NFL career. If Benson goes to the bench, he could replace Suamataia the next time he mysteriously sits out an entire game. The Chiefs do plenty of self-scouting during the bye week, and the left side of the line is certainly something the team should be thinking hard about as the season moves forward.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs sign wide receiver Justin Watson to practice squad
summary: After the bye week, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid met with local media via video call on Monday. Before taking any questions, he revealed the Chiefs are signing former wide receiver Justin Watson to the practice squad. Reid explained why the team is bringing back Watson, who played in Kansas City from 2022-2024 […]
full_text: (Photo by Mario Hommes/DeFodi Images via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images After the bye week, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid met with local media via video call on Monday. Before taking any questions, he revealed the Chiefs are signing former wide receiver Justin Watson to the practice squad. Reid explained why the team is bringing back Watson, who played in Kansas City from 2022-2024 before signing a free-agent contract with the Houston Texans in 2025. He played two games before suffering a calf/Achilles injury that landed him on the Reserve/Injured list until the season finale; he also appeared on special teams for Houston in the postseason. “He was a good player for us when he was here,” Reid said. “Obviously, he can run, and he’s fast; he has great size. He’s willing to do everything; he knows the offense; he’s a smart kid. To make room for the practice-squad signing, Reid explained that wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) will be placed on the Reserve/Injured list and linebacker Cam Jones will be signed to the active roster. Justin Watson caught 64 passes with the Chiefs 49 1st downs 7 TDs — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) October 9, 2026 During his time with the Chiefs, Watson was a downfield option who seemed to impact the game almost exclusively by hauling in deep passes from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. In his brief stint with Houston, he caught only three passes over three games, but in Kansas City, he caught 64 passes over three years; 49 of them came on throws 10 or more yards downfield, according to Pro Football Focus . “We felt like he could come back in and, as needed, contribute,” Reid said. “Step in and go with just a slight review, he should be fine and good to go.” The 30-year-old Watson is listed at 6 feet 2 inches tall and 215 pounds, “great size,” as Reid put it. Before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him in the fifth round of the 2018 NFL Draft, he ran the 40-yard dash in 4.42 seconds at the University of Penn Pro Day and recorded a vertical leap (40 inches) that would have tied for first among receivers at that year’s NFL Combine. That was over eight years ago, but the team clearly sees value in bringing Watson back into the fold now that Thornton, the team’s primary downfield threat, will likely miss the remainder of the season. “Tyquan was doing a tremendous job,” Reid said. “It was nice to see Xavier get a deep one in the game also; we know he can do all that. Then the other guys will mix in; they all have good speed and ability to get down the field as needed.” Reid was asked directly about whether wide receiver Xavier Worthy’s role could change due to Thornton’s injury. “Xavier actually had a strong game the other day,” Reid began. “He’s going to continue to be a target, for sure. I don’t know how much his role will change. He has a big part of the pass game to start with, so I’m sure that will continue on.” When asked about rookie wideout Cyrus Allen’s spot in the rotation, Reid sounded open to the idea of seeing more from the training camp standout. “I think he would probably work into the mix there a little bit more,” Reid shared. “He’s a good football player; even though he’s young, he has good ability.” Kansas City should absolutely see what players like Allen and second-year wideout Jalen Royals can do with more playing time after the Thornton injury, but don’t be surprised if you see Watson — presumably No. 84 again — streaking downfield on a deep pass from Mahomes soon.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

SlyMutha No. If anything, the Chiefs need to be collecting draft picks next year, not trading them away for more baggage. title: The Chiefs could put a stranglehold on the AFC West over next 3 weeks
summary: After a week off, the Kansas City Chiefs will be at the facility this week, preparing to host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium for a Week 6 divisional matchup. Two weeks after playing the Chargers, the Chiefs will hit the road and play the Denver Broncos. The games will be the team’s third […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a week off, the Kansas City Chiefs will be at the facility this week, preparing to host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium for a Week 6 divisional matchup. Two weeks after playing the Chargers, the Chiefs will hit the road and play the Denver Broncos . The games will be the team’s third and fourth divisional games this season. The 4-0 Chiefs are 2-0 in the division, which has given them an early lead in the AFC West. Division Standings after Week 5 Chiefs (4-0) Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) Broncos (3-2) Chargers (0-5) The Chiefs could put a chokehold on the division race if they come out of the bye week and take care of the lowly Chargers, then find a way to go to Denver and leave with a win in Week 8. Even if the team falls to the Seattle Seahawks on the road in Week 7, wins in Week 6 and Week 8 would strengthen the divisional record and the record against conference opponents, the two tiebreakers for division standings at season’s end. The Chiefs already have four wins against AFC opponents, while the Raiders are 2-2 in those matchups. The Broncos’ only conference loss so far is to Kansas City, but sweeping Denver in the season series would give them the season-end tiebreaker regardless of AFC games. If the Chiefs enter the second half of the regular season with a 4-0 division record and both wins over the Broncos, it gives the team some margin for error as it navigates the rest of the schedule, which features plenty of games against playoff contenders. The two remaining divisional games are the season’s final games: a road trip to Los Angeles, then a home game against the Raiders. If Kansas City wins the rivalry games ahead of them over the next three weeks, neither game may matter for the divisional standings by the time the Chiefs get there.

title: Analyzing the Chiefs’ defensive snap counts through 4 games
summary: Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has described the first quarter of the season, the first four games, as a period to settle into the scheme and learn his personnel. It’s been a strong start to the year, but the young, fresh-faced unit needs to improve moving forward. Schematic changes in Week 6 and […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has described the first quarter of the season, the first four games, as a period to settle into the scheme and learn his personnel. It’s been a strong start to the year, but the young, fresh-faced unit needs to improve moving forward. Schematic changes in Week 6 and beyond could be based on what the group has put on film so far. Don’t be surprised if the rotation gets tweaked immediately after the bye week. So let’s dive into the snap counts, courtesy of Pro Football Focus, to see how the group is shaping up and what it suggests for the rest of the season. The 11 “starters” The top 11 players by defensive snaps through Week 4 Linebacker Nick Bolton (100% of snaps) Safety Alohi Gilman (97%) Cornerback Nohl Williams (93%) Defensive end George Karlaftis (86%) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (84%) Safety Jaden Hicks (80%) Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (77%) Defensive tackle Chris Jones (70%) Cornerback Mansoor Delane (56%) Defensive end R Mason Thomas (53%) Defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah (48%) While Bolton has never left the field, Gilman has been a mainstay in the back end of the Chiefs’ pass defense that has allowed the fifth-lowest passing yards per attempt (6.2) so far this season. He has played free safety on 65% of his snaps, putting Hicks, Conner and Sneed in position to roam the middle of the field and play closer to the line of scrimmage. Safety Chamarri Conner played 75% of the defensive snaps in his only game against the Las Vegas Raiders , indicating he will be part of this top-11 moving forward. Hicks has played well enough to maintain a consistent role in the starting defense, regardless. Chris Jones has been primarily used as a pass rusher, getting after the quarterback on 69% of his snaps this year. He has aligned over or outside the offensive tackle on 56% of his snaps, but has generated pressure on only 8% of his pass-rush snaps, with just two quarterback hits and no sacks. Thomas (68%) and Anudike-Uzomah (64%) have also been tasked with pass rushing on the majority of their snaps. While Thomas has stuck to the edge, Anudike-Uzomah has lined up in the B-gap for 47 snaps. His impact as an interior pass rusher has generated eight pressures over 84 pass-rush snaps (9.5%) and has the third-most quarterback hits (4) on the team. The rotational players 4 players that are just outside of the top-11 for snap counts Defensive tackle Peter Woods (46%) Nose tackle Khyiris Tonga (44%) Cornerback Kristian Fulton (42%) Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (41%) Woods leads the Chiefs in B-gap snaps (95) through four weeks; 75% of his snaps have aligned as the three-technique Jones has excelled at throughout his time in Spagnuolo’s scheme. It speaks to Woods’ impact on early downs, spelling Jones and being a handful for blockers on both run and pass plays. 43% of Woods’ snaps have been to defend the run; he has three Stops (tackles that constitute a failure for the offense), which is one less than Jones and Thomas. Tonga has seen the eighth-most run-defense snaps (66) through four weeks, indicating that he is a regular on neutral downs. When the downs get long and the game situation becomes late in the half or late in the game, he isn’t on the field. That speaks to the team’s success, playing with a lead for the majority of the season. Fulton may not be on the field as much with Delane healthy, but he has an impressive stat line in his rotational role so far: eight targets, four catches, 19 yards, one interception, and a 16.7 passer rating allowed when targeted. 46% of Gillotte’s snaps have come against the run; he has played more run-defense snaps than Anudike-Uzomah and Thomas. Sub-package players 2 players who only see the field for specific roles Linebacker Jack Cochrane (25%) Safety Christian Roland-Wallace (20%) When the Chiefs run base formations, Cochrane has been the third linebacker. It will be interesting to see whether second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa can fill that role in packages moving forward; he has only seen 18 snaps so far this year. When Kansas City plays dime defense, with six defensive backs on the field, Roland-Wallace has appeared as the second slot defender opposite Sneed most of the time. The bottom line Kansas City’s back-end rotation will need to sharpen with Conner’s return; Hicks is making too many downhill plays to keep him off the field, but Conner makes similar plays. It will be interesting to see how the team deploys the two. Woods seems to be properly spelling Jones, so the All-Pro pass rusher needs to take advantage of that and be more disruptive when he is on the field. The Chiefs’ defensive backfield looks strong on the perimeter, but watch for Williams or Delane to play more in the slot at some point this season to maximize the group’s talent.

summary: We know the Kansas City Chiefs won’t be trading for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. now; the Arizona Cardinals struck a deal with the Houston Texans to trade him during his third NFL season. The Chiefs could still be looking to take a big swing at adding to the receiving room with a few weeks […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images We know the Kansas City Chiefs won’t be trading for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. now; the Arizona Cardinals struck a deal with the Houston Texans to trade him during his third NFL season. The Chiefs could still be looking to take a big swing at adding to the receiving room with a few weeks until the trade deadline, but for now, the team will reportedly be exploring a reunion to begin Week 6. A familiar face is visiting Monday: Source | The Kansas City Star Wide receiver Justin Watson will visit the Chiefs on Monday, a source told The Star. Watson, 30, entered the league as a fifth-round pick of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2018 NFL Draft. The 6-foot-2, 215-pound receiver beat the Chiefs in Super Bowl LV along with Tom Brady. Watson signed with the Chiefs in 2022 and stayed with the club through 2024. Over that span, he appeared in 50 regular-season games, compiling 64 receptions for 1,064 yards and seven touchdowns. Las Vegas Raiders need to be thanking the New England Patriots for doing what the Kansas City Chiefs couldn’t | A to Z Sports They needed a butt whooping. The Raiders needed to be humbled. Now, no one is saying they were cocky or showing anything like that. But this is a young team, a lot younger than people realize. And this team is still learning how to win. Learning how to win is more than just starting 3-9. A season is 17 games long, and they got whooped by the team that did that the best in the AFC last season. The Patriots were in the Super Bowl, and they humbled Las Vegas in a great way. 4 Chiefs Questions That Will Define the Rest of the Season | Heavy Sports Who Is Going to Be the Chiefs’ Big-Play WR? Tyquan Thornton being out for most, if not the remainder of the season is a big blow to the Chiefs’ offense. Thornton has been its only legitimate downfield threat that can beat man-to-man coverage, averaging 19.9 yards per catch. The rest of Kansas City’s receiving corps is made up of short-to-intermediate route runners who play better against zone coverage. The only other receiver the Chiefs have who possesses top-end speed is Xavier Worthy. However, Worthy has been inconsistent so far this season, and hasn’t been the deep threat that he was expected to be when he was drafted back in 2024. If nobody can step up, Kansas City may have to acquire someone via trade or free agency. Chiefs Cornerback Nohl Williams Escapes Penalty for Forceful Hit | Athlon Sports The 24-year-old was flagged at the 5:30 mark of the second quarter. Williams was penalized for a forceful, high hit on Nailor, who was assessed for a concussion and had to miss the remainder of the game. The NFL reviewed the incident and decided not to fine Williams. For context, a hit on a defenseless player would have carried a $17,911 fine for a first offense. Alternatively, a fine of $23,882 is issued for impermissible use of the helmet/launching, under the 2026 NFL fine schedule. Chiefs TE Travis Kelce celebrates the Cleveland Guardians ALDS victory | Chiefs Wire Kelce was front and center, cheering on the team he co-owns and grew up supporting, the Cleveland Guardians, in their Game 5 matchup with the Chicago White Sox in the American League Division Series. Cleveland rallied from 0-2 down to win the best-of-five series in front of the home crowd. Around the NFL Nick Sirianni took the blame in London. If blunders continue, will he be held responsible? | The Athletic “I didn’t make the right decision,” Sirianni said, “and I lost us that game.” That decision was allowing the Jaguars to return a kickoff with eight seconds left and no timeouts after the Eagles took a 17-16 lead. You know the rest. It’s a loss that will sting Eagles fans for a long time, including the legions who traveled across the ocean to make North London feel like South Philadelphia. It will sting Sirianni even longer, the 24-hour rule of moving past a game be damned. Broncos beat Chargers in Sean Payton’s return to playcalling | ESPN The numbers weren’t pretty, and there were times the Denver Broncos’ offense was mired in neutral, but coach Sean Payton’s return to playcalling duties ended with a 23-17 win Sunday over the Los Angeles Chargers. “The guys compartmentalize things pretty well,” Payton said. “Honestly, I didn’t have a big kumbaya meeting.” Marvin Harrison Jr. trade: Cardinals send former top-5 pick to Texans for multiple draft choices | CBS Sports The trade was announced during the Cardinals’ game against the Detroit Lions, a game in which Harrison was inactive due to the pending trade. Rumors swirled over the weekend that a trade could be imminent, and now Harrison will get a fresh start after his time with the Cardinals didn’t go as expected. Texans quarterback and Harrison’s former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud was asked about the trade after his game. “You want to know more? I don’t know what more I can tell you,” Stroud said with a smile. “I think he’s a great guy, think he’s a great player, and I’m excited to get him here.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Examining the Chiefs’ short-yardage offense through four weeks Updated with GIFs Converting on fourth and short is about creating a charge at the line and having the ball carrier make a quick decision off it. Penetration from the defensive front ruins looks and can change the game’s outcome. So far, these issues haven’t affected the Chiefs’ win-and-loss record, but they must improve in this area moving forward. The talent and play calls are there; the team must simply execute in these critical moments. title: Chargers Week 5 PFF Grades: Scott Matlock returns with a bang, Akheem Mesidor nearly elite
summary: The Chargers defense was once again, for the fifth consecutive game this season, the better unit compared to the offense. Linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips played his best game as a pro, nearly earning a game grade in the 90.0+ “elite” territory. What happened to the Chargers in the fourth quarter was fairly unbelievable, but you know […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Scott Matlock #44 of the Los Angeles Chargers warms up prior to the game against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers defense was once again, for the fifth consecutive game this season, the better unit compared to the offense. Linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips played his best game as a pro, nearly earning a game grade in the 90.0+ “elite” territory. What happened to the Chargers in the fourth quarter was fairly unbelievable, but you know what may even harder to believe? Fullback Scott Matlock, fresh off of injured reserve, finished with the offense’s highest individual grade. What a world we’re living in. The defense’s best player this week was an undrafted free agent who is just now becoming a starter in year eight while the offense’s best player was a defensive tackle-turned-fullback who was drafted in the sixth round. Wellcome to the Chargers experience in 2026. Alright, let’s take a look at this week’s grades. Offense Best FB Scott Matlock – 77.7 TE Hayden Rucci – 77.1 OT Travis Burke – 73.6 WR Tre’ Harris – 69.8 TE Charlie Kolar – 66.0 Welcome back, Scott Matlock! After returning from IR and making his season debut, Matlock turned in the Chargers’ highest grade on offense. He excelled as when used as an extra pass protector (his 82.5 grade led the team) while also earning a run block grade of 70.2 (5th best). His best play of the day came on Kimani Vidal’s 42-yard touchdown run where Matlock hauled himself down the field to throw a key block alongside receiver Theo Wease. Of the four rookie offensive linemen who started Sunday’s game, Burke performed the best and graded out as the offense’s third best player. He unfortunately allowed a sack and ended with a porous pass block grade (39.7) but was outstanding in the run game (84.2). Harris’ injury hurt the Chargers’ run game after he was forced to exit the game. Before going down, he had the team’s third-best run block grade at 81.6. Worst QB Justin Herbert – 41.8 OG/T Logan Taylor – 44.0 TE Oronde Gadsden II – 44.7 OG Cole Strange – 50.1 C Jake Slaughter – 51.6 Taylor ended up being the worst-graded rookie offensive lineman against the Broncos. It was a shock that the Chargers put Taylor at guard when he had mainly played tackle in the preseason, on top of putting Harkey at riht tackle after he played mainly at guard in the month of August. Either way, it was a rough outing for Taylor who finished with a 31.9 in pass pro. Many of the tight ends were used as extra pass protectors and Gadsden somehow finished with an actual 0.0 in that category. Not a surprise that Herbert was the offense’s worst. His pick was ugly and his production was one of the worst he’s ever had in his career on top of yet another lost fumble. Defense Best LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 89.9 EDGE Akheem Mesidor – 89.6 EDGE Bud Dupree – 85.4 LB Daiyan Henley – 75.4 S Elijah Molden – 69.9 Earlier Monday morning, Phillips had an elite 90.0 game grade. After checking back while typing this up, it changed to an 89.9. I don’t know what the change came from, but Phillips deserved his first elite game at linebacker even in a loss. He had run defense and tackling grades above 80.0 and the team’s second-high coverage grade at 77.3. All while playing the second most snaps among defenders. Mesidor earned the Chargers’ only sack of Bo Nix and later helped force a fumble when he hogtied Nix before Tuli Tuipulotu punched the ball loose. Henley was in his bag as a coverage player, earning the team’s highest mark at 85.1. His 79.4 in tackling was also second best. Worst S Genesis Smith – 35.5 LB Marlowe Wax – 36.5 DT Nick Barrett – 44.8 DT Teair Tart – 47.9 S Tony Jefferson – 49.5 It continues to be an up-and-down rookie season for Smith. Just two games after being the highest-graded player in all of Week Three, Smith ended Sunday’s game with the lowest grade on the entire team. His 36.7 coverage grade was the worst on the defense by a wide margin and he was given fault for allowing Courtland Sutton to go untouched and uncovered for the Broncos’ fourth-quarter touchdown. Jefferson’s 49.5 in coverage was the next worst coverage grade on the team. The roughing the passer penalty called on him (should not have been flagged) also dropped his grade a bit this week. Otherwise, Unc was fairly solid with grades above 63.0 in run defense, tackling, and pass rush.

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Bolts earn ‘C’ grade in loss to Broncos
summary: The Chargers were truly this close to finally earning their first win of the 2026 season and they nearly managed to do it against a divisional opponent. The Chargers held a seven-point lead several minutes into the fourth quarter. Every ounce of momentum they had seemed to get flipped on its head the moment Jim […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Hayden Rucci #40 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates after a receiving touchdown with teammates Charlie Kolar #88 during the third quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers were truly this close to finally earning their first win of the 2026 season and they nearly managed to do it against a divisional opponent. The Chargers held a seven-point lead several minutes into the fourth quarter. Every ounce of momentum they had seemed to get flipped on its head the moment Jim Harbaugh’s fourth-down risk failed, however. With roughly 10 and a half minutes left in regulation, the Chargers’s quarterback sneak attempt was stuff and the Broncos took over at the Chargers 41-yard line. From there, Denver scored 13 unanswered points and basically played the remainder of the game inside Chargers territory. Justin Herbert and the offense turned it over two more times on consecutive drives to help turbo the fourth-quarter collapse. Even with such a cataclysmic ending, the Chargers still came away with an average “C” grade for their performance from CBS Sports’ John Breech. Here’s what he had to say: “ It’s official: The Chargers offense looks broken. You can blame it on Mike McDaniel or you can blame it on the rash of injuries, but whatever the reason, this team just can’t do anything on offense. This week, the Chargers were forced to play without starting left tackle Rashawn Slater, and it showed. Justin Herbert barely had time to breath in this game. Every time he dropped back to pass, the Broncos were on him, which led to five sacks (Herbert only threw for 121 yards). It seems almost impossible to believe that this team made the playoffs last year, because, at the rate things are going, they might be eliminated from the playoff race before we get to December this year. ” Is this the correct grade for the Chargers? Should the fourth-quarter debacle have earned them a worse mark? Let us know below. And now for today’s links. title: Rams’ Alaric Jackson throws punch in postgame altercation
summary: Rams’ left tackle, Alaric Jackson was involved in a postgame incident following the Rams loss to the Bills on Monday Night Football. Jackson was seen jawing with Bradley Chubb, the Bills edge rusher after the game, and the exchange reportedly escalated when the Rams left tackle threw a punch. What began as postgame trash talk […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 2: Alaric Jackson #77 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rams’ left tackle, Alaric Jackson was involved in a postgame incident following the Rams loss to the Bills on Monday Night Football. Jackson was seen jawing with Bradley Chubb, the Bills edge rusher after the game, and the exchange reportedly escalated when the Rams left tackle threw a punch. What began as postgame trash talk quickly became a situation that could have disciplinary consequences for Jackson moving forward. Here is the incident following the game and during ESPN’s Scott Van Pelt postgame segment… Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe — ESPN (@espn) October 13, 2026 Postgame altercations are nothing new in the NFL, where emotions can spill over after four quarters of physical competition. However, throwing a punch is a different story, particularly when it involves a player who is expected to be a key part of the offensive line. Jackson’s confrontation with Chubb puts the Rams left tackle in the spotlight for the wrong reasons. Players are expected to maintain their composure once the final whistle blows. Losing that composure can turn a brief exchange into an expensive mistake and potentially more discipline from the NFL’s league office… Alaric Jackson has already been involved in off the field matters and this could provoke the league office to make an example of a player. A one game suspension could be something the league looks at when considering Jackson’s lack of a clean record… No one feels good following the Rams heartbreaking loss to the Bills. But it will feel worse if LA’s left tackle is inactive next week because of a stupid emotional mistake that he could have kept within his control.

title: Rams should consider these kickers to upgrade over Harrison Mevis
summary: With two missed field goal attempts on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills, Harrison Mevis potentially just played his final game with the Los Angeles Rams. Sean McVay said in his post-game press conference that he would “evaluate everything” in regards to the team’s kicking operation. So let’s do that part for him. If […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA- AUGUST 15: Lenny Krieg #46 of the Atlanta Falcons warms up prior to a NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Tennessee Titans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 15, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images With two missed field goal attempts on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills, Harrison Mevis potentially just played his final game with the Los Angeles Rams . Sean McVay said in his post-game press conference that he would “ evaluate everything ” in regards to the team’s kicking operation. So let’s do that part for him. If the Rams move on from Mevis, what available alternatives exist? Currently on a practice squad The Rams would need to open a space on the 53-man roster in order to poach a player from a practice squad. Street free agents have an advantage because they can move to LA’s practice squad during a trial phase. The NFL allows two practice squad players to be activated on a weekly basis. Each individual player can be elevated for a maximum of three times per season before they must be signed to the 53-man roster. Lenny Kreig, Green Bay Packers Kreig likely doesn’t make sense for the Rams because Green Bay is keeping him as an additional player under the international player developmental exemption. He was born in Berlin, Germany and is transitioning to American football from the sport of soccer. Kreig is 24 years old. Kansei Matsuzawa, Las Vegas Raiders Nicknamed “The Tokyo Toe”, Matsuzawa is also on the Raiders practice squad under an exemption through the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. He’s 27 years old. Matsuzawa played college football at Hawaii. He converted 27 and 29 field goals over the 2025 season and tied an FBS record with 25 consecutive makes to start the season. Similar to Mevis, range is an open question. Matsuzawa’s longest make is from just 52 yards. Charlie Smyth, New Orleans Saints Smyth is also an international player from Northern Ireland, although he boasts the most NFL experience of this group so far. He played the final six games of the 2025 regular season for the Saints and made 12 of 16 field goal attempts with a long of 57. Smyth was perfect on all 13 of his extra point tries. If the Rams are looking for a kicker with more range, Smyth might be their guy. He was 4/6 for New Orleans last year. He made all five of his attempts from within 39 yards. Blake Grupe, New York Jets Grupe has been around the NFL for a while and is still just age 27. He signed with the Saints as an undrafted free agent in 2023 and earned the starting job over Will Lutz—who was traded to the Denver Broncos. He held the job for two-and-a-half years until a late November slump ended his run in New Orleans. The Colts immediately claimed Grupe and he made all 11 of his field goals with the team last season. His career long is 60 yards; however, he’s made just 19 of 27 attempts from beyond 50. Street free agents Tanner Brown Originally signed by the Rams after going undrafted in 2023. He competed with Christopher Dunn in training camp. Effectively both players lost the job as LA signed Brett Maher before the start of the regular season. But Brown has found his footing in the United Football League (UFL). He made 25 of 28 field goals during the 2026 season for the Louisville Kings. He made all three of his attempts from beyond 60 yards, which is a four-point play in the UFL. Younghoe Koo Started the 2025 season with the Falcons before struggling in Week 1. He landed with the Giants and was released in December. Koo spent a portion of offseason team activities with the Jets before being cut in May 2026. He tried out for the Tennessee Titans in August and remains unsigned. It’s uncertain whether Koo would be better than Mevis or simply just different.
author: JB Scott

title: Takeaways from Week 5 Rams-Bills OT thriller
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills delivered a Monday Night Football thriller in Week 5, with overtime deciding a game that exposed both the promise and the problems of Sean McVay’s team. The Rams showed resilience against one of the NFL’s toughest opponents, but costly mistakes and another special teams catastrophe threatened to overshadow […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Ty Johnson #26 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball against the Los Angeles Rams during the second quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills delivered a Monday Night Football thriller in Week 5, with overtime deciding a game that exposed both the promise and the problems of Sean McVay’s team. The Rams showed resilience against one of the NFL’s toughest opponents, but costly mistakes and another special teams catastrophe threatened to overshadow their performance. From clutch plays to missed opportunities, Los Angeles left plenty to evaluate as the season moves forward. Here are four key takeaways from the Rams’ overtime battle with Buffalo. 1st Down: Special Teams Makeover (Once again…) Five games into the 2026 season and the Rams are in the midst of another special teams yearly trainwreck. The Rams started with the game with a special teams blunder, a huge kick return by Buffalo. And the Rams last possession of the night ended with a special teams blunder. The Rams special teams issue has never been solved, it’s been band-aid after band-aid. The result: close loss after close loss. Sean McVay also commented after the loss that “He will evaluate everything moving forward…” Per @NextGenStats : the Rams lost about -110% in win probability across the course of the 2025 season from special teams snaps In 2026, they've already lost -104% in total win probability on special teams — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 13, 2026 *Sidenote: Stay tuned for an article later this week about how the Rams will address this situation with a trade 2nd Down: Tyler Higbee deserves huge apology from TST There have been so many voices over the years that have questioned Tyler Higbee’s play and contracts throughout his tenure as a Ram. The Rams all-time receiving TE leader deserves better. He has been huge for LA this year considering Los Angeles lost Terrance Ferguson to IR (ankle) and Colby Parkinson has seen significant regression from last year. HIGZ, HIGBEAST, BIG-RIG-HIGZ is the type of guy I want on this team and on the field. Period. Tyler Higbee is making big plays today 💪 @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Mm4Z3DNMmd — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 3rd Down: Conversion battle If there is a silver lining to this loss, it should be this. The Rams are winning 3rd downs on offense and defense. The offense was 7 of 14 (50%) on 3rd down and 2 of 2 (100%) on 4th down. On the other side of the football, the Rams defense only allowed 2 of 7 3rd down conversions (28.5%). That is a recipe for being a Super Bowl team. Even though the Rams are not playing at their full potential (and are without key players), they are positioning themselves where they need to be. It will matter come January and February. The graphic below does not include tonight’s game but gives indication of where the Rams are trending… 3rd Down Conversion Rates through Week 4 Offense: #1 SF, …, #32 GB Defense: #1 CHI, …, #32 DET pic.twitter.com/u6ImD7sAny — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 6, 2026 4th Down: Run Defense led to 37 points against Hard to win when you give up 234 yards on the ground; averaging 6.3 yards per play. The Bills kept running down LA’s throat with James Cook and then Josh Allen would scramble up the middle when needed. Los Angeles could not solve it and explains why there is a stark difference from last week’s defensive performance and tonight’s game.

title: Rams Winners & Losers: From special win to more special teams blunders
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had the Buffalo Bills right where they wanted them. Kicker Harrison Mevis lined up for a potential game-winning field goal in overtime from 48 yards out. Greg Rousseau blocked the kick. Josh Allen did the rest to get the Bills the field goal they needed to seal the win. Buffalo finishes […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Harrison Mevis #92 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after missing a field goal against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams had the Buffalo Bills right where they wanted them. Kicker Harrison Mevis lined up for a potential game-winning field goal in overtime from 48 yards out. Greg Rousseau blocked the kick. Josh Allen did the rest to get the Bills the field goal they needed to seal the win. Buffalo finishes on top 37-34 . The Rams fall to 2-3 on the season. LA is third in the NFC West divisional race behind the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers. It’s too early to pay too close attention to the standings. Still, the Rams would feel much better if they were instead moving into a favorable stretch of their schedule with a winning record. How did they get here? Let’s take a look at the individual performances from Monday Night Football. Winners Nate Landman, LB Nate Landman broke out early in his first season in LA. The Rams gave him a contract extension around this time last year. His production fell off a cliff. Perhaps the most important aspect of his production is his ability to create splash plays. Landman punched out two fumbles from James Cook. The first was initially called as recovered by the Rams before being reversed. The second came in overtime and set up LA for a potential game-winning field goal. It’s not sustainable to expect punch outs all the time. Landman needs to be a more consistent defender on a down-to-down basis. However, turnovers can swing outcomes as we saw on Monday night. Landman also has a knack for making important plays at the right time. The veteran linebacker did enough to help the Rams get a win. FUMBLE 🚨Nate Landman punches it out and Aaron Donald recovers! @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oUWPBMxS6h — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Puka Nacua, WR The offense ran through Puka Nacua against the Bills. Matthew Stafford attempted 54 passes. 24, good for 44% of the total, went in Nacua’s direction. He caught 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown. It’s more of a running back statline than you’d normally expect for one of football’s most dangerous receivers. Davante Adams was productive in the red zone with two touchdowns as an honorable mention. Adams still needs to be more productive between the 20 yard lines and co-exist with Nacua as dual focal points in the offense. We saw Adams perform at a high level with Nacua out due to injury. They both rarely fire on all cylinders at the same time. Puka Nacua came into this game at 86th in the NFL in receptions. He is now 7th. — Brett Kollmann (@BrettKollmann) October 13, 2026 Trent McDuffie & Jaylen Watson, CB If you carve out a 57-yard catch by Khalil Shakir in overtime that can be attributed to Quentin Lake, Buffalo receivers finished with just three receptions for 30 yards. The corners were stingy in this game. Allen only completed 12 passes and most went to either running backs or tight ends. While the defensive front continues to be a going concern without Myles Garrett, the revamped secondary is doing their part to make life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Losers Harrison Mevis, K Mevis missed both of his field goal attempts including the aforementioned blocked kick in overtime. While he made all four of his extra points, his shortcomings easily made the difference in the outcome. The Rams do not have much confidence in Mevis outside of 45 yards. Still, for some reason, they opted to play their final offensive ultraconservative and settle for a 48-yard field goal. That is inexplicable. But you have to assume your kicker is capable of knocking in the game-winning kick from inside 50 yards. The fact the Rams obviously do not have a reliable player in this facet is telling. LA should be keeping an eye on the market for an upgrade. Harrison Mevis Gets His Kick Blocked From 48 Yards. More Special Teams Problems Continue For LA. Blocked. 😬 pic.twitter.com/B6hyTOwZVL — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 13, 2026 The rest of special teams LA opened the game by allowing a long kick return to hand Josh Allen the ball in scoring position. The defense fortunately held the Bills to a field goal following a dropped touchdown pass and a sack by Josaiah Stewart. The Bills accumulated 219 kick return yards in this game and averaged 31 yards per run back. The punting game was a nonfactor, which just means the Rams didn’t have much of an opportunity to screw that up too. What a way to start off MNF 🔥 @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SDxP5untYs — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Run defense & contain on Josh Allen It’s not often that a team like the Bills finishes with more rushing than passing yards. James Cook had 111 yards on 25 rushes (4.4 average) with two scores. Allen added 121 yards on 10 rushes of his own with a touchdown. Buffalo finished with 234 yards on the ground compared to Allen’s 210 gross passing. You can live with Cook’s rushing output most days. Allen’s ability to break contain was crippling to the Rams’ defense. Josh Allen cannot be stopped 🏃 @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ha3oxH1VpL — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Quentin Lake, DB Credit to Quentin Lake for battling through an injury to suit up for this game. He was listed as “questionable” on the final injury report for the week. But it’s clear that Lake was not at full force Monday night. He allowed a long reception in overtime with the Bills backed up because of a holding penalty. He also just looked out of sorts for most of the game. Lake has been one of the NFL’s best safeties to start the year. The Rams must hope that he can return to health and his pre-injury level of performance down the stretch. What he showed on tape against the Bills was not good enough.

title: 5 key plays from Rams-Bills classic MNF shootout
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills delivered a Monday Night Football thriller, with Buffalo escaping with a 37-34 victory after a back-and-forth battle that came down to the final moments. The Rams had opportunities to pull out a statement win, but five pivotal plays helped determine the outcome. Both offenses found ways to move […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Harrison Mevis #92 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to a preseason NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills delivered a Monday Night Football thriller, with Buffalo escaping with a 37-34 victory after a back-and-forth battle that came down to the final moments. The Rams had opportunities to pull out a statement win, but five pivotal plays helped determine the outcome. Both offenses found ways to move the football, putting pressure on their opposing defenses to deliver in critical situations. For Los Angeles, the difference came down to… special teams. Surprise, surprise. Buffalo capitalized on two Rams missed field goals, turning key moments into a narrow road victory. From explosive offensive plays to crucial defensive sequences and the decisive finish, these five moments tell the story of how the Bills edged the Rams in a game that kept fans on the edge of their seats until Tyler Bass’s field goal. 1a. Rams miss 2 point conversion The Rams have not converted a 2 point conversion in three years. With a chance to go up 3 instead of 2, the Rams couldn’t even make a play for the endzone on their 2 point conversion as Stafford was sacked. STAFFORD BROUGHT DOWN BY TJ SANDERS 2 POINT TRY IS NO GOOD ❌ #NFL #Bills #BillsMafia #Rams #RamsHouse #BUFvsLAR pic.twitter.com/T0MHG73Js2 — Dom (@ZeroChillSports) October 13, 2026 1b. Bills convert 2 point conversion On the flip, the Bills got the ball back immediately. Went 80 yards on 5 plays. Josh Allen connected with Dalton Kincaid on the Bills 2 point try. With both conversions, it was a net loss of 4 points for the Rams. Bills get the 2-point conversion to extend their lead 👏 @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DciIJE2UI6 — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 2. Stafford-Kyren can’t connect on 1st & 10 from BUF 35 After a James Cook fumble via a Nate Landman punchout, the Rams drove down to the Buffalo 35 yard line. On 1st & 10, the Rams threw the ball but Stafford’s throw was just high and wide of Kyren. Had they connected, there was not a Bills defender within sight and Kyren would have likely walked into the endzone and the Rams wouldn’t be 2-3… For everyone who's saying McVay got conservative — are we just going to pretend Stafford didn't miss Kyren on the motion in the MOF on the Texas route that would've ended that game? They had their shot dialed up, took it, and they missed it. I get they could've kept throwing,… — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) October 13, 2026 3. Harrison Mevis OT field goal blocked You just knew that if the Rams attempted to a kick a field goal to win the game that something bad would likely happen. And it did. Mevis’s 48 yard field goal was blocked by Greg Rousseau and fell at the back of the endzone, shy of the uprights. To be honest, I thought Mevis’s kick looked wide left off his foot… but I may be wrong. Peyton and Eli were calling out the stoppage right before the blocked FG in OT 👀 "There's no timeouts, why's the clocked stopped? … The referees are icing them." pic.twitter.com/EmFgJSFc01 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 13, 2026 4. Josh Allen OT scramble The Rams defense was gashed from the run all night whether it was James Cook up the middle or Josh Allen via the scramble. On 2nd & 7 at their own 41, Josh Allen scrambled up the middle to LA’s 40 yard line. The first down guaranteed that the Rams were unlikely to get the ball back and that Buffalo was primed to set up a game winning field goal. Extending plays with his legs! 👟 Josh Allen totaled 107 scramble yards, 2nd-most in a game in his career and most since his rookie season. He's the only player with multiple games with 100+ scramble yards since 2018. pic.twitter.com/gnG7Iuqu4l — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) October 13, 2026 5. Tyler Bass Game-Winning Field Goal Special teams matter and Tyler Bass made his kick, unlike Harrison Mevis. Joe Brady was so confident and not ready to mess around that he sent Bass out there on 2nd & 10 for a 45 yard field goal. Bass drilled it and knew it after it left his foot. Ball game.

title: Rams-Bills final score: Special teams costs L.A. on Monday night
summary: The Los Angeles Rams (2-3) lost to the Buffalo Bills (4-1) by a final score of 37-34 in Week 5 of the NFL season in overtime. The Rams basically lost because of bad special teams play more than anything else. Yes, the Rams defense faltered later on in the contest against Josh Allen, but they […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Harrison Mevis #92 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after missing a field goal against the Buffalo Bills during overtime of the game at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams (2-3) lost to the Buffalo Bills (4-1) by a final score of 37-34 in Week 5 of the NFL season in overtime. The Rams basically lost because of bad special teams play more than anything else. Yes, the Rams defense faltered later on in the contest against Josh Allen, but they did enough. It was the special teams who truly let the Rams down Monday night as Harrison Mevis both missed a field goal, and had another blocked to functionally end the game in overtime. This was billed as a potential offensive game, but the first half was a defensive style contest as both defenses held Matthew Stafford, Allen and their respective offenses in check. The second-half offered more scoring to go with a plethora of penalties, but more points nonetheless. For the Rams, their offense mostly went by Stafford’s arm as he threw over 380+ yards, while the Bills struggled a bit through the air, they made up for it on the ground with over 200 rushing yards and multiple scores between the Bills combination of running backs and Allen’s legs. It was a battle between both teams with the Rams and Bills combining for 48 points in the third and fourth quarters before taking the game to overtime. The Rams lost in overtime after the blocked Mevis field goal as the Bills hit their own walk-off by Tyler Bass after the blocked kick on L.A. It was perhaps the most deflating loss of the year, and it was another reminder that the Rams haven’t had a consistent special teams’ unit in too long. The first half The special teams was partly a disaster to start the game. A busted coverage on the opening kickoff allowed Ray Davis of the Bills to quickly put Buffalo in scoring position. They’d open up the scoring with a field goal a few plays later. Then on the Rams opening drive, Mevis missed a field goal allowing the Bills to tack on another quick field goal to take a 6-0 lead. 6 points in the first quarter scored by the Bills because of faulty special teams play. In the second quarter, the Rams took a lead with a lengthy drive capped off with Stafford finding Adams for the score. Mevis made the extra point to take a 7-6 lead with about half of the second quarter remaining. The Bills answered with a James Cook rushing score to take a 13-7 lead as L.A.’s defense played its sloppiest drive of the half with missed tackles as a long Ty Johnson catch and run set up the eventual Cook score. The score stayed 13-7 after a Josh Allen interception to almost end the half. Stafford had a chance to hit Nacua for a deep shot before the end of the sec0nd quarter, but they didn’t connect. The second half The Rams came out in the third quarter and took a 14-13 lead after a steady drive by Stafford and a rushing score by Blake Corum. When the Rams forced a Buffalo punt midway through the third quarter, L.A. had the chance to take a more commanding lead. Instead, the Rams punted it back to Buffalo after a three and out, and the Bills were able to score a touchdown to take a 19-14 lead when Allen found Keon Coleman for a passing score. The Bills did miss the extra point. The Rams were able to respond with another long drive and a Stafford throwing score to Nacua. However, L.A. missed the two-point conversion and the score stayed 20-19 in favor of L.A. The Rams tried to make it a 3-point lead, but instead led by one after the failed attempt. The Bills then added another touchdown with an Allen rushing score and a two-point conversion to Dalton Kinkaid to make the score 27-20 in favor of the Bills. The Rams met the moment and tied the game at 27-27 when Stafford found Adams for another score and Mevis hit the extra point. The Bills had the chance to milk the clock, and walk this game off, but the Bills scored to make the game 34-27 with 1:39 remaining. Leaving Stafford and the Rams a chance to tie. The Rams did just that when Stafford and Kyren Williams led the Rams to a 34-34 score after Williams found the endzone on the ground, and with 4-seconds left in the fourth, the game went to overtime. Overtime The Rams forced a fumble as Nate Landman punched the ball away from Cook. The Rams drove down the field for a walk-off field goal, but Mevis’s kick was blocked in yet another mistake by the special teams. Then the Bills marched down the field and won off of Tyler Bass’s leg. And just like that, the Bills won a game that the Rams had. The Final The Rams fought hard and they lost as a team, but they lost because of their special teams. Yes, the defense didn’t do enough to totally contain Allen, but it did enough to win. No, Stafford and the Rams didn’t score on every drive, but they did enough to win. This loss falls on the third unit of the team. That’s on the coaching. That’s on Sean McVay. And expect it to be a hot talking point this week as the Rams fall to 2-3 and look far from the “super team” so many expected going into 2026.

title: NFL analyst: Stafford has been ‘weird’ this season
summary: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is the reigning NFL MVP, but he hasn’t looked quite the same through four games this season, and with a huge matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football coming up tonight, Sean McVay would love for his star passer to snap back into that elite form. The […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is the reigning NFL MVP, but he hasn’t looked quite the same through four games this season, and with a huge matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football coming up tonight, Sean McVay would love for his star passer to snap back into that elite form. The only problem? According to Nate Tice, the quarterback’s season has been too “weird” to expect the same results that Stafford had last year. “Stafford’s been weird to me this year,” Tice said, noting first that he’s already scrambled more times in 2026 than he did in all of 2025, before getting into the meat of his argument: “The Eagles ran just a bunch of cover-2 and cover-6, and it wasn’t like the Rams were like, ‘Here come the digs, here come the in-breakers’ like I’ve seen him do against those coverages before. Everything was outside and vertical. That’s not really how you beat cover-2 […] but now Stafford’s just not really throwing over the middle.” Nate Tice has emerged as one of the biggest names in the modern NFL media space as the host of his podcast, Football 301, along with guest spots on maybe every other football podcast that exists. A former college quarterback and NFL coach, he’s arguably as good as anyone in the business right now at breaking down quarterback play and offensive systems. So, when he says Matthew Stafford has been “weird,” it makes your ears perk up. Stafford has thrown six interceptions and six touchdowns in L.A.’s first four games, including two starts without number one receiver Puka Nacua. His passer rating is down from 109.2 last season to just 80.5 so far this season, a stat that could reflect what Tice is talking about in terms of throwing over the middle of the field. MOF Tice continued the thought with stats backing up Stafford’s more limited attack over the middle of the field. This season, only 6.5% of Stafford’s throws are to the intermediate middle, or 10-22 yards downfield and between the numbers. Tice said that’s one of the lowest marks in the NFL this season, and it pales in comparison to some of his previous rates, like when he threw there upwards of 11.5% of the time last year and around 14% when he arrived in Los Angeles in 2021. What’s more, Stafford isn’t targeting his receivers as often as he typically does. This season, he’s only targeting receivers about 48% of the time, compared to nearly 61.5% of the time last season and about 73% in 2024. To play the fairness game, there are reasons to explain away a lot of these critiques. Nacua has been banged up and it wouldn’t be smart to use an aging Davante Adams on a ton of in-breaking routes all game long. The offensive line hasn’t been perfect by any means (see the chart below) and when you roster as many tight ends as the Rams do, you’re not going to use them the same way you’re using your wide receivers, generally speaking. Pass block grade of offensive linemen in true pass sets only Mahomes/Trevor good What happened to the Broncos' OL?? pic.twitter.com/DQCqy3lTpE — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) October 7, 2026 All of those are fair counters to Tice’s point. But it’s also easy to find the validity in what he’s saying. The Rams want to hunt explosive plays. Sean McVay wants to create as many as he can. One of the best ways to do that is to throw receivers open over the middle and to give them chances to run after the catch. That’s not the only way to generate YAC, but it’s one of the most consistent ways to do it. Thus, if Stafford is throwing to that YAC-heavy area of the field at a starkly lower clip than usual, that’s going to impact the offense and it’s going to hamper Stafford’s production. It’s not time to sound the alarm yet. It’s too early to assume Stafford is washed up or anything like that. But there’s clearly something different about the Rams’ starting quarterback this year, and this could be a reason behind that. Monday night is his next opportunity to prove that he’s still got the same juice that helped him win MVP.

title: Should the Rams have made a bigger push for Mike Evans?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had a hectic offseason by adding Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Myles Garrett and drawing Aaron Donald out of retirement, but now with hindsight, should the Rams have made more of a push for Mike Evans? The 33-year-old receiver is having a resurgent season with the San Francisco 49ers and may have […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams had a hectic offseason by adding Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Myles Garrett and drawing Aaron Donald out of retirement, but now with hindsight, should the Rams have made more of a push for Mike Evans? The 33-year-old receiver is having a resurgent season with the San Francisco 49ers and may have been a more valuable addition than one of L.A.’s other signings. The Rams could’ve avoided Jaylen Watson, added Mike Evans Evans and Watson both signed deals with their new respective NFC West teams before the start of the 2026 season. Watson signed his three-year $51 million deal, and he’s been solid for the Rams, but he missed Week 4, and hasn’t been as dominant for the Rams as Evans has been for the 49ers. Evans signed a three-year $42 million deal , and has looked as great as he ever has with 24 catches, 300+ receiving yards and three touchdowns to go along with 5 wins. He’s been everything the 49ers could’ve hoped for and more. The Rams added Watson, while Evans ended up on the 49ers In defense of the Rams, they already had Puka Nacua and Davante Adams for 2026, and it was their defensive unit that they chose to retool over their offensive one. This made sense given the offense retained the bulk of its stars. But with hindsight, perhaps Sean McVay and Les Snead should’ve considered adding Evans and unleashing what could’ve been a top offense with the depth to handle missing either Nacua or Adams with Evans in the fold. Of course, Adams has been tremendous so far for L.A., but wouldn’t the Rams be better with Evans also in the mix? It’s a fair question. The Rams weren’t wrong adding Watson The Rams weren’t wrong adding Watson. No one should be saying that in the first year of his deal, but one can wonder if Evans would be doing more for the Rams and their ability to win football games than Watson? It’s fair to wonder with the power of hindsight if the Rams let one of the biggest free agent weapons of 2026 go to their division rival. And now it’s fair to wonder if Evans will be helping the 49ers win the NFC West, while the Rams fight for a playoff spot. Of course, in a few weeks we could be saying that Watson was absolutely the right move for L.A. Perhaps Evans never wanted to go to L.A. We’re speculating here. Call it hindsight, call it preference and or perception, but one could argue the Rams should’ve made more a push for Evans over Watson in 2026, whether that’s actually true or not. One could argue the Rams should’ve ignored Donald wanting to come out of retirement, and instead used his guaranteed money to try and lure Evans. It’s all fair speculation. What’s not speculation is the 49ers are 5-0 since signing Evans. The Rams are 2-2 since all their offseason signings. L.A. will look to rise to 3-2 on Monday Football against the Buffalo Bills or fall to 2-3. Evans and the 49ers will be watching.

title: Rams could have a punt return upgrade on the roster already
summary: The Los Angeles Rams continue to have the league’s worst special teams units, an ongoing problem for Sean McVay that dates back years, and one of the glaring issues this season is at punt returner. The Rams waived punt returner Xavier Smith before Week 4 and pivoted to Alex Bachman, but in his first game […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams continue to have the league’s worst special teams units, an ongoing problem for Sean McVay that dates back years, and one of the glaring issues this season is at punt returner. The Rams waived punt returner Xavier Smith before Week 4 and pivoted to Alex Bachman, but in his first game he had four opportunities and gained just 30 yards. Sn even better option would be running back Dean Connors. Signed to the 53-man roster two weeks ago, Connors should immediately take over for Bachman as the punt returner . And they should do so before Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills because the Rams special teams currently ranks 32nd in the NFL in Special Teams DVOA (-14.5%). One bad punt and it’s over https://t.co/u3Q0mS0Gf9 — Dean Connors (@deanconn0rs) August 1, 2022 The Case for Dean Connors Connors could provide a more dynamic option for a Rams team looking to create explosive plays and improve its field-position battle. Punt returning is about much more than simply catching the football and avoiding a turnover. The position requires sound decision-making, reliable hands, quick acceleration, vision, and the ability to turn an ordinary return into a game-changing play. In fact, I think the most important part of a returner’s game is the ability to read blocks, make cuts, and ball security. Connors background as a running back offers that skill and better fits what the Rams need from the position. We all saw his ability to read blocks and make cuts in the preseason. Why not place him back there to field punts? Connors ball security has makes sense considering the Rams have been knocked out of the playoffs (2017 & 2025) because of punt fielding issues. Xavier Smith fumbled the punt, Sean McVay doesn’t like it. Special teams 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/sKZMAbrNXG — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) January 26, 2026 The Case Against Alex Bachman The biggest question to ask here is: Does Bachman possess the ability to change the game with the football in his hands? I think the answer is pretty straightforward: “No.” There is a reason that Bachman has played for 4 separate teams since 2019: New York Giants, Houston Texans, Las Vegas Raiders, and the Los Angeles Rams. His career average for punt returns is 6.3 yards/return. Nothing to write home about. Bachman is also in the middle of his age 30 season. The burst and twitch is far less than a guy like Dean Connors (23). No offense, but Bachman is just not the guy. So, who do you want fielding the Rams punts? Keep with Alex Bachman? Use Dean Connors? Or it is someone else, like an elevation for Brennan Presley? It’s not like it can get any worse than what the Rams have experienced the last 3 years. Connors would be the best choice in Week 5.

title: Geno Smith leads New York Jets to victory with 10-point 4th quarter
summary: Week 5 was a tough one for the Las Vegas Raiders, with a multi-possession loss to the New England Patriots. But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how Sunday fared for Geno Smith, Tyree Wilson and Jakobi Meyers. Geno Smith Score: 17-12 Jets win Stats: 17/30 (56.7%), 182 yards, 1 TD, […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Week 5 was a tough one for the Las Vegas Raiders , with a multi-possession loss to the New England Patriots . But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how Sunday fared for Geno Smith, Tyree Wilson and Jakobi Meyers. Geno Smith Score: 17-12 Jets win Stats: 17/30 (56.7%), 182 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs This game was certainly more of a defensive battle, as neither quarterback eclipsed 200 passing yards and neither team had even reached 300 total yards. However, the Jets did march down the field on their opening drive, where Smith connected with wide receiver Garrett Wilson for a 32-yard touchdown. Then, Smith led a pair of fourth-quarter scoring drives — a field goal and a touchdown that was aided by a turnover — to seal the ‘W’ for New York. So, the quarterback certainly wasn’t perfect; he also was strip-sacked for a turnover, but he was enough to get the job done. That helps set the stage for a revenge game in a couple of weeks. Tyree Wilson Score: 23-13 Saints lose Stats: 3 tackles The New Orleans Saints continue to struggle, dropping their third game in a row and falling to 1-4 on the season. However, Wilson has been getting more playing time and has been decently productive over the last two weeks. He’s logged 44 defensive snaps and recorded nine total tackles and a sack during that timeframe. Not bad for a guy who didn’t see any action in Weeks 2 and 3. Tyree Wilson gets home for the sack 😤 @ATLvsNO on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jXJqUELAwZ — NFL (@NFL) October 6, 2026 Jakobi Meyers Score: 19-17 Jaguars win Stats: 2 catches, 37 yards This was a crazy game where the Jacksonville Jaguars needed some last-second magic to get a win in one of their “home” games across the pond. A massive 53-yard kick return from another former Raider, Ameer Abdullah, set up a game-winning 57-yard field goal to pull off an incredible comeback. Meanwhile, Meyers had a couple of big catches — one for 18 and another for 19 yards — to help the effort. However, he hasn’t been a major factor in Jacksonville’s offense this season. He only has 13 catches for 165 yards and two touchdowns through five games, and has only posted more than 50 yards in a single game once.
