title: Klint Kubiak confirms Kirk Cousins is still Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback despite Fernando Mendoza’s debut
summary: With No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza making his NFL debut during the Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots, questions arose after the game about whether he’d be the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback moving forward. However, head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that there won’t be a change on the depth chart — meaning […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images With No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza making his NFL debut during the Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots , questions arose after the game about whether he’d be the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback moving forward. However, head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that there won’t be a change on the depth chart — meaning Kirk Cousins will remain behind center — during his press conference the day after the game. “That’s why [Fernando is] here; we have a lot of confidence in him,” Kubiak said when asked about how the coaching staff feels about the rookie (h/t Silver & Black Sports Network’s Jesse Merrick ). “Kirk’s the starter. If Fernando’s called upon, he’ll be ready to go just like he was yesterday.” Mendoza didn’t see the field until garbage time, when the Raiders were down 45-17 with about six minutes left in the fourth quarter. He completed six of eight passes for 48 yards and came up one yard short on a fourth-down scramble that led to a change of possession. “[Fernando] was prepared, he played fast, he got through his progressions quickly, he knew his hot issues. It was a solid start for him,” the head coach said, via Merrick . Meanwhile, Cousins was 19-for-28 with 243 yards and a touchdown . His 1,268 passing yards are the seventh-most in the NFL before the Week 5 Monday Night Football matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills. The 38-year-old is also tied for second in touchdown passes with 12. So, a quarterback change never seemed to be imminent. However, the combination of the Raiders dropping back-to-back games, having a stagnant offense in New England and seeing Mendoza get his first regular-season reps led to some intrigue. But Kubiak put a halt to those talks before they ever really took off. Below are a few other highlights from the head coaches’ press conference: Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway, who excited Sunday’s game with an injury, is in concussion protocol (via Merrick ). Some changes to the offensive line could be coming: “We have to look at everything. We have to improve [running the ball]. It’s something I’ve been saying for multiple weeks now that’s not getting done, and so, as a coaching staff, it falls on me. It falls on me to get it fixed.” (via Merrick ). Kubiak also said that the offensive line struggles will open opportunities for others to get playing time (via T he Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) is expected to practice this week after missing the Patriots game (via Warren ). Wide receiver Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is expected to “take another jump” in his second week of practice since getting his window openend to return from IR. “He’s got to compete in practice and show us that he’s ready to go.” (via Warren). Cornerbacks Darien Porter and Hezekiah Masses will continue to compete for the second starting cornerback spot (via Merrick ). Porter began the season as the starter before getting injured and losing the job to Masses, but Masses was benched in favor of Porter on Sunday. On Porter: “He’s a guy that was starting, lost his starting job for a week and is so mentally tough that he came back in and played really good football yesterday. Played very competitive, and that’s not a surprise. That’s the kind of guy that he is. He’s just gonna continue to get better, and him and Zeke will compete for that job.” (via Warren ). Why Dylan Laube got extra reps on offense in New England: “Overall, Dylan’s been a really good protection back for us. That gets you into the game on third down and gets you in the game in passing situations, and he’s been very reliable on special teams. Just overall, a very reliable player that’s an ascending player.” (via Merrick ). Kubiak also said Mike Washington Jr. needs more opportunities, and that starts with him giving them to Washington. On the loss: “I just didn’t have a good plan for our guys. We didn’t execute well. We got behind early, and we weren’t able to get the run game going. There’s just a lot of reasons why that game didn’t work out, and it starts with me.” (via Merrick ).
author: Matt Holder

title: Honeymoon period for Rob Leonard is over after Las Vegas Raiders give up 45 points in loss to New England Patriots
summary: There’s no sugarcoating it: The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t look like they belonged on the same field as the New England Patriots in the 45-17 Week 5 loss. The Raiders had an opportunity to build on the momentum they generated in the first month of the season and show the rest of the league that […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s no sugarcoating it: The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t look like they belonged on the same field as the New England Patriots in the 45-17 Week 5 loss . The Raiders had an opportunity to build on the momentum they generated in the first month of the season and show the rest of the league that the Silver and Black are legitimate playoff contenders. However, the team fell completely flat and was dominated in every way . So, there’s no room for winners in this week’s winners and losers, as Las Vegas hit a collective “look yourself in the mirror” moment on Sunday. LOSER: Rob Leonard Three weeks ago, it looked like Leonard had revolutionized the Raiders defense. The unit was creating turnovers and held its first two opponents to 14 points or less. Then, the New Orleans Saints managed to put up 27 points, but a flurry of fourth-quarter turnovers saved the day. But in the last two weeks, Las Vegas has given up 75 points and 935 yards with no interceptions and only one fumble recovery. While Leonard has a good scheme that can create confusion for opposing offenses, he’s clearly become way too predictable as a play caller. That was evident in New England, where Patriots offensive coordinator (and former Raiders head coach) Josh McDaniels called max protection when he knew a pressure look was coming and gave quarterback Drake Maye ( 26/34 (76.5%), 374 yards, 4 TDs, 0 INTs ) plenty of answers for the Raiders’ coverages. In other words, Leonard got outcoached for at least the second time in as many weeks. The first-year defensive play caller still has time to turn it around. But he needs to get with the analytics department and understand what his tendacies are to break them and get back to keeping offenses on their toes. LOSER: Hezekiah Masses Speaking of the honeymoon period being over, Masses’ three interceptions in Weeks 2 and 3 led to him getting a starting cornerback job over Darien Porter. However, in the last two weeks, the rookie has been targeted nine times and has given up six catches for 102 yards and three touchdowns, according to Pro Football Focus . Only two of those catches and targets came in New England, but 50 yards and a touchdown were the straw that broke the camel’s back, with Masses getting benched for Porter. Meanwhile, Porter was one of the few defenders who had a decent showing against the Pats, giving up a 49-yard catch but coming up with two pass breakups on four targets and a ‘ defensive stop ’ against the run. If Sunday is any indication, the second-year pro likely earned his spot back. LOSER: Quay Walker To be honest, both linebackers could be listed here since Nakobe Dean didn’t play well either. But it seemed pretty clear that McDaniels was looking to go after Walker in the passing game, targeting him five times for five completions and a team-high 66 yards, per PFF . On top of that, the free agent signing posted a season-low 49.1 PFF run defense grade and had a rare missed tackle. Walker has been a good addition for most of the season so far, but Sunday was certainly a performance he’ll want to forget. LOSER: Spencer Burford PFF grades aren’t the be-all and end-all, and they leave plenty of room for ambiguity. But Burford posting a 0.0 in pass protection against the Patriots is alarming. He wasn’t charged with a sack, but five pressures (and plenty of losses outside of those reps) aren’t going to cut it. On top of that, he earned a season-low 32.7 mark in the run game as the Raiders averaged a putrid 2.1 yards per carry . Vegas’ offensive line has been an issue for a few weeks now. Burford may not be the only problem, but it feels like it’s time to try someone else at left guard. For the record, he had a 4.0 pass-blocking grade and six pressures allowed in New Orleans two weeks ago. LOSER: Tyler Linderbaum To be clear, Linderbaum is far from the Silver and Black’s biggest issue in the trenches. However, after making him the highest-paid interior offensive lineman in NFL history by a significant margin this offseason, the organization hasn’t gotten what it bargained for. Through five weeks, the fifth-year pro has a career-low 63.1 PFF grade after steadily sitting in the mid to high 70s during his tenure in Baltimore. The former is 18th among qualifying centers (minimum 156 snaps), and he posted a season-low 50.6 while giving up a sack in pass protection against the Patriots. In fairness to Linderbaum, that was the first sack he’s given up in 2026, and he’s only yielded five pressures on the campaign. However, the Raiders need more than a 64.1 run-blocking grade for the season and a 58.1 on Sunday, given how much he’s getting paid. LOSER: Kolton Miller The running theme of Las Vegas’ season so far is that the last two weeks have felt like a completely different team than the first three games. Miller is part of that, especially in pass protection. He went from surrendering five pressures in the first three games combined to 12 over the last two, including six pressures and two sacks in New England, per PFF . On top of that, the veteran tackle has been in the 50s for his run blocking in back-to-back outings. The 31-year-old has the track record to suggest he can turn it around. However, his age also suggests that it might be time for the organization to think about the long-term plan when it comes to protecting Fernando Mendoza’s blind side. LOSER: Wide Receivers The Raiders are five weeks into the season and still waiting for a wide receiver to establish himself as a reliable contributor. Tre Tucker had a good game against the 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers, but hasn’t been very productive since then. And the latter can be said about nearly every other wideout on the roster. With the Patriots being down four cornerbacks, including Pro Bowler Christian Gonzalez, this was a great opportunity for a receiver to have a big game and take command of the position group moving forward. Instead, it was the Brock Bowers show again, and the offense is still waiting for a second option in the passing game to emerge.
author: Matt Holder

title: Fernando Mendoza gets his feet wet in live action
summary: Fernando Mendoza, the Las Vegas Raiders 2026 #1 overall pick, saw his first live action of the regular season. At the end of a 45-17 blowout to the New England Patriots, Mendoza was brought in to run the no-huddle offense for a series. Watching him come in and go through his progressions, make the correct […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza, the Las Vegas Raiders 2026 #1 overall pick, saw his first live action of the regular season. At the end of a 45-17 blowout to the New England Patriots, Mendoza was brought in to run the no-huddle offense for a series. Watching him come in and go through his progressions, make the correct reads and good throws should remind us of something ‘The Sheriff’ once said. “I learned a lot of good football at the end of bad football games.” – Peyton Manning Fernando Mendoza, smooth operator 👀 Solid debut for the No. 1 pick: 6/8 for 48 yards plus 3 rush yards in a single drive. Spread it around and showed mobility. Looks as advertised, albeit in garbage time. pic.twitter.com/4E4kIghIUE — Nick Walters (@nickwalt) October 11, 2026 Sure, it was garbage time and the Patriots had called off the dogs. However, even when the Patriots dialed it up once Mendoza and the offense ventured into plus territory, he proved up to the task. Mendoza showed some escapability and a willingness to tuck it and run when there wasn’t anything downfield. Every pass delivered had some zip on it and none of the wideouts dropped a pass he threw. His first five passes were all accurate completions to four different receivers. His sixth pass was caught, but Malik Benson couldn’t get his second foot down in bounds. His seventh pass was broken up by Elliott Davison, who sat on the out route and waited for him to throw out when the blitz rushed his throw. It was a good outing for Mendoza. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was quick to tell reporters that it didn’t signify a change in the plans for which quarterback would be starting moving forward. It’s still Kirk Cousins’ job, but an opportunity to get reps for his young signal caller presented itself and he took it. It was a small sample size of things to come, but definitely cause for excitement.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders outclassed, out-performed by Patriots in humbling 45-17 loss
summary: There was no escaping the quick sand on Sunday for the Las Vegas Raiders. That same resolve and resilience the team produced to overcome adversity and surge to a 3-0 start to the 2026 campaign under head coach Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff, was non-existent in Foxborough as the Silver & Black were thoroughly […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was no escaping the quick sand on Sunday for the Las Vegas Raiders. That same resolve and resilience the team produced to overcome adversity and surge to a 3-0 start to the 2026 campaign under head coach Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff, was non-existent in Foxborough as the Silver & Black were thoroughly throttled by the host New England Patriots 45-17 . The glaring absence of complementary football from the Raiders allowed the Patriots to outclass and out-perform the visitors and it was a contest where the offense, defense, and special teams was so out of whack, one had to openly wonder if Las Vegas got off the plane in New England. The lopsided humbling defeat was the first time where Las Vegas coaching staff truly looked neophyte — Kubiak and his chosen defensive coordinator Rob Leonard are rookies in their respective roles — and the seasoned veterans of head coach Mike Vrabel and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels took full advantage. In total, McDaniels — a former Raiders head coach and play caller himself — dialed up an offense that dropped 536 total yards (371 through the air, 165 on the ground) on Leonard’s surprisingly soft defense. Kubiak’s offense couldn’t find that kind of success as Zak Kuhr’s Patriots defense stymied the Raiders to the tune of 306 total yards (268 passing and a meager 38 rushing). The drubbing was so thorough that even sure-handed elite tight end Brock Bowers lost the ball on an impressive punch out by the Patriots defense — adding to the Raiders’ all-game misery. Patriots defense force a fumble ‼️ @LVvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sOVPbkDCQM — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 What truly makes the defeat disheartening for the Raiders: The Patriots were decimated by injury heading into this contest missing key elements on offense, defense, and special teams but didn’t let that hinder them. They showcased determination, resolve, and sense of urgency — all of which Kubiak’s team exhibited to go 3-1 heading into this game. Instead, McDaniels and the Patriots get a measure of revenge for the 20-13 2025 season-opening loss the team suffered at the hands of the Raiders in New England last season. Of course, we know how that went as the trajectory for both teams were polar opposites. After Sunday’s result, the conversation goes from “ What’s wrong with Drake Maye? ” to “What’s wrong with Klint Kubiak and Rob Leonard?” — highlighting how quickly narratives in the NFL can change. There’s plenty of teach tape for the Raiders, however. And once again, Kubiak did well to take ownership of the team’s issues and result against the Patriots. As I noted earlier this past week, accountability is great, but without action to correct the issues is troublesome . Fortunately for Kubiak and Co., they have several opportunities this season to show they are indeed all about that action. And the first is against the incoming Bills next Sunday at home. Credit to New England for showcasing the ugly warts Las Vegas has. It was there for anyone to see. All eyes turn to the Raiders coaching staff and players ensuring that was an anomaly and not habit. That said, we did get to see Las Vegas No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza get snaps at quarterback. Brief as it was, the experience was a good one for the Indiana product. Fernando Mendoza with a strike for a first down pic.twitter.com/I7k1qyrcRj — T.J. Randall (@TJ_Randall12) October 11, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as the Patriots put peddle to the metal and boat raced the visiting Raiders: —New England’s seven explosive plays (for 20 yards or more) against the Las Vegas defense was eye opening as McDaniels dialed up an aggressive attacking scheme, one that they deployed to stun the Buffalo Bills in Week 4. The Patriots opened the game with a 35-yard touchdown reception by DeMario Douglas and then got a 34-yard TD catch from Kyle Williams in the third quarter. —In comparison, Las Vegas generated just three explosive plays — Bowers’ 28-yard catch, Ashton Jeanty’s 31-yard catch-and-run, and Cody White’s 28-yard grab. That 31-yard reception from Jeanty marked the team’s longest play while the 49-yard catch from Williams marked New England’s longest play of the day. —Kubiak’s ground game continues to struggle with a pathetic 38 yards on 18 carries (2.1 yards per carry average) with the longest run being five-yard gains by Dylan Laube, Mike Washington Jr., and Tre Tucker. McDaniels’ run game, in comparison, was a group effort with Rhamondre Stevenson leading the group with 64 yards on 13 carries and Corey Kiner adding 52 yards on six totes. —Turnover prone heading into the matchup, Maye didn’t lose the ball once while dropping dimes all over the field racking up four passing touchdowns and running another one in for five total end zone visits. May was comfortable in the pocket and surgically dissected the Raiders secondary going 26 of 34 for 374 yards and getting sacked just once. That's 4️⃣ total TDs for Drake Maye! @LVvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/deqpkDW3k1 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 —McDaniels offense found the end zone six times — four through the air and twice on the ground — having it’s way with Leonard’s defense that couldn’t pressure May. The result of Maye having seemingly all day to throw was throwing over Raiders defensive backs sprinting to recover. Other than Bowers’ first-quarter touchdown catch, Las Vegas struggled throughout with Laube’s two-yard plunge in the fourth quarter the only other TD. —Cousins finished 19 of 28 for 243 yards and a touchdown. He didn’t throw an interception but was sacked three times and hit quite often. With the game out of hand, he ceded to rookie Fernando Mendoza and the No. 1 pick went six of eight for 48 yards with one carry for three yards. —Bowers paced the Raiders air attack with 110 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions. The de facto WR1 continues to showcase he’s a tight end in name only as he was deployed all over the alignment, even in spots normally reserved for a traditional wide receiver. Jeanty added 50 yards on three catches while White had two grabs for 44 yards. Quotes of Note Raiders' Klint Kubiak addresses media after loss to Patriots https://t.co/SOA5cr4BQV — Las Vegas Review-Journal (@reviewjournal) October 11, 2026 Up Next The Bills are set to visit Allegiant Stadium next Sunday for an AFC afternoon clash in Las Vegas. Buffalo (3-1 overall) is looking to rebound from the Week 4 loss to New England and stay ahead in the AFC East race in their Monday Night matchup with the Los Angeles Rams (2-2). Interestingly enough, tonight’s clash features the two teams the Raiders play the next two weeks. First come the Bills, then a week later, the Rams roll into Allegiant.

The Kansas City Chiefs were on a bye this weekend, but let’s check in on the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers, who played each other on Sunday. Broncos vs. Chargers Score: 23-17 Broncos win DEN Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 16/27 (59.3%), 123 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 4 rushes, 10 yards RB J.K. Dobbins: 18 carries, 68 yards, 1 TD TE Evan Engram: 4 catches, 55 yards S Brandon Jones: 4 tackles, 1 INT, 2 PDs ED Nik Bonitto: 4 tackles, 2 sacks, 3 TFLs LAC Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 14/24 (), 121 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT, 6 rushes, 54 yards RB Kimani Vidal: 8 rushes, 57 yards, 1 TD TE Charlie Kolar: 3 catches, 37 yards DE Ahkeem Mesidor: 8 tackles, 1 sack CB Elijah Molden: 7 tackles The only thing left to say about Los Angeles’ season is that the Chargers continue to Charger. Their roster is already beaten up, and they had a chance to win this game with a 14-point third quarter. That gave the Bolts a lead heading into the final frame, only to see it disappear with a 13-0 fourth quarter from the Broncos. That puts Los Angeles at 0-5, leading to plenty of questions and potentially some major changes, especially with how poorly Herbert has played. Meanwhile, Sean Payton took back Denver’s offensive play-calling duties after letting offensive coordinator Davis Webb have a run at it during the first month of the campaign. However, the results weren’t much different. The Broncos’ offense and Nix didn’t show much until the fourth quarter, when over half of their points came. The defense is still carrying the team, as both of the offense’s touchdowns came from short fields (40- and 41-yard drives) via a fumble recovery and a turnover on downs. title: Miami Dolphins will not bench Malik Willis following off week
summary: The Miami Dolphins will not be playing football this weekend — which if you’ve been watching the last five weeks, may be a good thing. Typically, during a bye week, teams will evaluate what they have at each position and decide if changes need to be made. Despite the cries for Miami to make a […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on before a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins will not be playing football this weekend — which if you’ve been watching the last five weeks, may be a good thing. Typically, during a bye week, teams will evaluate what they have at each position and decide if changes need to be made. Despite the cries for Miami to make a move at the quarterback position from an impatient fanbase, the Dolphins have no plans to bench Malik Willis in favor of backup, Kyle McCord. On Monday, following a 31-24 loss in which in Willis had three turnovers — two interceptions and a fumble lost — Dolphins rookie head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media and was understandably asked about his plans for the team’s starter at the QB position when they return from their break to face the New York Jets in week seven. Are the Dolphins giving any thought to starting Kyle McCord against their division rival when they return to action? Hafley was blunt with his answer. “No.” When asked to elaborate on his thinking, Hafley responded: “We’ve played five games and Malik is our quarterback.” Hafley would continue: “Malik needs to be better, okay? And that’s not the headline. The headline is, we all need to be better. And I mean that. I thought yesterday, for the first time, we ran the ball really well and we moved the ball. We ran for 200 yards against a really good team. But everything in the pass game has to be better. Okay? It’s the receivers. It’s the tight ends. It’s the protection. It all has to tie in. And it all has to be better. And that’s the quarterback. That’s the coaches — the offensive line, the running backs… This is a team game… We will work through that. I have confidence in the coaches. I have confidence in the players that we have. We will work through that and we will get better. It’s five weeks.” It’s clear Miami’s fanbase is frustrated — and considering the quarterback carousel that has been a staple of this team since the great Dan Marino retired over a quarter-century ago, who can blame them? However, Hafley is preaching patience. I agree with that approach. Rome wasn’t built in a day — and neither will a Miami Dolphins championship team be built in a little over a month of playing time.
author: Marek Brave

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week five defeat
summary: The Miami Dolphins dropped another heartbreaker on Sunday — losing to the visiting Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 31-24. The team kept it close for much of the afternoon, but ultimately fell short due to the firepower possessed by Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and company, in addition to their own inability to play a […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins reacts to a first down against the Cincinnati Bengals in the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins dropped another heartbreaker on Sunday — losing to the visiting Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 31-24. The team kept it close for much of the afternoon, but ultimately fell short due to the firepower possessed by Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and company, in addition to their own inability to play a consistent football game from start to finish. It’s been a rough season so far, but if you weren’t expecting this year to be one filled with mistakes and growing pains, that’s probably more on you than it is on the team. 2026 was always about stripping the squad down to the screws and building it back up again while evaluating who can be a building block for a better future. As we do after every game, let’s take a look at whose stock is rising — allowing them to be a part of Miami’s plans moving forward — and whose stock is falling. FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is second-year running back Ollie Gordon II. Gordon was selected in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, but failed to make much of an impact during his rookie season — totaling just 199 yards rushing on 70 attempts (2.8 yards per carry) and three rushing scores. Fast forward to 2026 where Gordon has taken over the starting running back role after an ACL tear to the team’s original starter, De’Von Achane. This season, Gordon has played in just four of five Dolphins games, but he’s already surpassed last year’s rushing yardage total, while equaling his touchdowns scored from last season as well. On Sunday, he had 88 yards rushing on 18 attempts, plus a rushing score. His power-running style punished the Bengals all game long, allowing Miami to keep the score close. Thankfully, Jon-Eric Sullivan didn’t give up on Gordon after his subpar first year in the league… FINS DOWN Speaking of someone fans are ready to give up on already, quarterback Malik Willis is our Fins Down player of the week for his three turnover performance against the Bengals on Sunday. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, effectively coughing-up any chance Miami had of stealing a victory. Willis has had a rough start to his Dolphins tenure. Through five games, Miami’s first-year starter has just 849 yards passing (169.8 yards per game), two passing scores, and four interceptions. He has added 186 yards rushing and two touchdowns with his legs. His poor play is a big reason why the Dolphins have yet to notch a win on the young season. However, despite the desperate cries from frustrated Fins fans, Willis should not be benched in favor of backup, Kyle McCord. In a year where the Dolphins aren’t expected to compete for a championship or even a division crown, they need to get a full evaluation of as many players as possible, including Willis, to determine how they’ll spend their cap space next offseason, as well as their draft picks. Five games is not enough of a sample size to say that Willis cannot be the guy moving forward, even if his play to start the season has been severely lacking. Jon-Eric Sullivan is too smart to give up on a player with Willis’ potential this early.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 5 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Miami Dolphins welcomed Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Chase Brown and company to Hard Rock Stadium for a clash in sunny South Florida on Sunday — with Jeff Hafley’s squad looking for their first win on the season. Unfortunately for Miami, as the dust settled, the Dolphins fell to their opponent once again — dropping […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins passes against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins welcomed Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Chase Brown and company to Hard Rock Stadium for a clash in sunny South Florida on Sunday — with Jeff Hafley’s squad looking for their first win on the season. Unfortunately for Miami, as the dust settled, the Dolphins fell to their opponent once again — dropping their record to a disappointing 0-5 on the season. There were some positives to take away from Sunday’s 31-24 loss, including another encouraging outing from running back Ollie Gordon II. Unfortunately, Miami’s special teams continued to be a problem, and quarterback Malik Willis delivered a performance that made overcoming the team’s other shortcomings nearly impossible. As we do after every game, let’s take a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly from Miami’s week five loss to Cincinnati. GOOD Ollie Gordon II continues to make the most of his opportunity Losing De’Von Achane to a season-ending knee injury was a significant blow to Miami’s offense. Achane was one of the Dolphins’ most explosive playmakers, and replacing that kind of production was never going to be easy. Enter Ollie Gordon II. The second-year running back continued to show that he deserves a significant role in Miami’s offense, finishing Sunday’s contest with 88 rushing yards and a touchdown on 18 carries. Gordon averaged 4.9 yards per attempt and repeatedly gave the Dolphins a reliable option on the ground with his hard running style. Gordon opened the scoring for Miami with a one-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, capping off the team’s opening drive and giving Dolphins fans a reason to believe this offense might finally be finding something to build around. While the Dolphins ultimately came up short, Gordon’s performance was another encouraging sign. He ran with physicality, showed patience by allowing his blocks to develop, and did a good job turning his opportunities into productive gains. Miami needs to find an offensive identity without Achane, and Gordon is making a strong case that the ground game can remain a meaningful part of that identity. Miami’s power-back deserves credit for stepping into a larger role and delivering. Predictably, there are very few bright spots on this winless football team, but Gordon’s continued development is certainly one of them. BAD Miami’s weak special teams unit strikes again While going against Burrow, Chase and and the rest of the Bengals’ offense was always going to be a tough match-up, the Dolphins immediately made things harder for themselves by allowing an 81-yard return on the opening kick. That massive kickoff return set up and easy opening drive for Cincinnati — which ultimately ended in just three plays with a touchdown pass from the opposing quarterback. Miami had barely settled into the game before finding themselves in a hole, and the special teams breakdown immediately put additional pressure on a team that has struggled to play complementary football all season long. A strong special teams unit could be a source of stability for a struggling ball club. Instead, Miami continues to surrender field position and give opponents easy opportunities they should have to work for instead. The problems weren’t limited to the opening kickoff, either. Dolphins’ kicker Riley Patterson also missed an extra point following Kevin Coleman Jr.’s fourth-quarter receiving touchdown. It didn’t matter much in the end since Miami didn’t recover the ensuing onside kick (surprise, surprise), but leaving a point on the field only added to the frustration of the day. The Dolphins have enough problems to address without their special teams unit adding another one to the weekly checklist. UGLY Malik Willis’ three turnovers sink Miami There’s plenty of season left, but Malik Willis’ performances are leaving more to be desired thus far — to put it lightly. His three turnover day on Sunday was the defining story of the Dolphins’ latest defeat. Willis finished with 15 completions on 27 attempts for 136 passing yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble — bringing his Sunday total to three turnovers. His late rushing touchdown provided a little life to his statline, but it couldn’t erase the damage done earlier in the contest. The turnovers were bad enough, but the decision-making and inconsistency surrounding them made matters worse. Miami needs their quarterback to protect the football, make sound decisions, and give the offense a chance to compete. Instead, Willis repeatedly put the Dolphins in difficult situations by going “big-play-hunting” instead of taking what the defense gave him — making an already challenging afternoon even harder. The first half was particularly damaging, as Miami struggled to sustain drives while Cincinnati built a 21-7 lead. The Bengals capitalized on their opportunities, while the Willis-led Dolphins failed to make the plays necessary to keep pace. To be fair, Willis isn’t operating in a perfect situation. His supporting cast is largely inexperienced and they’ve had their own struggles, but a good quarterback lifts his team up when times get tough, and Willis isn’t doing that at the moment. Despite his struggles, the flashes he’s shown, while infrequent, should remind the fanbase that his athleticism can be a mighty weapon — as demonstrated by his 39-yard scramble late in the game. He finished the contest with six carries for 63 rushing yards. However, the turnovers are impossible to ignore. A quarterback can survive an occasional bad throw. He can overcome a stalled drive or a negative play. What he cannot do is consistently hand the opposition extra possessions and expect the rest of the team to compensate. At 0-5, the Dolphins need to determine whether Willis can be a dependable part of their future or whether they need to explore other options. Sunday’s performance did little to inspire confidence, but again, there are plenty of games to go. For the sake of the franchise, let’s hope he turns things around. ___ The Dolphins find themselves sitting at 0-5 heading into a much needed bye week. They have a lot of things to work on in all aspects of the game. Do you think they can come back from their off week with a victory against the New York Jets? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: Vikings Work Out Several Veteran Wide Receivers
summary: On the heels of signing Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad last week, the Minnesota Vikings may be feeling the urge to add even more to their collection of veteran wide receivers, as they brought in a few more for a workout on Monday. The most prominent name to show up in the Twin […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 14: Juju Smith-Schuster #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs lines up before a play during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the heels of signing Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad last week, the Minnesota Vikings may be feeling the urge to add even more to their collection of veteran wide receivers, as they brought in a few more for a workout on Monday. The most prominent name to show up in the Twin Cities for a workout on Monday was Juju Smith-Schuster, and he was joined by D’Wayne Eskridge and Dayton Wade. Smith-Schuster is now in his tenth year in the NFL, having been drafted by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the second round back in 2017. He caught his first career touchdown pass against the Vikings back in Week 2 of that 2017 season, when the Steelers beat the Vikings in Case Keenum’s first start that year. After spending his first five NFL seasons with the Steelers, he moved on to play for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2022, then to the New England Patriots in 2023, then back to Kansas City for the 2024 and 2025 seasons. He had been with the New York Giants, but they released him in August. For his career, he’s caught 481 passes for 5,624 yards and 33 touchdowns. Eskridge was a second-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks in 2021 and hasn’t done a whole lot in the NFL. He’s had two notable stints on injured reserve, one in 2021 for a concussion and one in 2022 for a broken hand. He also served a six-game suspension at the start of the 2023 season for a violation of the league’s personal conduct policy for an incident stemming from a confrontation with the mother of his child. The Seahawks waived him in August of 2024, and he spent parts of the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Miami Dolphins. Wade went undrafted out of Western Kentucky in 2024 and spent parts of the 2024 and 2025 seasons on the Baltimore Ravens’ practice squad. He has not appeared in an NFL game. The Vikings also worked out former North Dakota State quarterback Cam Miller. Miller was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft and was signed off the Raiders’ practice squad by the Miami Dolphins late in the 2025 season. He was waived by the Dolphins this offseason as part of their final cuts. With Max Brosmer being moved to the active roster following the J.J. McCarthy trade, the Vikings might want a quarterback on the practice squad, so having Miller in for a workout makes some sense. The team has also lost a player from the practice squad, as running back Audric Estime was signed away by the Cleveland Browns. Estime had been signed by the team on 30 September but is now headed to the shores of Lake Erie. So, it was a somewhat eventful start to the bye week for our favorite squad. We’ll see what the next couple of weeks hold as the team rests up and (hopefully) gets healthy and prepares for the remainder of the 2026 season.

title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Vikings at Saints
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have moved to 5-0 beating the New Orleans Saints, 23-13. The game wasn’t as close as the score was. The Vikings defense continues to dominate teams. The offense looked as good as it has all year with Kevin O’Connell giving game balls to Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson, and Aaron Jones. Will Reichard […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings scores a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have moved to 5-0 beating the New Orleans Saints, 23-13. The game wasn’t as close as the score was. The Vikings defense continues to dominate teams. The offense looked as good as it has all year with Kevin O’Connell giving game balls to Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson, and Aaron Jones. Will Reichard The team’s MVP continued his perfect season, going 3-for-3 on field goals and 2-for-2 on extra points. Reichard has become much more than just a reliable kicker. He’s a legitimate weapon and a difference-maker. It feels like every time Minnesota crosses midfield, three points are almost automatic. Kyler Murray Murray wasn’t spectacular, but he did enough. With Addison and Darrisaw out and Hockenson going down early, the Vikings didn’t need him to play hero ball. They just needed him to avoid the killer mistake. Aaron Jones Jones did have a costly fumble in the red zone, but it shouldn’t overshadow another outstanding performance. Ever since Jordan Mason went down, Jones has carried a massive workload and continued to deliver. His 113 rushing yards helped control the tempo of the game and kept the Saints defense on the field. Hopefully there is help coming after the upcoming bye. Byron Murphy Jr. Murphy put together one of the best games of his Vikings career. He came away with two interceptions and essentially erased his side of the field, allowing just three yards in coverage. The pressure generated up front certainly helped, but Murphy took advantage of every opportunity that came his way. The Vikings defense continues to overwhelm opponents, and Murphy has developed into one of the biggest reasons why. Brian Flores The Vikings are 5-0 because of Brian Flores’ defense. Every week it’s difficult to single out just one player because everybody seems to be contributing. One week it’s Dallas Turner. The next week it’s Byron Murphy Jr. Then it’s Jalen Redmond, Blake Cashman, or Eric Wilson. Flores has built a defense where all 11 players are flying around and making plays. The Vikings have held opponents under 20 points in every game this season and continue to force turnovers at critical moments. At some point, the credit has to go to the guy putting everyone in position to succeed. Flores continues to dial up pressure, confuse quarterbacks, and make offenses look uncomfortable for four quarters. When it’s impossible to pick just one defensive player, it’s usually a good time to recognize the coach behind it all.

title: Patriots vs. Raiders: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat
summary: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England […]
full_text: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots are back looking like one of the best teams in football, and doing what good teams do: take care of business against inferior opponents. The Las Vegas Raiders, despite entering Week 5 with a 3-1 record, were just that. However, that does not mean the Patriots were not also very good; you don’t win 45-17 by accident. With that said, let’s dive into our weekly breakdown of the good and the not-so-good from the win in Buffalo. The good: Drake Maye and a whole lot else As Pats Pulpit’s own Andrew Guindon so aptly put it, the Patriots’ starting quarterback has found his mojo again . Maye was simply excellent against the Raiders. The third-year passer completing 26 of his 34 attempts for 374 yards and contributing five total touchdowns: he threw four of them and also found the end zone himself on a 3-yard run. A second straight AFC Offensive Player of the Week trophy coming his way looks like a formality at this point. Drake Maye was pretty good today. — Bernd Buchmasser (@berndbuchmasser.bsky.social) 2026-10-11T22:13:41.380Z “I felt like he was in control,” said Mike Vrabel after the game. “Gave him some time, and we always talk about when we have clean pockets and his ability to transfer up into really good pockets that we’re going to gain yards — and being able to recognize man or zone, or where he wants to go with the football, and the timing of it.” For as good as Maye was, he is not the only Patriot deserving of a mention in this category. Wide receivers DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, offensive tackle Caleb Lomu, outside linebacker Elijah Ponder, and cornerback Kindle Vildor were all among the players to rise to the occasion on Sunday and help New England celebrate a decisive victory; the same is true for Dre’Mont Jones, who made one of the biggest plays of the game on an 11-yard tackle for loss. In fact, the entire operation was mostly clean. The offense was efficient outside of Maye’s showing and also managed to overcome setbacks such as losing both left tackle Will Campbell and running back TreVeyon Henderson to injury within a span of only three plays in the second quarter; the defense, meanwhile, put the clamps on the Raiders despite missing four cornerbacks due to injury. Needless to say, there was a lot to feel good about coming out of this game. The bad: TE1 coverage We could mention injuries here, because losing players the caliber of Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson can have a direct impact on winning or losing. That said, injuries are mostly freak accidents and do not reflect upon a team’s abilities. So, what does fall into this category? Honestly, not a lot; the Patriots did play a relatively clean game outside of some hiccups. The most notable of those was the team’s inability to cover Raiders tight end Brock Bowers even though him being the team’s favorite target was no surprise. And yet, he still finished with eight catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots were short-handed in the secondary without Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis, and the former in particular should have helped against Bowers. Nonetheless, the replacement players had their hands full with him. Of course, if this level of performance by one of the best TEs in the NFL is what it takes to land in this here category, it tells you all you need to know about the quality of New England’s performance on Sunday. Bower’s outing ultimately was a blip on the radar. The s—t that gets you beat: Excessive enalties The officials were admittedly quick to toss penalty flags on Sunday, and some of those fell into the ticky-tacky category. That said, the Patriots need to be able to clean up the operation especially when being officiated by a crew setting the tone from the very get-go. Getting flagged 12 times for a loss of 116 yards is typically not a winning recipe, regardless of the refs. It didn’t matter too much versus the Raiders because the rest of the performance was of a high standard, but Mike Vrabel was still clearly unhappy after the game. “The penalties are ridiculous,” he said. “We’ll have to focus on that and figure out things that we can improve on, which there’ll be a lot of.”

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA- AUGUST 15: Dontae Manning #41 of the Atlanta Falcons in coverage during a NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Tennessee Titans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 15, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Las Vegas Raiders visited Gillette Stadium, so did two free agents. The New England Patriots hosted defensive end Diego Paz Gonzalez and defensive back Dontae Manning for workouts on Monday, according to the NFL transaction wire. Gonzalez, 23, checks in as a member of the NFL International Player Pathway. Born in Galicia, Spain, the 6-foot-3, 223-pound edge rusher was named the American Football League Europe’s Most Improved Defensive Player Player of the Year in 2026. From the regular season into the postseason with Germany’s Rhein Fire, he registered 48 tackles, nine sacks, four pass breakups as well as one interception returned for a touchdown. Manning, 25, entered the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons as an undrafted free agent in 2025. The 5-foot-10, 190-pound cornerback out of Oregon cleared waivers following his rookie training camp and signed to the Chicago Bears’ practice squad at its formation. Manning was retained in the NFC North on a futures contract in January before being part of the league’s cutdown in August. His 2026 preseason brought 11 tackles over the course of 121 snaps between defense and special teams. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 3-2 Patriots currently carry one open spot on the 53-man roster and one open spot on the 17-man practice squad. That’s following a series of weekend moves that included the activation of safety Brenden Schooler from the non-football injury list, the promotion of cornerback Kindle Vildor, as well as the placement of fullback Reggie Gilliam and wide receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve. Linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Elliott Davison reverted to the practice squad after serving as standard elevations for the 45-17 rout in Foxborough. The New York Jets head to Gillette Stadium next Sunday. The AFC East kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: K.J. Britt, Elliott Davison revert to Patriots’ practice squad following Week 5
summary: K.J. Britt and Elliott Davison officially reverted to the New England Patriots’ practice squad on Monday after serving as standard elevations against the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker and safety both made their 2026 debuts during the 45-17 rout at Gillette Stadium. Britt, 27, played 14 snaps on special teams and notched his first tackle […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 11: K.J. Britt #35 of the New England Patriots reacts during the fourth quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images K.J. Britt and Elliott Davison officially reverted to the New England Patriots’ practice squad on Monday after serving as standard elevations against the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker and safety both made their 2026 debuts during the 45-17 rout at Gillette Stadium. Britt, 27, played 14 snaps on special teams and notched his first tackle of the regular season on a kickoff return by running back Dylan Laube. The 6-foot, 240-pound linebacker signed in Foxborough as an unrestricted free agent in March. He then joined the practice squad as the calendar turned to September after being released from the initial 53-man roster as a vested veteran. Selected in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL draft at No. 176 overall, Britt stands 77 games and 16 starts into a journey that began with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Auburn product spent last year with the Miami Dolphins and finished atop his previous AFC East club with 76.9 percent of the workload in the kicking game. His career spans 162 tackles, half a sack, four stops for loss and three passes defensed through 994 downs on defense and 1,303 downs on special teams. Davison, 24, dressed for his first NFL game beyond the preseason on Sunday. Having a hand in two tackles and a third-down pass deflection versus quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the final quarter, the sophomore safety handled 10 snaps on defense and 19 snaps on special teams. Joining New England’s practice squad during the initial week of September before being released and re-signed , Davison originally entered the league as an undrafted free agent out of UTSA in 2025. The 6-foot, 190-pound former Roadrunners defensive back spent the entirety of his rookie year on the practice squad of the New Orleans Saints. Retained on a futures contract in January, he made one August start before clearing waivers at the cutdown deadline. Two standard elevations remain for both reversions before 53-man contracts would be required to take the field. For now, head coach Mike Vrabel’s 3-2 team carries an open spot on the practice squad as well as the roster. That’s after the weekend’s transactions saw cornerback Kindle Vildor promoted and safety Brenden Schooler activated, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and wide receiver Mack Hollins landed on injured reserve. The New York Jets visit Gillette Stadium next Sunday. The divisional kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Confident Caleb Lomu ready for starting role after Will Campbell injury
summary: The New England Patriots saw another starter go down during Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Will Campbell, the team’s left tackle, suffered a reported knee sprain when he was rolled up on in the early second quarter. Even though he briefly returned to the sideline after initially departing for the locker room, the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots saw another starter go down during Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders . Will Campbell, the team’s left tackle, suffered a reported knee sprain when he was rolled up on in the early second quarter. Even though he briefly returned to the sideline after initially departing for the locker room, the second-year man was unable to reenter the contest. In his place, Caleb Lomu finished the game as New England’s left tackle — a role he will likely continue playing for however long Campbell is out. For Lomu, it was simply a case of taking his preparation to the game field and head coach Mike Vrabel’s messaging to heart. “Injuries are a part of football, which sucks,” he said after the game. “Praying for everyone who has an injury, especially Will. But whatever happens, ‘You’ve got to prepare like a starter,’ is what Coach Vrabes tells us. It’s completely true. Anything can happen. So, prepare as a starter throughout the week, even if you’re not going to start, because things like this can happen.” Lomu was the Patriots’ first-round draft pick earlier this year, but he entered the season as the team’s No. 3 offensive tackle behind Campbell and right-side starter Morgan Moses. As a result, his opportunities before Week 5 were limited to jumbo tight end work and mop-up duty. Versus the Raiders, however, Lomu played a career-high 49 offensive snaps. Of those, 47 came in place of Campbell at left tackle. For the 21-year-old it was a return to familiar spheres: while primarily trained as a right tackle since arriving in New England, he spent his college career at Utah on the left side. Regardless of assignment, Lomu felt ready to be thrown into the fire. “I was just ready to go,” he said. “Just like I said, prepare like a starter no matter what happens. As soon as it happened, I was ready to go do what I could to help the team win, and that’s what we did.” For Morgan Moses, that confidence is what defines Lomu even at this early stage in his career. “He’s confident,” the team captain said. “That’s the most important thing. You never know when your number’s going to be called, and obviously he’s been able to get some snaps at the big tight end spots. So, he’s been able to get used to the speed from preseason into the regular season. That’s always good. But he works hard. He’s a young rookie that asks a lot of questions in meetings. And he asks like, ‘Hey, how do you see things?’ “When you build that camaraderie off the field to be able to ask questions in meetings with me and Will, it just boosts the morale for everybody. He came in, and obviously, we’ve got to look at the film. There are some things that we all got to correct, but I think he did a hell of a job.” With Campbell’s outlook unclear, Lomu might be in line for his first career start at either of the two tackle spots this week. The Patriots will host the New York Jets in Week 6, a team that registered eight sacks in a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots injury updates: News on Will Campbell, A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson
summary: The New England Patriots added two more key players to their listed of injuries on Sunday. Neither left tackle Will Campbell nor running back TreVeyon Henderson were able to finish the 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave some updates on the two youngsters […]
full_text: The New England Patriots added two more key players to their listed of injuries on Sunday. Neither left tackle Will Campbell nor running back TreVeyon Henderson were able to finish the 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave some updates on the two youngsters as well as veteran wide receiver A.J. Brown. Patriots injury updates: 10/12 RB TreVeyon Henderson: The Patriots running back exited Sunday’s game in the second quarter with an ankle injury, and was initially labeled questionable to return. He never emerged from the locker room, however, and was ultimately ruled out for the remainder of the game. “We’ll evaluate here and see how it looks,” Vrabel said. “Wasn’t able to finish the game and if we see that on Wednesday, he’s going to be limited, then we’ll let you know he’ll be limited. And I know that [Henderson and Campbell] will do everything that they can to get back. But unfortunately, they weren’t able to finish the game. So, I don’t know where their availability will be just less than 24 hours after the game.” WR A.J. Brown: With Week 5 in the books, the door is now open for the veteran wide receiver to return from injured reserve. Brown originally was sent to IR after the Patriots’ Week 1 loss in Seattle due to a high ankle sprain. There has been some recent optimism about his recovery, and Mike Vrabel did not rule out a return this week when asked whether there is a chance he returned to practice on Wednesday. “A chance? Yes, there is.” OT Will Campbell: New England’s starting left tackle left Sunday’s game on the same drive as Henderson, and like his teammate and fellow second-year player was originally announced as questionable before being ruled out. Campbell is reportedly dealing with a knee sprain, the severity of which was determined by an MRI on Monday. His status remains to be determined, but Vrabel appeared to be cautiously optimistic. “We’ll see how the week goes,” he said. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.”

title: Patriots vs. Raiders: Fan observations from Week 5 win
summary: Beatdowns like this one almost make me feel sorry for the opposing team. Almost. The Patriots took the Raiders behind the woodshed yesterday in one of the more statementiest statement wins in a while. You’d have to go all the way back to last Sunday to find another win that shut the folks who wrote […]
full_text: Beatdowns like this one almost make me feel sorry for the opposing team. Almost. The Patriots took the Raiders behind the woodshed yesterday in one of the more statementiest statement wins in a while. You’d have to go all the way back to last Sunday to find another win that shut the folks who wrote this team off up. And while it’s still to early to officially say “we’re back,” things are really starting to come into shape right as the season really starts to gain some steam. I feel like I have opened several Fan Notes with some version of “It was gross and rainy out yesterday, I’m sure glad I was home watching this game on TV.” Which would suck if we weren’t on a pretty solid hot streak of gorgeous Saturdays to precede them. Spending a beautiful autumn Saturday outside doing cool things and then spending a rainy Sunday afternoon watching the Patriots stuff the Raiders in a locker represents an absolutely perfect weekend if I’m being honest. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: October is the best month of the year and it isn’t even close. It’s warm and sunny during the day and then gets crisp and cool at night. The air smells like leaves and chimney smoke. It’s Spooky Season for us horror nerds, with tons of scary movies on all month long. It’s also the best month on the sports calendar; the NFL is in full swing, college football is dominating Saturdays, the baseball playoffs are ramping up, and the NBA and NHL are back. There’s pumpkin everything for those who celebrate. And if there’s a better month for beer, I don’t know what it is. Hoppy IPAs. Nut Brown Ales. Oktoberfests. Marzens. Sipping good bourbon in front of the fire or woodstove. Plus, I can put on extra layers to hide all of the pudge that keeps accumulating in very weird places as I get older. These are my favorite kinds of regular season Patriots games. Sure, they don’t have the staying power of last-minute field goals or Kenbrell Thompkins end-zone catches with three seconds on the clock. But when the game is well in hand by halftime and I spend the second half as relaxed as they come, already soaking in the win, it maximizes the enjoyment and does wonders for the ol’ ticker. Because as far as dominating performances go, this was the most complete Patriots game in recent memory. All three phases looked great. Drake Maye had his best game as a pro. Depth guys all across the roster stepped up to compensate for a wildly depleted starting corps. And even without everyone’s favorite Christian since Marilyn Manson, the secondary had themselves a day. The 45-17 score makes this game seem closer than it actually was and at no point did Vegas look threatening. And this is a Raiders team that started the season 3-0 and took the Chiefs to the wire last week. It just goes to show that the first four weeks of the season don’t make any sense at all and nobody has a damn clue what they’re talking about. There’s no way I can’t start with Drake Maye, who was about as flawless as they get yesterday. I’m trying to think of my favorite throw and I’m having a tough time. The one that keeps popping up is that wheel route to Eli Raridon about halfway through the third quarter. Hit him in stride right between two Raiders DBs. It was his first read and he stared Raridon down the whole time, didn’t even try to disguise the throw. Hit him right on the numbers for 31 yards. The drive would end with Maye’s lone rushing touchdown of the day. Lone rushing touchdown to go with four through the air, to household names like DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams. Mack Hollins has been Maye’s safety blanket through the early part of the season and you wouldn’t even know he was gone. Plus, A.J. Brown is eligible to come back this week. And a lot of Maye’s day starts up front. He only took one sack for three yards and had all day to throw back there. I’m sure that there are plenty of people spin-zoning this Raiders defense as terrible right now. But they came into yesterday’s game ranked 8th against the pass and 11th in points allowed. Their real weakness was supposed to be in the running game. But 539 total yards allowed to go with the six touchdowns they surrendered is more than anyone has put up on them this season. That’s a whooping. Actually, I think the best term here is “whoopin’.” And it’s very important to really emphasize the WH when you say it. I don’t know what they put in the water in and around Gillette Stadium, or how long the Patriots will be able to find the Efton Chisms of the world. Chism seems poised to be the latest in a long, proud lineage of short white receivers that nobody can cover. Maybe that’s why the team signed Kindle Vildor. When he isn’t shutting down receivers and earning game balls from the coach, he’s in the woods behind the practice facilities using the magic he learned in Middle Earth to sprout guys like Chism from the enchanted soil. All Tolkien jokes aside, though, good for Vildor. The Patriots are his sixth team, and he has stepped up in way more ways than representing New England proudly on the all-time name team. I feel like that’s a great transition to start extolling the defense, but I don’t think I’ve done the offense justice yet. Because pretty much everything they tried worked. McDaniels was dialed in on his playcalling, They took advantage of a very fierce and urgent pass rush with delayed draws and misdirections, which forced Vegas to drop more back into coverage. That gave Drake Maye all day to light them up through the air. A classic “If you do this, then I’l just do that. Oh, you’re doing that? Now, I’ll just do this” type of game. If I try and think about Kyle Williams career highlights, I remember that crosser he took to the house against Tampa Bay, and pretty much every other play is more or less identical to yesterday’s touchdown. Quick hitch and go, perfect throw, back shoulder, sideline catch. That’s his route, Maye knows it, and he just places it perfectly every single time. That Maye-to-Williams back shoulder deep ball is very similar to how Joe Flacco earned his contract when he had Torrey Smith. The only small difference is that Maye leads Williams and hits him perfectly in stride, whereas Flacco would wildly underthrow Smith, he’d have to stop mid-route to try and adjust, the DB would crash into him by accident, and he’d draw a DPI flag. Six of one. Speaking of flags… good lord. That’s one real negative from yesterday. Over 100 yards of penalty yards for the Patriots, 20 accepted penalties between the two teams. I legit can’t remember watching a game with more flags. It completely screwed the flow of the game. If there was a decent “flags as laundry” joke, I’d tell it here. But they’re all terrible. Oh what the hell. Here are a few. These refs must run a laundry mat in the offseason with all the clothes they’re throwing around! Jeez, refs, just spring for a washing machine already! There were so many flags thrown yesterday, they may have to change the penalty from “excessive holding” to “excessive flogging!” There was so much laundry on the field, the ref started sorting their flags into lights and darks! The only other real negative from yesterday is how riddled with injury this team is, with Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson now both expected to miss some time. Lomu filled in for Campbell so well that I completely forgot he was even there, but it’s insane how banged up this team is. I really wish “I completely forgot you were even there” worked as a compliment anywhere other than when talking about an offensive lineman. I mean the only real negative play on offense came when a third-string running back coughed the ball up. But the Raiders came away with no points from the turnover and the Patriots scored a touchdown on the next drive to more or less put the game away. And that RB had 52 yards rushing on six carries, good for over an 8 yards per carry average. I could talk about the offense all day. I feel like I haven’t even really done that much of a…

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Raiders
summary: The New England Patriots went into their game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday severely shorthanded and missing starters on both sides of the ball. It wasn’t a problem for them, though, as they cruised to a 45-17 win at Gillette Stadium. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ third win of […]
full_text: The New England Patriots went into their game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday severely shorthanded and missing starters on both sides of the ball. It wasn’t a problem for them, though, as they cruised to a 45-17 win at Gillette Stadium. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ third win of the season. Drake Maye is back The Patriots’ starting quarterback started this season looking bad, but, similar to last year, it seems like the game against the Bills was the start of the turnaround for him. On Sunday against the Raiders, he was impressive, making some gorgeous throws, some excellent off-schedule plays, and, maybe most importantly, great decisions all day long. This is the Drake Maye that we’re used to seeing, if he can play like this moving forward, the Patriots are going to be in just about every game this season. Elijah Ponder is a problem The Patriots found a diamond in the rough when they signed outside linebacker Elijah Ponder as an undrafted free agent out of Cal Poly last year. He’s already up to 4.5 sacks this season, and almost gave his team a field goal on Sunday. when he strip-sacked Kirk Cousins at the end of the first half. He’s been a demon since midway through the season last year, and he’s been consistently getting even better as time went on. If he can continue to grow, the Patriots might have a guy who will be a force for years to come on this defense — and a viable long-term replacement for Harold Landry on the edge. Injury concerns continue As noted above, the Patriots came into Sunday’s game rather short-handed, and they lost some key contributors during the game as well. Will Campbell went down with a knee injury, and is reportedly expected to “miss some time” after suffering a sprain on the same knee he tore his MCL on last season. In addition, TreVeyon Henderson went down with an ankle injury, while Dre’Mont Jones and Cory Durden both were banged up. as well. It remains to be seen how bad these injuries are, but, with the depth already being tested, losing more guys could be a problem for the Patriots moving forward. Rhamondre Stevenson looks great The final stats may not look gaudy — 64 yards and a. touchdown on 13 carries — but Rhamondre Stevenson ran the ball well on Sunday. His wiggle is impressive, and he was able to continuously break the first tackle and pick up extra yards; he forced five missed tackles during Sunday’s game. The Patriots might need to add another back with Henderson going down, but Stevenson being so solid is a great thing for the Patriots. Being able to run the football is key, and having a back that is able to not only run, but also be effective out of the backfield, is huge for their offense. Caleb Lomu impresses The Patriots surprised some people earlier this year when they traded up in the first round to take offensive tackle Caleb Lomu. The Utah product has been a reserve behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses all season, outside of coming in for Moses a few weeks ago against the Jaguars, before being called in after Campbell left with due to the aforementioned knee injury in the second quarter. When he went in, there were natural questions about his ability to hold up, but he played very well when he was in the game. Of course, with offensive line play, to really know how well they played, we have to watch the full film and take a closer look, but, on first watch, it was an impressive performance. That’s good too, because the Patriots are most likely going to have to rely on him to be their starter at left tackle for a bit. Short-handed receiver group gets the job done The Patriots were without A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, but Drake Maye still had one of the best passing days of his career. DeMario Douglas had a great game, finishing with two touchdowns; Efton Chism continued to look like a more than capable contributor; Romeo Doubs didn’t finish a lot of his catches, but he did force a few defensive penalties; Kyle Williams even got in on the action, catching two deep passes, including a 34-yard touchdown. Tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon had solid games as well. So, even with a bunch of guys out, the Patriots were still able to have multiple threats in the passing game. When Brown and Hollins come back, that depth will be a great thing for the Patriots to lean on. Josh McDaniels is cooking For the second week in a row, offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels put together a fantastic game plan that consistently put his players in a position to be successful. He had Drake Maye making plays that were comfortable for him, and you could tell that the team was feeling good about itself including on the Hunter Henry screen and the Efton Chism throw back to TreVeyon Henderson. If McDaniels continues to construct game plans and call them like he did against the Raiders, this offense is going to be in a good position moving forward. Reports of his demise were exaggerated. Penalties keep disrupting proceedings Patriots vs. Raiders featured 20 accepted penalties, and at least a handful of them were questionable at best. This has been a problem around the league, and unacceptable for a multi-billion dollar business. The Raiders game last week is one where it clearly wasn’t a catch, but they didn’t trigger the review quick enough. This week, the Seahawks lost, in part, because the ref marked the ball in the wrong spot when he couldn’t see where Cooper Kupp went out of bounds. I get that it’s a hard job, and that they make a lot of good judgment calls as well, but the refs across the league need to be better. Brock Bowers is incredible, and you just have to tip your hat The Raiders don’t have a ton of talent, but they have the best tight end in the league, and arguably a top-10 pass catcher in the league with Brock Bowers. If I were the Raiders, I would consider throwing to him every play. They didn’t quite do that on Sunday, but Kirk Cousins still targeted him 10 times, and he ended up with eight catches for 110 receiving yards, with a touchdown. He also fumbled once as well, but the verdict is still clear: he is a monster. The Patriots not having Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis made it a lot more difficult to cover him, but they were able to shut down most every other player on the team. Regardless of what the rest of the Raiders offense looks like, having a player of his caliber is a huge boost, especially with a rookie quarterback eventually taking over. A tough defense awaits Next up for the Patriots is another home game, this one against the New York Jets, who are coming off a 17-12 win over the Browns. The Jets terrorized the Browns offense all day, sacking Deshaun Watson eight times, forcing a total of five fumbles, and recovering two of them. The Patriots do have a much better offensive line than the Browns, but the Jets have heavily invested in their defense, including the No. 2 pick in this year’s draft, David Bailey, who had three sacks on Sunday. With Will Campbell likely out for this one, it bears watching if Caleb Lomu is going to make his first career start. Depending on what happens with the Bills on Monday night, the Patriots could be in first place in the division, and you’d hate to see them lose that with a home defeat to the Jets. It doesn’t look like they’re going to be a push over, however, so I’m looking forward to watching this one to see how the Patriots fare. One spot where they should have a clear advantage is coaching, which is important, especially with the amount of players that they have hurt right now.

title: Drake Maye has found his mojo again
summary: After a rough first three games of the 2026 season, in which Drake Maye turned the ball over seven times, the New England Patriots’ quarterback has now delivered back-to-back resurgent performances, resembling the MVP runner-up form he showcased last season. On Sunday, Maye and the Patriots handily defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, 45-17, returning home […]
full_text: After a rough first three games of the 2026 season, in which Drake Maye turned the ball over seven times, the New England Patriots’ quarterback has now delivered back-to-back resurgent performances, resembling the MVP runner-up form he showcased last season. On Sunday, Maye and the Patriots handily defeated the Las Vegas Raiders , 45-17, returning home to Foxboro following a two-game road trip. The third-year signal-caller finished just six yards shy of his career total in passing yards, throwing for 374 yards and four touchdowns while adding a fifth score using his legs. Setting the tone early, New England’s opening drive ended with Maye capitalizing on a Raiders’ busted coverage to find DeMario Douglas wide open for a 35-yard touchdown pass. With stout protection, Maye, standing poised in the pocket, delivered the deep attempt to cap off a five-play, 79-yard scoring drive, giving the Patriots an early 7-0 lead. “I’m going to come in at every game and week and attack it. I’m confident in myself, my abilities and the guys around me — and part of it is the first touchdown to [Douglas],” Maye said. “I had all day back there [in the pocket], and those are things I’m working on, when I have time, just to sit in there and find somebody open.” Through New England’s three initial matchups, the offense managed just two offensive touchdowns. On Sunday, it recorded five completions of 20 yards or more, following three against the Buffalo Bills last week. Maye’s rediscovered poise was a key factor in that downfield production, leading the Patriots to four scoring drives in under three minutes that totaled 24 points. “We need to hit [those plays] when we get the chance to, and we hit most of them today,” Maye said. “We still had some [plays] where we could have had even more explosives. I’m proud of the guys for executing when we got the chance. I thought everybody was making plays.” Opening the second half, Maye found another downfield target from 34 yards out, connecting with second-year receiver Kyle Williams down the left sideline, extending the Patriots’ lead to 28-7. “I felt like [Maye] was in control,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “We always talk about when we have clean pockets and his ability to transfer up into really good pockets [where] we’re going to gain yards. Being able to recognize man or zone [coverage], or where he wants to go with the football, and the timing of it.” Linebacker and defensive captain Robert Spillane credited the offense’s explosive plays for taking some stress off of the defense. In turn, New England’s defensive unit held Las Vegas to 17 points and forced the visiting offense into a third-quarter fumble. That dynamic was absent two weeks ago against the Jacksonville Jaguars. After two first-half turnovers, the Patriots, trailing 14-3, had a chance to make the deficit a one-score game with an Andy Borregales field goal; however, New England’s kicker missed, and after the offense failed to capitalize on the defense’s first-half efforts, the Jaguars scored three consecutive touchdowns in the second half. But the past two weeks have been different, as the Patriots have scored a combined 79 points over that duration. “It’s just fun to see Drake smiling big on the sidelines,” Spillane said. “That confidence is obviously back, and just watching him lead and push the ball down the field was fun.” While Maye reiterated his confidence in himself entering every game to make plays, as he said after the Jacksonville loss, his performance in Buffalo marked a turning point.
