title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly from the Saints loss to the Vikings
summary: The Good: Causing fumbles The only real moments of excitement in this game were two fumbles caused by the Saints in the red zone. Khristian Boyd punched the ball out of Aaron Jones’s hands and it was scooped up by Chase Young and returned 27 yards to set up an eventual touchdown drive. Later in […]
full_text: The Good: Causing fumbles The only real moments of excitement in this game were two fumbles caused by the Saints in the red zone. Khristian Boyd punched the ball out of Aaron Jones’s hands and it was scooped up by Chase Young and returned 27 yards to set up an eventual touchdown drive. Later in the third quarter Pete Werner and Martin Emerson Jr. caused receiver Myles Price to fumble which was returned 87 yards for a game tying touchdown by Jonas Sanker. The Saints would miss the extra point to leave the game tied, but these two forced fumbles and returns by the defense set up every point the Saints would score on Sunday. The Bad: Keeping the QB in the pocket Kyler Murray looked like his old self on Sunday, as the Saints allowed him to scramble around the field with impunity. Murray ran for multiple first downs, many of which on third down, and extended multiple plays leading to completions. Murray ran 10 times for just 51 yards, but it seemed like every time he ran it was impactful, either moving the chains or avoiding pressure and completing a pass. The Saints have struggled with this for a while, and did not make any adjustments during the game to mitigate the impact Murray was able to make with his legs. The Ugly: The offense The Saints offense gained just 142 yards against the Vikings. Minnesota does have the league’s top defense, but still we should have seen more. Tyler Shough had his worst game of the year, throwing for just 96 yards and 2 interceptions. The run game did nothing outside of a few good runs by Kendre Miller in the first quarter, and Chris Olave was held under 50 yards. The Saints offense did not have a play of longer than 20 yards, and every drive aside from the one scoring drive either finished in a 3 and out or a turnover/turnover on downs. The Vikings defense is great, but still it was an ugly game for the offense in a game that they could have won if they were able to put together just two more scoring drives.

title: Game Recap: Saints host Vikings in Week 5 matchup
summary: The New Orleans Saints were hoping to avoid falling to 0-3 at home when the Minnesota Vikings visited the Crescent City on Sunday. Here’s a recap of all the action. First Quarter Minnesota received the opening kickoff, and Kyler Murray got the Vikings offense off to a quick start. He converted all 5 of his […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the Minnesota Vikings during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were hoping to avoid falling to 0-3 at home when the Minnesota Vikings visited the Crescent City on Sunday. Here’s a recap of all the action. First Quarter Minnesota received the opening kickoff, and Kyler Murray got the Vikings offense off to a quick start. He converted all 5 of his throws on the opening drive, including a throw to Tai Felton for 23 yards. But a sack by Carl Granderson and an illegal formation penalty meant the visitors had to settle for a field goal. Will Reichard converted from 40 yards to establish a 3-0 lead. The Saints then went three-and-out, and the Vikings offense returned and continued to move the football. Murray converted a 3rd down near midfield with a 19-yard pass to Justin Jefferson. Aaron Jones proceeded to find some yards on the ground before he fumbled on a 3rd-and-short in the red zone. Chase Young recovered the ball for the black and gold. Shough found Chris Olave for 14 yards as the Saints offense found its first first down of the game. Second Quarter CJ Donaldson and Alvin Kamara split carries as the hosts drove down the field, and Shough converted a pair of fourth downs with short throws to Olave and Devaughn Vele. It was then Kendre Miller getting inside the red zone with a number of runs, before also running in a 2-yard touchdown for a 7-3 Saints lead. Both teams proceeded to go three-and-out twice, and the Vikings got the ball back with just under two minutes to go. Three completions for 41 yards by Murray helped Minnesota into field goal range before halftime, and Reichard converted again from 54 yards. Third Quarter Leading 7-6, the Saints received the second-half kickoff. But Jayden Price fumbled the ball on the return, and Minnesota took over with a short field. Murray took advantage, taking off for an 18-yard scramble shortly before throwing a 15-yard touchdown to Justin Jefferson to give the visitors a 13-7 lead. Shough returned and got the ensuing Saints drive off to a promising start, but he was then picked off at midfield by Byron Murphy. Minnesota looked poised to score with another short field position as Murray ran into the red zone with a 14-yard scramble. However, Myles Price fumbled after a catch, and Jonas Sanker returned it 87 yards to the house for the black and gold. Daniel Carlson missed the extra point wide left, so the score remained 13-13. The Vikings responded effectively, though. The opening plays of the ensuing series were a 32-yard connection from Murray to Jeshaun Jones and an 18-yard run from Aaron Jones. Fourth Quarter After more gains on the ground from Murray and Jones, the latter ran in an 8-yard touchdown to restore the Vikings’ lead at 20-13. New Orleans then went three-and-out at a bad time, and the visitors proceeded to find more success running the football as time ran off the clock. Colby Wooden did force the ball out from Jefferson after a catch, but Murray fell on it for the Vikings. Nonetheless, it helped hold Minnesota to a field goal attempt, which Reichard nailed again from 55 yards. Trailing 23-13, the Saints turned it over on downs near midfield. Minnesota then went three-and-out, but it wouldn’t matter. Shough was sacked on the opening play of the ensuing drive and threw another interception into the hands of Murphy two plays later. After Jones ran for their only required first down, Murray was able to kneel out the rest of the clock to secure the 23-13 Vikings victory. The Saints now hit the road for a Week 6 trip to New York to face the Giants on Sunday.

title: NY Giants news: Giants open as underdogs, Jameis Winston should be the quarterback, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for the NFC East- leading New York Football Giants. Why the Giants’ tie with the Commanders proved they’re finally different | SNY.tv For the Giants, though, it’s hard not to err more on the side of optimism. They are not Super […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for the NFC East- leading New York Football Giants. Why the Giants’ tie with the Commanders proved they’re finally different | SNY.tv For the Giants, though, it’s hard not to err more on the side of optimism. They are not Super Bowl contenders. They are not ready to run away with the wide-open NFC East. They have their flaws. But it’s very clear, through the first five weeks, they aren’t the team they’ve been the past few years. That’s truly all that matters. Compare these Giants to the ones run by Brian Daboll … or Joe Judge … or Pat Shurmur … or Ben McAdoo and there are so many ways this game never reaches its tied conclusion. The Giants were not a team built to handle adversity — it suffocated them in painstaking fashion like a plague. Time and time and time again. But these Giants are different. A month-plus of football is enough a sample size to state that. Abdul Carter continues to be a difference-maker Abdul Carter highlights from the WEEK 5 TIE pic.twitter.com/hrdMtm4eb6 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 12, 2026 How grit and mental toughness of John Harbaugh’s Giants showed up again | The Record Given the circumstances, the New York Giants will take their 27-27 overtime tie with the Washington Commanders from a wet and wacky Sunday afternoon in Maryland with appreciation for the big picture impact on the season. Week 5 was a disaster for the NFC East. Which team is down the worst? | The Athletic The good news? It’s over. What’s one other reason to be optimistic coming out of the Week 5 fiasco? Carroll: That the Giants even got to the point that this game could become a fiasco is impressive. As we’ve seen over the last few weeks, this is a team that will not quit and has pulled off late-game defensive stands to seal victories. Sunday, it was Winston who turned up the heat and mounted a 14-point comeback to tie the game. Winston’s play can be erratic, but he put on a show and became the only Giant since 1950 to amass 300-plus passing yards, three-plus passing touchdowns and 25-plus rushing yards in the same game. The other big plus coming out of Sunday’s game was the play of New York’s top pass catchers: tight end Isaiah Likely (11 catches, 94 yards, two touchdowns) and receiver Malik Nabers (11 catches, 121 yards, one TD). The two are huge focal points of the offense, so to see them get more involved, especially in big moments, will be crucial for this offense going forward. Seismic defensive pivot on full display | New York Post It is perfectly understandable to not know how to feel if you were pulling for the Giants coming out of the bizarre 27-27 tie with the Commanders. There is no doubt the Giants, after staging a strong, resilient comeback from down 14 points in the fourth quarter, wasted an opportunity to gain their first road victory of the season. QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 5 | Bleacher Report Everyone understands that Jameis Winston can sling the ball all over the yard. Everyone also understands he could implode at any moment and make a gut-wrenching mistake. Instead of eating a second-quarter sack, Winston tried to make something happen against the Washington Commanders and fumbled the ball. From that point forward, he led the New York Giants on seven drives that should have ended in points (not including a kneel-down at end of regulation). However, two missed field goals and a Cam Skattebo fumble prevented that from happening. “It’s just a whole bunch of stuff that people want to talk about as bad, but like, bro, the good outweighs the bad,” said running back Tyrone Tracy Jr..”It overwhelms the bad. So, you have to continue just to keep talking Jameis up, man. Keep talking Jameis up because like, people want to bench him, people want to talk bad about him. But like, at the end of the day, man, that boy is a hooper. He goes out there and plays ball.” Grade: B Tiki on advice he gave to Skattebo Tiki says Cam Skattebo's mindset has to change if he wants to fix his fumbling issues: pic.twitter.com/H2mccpsMPE — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) October 12, 2026 New York Giants have a ball security problem and that’s, well… A problem | USAToday.com The fumble fit a broader pattern the coaching staff has emphasized. Harbaugh acknowledged that ball security has not yet reached an unacceptable threshold, but the group must continue pursuing improvement rather than accepting current results. “Gotta keep chasing it. I mean, that’s the thing. You just can’t throw your hands up and say, ‘Well, we’re just not good at it.’ We have to believe in our players,” Harbaugh said. “We understand that at some point in time, it becomes unacceptable, but we’re not there yet. We’ve got guys that want to do the right thing, and we have to, as a team, as an offense, we have to get to the point where we protect the football.” NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Trend to watch: After posting less than 100 rushing yards against the Cardinals last week, Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. combined for 21 yards on 11 carries in the first half vs. Washington. The RBs also combined for 1.9 yards per catch in first half. Skattebo then had a crucial fumble with less than two minutes remaining in overtime when the Giants were in field-goal range. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Waiver wire, Week 6 edition
summary: Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 6. Week 5 gave us a much-needed respite from the injury onslaught. Even better, a few players returned to the field a little ahead of schedule, which was a boost for fantasy managers. But now we have bigger Bye weeks to contend with, on top of […]
full_text: A-Rod is dealing | Getty Images Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 6. Week 5 gave us a much-needed respite from the injury onslaught. Even better, a few players returned to the field a little ahead of schedule, which was a boost for fantasy managers. But now we have bigger Bye weeks to contend with, on top of all the injuries. The Waiver Wire is pretty bare this week, but savvy fantasy managers will continue to work it to improve their lineups. Don’t leave yourself behind on that. The Process : Each week, I try to identify the top Waiver Wire targets and evaluate the short- and long-term prospects of those players. I also do my best to reveal which players who are coming off a big week are fool’s gold. Finally, I look at streamers who might help you in a pinch (this is usually more important during Bye weeks). Some players discussed won’t be available in your league. I try to list players who are available in more than 50% of leagues. But what does that even mean? A 10-team league with six bench spots will have a much larger Free Agent pool than a 14-team league with eight. Most leagues fall somewhere in between. This isn’t “one size fits all.” By way of example, I won’t list Bryce Young, Woody Marks, Emanuel Wilson, Zach Charbonnet, Denzel Boston, and Keon Coleman, among others who probably aren’t available in any of your leagues. Note that I’m writing this column BEFORE the Week 5 Monday night game (BUF @ LAR). WEEK 6 BYES: Bengals, Dolphins, Lions, Vikings Week 6 Waiver Wire Quarterback: Aaron Rodgers is dealing. He’s on fire, folks, and I’m listing him for the third straight week. Did all that ayahuasca change his brain and body chemistry? Did it lead him to the actual fountain of youth? I don’t know, and I don’t care. Nor do I know how long he can keep this up, but he now has three straight games with at least 22 fantasy points, and he’s the QB3 over that stretch (pending the Monday night game). His next four games aren’t scary, either: Bucs, Saints, Browns, Bengals. C.J. Stroud is playing pretty well, and the Texans just bolstered their receiving corps by trading for Marvin Harrison, Jr., who gets a fresh start in Houston after failing in Arizona. Tank Dell could return soon, as well, and Kayshon Boutte is a nice deep threat. If you need a second quarterback in a Superflex, Stroud won’t be available. But if you need emergency help in a one-QB league, consider him a mid-range QB2 with upside. The Texans can’t run the ball, so he should continue to sling it plenty. At some point the Cardinals will give Carson Beck a look. Until they do, Jacoby Brissett should continue to put up good numbers most weeks, on an offense that chases points like dogs chase cars. He’ll face the Rams in Week 6, and that should provide him with at least 30 minutes of fantasy-friendly garbage time. Need a Week 6 streamer? I’ll give you three options. Jameis Winston (back-to-back games with three TD passes, and at least 20 fantasy points) is starting to feel it, and he gets the Saints on Sunday, at home. Michael Penix, Jr. doesn’t throw it all that much most weeks, but a home date with the Bears in Week 6 is pretty attractive. He hurt his ribs at the very end of the Sunday night game, so check his status. If he can’t go, I’d stay away from Tua Tagovailoa . Jalon Daniels had a nice game in Week 5, and he’s got the rushing upside that fantasy managers crave. But it was was against the very generous Dallas defense, so let’s not go crazy. I don’t think Baker Mayfield will be back for Week 6. If you’re stuck, a date with the Steelers is on tap – not ideal, but he should keep getting better with each start. Running Back: Another week, another Philly running back goes down. This time it was third-stringer Will Shipley, with a foot injury. That paved the way for practice squad call-up Dameon Pierce to get the bulk of the work. Pierce didn’t look good on Sunday, but the Eagles’ offense did show signs of life against a good defense, and in any case, any player who is starting at RB for even just a week or two should be rostered in fantasy, and especially during the Bye weeks. If MarShawn Lloyd got dropped in your league, pick him up. It might be hit-or-miss, but the door has opened and he’s getting the bulk of the work. The Chargers are a mess, and their three-headed backfield is a fantasy annoyance. If you want to chase Kimani Vidal ’s long touchdown run, go ahead, but right now starting any of the Los Angeles backs is going to be a mostly frustrating exercise. I’d use my waiver claims and FAAB dollars elsewhere. A few other names to think about, if you’re in need and/or want some depth that could pop later: Rachaad White , Tyler Allgeieir , Tyler Goodson , Kendre Miller , Brian Robinson, Jr., and Mike Washington, Jr. Wide Receiver I’ll mention Tyreek Hill again, although he probably got scooped up in all but the shallowest of leagues. Another speedster who might return soon is the aforementioned Tank Dell , and he’s worth a flier if you’ve got a deep bench. I felt so smart when I picked up Kendrick Bourne in a couple of leagues on Saturday, after it was announced that MHJ was going to be inactive on Sunday, with a trade in the works. Bourne was targeted eight times in Sunday’s blowout loss to the Lions and turned that into five catches for 70 yards. Not bad. It’s not exciting, but he’s a capable veteran who figures to have a decent workload as the third passing game option on a team that’s always chasing points. Jordyn Tyson should be on your radar. A Week 9 return seems likely. He’s worth stashing and especially if you can keep him in an IR spot. Jerry Jeudy is a trade candidate, and depending on where he lands, he could have some value. We’ve been down this road with him before, and I wouldn’t prioritize him. But if you have a deep bench, you can consider it. Need depth? I’ll repeat a bunch of names I’ve listed in recent weeks, together with some new ones: Malik Washington, Chris Bell , Antonio Williams , Cyrus Allen , Germie Bernard , DeMario Douglas , Darius Cooper , Kayshon Boutte , and Tre Harris . Tight End: Brenton Strange is a featured part of the Jaguars’ offense, and he just put up consecutive games with seven catches on eight targets. He should be rostered everywhere. Others to consider if you need help: Pat Freiermuth (low volume, but three TDs the past two weeks), Darren Waller , Chig Okonkwo , and Tyler Higbee . That’s all I’ve got. Good luck with your waiver claims! ***This column appears each Monday right here at Big Blue View. Each Thursday, my weekly fantasy preview with my rides, fades and sleepers (start/sit) appears here, and on Fridays you can find my weekly Giants Props of the week, also right here. ***

title: NY Giants sign another veteran defensive lineman to practice squad
summary: The New York Giants continued what has become a “kitchen sink” approach to improving the depth of their defensive line on Monday, signing veteran defensive lineman Dawuane Smoot to their practice squad. The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jordan Ranaan, and was subsequently confirmed by a Giants source. Smoot, 31, is in his 10th […]
full_text: Dawuane Smoot | Getty Images The New York Giants continued what has become a “kitchen sink” approach to improving the depth of their defensive line on Monday, signing veteran defensive lineman Dawuane Smoot to their practice squad. The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jordan Ranaan , and was subsequently confirmed by a Giants source. Smoot, 31, is in his 10th NFL season. The 6-foot-3, 275-pounder was a third-round pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2017 NFL Draft. Smoot has played in 127 regular-season games, with 21 starts. He has 27.0 career sacks. Smoot spent 2024 with the Buffalo, but has spent eight of his nine seasons with the Jaguars. Last year with Jacksonville, he had 2.0 sacks, 23 tackles (3 for loss) and five quarterback hits in 17 games. The Giants, searching both to improve their run defense and to provide options on the outside after losing Brian Burns for the season, have continued to add veteran options to the 53-man roster and practice squad. They signed outside linebacker Jihad Ward off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad, and added experienced defensive tackles P.J. Mustipher and C.J. Ravenall to their practice squad. Now, Smoot has been added to their collection. Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday afternoon that the Giants have been “feast or famine” defending the run. “I think we’ve had too many chunk plays overall,” Harbaugh said. “We’ve played kind of feast or famine run defense. We’ve had a lot of really good plays, a lot of really good plays in that game where we stuffed the run, which we’re very capable of doing. And then there’s a couple of line of scrimmage runs that get out on us that we’re not happy about that can be played so much better. Whether we don’t adjust to a motion the right way, we don’t get over in our gaps, we don’t quite come in through the angles.”

title: What advanced stats tell us about Giants vs. Commanders in Week 5
summary: On a Sunday of wild endings in the NFL, the Giants-Commanders game ending may have been the wildest. The Giants should have won the game after they finally started moving the ball in the second half, but they probably feel better about Cam Skattebo’s physical error than Washington does about Jayden Daniels’ mental error. Let’s […]
full_text: On a Sunday of wild endings in the NFL, the Giants-Commanders game ending may have been the wildest. The Giants should have won the game after they finally started moving the ball in the second half, but they probably feel better about Cam Skattebo’s physical error than Washington does about Jayden Daniels’ mental error. Let’s a take a look at what Pro Football Focus thought of the performances of individual players and what other interesting information has popped up on X. PFF grades: Offense No one on offense was judged to have played an excellent game for the Giants except Isaiah Likely. Malik Nabers did grade above average, though. Likely would probably have graded even higher had he not incurred two penalties. The character of this Giants offensive line has started to come into focus. In general it is an excellent pass-blocking offensive line, led Sunday by Jon Runyan, Jermaine Eluemunor (whose calf will be MRIed Monday), Andrew Thomas (still effective but a notch less dominant due to his groin injury) and center Bryan Hudson, who will remain the starting center, per what John harbaugh said on Monday. Sisi Mauigoa was average vs. the Commanbders, though he did surrender 3 hurries. The problem was a lot of mediocre run blocking (average or below average run block grades). Unsurprisingly, the Giants’ running backs are also grading mediocre to below average, although it’s hard to say that any of them have looked explosive even when they get a little space. Jameis Winston also graded in the average range yesterday, pretty much like he has in every game he’s started this season. You may think that 326 passing yards, 3 TD passes, and no INTs (he did have one but it was nullified by defensive pass interference) would lead to an excellent passing grade. Remember, though, that PFF grades process, not just results. Winston’s 326 yards came on 54 attempts and only 33 completions for a measly 6.1 yards per attempt. More importantly, PFF, which emphasizes balls that should have been turnovers, gave Jameis two “turnover-worthy plays” (the nullified INT probably being one of them) and only one “big-time throw.” He also had a fumble. So as is always the case, with Jameis you take the good with the bad. It’s worth noting, though, that the Commanders blitzed Jameis on about half his dropbacks, and he performed as well on those as when not blitzed in addition to having 2 of his 3 TDs on plays he was blitzed, one of them on a play when the blitz resulted in a pressure. Isaiah Likely had an excellent day catching the ball, with Malik Nabers not far behind (and only because of his first drop of the season). The other receivers were slightly below average, the worst being Darnell Mooney, who only caught 2 of 7 targets. The running backs were a different story, with all three backs grading slightly below average. PFF grades: Defense Things looked better for the Giants defense. Abdul Carter is really starting to realize his potential. He had 6 pressures, the second week in a row he has done that, and also his second sack of the season. Inside, D.J. Reader has been every bit what the Giants hoped for, solidifying the run defense (fourth game in five with an above average overall and run defense grade) and giving them a little push in the pass rush too. Likewise, Shelby Harris has picked it up too, grading above average for the second week in a row. Kayvon Thibodeaux had three pressures and was the Giants’ second-best run defender. Darius Alexander was a bit below average overall but did get two pressures (plus an award for taking his time standing around and nudging the ball a bit on his way back across the line of scrimmage on the last play of the game, preventing Jayden Daniels from picking it up and spiking it before time ran out). At linebacker, Arvell Reese didn’t have the other-worldly performance he gave last week, but he still graded elite in run defense. His overall grade was low because he gave up 3 receptions and missed one tackle (perhaps the ill-fated attempt to spy on Daniels, who went right by him). Tremaine Edmunds was slightly below average but did sack Daniels once. In the secondary, Dru Phillips got his third consecutive Very Good grade from PFF, but for a completely different reason than in the past two weeks. Phillips rushed the passer seven times yesterday and got five pressures, including two sacks and two QB hits. He also had 3 tackles, all three of them “stops” (unsuccessful running plays), though he did miss one tackle. His draft class mate Tyler Nubin wasn’t as fortunate, grading below average. Nubin had three tackles and an assist and wasn’t given any missed tackles, but his overall low grade was due to a 48.4 run defense grade. Apparently, when you take such a poor angle that you can’t even get into the same zip code as a running back who has burst into the second level they don’t call it a missed tackle. Elsewhere in the secondary, keep an eye on Ar’Darius Washington, whose 29 snaps were his highest of the season. He had a missed tackle but also two stops and allowed one reception in two targets for only one yard and an overall Very Good defense grade. Those came at the expense of Nubin. Let’s see whether Washington starts next week. At the other safety, Jevon Holland graded slightly below average, even though he had a sack, because he missed three tackles and gave up a 16-yard reception. Greg Newsome and Deonte Banks each gave up two receptions for 23 and 36 yards, respectively. Advanced stats Here’s an amusing note. I’ll take ESPN’s word for it: Entering today, the New York Giants were 0-230 since 1970 when trailing by 14+ points in the final 8 minutes of regulation. They're now 0-230-1. pic.twitter.com/Ridz5TPoFv — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) October 11, 2026 And that does speak to something about this Giants team under Winston: He’s nothing if not confident in his ability. More about that in a moment, but first… Here are two different metrics of Winston’s play against Washington relative to other quarterbacks in Week 5, one (PFF grade) subjective based on an analyst’s assessment of his performance on each passing play and the other (EPA/play) based on objective statistics related to how well he advanced the offense toward points: Quarterback PFF grading versus efficiency (EPA/play), through Week 5 SNF, min 60 dropbacks – Top right Lamar, Purdy and … Goff – Darnold sliding in EPA, but grading not awful – Nix bottom-3 PFF grade pic.twitter.com/wdCOGEAtHY — Kevin Cole (@KevinCole___) October 12, 2026 As we’ve noted before, PFF grades and EPA/play do not agree completely but are significantly positively correlated. In this case, both metrics agree strongly that Winston’s play was…average, barely. The reason, despite his 326 yards and 3 TDs, is that it took him 54 passes (33 completed) to do it, i.e., he had a lot of passes that accomplished nothing. Daniels graded higher, but solely because of his running (even though he ultimately cost his team a win by not spiking the ball – there is apparently no objective metric for bonehead decisions). Now, about that Winston confidence: An interesting perspective by Kevin Cole is to take the above EPA/play numbers, but for the entire season to date, and separate them by early vs. late downs: Early-down and late-down EPA per play. The potentially worrying spot is upper-left, with high variance outperformance on late downs. Really only the Giants who are likely getting a bit lucky and could regress pic.twitter.com/h7jeBNy7FZ — Kevin Cole (@KevinCole___) October 12, 2026 If you’re an optimist, you say that Jameis is “clutch,” making things happen when his back is against the wall (top four EPA/play on third and fourth down, trailing only Brock Purdy, Trevor Lawrence, and Joe Burrow). If you’re a pessimist, as Cole seems to be, you attribute it to luck and suggest he could regress over time. There’s a third interpretation I can imagine, that Matt Nagy is playing it too safe on first and second downs…
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: Giants-Commanders: 5 plays that led to this game ending in a tie
summary: The New York Giants tied the Washington Commanders in an epic comeback on Sunday, with emotional swings that could fracture one’s spirit. New York battled back from a 27-13 deficit in the final eight minutes. Jameis Winston finished with 326 passing yards and three touchdowns. The game had frustrating moments and very impressive individual efforts, […]
full_text: Isaiah Likely celebrates one of his two touchdowns. | Getty Images The New York Giants tied the Washington Commanders in an epic comeback on Sunday, with emotional swings that could fracture one’s spirit. New York battled back from a 27-13 deficit in the final eight minutes. Jameis Winston finished with 326 passing yards and three touchdowns. The game had frustrating moments and very impressive individual efforts, but missed field goals and a costly Cam Skattebo fumble took the win away from the Giants. However, Washington was in position to win this game multiple times, but destiny dictated that neither team would win this football game. Here are five plays or sequences of plays that defined this wacky game. Play(s) 1: The Giants don’t go away The Giants are a resilient team. They were frustrating for most of the game. They were inefficient on the ground, made terrible defensive lapses, and the Jameis Winston Experience was on full display. Despite all of this, the Giants tied the game in the fourth quarter — the Giants just didn’t go away! Winston put the team ON HIS BACK and led three consecutive touchdown drives that totaled 32 plays, and resulted in two Isaiah Likely touchdowns and a Malik Nabers touchdown. It felt bleak, but the Giants battled back to send the game to overtime – that’s impressive resilience and excellent coaching. The Giants play with pride. Play(s) 2: What?! The Giants led an improbable comeback where they were down 27-13 to start the fourth quarter. The defense forced a punt after one of Dominic Zvada’s sthree missed field goals and the Giants ripped off 67 yards on eight plays, where it looked like they were going to win the game, but Skattebo fumbled. Washington drove the football down the field and got into field goal range, but with not timeouts…this happened! Dan Quinn says the final sequence should’ve been throwing the ball out of bounds/clocking it to kick the FG. Quinn says it’s his responsibility pic.twitter.com/WYCngo4Xlb — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 11, 2026 A WILD ENDING IN WASHINGTON! With no timeouts remaining, the Commanders can't spike the ball before time expires, and the game ends in a tie! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/GgTTHtyRVC — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 11, 2026 Dan Quinn took responsibility by saying this, but questioning Jayden Daniels’ actions only makes sense. Play 3: Slow start to on defense again, SPY THE GUY Jacory Croskey-Merritt breaks free for a 33-yard TD run! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/9wfDhRQB9V — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 11, 2026 No defense wants to go down seven in the first three plays of the game, but Dennard Wilson’s unit found themselves in that exact situation. PISTOL power run with presnap motion from the H-Back and Josh Conerly (72) pulling to the play side. Washington beat the Giants to the fit and Tyler Nubin (27) took another bad angle that his athletic ability could not rectify – an unfortunate all too familiar sight. The result was this 33-yard touchdown run by Jacory Croskey-Merritt. It’s not all on Nubin; he’s the face that will rightfully be chastised, but several Giants failed to execute their assignments well, which placed Nubin in that position. C.J. Okoye (99) is removed from the gap and Arvell Reese (52) was picked up by Conerly. Tremaine Edmunds (49) was washed to the inside by the climbing offensive lineman, and the seas were parted by Washington. Also, the Giants ran a lot of man coverage last week in their win over Arizona. It was successful, but Jayden Daniels has a bit more mobility than Jacoby Brissett. The Giants were burnt TWICE on Daniels’ rushing touchdowns against man coverage. 38-yard TD run! Jayden Daniels is so back @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/un8ws01KAe — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 ANOTHER JAYDEN DANIELS TD RUN @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/I2cNFG2TFW — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 I’m not sure if it’s a blown assignment by the Giants or just questionable play calling – either way, it has to be fixed. Play 4: Jameis’ fumble Ball is out and the Commanders defense lands on it! @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6pE1cfRuAn — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The Giants tried to run an under center play action shot on second-and-8. Winston looked to Malik Nabers’ quick curl, which was promptly covered by Jeremey Reeves (39). Bryan Hudson (60) was backed into the pocket slowly by Tim Settle (97) and Deatrich Wise Jr. (91) hit Winston, as the veteran quarterback attempted to fall on the football. Tim Settle of Washington recovered, giving Daniels excellent field position, which resulted in a 40 yard field goal. Great job by the Giants defense to stiffen and force only a field goal. Up until this point of the game, the Giants’ offense showed very little. They had 41 total yards, which would obviously change. Play(s) 5: Controversy The Giants scored after a 13-play, 63 yard drive that took up seven minutes of game clock. However, the drive was seemingly stopped by an Amik Robertson interception on the goal line: Instead of being an interception, this is ruled DPI by Amik Robertson. Good call/bad call? pic.twitter.com/FsnMBtFA5Q — Chad Ryan (@ChadwikoTWW) October 11, 2026 The interception was negated by a defensive pass interference against Robertson. Is there contact? Yes. Is it egregious? No. It’s not the worst call in the world – we see the tug – but I’ve seen much worse not called, and it was a risky – bad – throw by Winston. The call gave the Giants the football back and Likely finished the job with the touchdown below: Isaiah Likely makes it a one-score game @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xDYyENnJlr — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The Giants stretched the zone defense toward the sideline with the the routes of Malachi Fields (88) and Darnell Mooney (17); Likely, then, slipped into the vacated spot and Winston just got the football toward his inside shoulder for six. The Giants reduced the lead to six points heading into the fourth quarter. Another somewhat controversial play happened to give the Giants’ life in the fourth quarter on fourth down. Isaiah Likely’s second touchdown: Isaiah Likely crosses the plane for another Giants TD @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H4QnwWuBJN — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 It does seem like Likely broke the plane of the goal line, though. Both of these plays were obviously consequential in the comeback. EXTRA Play(s) 6: The J.J. McCarthy Package The Giants had plays designed with McCarthy as the quarterback – none of them worked. The first was a blown up touch-pass to Darnell Mooney that was easily sniffed out by Washington. The second was a solid screen pass to Malik Nabers that was called back by an illegal formation. Then, on third-and-2, Matt Nagy tried to leverage McCarthy’s athletic ability and ran a jet-zone-read that Frankie Luvu easily sensed and blew up, which led to a Dominic Zvada 56-yard field goal. McCarthy also ran a zone-read that gained 1 yard. It’s obvious the Giants want to use McCarthy’s mobility, but it did not work in Washington, as Nagy tried to do anything to get the offense going.

title: NY Giants’ injuries: Jermaine Eluemunor’s calf issue headlines the list
summary: New York Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor is undergoing an MRI on his calf on Monday, after injuring it during Sunday’s 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders. The veteran right tackle played 44 snaps before suffering the injury, and having to be helped off the field by teammates Aaron Stinnie and John Michael Schmitz. Second-year […]
full_text: Jermaine Eluemunor is helped off the field on Sunday vs. the Washington Commanders. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor is undergoing an MRI on his calf on Monday , after injuring it during Sunday’s 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders. The veteran right tackle played 44 snaps before suffering the injury, and having to be helped off the field by teammates Aaron Stinnie and John Michael Schmitz. Second-year player Marcus Mbow took over at right tackle, playing the final 45 offensive snaps. Pro Football Focus charged Mbow with two pressures allowed in 36 pass-blocking snaps. If Eluemunor misses time, rookie J.C. Davis would likely take over as the swing tackle. Davis has been inactive for all five games this season. Cornerback Colton Hood suffered a concussion making a tackle on a kickoff late in the third quarter. How quickly he progresses through the league’s concussion protocol will determine whether or not he will be available this Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. Nubin suffered a neck injury in the fourth quarter when he was hit by Washington center Lucas Patrick while trying to help make a tackle. — More on all of these injuries as information becomes available.

title: Jameis Winston is, and should be, the NY Giants quarterback
summary: Can we stop now with the breathless drum-banging for J.J. McCarthy to replace Jameis Winston as quarterback of the New York Giants sooner rather than later? The Giants unquestionably lose Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders without Winston’s heroics — 254 yards passing and three touchdowns, two of those in the final eight minutes of […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Can we stop now with the breathless drum-banging for J.J. McCarthy to replace Jameis Winston as quarterback of the New York Giants sooner rather than later? The Giants unquestionably lose Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders without Winston’s heroics — 254 yards passing and three touchdowns, two of those in the final eight minutes of regulation to erase a 14-point deficit, and the first 50+ pass game of his 12-year career without an interception. Albeit, the last fact comes with help from a questionable call. Winston, as he reminded reporters recently, is the Giants’ starting quarterback. With Jaxson Dart gone for the season, he deserves to be. The Giants, trailing 12-3 and with just 77 yards of total offense in the first half, changed things up after halftime. They went with more no-huddle, and put the game on Winston’s right arm. He went 26 of 38 after intermission and had the Giants in position to win the game twice in overtime. The Giants scored three touchdowns and a field goal on their four third- and fourth-quarter possessions. Had the Giants lost in the extra session on Sunday, that would not have been on Winston. Over the final 40 minutes of play, he did everything a quarterback can do to give his team a chance to win. In overtime, Dominic Zvada’s 46-yard missed field goal and Cam Skattebo’s untimely fumble denied the Giants a chance to get to 4-1. “I thought he [Winston] was amazing in the fourth quarter. I thought he was amazing in the second half,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “I thought his ability to come out and change like that. And I felt we changed our offense up, we tried some different things, and he really settled into the things we did offensively. And he was amazing. “First half, he wasn’t. He’d be the first to tell you that, but that’s on everybody. I tell the guys, nothing good is all the one person. We’re all responsible for all the good, and we’re all responsible for all the bad or the not good. And so, he’s right in the mix with everybody else that way. I called him up, broke the huddle, I said, what he showed out there was really remarkable.” Winston was matter-of-fact about the performance. “I think when your back is against the wall, you have to depend on your playmakers, and I think we did a good job of doing that, getting the guys the football, and mixing up on them, and kind of just threw them off schedule,“ Winston said. “We never give up, and our focus is to do whatever is required for us to win a football game. And I’m just grateful that the guys rose to the challenge, and we put on tape what we’re capable of doing if the game has to go the other way. However, we still have to, you know, focus on the things that we can control, and the things that we can control are us being our very best on every single play.” Winston is now 2-0-1 in three games replacing Dart. Even after Sunday, he was again asked about the skepticism in some quarters that he should be the starting quarterback. “I always focus on what my heart desires, and I say this over and over again, my desire is to be the New York Football Giants Super Bowl-winning quarterback. My desire is to be a great starting quarterback in the NFL. I dreamed of this, and this is who I am, and I know that I’m going to continue to get better and find ways to help this team win football games.” The Giants are an imperfect team. Their flaws are evident each time they play. You can easily argue that that they are a few twists and turns from being 1-4 instead of 3-1-1 and in first place in the there-for-the-taking NFC East. In some ways, Winston is the perfect quarterback for the Giants in this place and time. He is obviously imperfect. There is always an element of ‘which team is he going to throw it to?’ when Winston drops back to pass. Sometimes, his eyes look like saucers ready to pop out of his head. He looks awkward when he starts to move around the pocket. Especially with two hands wrapped around the ball, with the obvious intent of trying to protect it. His facemask somehow makes him look like he should be playing the 1960s. Yet, Winston, like these Giants just keeps playing and keeps slinging the rock, mistakes or no mistakes. “It’s faith. When you have unwavering faith, you’re not phased by the circumstances, conditions, and facts. That’s something that I am continuing to share with the guys, I say ‘let’s not get phased’,“ Winston said. “Russell Wilson used to always say this thing, and one of his good friends wrote a book called ‘Remain Neutral’. I think Russ did an incredible job that no matter the highs or the lows, he remained neutral. I was happy I was able to pick that up from him. Also understanding, biblically, one of my favorite verses, Philippians 4:13 says ‘I can do all things through Christ, through him who strengthens me’. Before that, Paul (an apostle) is in jail. He’s talking about being happy with a lot and being happy with a little. At the end of the day, he’s learned the secret to being content. That is: taking whatever you get, do what you can with what you have, where you have it, and making the most out of it.” Winston and the Giants have been doing that no matter the circumstances thus far. Maybe the time will come when Winston plays his way out of the starting quarterback job. Right now, though, he is the starting quarterback. And there is no reason for that to change. A few other quick ‘things I think’ The chatter that the Giants’ pass rush stinks needs to stop. The Giants defense had a 2.14 average time to pressure against the Commanders That is the fastest time to pressure for any team in a game this season and is in the 98th percentile since 2016, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) October 12, 2026 These two numbers, which I dropped into ‘ Kudos & Wet Willies ’, are insane. I have to trace them to the belief Harbaugh has instilled in this team that if they just keep going, they will have a chance. — Per the FOX broadcast, the Giants had lost 24 straight games when trailing at halftime. Well, at least now they have not lost 25 straight. — From ESPN Insights , comes this unbelievable nugget. Entering today, the Giants were 0-230 since 1970 when trailing by 14+ points in the final 8 minutes of regulation. They’re now 0-230-1. “The one thing that has become very evident is what is inside of our players. Their heart, their grit, their mental toughness, their ability to overcome adversity is A plus, plus, plus. And that showed up today, so I’m very proud of that. And I’m also very excited for the fact that we can improve so much. We improved throughout the game, we did a lot of really good things … So, proud of the guys though, for their fight. Would have wanted the outcome to be a win, and we’ll talk about that now, I’m sure. But there’s a lot to be proud of.” Until overtime on Sunday, the run-blocking was horrid. I can’t help but think that sometimes teams need running backs who can make players miss, and who make their blockers right. I’m not sure the Giants have that. It’s why they had interest in Kenneth Walker and Jeremiyah Love this offseason. If I’m Commanders owner Josh Harris, I would be seriously considering firing Dan Quinn this morning. You simply cannot botch the clock management at the end of the game, giving your quarterback conflicting — and wrong — guidance , as a veteran head coach and not find your job in jeopardy.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants-Commanders quotebook: What they’re saying about the final play
summary: Here is how both teams reacted to the crazy finish of the 27-27 tie Sunday between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. Giants coach John Harbaugh on the end of the game … “Well the time ran out. That was what I saw, so that’s what happened. It wasn’t expected … ‘Was it a […]
full_text: Here is how both teams reacted to the crazy finish of the 27-27 tie Sunday between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. Giants coach John Harbaugh on the end of the game … “Well the time ran out. That was what I saw, so that’s what happened. It wasn’t expected … ‘Was it a win?’ No. ‘Was it a loss?’ No. It was a tie. ‘How does that make you feel?’ I’m happy it wasn’t a loss and I’m sad it wasn’t a win. So that’s how I feel. It’s a tie. It’s a heck of a lot better than a loss, but it’s not as good as a win. So I know that just sounds so obvious, but that’s kind of how you feel. I mean, we’ve had a lot of these conversations over the years. We’ll take it. We’ll take it right now. We were down 14. Came back, and we got a tie, alright? … “I wanted to get off the field before they could take it away from us, I guess. I was surprised. I was surprised. I can’t say that I wasn’t. It was a pretty shocking end there.” Jameis Winston on the result … “I’m really just grateful that it was a tie. That’s the first time that I’ve been a part of. So, it’s just really good to know that we can just get so much better and just eliminate the negatives and build on the positives emotionally. And I’m just grateful that we found a way to persevere and make it a game … I was just thankful. Thank you, Lord. Thank you, Lord.“ Abdul Carter on the final play … “I’m just shocked, honestly. I seen the clock winding down, it was like two, three seconds left. I’m like, ‘all right, they gonna get a snap’. Then I seen they were still laying on the ground. I was like, ‘oh, game over.’ … I felt grateful, honestly. Just grateful.” Jevon Holland on the wild finish … “Man, it’s emotional. I mean, it’s like left and right, left and right, [and] kind of just trying to stay resilient. Like whatever happens, happens. Whatever happened in the game, happened, and you can’t control it anymore. How can we win the game? You know what I mean, finish the game? Coming out of the half, [and] overtime, we’re going to just do everything to win the game. Then even the swing at the end, [New York Giants RB Cam] Skat [Skattebo] fumbled. We’re like, ‘we’ve got to go back out.’ Some guys on the sideline were going to take their gloves off. It was crazy. And then for it to run out, I mean, even when the clock ran to zero, there was a second where I was like, ‘is it going to go to the second overtime?’ I don’t know if it was two overtimes or not. I’ve never been in an overtime tie like this. Yeah, that was crazy. They were just like, ‘game’s over,’ and I was like, ‘oh, sure.’” Cam Skattebo on his fumble … I” fumbled the ball. We can’t have that. I understand that. I’m going to go into the film room and get it fixed. I felt like I had good protection on it. The kid made a hell of a play. I think in that situation what I think I could do differently is try not to get the extra yards because we’re already in a good position and continue to take care of the ball. If I get tackled for a loss at one yard, then I get tackled for a loss at one yard. I’m the player that tries to fight for as many yards as possible for this team. It kind of bit me in the ass there. I got to make sure I protect the ball for this football team. We win that game if I do.” Skattebo on the game ending in a tie … “It was a sigh of relief. I probably won’t get reamed as much, but I’m still going to get reamed. At the end of the day, like I said, my number was called. I gave the ball up. If that happens again this year, I promise you it won’t happen.” Washington coach Dan Quinn on the ending … “Leaving tonight, with a tie feels like a loss. And the last sequence, we throw it out of bounds, we clock it, you give yourself a chance to kick it. And we pride ourselves on those moments at the end of the game. And after the first down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. The right call is honestly like we can go clock it early and don’t put ourselves in that spot and that is my responsibility. Nobody else’s. I’m gutted for our team.“ Quinn on Jayden Daniels’ responsibility on the final play … “The sequencing of that does not fall on him. It’s an outside throw or a clock. You know, those are the two, out of bounds throw or a clock. And that has to come from me. I don’t even have to put him into that spot. I can do that earlier and we can finish the kick early. We don’t need to gain more yards, so that’s on me. Yeah, I’m saying we don’t need to gain anymore. We were just trying to gain more and we don’t need to. Like it’s easy enough to say, ‘Hey man, let’s clock it right here. We’re early enough and go get it.’” Jayden Daniels on the end of the game … “We just have to be better. We all have to be better. Situational football. Starts with me. Everybody will say the same thing, but we have to be better at situational football. “We have to stop the clock. We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it’s on me.” Washington wide receiver Terry McLaurin on the final play … “I’m not quite sure what the call was over the headset. I think in that situation we practice to try to maybe center the ball. But, I mean, obviously we didn’t have it executed or communicated right, as an offense, because that’s what happened. That just can’t happen. So, we got to take that, and that’s a bad lesson to learn. You got to be better at the NFL level. But, we just gotta move on.”

title: NY Giants news: A tie is, well, good enough
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! The Giants did not win Sunday. They didn’t lose to the Washington Commanders, either. Sunday’s hard-to-comprehend 27-27 tie leaves the Giants alone in first place in the NFC East, and leaves the Commanders searching for answers. NFC East standings Giants 3-1-1Philadelphia Eagles 2-3Dallas Cowboys 2-3Commanders 1-3-1 Commanders’ Daniels takes […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! The Giants did not win Sunday. They didn’t lose to the Washington Commanders, either. Sunday’s hard-to-comprehend 27-27 tie leaves the Giants alone in first place in the NFC East, and leaves the Commanders searching for answers. NFC East standings Giants 3-1-1 Philadelphia Eagles 2-3 Dallas Cowboys 2-3 Commanders 1-3-1 Commanders’ Daniels takes blame for botched final play in OT | ESPN The Washington Commanders were in position to attempt a game-winning overtime kick to beat the New York Giants. But all they ended up kicking was themselves after botching the final play in overtime preventing a potential field goal attempt. Quarterback Jayden Daniels was tackled for no gain with eight seconds left in overtime and, with no timeouts, the Commanders could not stop the clock. So rather than a potential Drew Stevens 42-yard field goal, they were left trying to explain what appeared to be inexplicable in a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants. “We have to stop the clock,” Daniels said. “We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it’s on me.” Giants Report Card: Offense, Defense Rally for 27-27 Tie With Commanders | Giants on SI Big Blue View isn’t the only site that does post-game grades. Who knew? Why the Giants’ 27-27 tie with the Commanders proved they’re finally different | SNY John Harbaugh summed it up perfectly, or at least he tried to, after the Giants traveled to Washington, played the Commanders in a monsoon, and tied. There were moments of dysfunctional, unsightly football. Excitement and euphoria. Super highs. Gut-wrenching lows. Culminating in a 27-27 final. “I’m happy it wasn’t a loss,” said the coach. “I’m sad it wasn’t a win.” The truth really is somewhere in the middle. For the Giants, though, it’s hard not to err more on the side of optimism. They are not Super Bowl contenders. They are not ready to run away with the wide-open NFC East. They have their flaws. But it’s very clear, through the first five weeks, they aren’t the team they’ve been the past few years. That’s truly all that matters. Heroes, zeros from Giants’ tie with Commanders: Jameis Winston powered comeback | NY Post Heroes and zeros? I still like the sound of ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ better. Magic Johnson calls out Commanders for clock management debacle vs. Giants | The Big Lead After the game was over, Johnson did not mince words about the debacle that was the end of the Week 5 game. “I’m in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today’s overtime game against the Giants,” Johnson said. “All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!” Johnson even added the “face palm” emoji for good measure. From Big Blue View Giants-Commanders ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’: Plenty of credit, and blame, to go around 4 things we learned during the Giants’ 27-27 tie with the Commanders Commanders’ bungled clock management lets grateful Giants escape with tie Giants-Commanders instant grades: Washington gets ‘F’ for clock management Giants-Commanders, Week 5: Giants and Commanders finish in overtime tie BBV mailbag Have a Giants-related question? Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Some may argue the New York Jets are catching the New England Patriots at a bad time. New England is coming off a beatdown of the Las Vegas Raiders, and Drake Maye has reset his factory settings to being a good quarterback. However, some key injury updates favor the Jets. NFL Insider Ian Rapoport revealed on X, “Patriots OT Will Campbell, whose day was cut short today with injury, is believed to have suffered a knee sprain, sources say, and he’ll have an MRI tomorrow to confirm. This will likely cause him to miss some time.” Campbell has only given up one sack this season. New England is going to be down their starting left tackle for this home game against the Jets. David Bailey is coming off the best game of his career with his three-sack performance in Week 5. He should be licking his chops. Now, personally, I wouldn’t have minded Bailey going against T. rex arms, who can’t reach things on the top shelf, but going against his backup is great news for the Jets. Also worth noting that the Patriots lost running back TreVeyon Henderson, who injured an ankle in Week 5. So his status is also very much up in the air. “The Patriots have been snakebit by injuries, having placed 19 players on injured reserve this year, which already surpassed their total from all of last season (17),” ESPN’s Mike Reiss revealed. title: Jets vs. Browns: Winning Ugly
summary: Sometimes in the NFL it’s really about surviving. There are weeks where your team desperately needs a win. It doesn’t matter how you get that win. You just have to get it, someway, somehow. The Jets faced one of those moments in Week 5 against the Cleveland Browns. A loss would have sent the team […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets defensive end David Bailey (31) sacks Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sometimes in the NFL it’s really about surviving. There are weeks where your team desperately needs a win. It doesn’t matter how you get that win. You just have to get it, someway, somehow. The Jets faced one of those moments in Week 5 against the Cleveland Browns. A loss would have sent the team to a 1-4 record. The season would be spiraling out of control. The discussion would start to turn to the 2027 NFL Draft and coaching candidates for next season as both the team’s and Aaron Glenn’s respective fates would seem sealed. Amazon’s Al Michaels was mocked on Thursday night for saying Dallas’ game against Tampa Bay wasn’t a “must win” but it was a “can’t lose.” Silly though it might sound, I viewed this game for the Jets as more of a “can’t lose” than a must win. I don’t know that this victory turns the 2026 season around. I hope it will. It might. It’s just more that the team could not afford to lose to the Browns because of everything that would have brought. It wasn’t always pretty, but the Jets found a way to get the win that they so desperately needed. They might have committed 10 penalties. They might have thrown for only 120 yards after their first possession. The winning score might have been set up by a colossal Cleveland special teams miscue. But when the clock hit 0:00 in the fourth quarter, the scoreboard showed the Jets with more points than the Browns. Of course that isn’t to say this was a poor performance across the board for New York. The defense had a stellar day a week after an embarrassing effort in Chicago. Everything was better for the team on that side of the ball. The standout performance came from rookie David Bailey who had a breakout game with 3 sacks, a quarterback hit, and 7 to 8 pressures depending on what tracking website you want to use. Bailey was a target of criticism all week in the media. It was difficult for me to understand why. Through the first four weeks, the Jets were not generating enough pressure as a defense, but Bailey was right at the top of most pressure stats among rookies. For whatever reason, Bailey took the blame over major free agent signing Joseph Ossai, who has done nothing, or fourth year player Will McDonald, whose feast or famine production is well-known, or a defensive tackle group that hasn’t shown an ability to collapse the pocket. The number two pick in the Draft has high expectations, but listening to the New York media, you would have thought it was a catastrophe that Bailey wasn’t Lawrence Taylor within his first four games. Even more puzzling was the implication that the Jets made a massive blunder passing on Bailey for Arvell Reese. Reese, of course was an outstanding prospect, who is likely to be an excellent player for the crosstown Giants. But his success is coming in a role where he is not primarily rushing the passer. If the problem was a lack of a pass rush from a first round pick, it’s difficult to understand how Reese, who just had his first sack yesterday in Week 5, was going to fix that. In any event, Bailey quieted his critics against Cleveland. Many of those critics will undoubtedly declare Bailey a superstar off this performance. Once again, this will be premature. Bailey is a talented prospect who is producing. His game, particularly his pass rush moves, still needs refinement. He’s right on the trajectory where you want a highly drafted rookie to be. He’s doing things well with room to grow. That’s how he should have been viewed before the game. It’s how he should be viewed now. Another star of this game for the Jets was Braelon Allen. Allen has been an afterthought for most of his three year career, essentially receiving his carries in short yardage situations and when Breece Hall needs a rest. The Jets might want to start reconsidering his usage. This isn’t about one big game for Allen, who ran for a career high 116 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries. It’s about the skills he brings to the table. Allen is a true North-South runner who falls forward and picks up positive yardage almost every time he runs. Hall is a homerun hitter but inconsistent in reading his blocks and prone to too much dancing behind the line of scrimmage. None of this is to say that Hall is a player the Jets should trade to make room for Allen. But Allen’s ability to keep the Jets offense on schedule is something valuable that merits a heavier workload. In many ways, Allen’s strengths are Hall’s weaknesses and vice versa. This has the makings of a very effective running back duo if the Jets can see clearly. All in all there were many standout performers in this one. T’Vondre Sweat, Jamien Sherwood, and Darrell Jackson Jr. were among the other standouts for a Jets defense that shut the Browns down for most of the game and finished with 8 sacks. As mentioned earlier, the game wasn’t pretty. The Jets committed 10 penalties. The temptation will be to rebut this by noting how poor the officiating is. And to be clear, it was both poor and one-sided in Cleveland’s favor. However, aside from a shaky fourth quarter flag on Brandon Stephens, the blown calls in the Browns’ direction tended to be on plays where Cleveland committed clear penalties, and the officials refused to throw the flag. The calls against the Jets were largely correct, an indicator of sloppy play that must be cleaned up. The Jets’ passing game was also an issue for a second consecutive week. There is no easy answer as to what is not working when the Jets throw the ball. The poor conditions surely played a role. The offensive line struggled in pass protection, particularly Joe Tippmann, who had maybe his worst game as a pro. The receiving group reached a depth emergency level once Kenyon Sadiq left the game with a concussion. All of the injuries have left the Jets with nobody other than Garrett Wilson showing the ability to produce a big play. And for a second straight week, Geno Smith showed an inability to function in the pocket. Smith can be forgiven for a lack of explosive passing plays given everything just mentioned, but a 14 year veteran needs to be able to navigate the pocket much better, find his outlets, keep the offense on schedule, and avoid taking bad sacks at a rate much better than we have seen from Geno the last two weeks. So there are clear things that need to be cleaned up. The Jets need to cut down on the penalties and get more from their passing game if they want to beat higher caliber opponents going forward. For this week, though, they got just enough to win. This was one of those weeks that was all about survival, and survive they did. Wins are precious things in the NFL. The Jets got one in Week 5, and that should be celebrated.

Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The moment we have all been waiting for: the David Bailey breakout game. Bailey was the No. 2 overall pick in the first round of April’s draft. The highest-drafted defensive player in Jets’ franchise history. Through the first month, he was meh. A plus run defender who also had two sacks. Fine but unspectacular. In Week 5, Bailey was ready to send a very clear message to the Cleveland Browns and a warning to the rest of the NFL: he is here. ESPN’s Rich Cimini shared: “David Bailey’s 8 pressures are tied with several others for 5th-most by a rookie in a game since ESPN began tracking that in 2017. title: Eagles Injury News: DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley have a shot to return against the Panthers
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles might have you feeling down in the dumps after three straight losses … but, hey, here’s some good news, maybe?! Sounds like DeVonta Smith and/or Saquon Barkley could return to the field for Sunday’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers: Smith has missed the Eagles’ last two games due to a […]
full_text: Football: Super Bowl LIX: Philadelphia Eagles DeVonta Smith (6) and Saquon Barkley (26) in action, celebrate vs Kansas City Chiefs at Caesar's Superdome. New Orleans, LA 2/9/2025 CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164676 TK1) The Philadelphia Eagles might have you feeling down in the dumps after three straight losses … but, hey, here’s some good news, maybe?! Sounds like DeVonta Smith and/or Saquon Barkley could return to the field for Sunday’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers: Indications are one, if not both, DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley have a shot to return against the #Panthers , though the #Eagles have to see how the practice week goes. https://t.co/JbVwyvjNRq — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 12, 2026 Smith has missed the Eagles’ last two games due to a hamstring injury. Last week, he was seen doing stretches near the rest of the team during warmups before being unable to participate in practice. I would guess he’s further along than Barkley, who wasn’t spotted at practices last week. Getting either player back — let alone both — would be a positive development for what’s arguably the worst offense in the NFL right now. Barkley’s return would be especially ideal since the Eagles will be without RB2 Tank Bigsby (who’s on injured reserve) and RB3 Will Shipley (who suffered a foot injury on Sunday). If Barkley can’t suit up, the Eagles’ three running backs will be: Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue. At the same time, you don’t want to see the Eagles rushing these players back before they’re truly ready to play or else they risk re-aggravating those hammy injuries. Also, it’s not exactly like the Eagles were crushing it on offense prior to Barkley and Smith getting hurt. Their returns alone will not fix the issues that are plaguing this team. But it certainly works towards pointing the team back in the right direction. The Eagles will hold their first practice in the lead-up to the Panthers game on Wednesday. The injury reports that will be issued then, Thursday, and Friday will be worth monitoring.

title: NFC East coaching catastrophes
summary: As you probably know, the NFC East all played a game this week and went winless, which is impressive because the Giants and Commanders played each other. There hasn’t been a loss-loss-tie trifecta among the Commanders, Cowboys, Eagles, and Giants since 1962. Everyone had a rough week and everyone is to blame. It starts at […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn reacts after the game against the New York Giants at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As you probably know, the NFC East all played a game this week and went winless, which is impressive because the Giants and Commanders played each other. There hasn’t been a loss-loss-tie trifecta among the Commanders, Cowboys, Eagles, and Giants since 1962. Everyone had a rough week and everyone is to blame. It starts at the top. New York Giants 3-1-1 (1-0-1) With 11:05 left in the game, the Commanders converted a two point attempt to take a 14 point lead over the Giants. The Giants rallied to bring the game to 27-26 with 1:43 left in the game. They kicked the PAT. Cowards. John Harbaugh, Super Bowl Winner, Leader of Men™, Culture Changer™, Former Ravens Employer, he wasn’t brought in for feel good ties. He’s not here for moral victories. You don’t change the culture and instill a winning attitude by playing it safe. Aggressive teams and coaches know that down 14 they should go for 2 when they score their first TD . Harbaugh balked twice. While the situations aren’t exactly the same, look at Kentucky Wildcats head coach Will Stein. Both this week and last Kentucky scored in the bottom of the 1st OT inning to bring the game to 34-33. Rather than take his chances in the second OT, he went for two to win the game right then and there. He won both times, getting a big upset of LSU in this weekend of sickos football. Fortune favors the bold. With their second string QB the Giants had a chance to take the lead late on the road against a divisional opponent. John Harbaugh didn’t take it. The Commanders didn’t score in the rest of regulation, and in OT Harbaugh’s kicker missed a FG and his supposed star RB, who has more TV commercials than TDs this season, fumbled the ball. Karma police, arrest this man. Philadelphia Eagles 2-3 (1-0) Much has been made of Nick Sirianni’s decision to kick off short to the Jaguars. There is little (no pun intended) need to revisit that fresh wound except to say that with a roster depleted from injury before the game started and then whittled away during the game through injury and ejection, your kickoff coverage team was already a risk. But the drive leading up to the FG to take the lead was just as brain dead as the decision to kick short. Why do you come out of the Jaguars second time out throwing the ball? Run the ball and force the Jaguars to use their final timeout. Why are you calling a one read play that has the receiver going out of bounds? The last thing you want to do is stop the clock. It should have been Jake Elliott, not Cam Little, kicking with 1 second left in the game. This team is a lethal combination of bad and dumb. Dallas Cowboys 2-3 (1-1) Brian Schottenheimer had no play, possession, or late game sequence in this week that was full of gutlessness or stupidity. But he’s got a whole season of it. The Cowboys have The Greatest Offense There Is. They also have the worst defense there is. Brian Schottenheimer does not seem to know this. On Thursday Tampa dominated time of possession 39:21 to 20:39. The Cowboys had a 21 to 9 pass to run ratio in the first half, and 8-3 in the 3rd quarter. Dak Prescott had 42 pass attempts. The Cowboys are 30th in time of possession, Schottenheimer is gassing his already terrible defense. The Cowboys defense is giving up the worst passer rating in the second half and the 5th most yards per rushing attempt. Only the Bears are giving up more yards per play than the Cowboys in the second half, only the Dolphins have fewer second half sacks. Brian Schottenheimer is a nepo baby, but he’s about the furthest thing from his dad. Washington Football Commanders 1-3-1 (0-2-1) If I owned the Washington Commanders and watched the end of that game I would bring Dan Quinn to my private jet just so I could tarmac him. After getting clobbered by the 49ers next week the Commanders have their bye. Start cleaning out your office Dan.
