title: Eagles vs. Jaguars: 8 winners, 8 losers, 6 IDKs
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles nearly had this game won. Nearly. Instead, they’re 2-3 with the Jacksonville Jaguars handing them their third straight loss. Time to hand out winners, losers, and I don’t knows. For even more analysis, check out my appearance on the PHLY Eagles postgame show along with Vinny Curry, EJ Smith, Anthony Gargano, Bo […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles nearly had this game won. Nearly. Instead, they’re 2-3 with the Jacksonville Jaguars handing them their third straight loss. Time to hand out winners, losers, and I don’t knows. For even more analysis, check out my appearance on the PHLY Eagles postgame show along with Vinny Curry, EJ Smith, Anthony Gargano, Bo Wulf, Fran Duffy, and Miles Johnson! WINNERS JALEN CARTER If you’re looking for a silver lining coming out of this loss, it’s that Jalen Carter is suddenly looking healthier and more effective. That much was likely related to him wearing a less restrictive cast than what was previously necessary due to the hairline fracture in his wrist. This might’ve been the best game of Carter’s career? If not, it’s up there. Carter finished the day with two strip sacks (both of which were recovered by the Jags), three TFLs, and one pass deflection. If he can maintain this level of impact more regularly, that’s a ceiling-raiser for this Eagles defense. Jalen Carter is the first Eagles DT to log multiple strip sacks in one game since Fletcher Cox in 2015. First NFL DT to do it in one game since October 2019. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 11, 2026 The Jaguars held Jalen Carter without a pressure in the second half, increasing his double-team rate from 31.8% in the first half to 47.1% in the second. (Next Gen Stats) — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 11, 2026 DARIUS COOPER Second week in a row where his shine was stolen (in part, at least) by the Eagles losing the game. Curses! Also the second week in a row where Cooper led the Eagles in receiving. His three targets in this game produced two catches for 71 yards, most of which were gained on his 62-yard touchdown reception. DARIUS COOPER 62 YARDS!!! pic.twitter.com/TTJayV78mF — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 11, 2026 Cooper is now up to four touchdowns on seven receptions this season. Seems pretty good to me. Despite his success, four players had more targets than Cooper in this game. He’s a good player who deserves more opportunities. The Eagles need to be more intentional about getting the ball to him. Darius Cooper is the first Eagles WR to reach 4 receiving TDs in the first 5 games of the season since Jeremy Maclin in 2014. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 11, 2026 VIC FANGIO The Eagles surrendered 408 yards, which isn’t great, but they allowed just 19 total points to a team that was averaging 26 points per game entering Week 5. Additional context makes this performance more impressive: The Jags’ first touchdown came after an Eagles turnover on downs. The Jags’ second touchdown came on a drive that started at their own 49-yard line and was capped off by Parker Washington (who’s clearly pretty good) making a ridiculous one-handed grab in the end zone on a Trevor Lawrence fourth down throw. The Jags’ game-winning field goal was scored on a drive where Fangio’s defense didn’t even take the field since Jacksonville’s kick return set up the three points with 0:01 left in the game. The Eagles forced the Jags into two turnovers on downs. The Eagles produced an interception and three forced fumbles. Carter’s two strip sacks both took bounces in the Jags’ favor. The other fumble occurred near the goal line and the officials determined their was no clear recovery, allowing Jacksonville to maintain possession. Going 0/3 on fumble recoveries is bad luck. The Eagles’ defense faced 72 total snaps since the Eagles’ offense can’t actually sustain drives. The Eagles almost won this game because their defense came to play. Fangio seems to be rebounding after a slow start to the season. QUINYON MITCHELL Mitchell is a “virgin” no longer! Due to his previous lack of regular season picks, that’s how Fangio referred to him back in training camp: “He still needs his first interception of his career. He’ll quickly remind you he’s got four in the playoffs, but he’s still a virgin in the regular season.“ Mission accomplished. Mitchell secured an underthrow by Lawrence (just the third interception thrown by him this season) to bail out an Eagles offense that gave the Jags a short field to work with after a turnover on downs. Naturally, the Eagles’ offense gained 15 yards on six plays before having to punt. Anyway, back to Mitchell, he’s been great, which is to be expected. He’s allowed just a 64.6 passer rating when targeted this season. ZACK BAUN Getting Baun back was a big development for this defense. He led the Eagles in total tackles with 11 and tied Arnold Ebiketie for a team-high two quarterback hits. One of those was very nearly a sack; Lawrence was fortunate to throw the ball away at the very last moment before his knee hit the ground. Looking like a heat-seeking missile, Baun prevented a touchdown by blowing up the Jags’ final play of the second quarter: A horrid goal-line sequence for the #Jaguars but a huge stop for the #Eagles . Big time swing before the half. pic.twitter.com/DFHWp4UoSw — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 11, 2026 DONTAYVION WICKS Wicks was targeted eight times for five receptions and 63 yards. Four of those grabs resulted in first downs. He notably helped the Eagles convert: 3rd-and-8 on the Eagles’ first touchdown drive 3rd-and-10 on the Eagles’ first touchdown drive 3rd-and-5 on the Eagles’ final drive Wicks drew a pass interference penalty that turned 3rd-and-goal at the 17-yard line into 1st-and-goal at the 3-yard line, which set up a Will Shipley rushing touchdown. Wicks drew another pass interference penalty that turned a 3rd-and-9 at the Eagles’ 40-yard line into 1st-and-10 at midfield. After a strong first two weeks to start the season, Wicks was quieter over the past two games. He returned as an impactful high-leverage option on Sunday. And he had success despite suffering a hamstring injury that kept him limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. BRITAIN COVEY Covey told the Inquirer that he petitioned the league to wear “Britain” instead of “Covey” on the back of his jersey for Sunday’s game. Covey’s request was denied. Nevertheless, he came up big playing in the country he was named after by logging four punts returns for 42 yards (10.5 average, long of 18) and three kick returns for 92 yards (30.7 average, long of 42). He’s done his part this season to help give a struggling offense good field position to work with. EAGLES FANS The Eagles fans who made the trip to this game deserved better. They created a loud environment that gave the Jags some trouble in terms of getting the snap off properly. The Eagles’ second goal line stand was powered in part by a crowd that contributed to a false start and a delay of game penalty. After the game, Jags players gave props to Eagles fans for making life difficult on them: “Their fans were mental. It was nuts” 👀 Jags Kicker Cam Little on Eagles fans taking over London after his walk off field goal for the Jaguars “It’s a home game for us technically, it was a home game for the Eagles… it was crazy” pic.twitter.com/OmI2sUg9RN — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) October 11, 2026 “I thought it was supposed to be a home game for us” 💚 Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence said he’s never seen fans like Eagles fans overtake 1 of their games in London “Usually we have more fans… This is really the only time I remember it was so lopsided” pic.twitter.com/DzThV0oVjY — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) October 12, 2026 LOSERS NICK SIRIANNI I was prepared to say some nice things about the Eagles’ head coach! The Eagles entered this game as 7.5-point underdogs and came very close to pulling off an upset despite missing a lot of key players due to injury. Unfortunately, Sirianni undid any goodwill he otherwise would’ve earned by mismanaging the end of the…

title: Eagles reportedly bring back defensive tackle on the practice squad
summary: Back from London, the Eagles will need to make several roster moves this week to account for injuries and significant depth issues. One of the first spots to be filled is on the practice squad, with the team re-signing interior defensive lineman Zion Wilson. Wilson was with the Eagles for some of the summer, signing […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images Back from London, the Eagles will need to make several roster moves this week to account for injuries and significant depth issues. One of the first spots to be filled is on the practice squad, with the team re-signing interior defensive lineman Zion Wilson. Source: Eagles are bringing back iDL Zion Wilson to the practice squad. — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) October 12, 2026 Wilson was with the Eagles for some of the summer, signing as an undrafted free agent in June 2026 after playing his collegiate career at Eastern Carolina University. He tried to play one more season for the University of Virginia, but the NCAA denied his waiver for additional eligibility. Here’s what BGN’s Brandon Lee Gowton had to say about Wilson several months ago : “The 6-3, 316 pound Wilson originally played offensive line for ECU with his first game action being a mere three snaps at right guard in 2023. He transitioned to defensive tackle in 2024, where he logged 13 snaps, in addition to playing an occasional fullback role. Wilson finally became a full-time player in 2025, producing 42 total tackles, 10 TFLs, seven sacks, and one pass deflection in 454 defensive snaps played. Wilson might’ve become a draftable player had he been able to play for Virginia this upcoming season. Instead, he joins Eagles in an uphill battle to make the 53-man roster. Making the practice squad would be a good outcome for him so that he gets more time to develop.“ It took a few months for Wilson to get a spot on the practice squad, but he’ll give the Eagles a fresh option.

title: Will Shipley injury: Eagles running back could miss multiple games
summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” and could miss multiple games as a result, according to a report from NFL insider Adam Schefter. Shipley’s injury occurred relatively early during the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While he was not listed on the injury report […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Will Shipley of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles running back Will Shipley suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” and could miss multiple games as a result, according to a report from NFL insider Adam Schefter . Shipley’s injury occurred relatively early during the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While he was not listed on the injury report entering Sunday’s game, he was listed on the report in previous weeks with a foot injury. Normally the Eagles’ third-string running back, Shipley started against the Jags because Saquon Barkley was ruled out due to a hamstring injury and Tank Bigsby was placed on injured reserve. With Shipley expected to miss time, the Eagles currently have two healthy running backs on the roster: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. Pierce logged a team-high 11 carries in Shipley’s absence but he only managed to gain 14 yards in no small part due to an undermanned and struggling offensive line. Steele was limited to special teams duty against the Jags. It remains to be seen if Barkley will be able to return to the field in Week 7. That seems soon to be returning from a hammy. If Barkley can’t suit up, the Eagles will have to ride with Pierce and Steele. Perhaps they’ll call up Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to round out that group. They might also need to sign another running back to the PS for depth purposes. Team health has been a problem for the Eagles this season and Shipley’s injury is just the latest bad news.

title: Eagles-Jaguars Takeaway: Nick Sirianni isn’t helping
summary: It’s a good thing there are more important things in life than the Philadelphia Eagles. If that wasn’t the case, Sunday’s stunning 19-17 loss in London to the Jacksonville Jaguars might have plunged you into a deep, dark depression. The Eagles had somehow overcome a myriad of injuries and, as seven-point underdogs, flown across the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a good thing there are more important things in life than the Philadelphia Eagles. If that wasn’t the case, Sunday’s stunning 19-17 loss in London to the Jacksonville Jaguars might have plunged you into a deep, dark depression. The Eagles had somehow overcome a myriad of injuries and, as seven-point underdogs, flown across the Atlantic Ocean and stunned a superior Jags team with a unclean-but-effective effort to move to 3-2 on the season. Until they hadn’t. The 2026 Eagles roster is not nearly as talented as preceding years, and it’s even less so with all their banged-up players. Now, more than ever, the coaching staff has to do everything in its power to put the players they have in the best positions to succeed. Nick Sirianni cannot be a reason the Eagles are losing games. On Sunday in London, he was. Sirianni admitted this publicly, and to the team, following their heartbreaker of a defeat. “I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game. And that’s what I told the guys,” he said. After Jake Elliott drained a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left in the game to put the Birds up 17-16, Sirianni and special teams coach Michael Clay decided to have Elliott place the ensuing kickoff inside the target zone for a return rather than through the end zone. A touchback would have put the ball at the 35-yard line, about 20-25 yards away from field goal range for Jacksonville’s outstanding long-range kicker, Cam Little. Sirianni was undoubtedly hoping his special teams unit (which had given up a touchdown on the opening kickoff of the game that was called back due to penalties) would tackle returner Ameer Abdullah while at the same time burning most of the remaining time off the clock. In 99 instances out of 100, that’s probably exactly what happens. But with many of the team’s special teams players forced into action on offense and defense due to injuries, that unit was more inexperienced and undermanned. As a result, Abdullah received the kickoff at the 5-yard line and ran it 53 yards into Eagles territory, setting up Little’s stunning 57-yarder with one second left. It probably goes too far to say Sirianni single-handedly lost that game for the Eagles. The offense’s second half struggles (no touchdowns and one field after halftime over the last three weeks) and injuries throughout the roster took their toll. But every fan watching this game was thinking the same thing prior to the kickoff: “Just kick it through the end zone. Just kick it through the end zone.” It’s always fascinating when the fanbase watching a sporting event is all screaming for one strategy while the coaches/managers on the field are thinking something entirely different. It’s also fascinating how often the fans are right, and the best football minds in the country get it so very wrong. Sirianni doesn’t call plays on offense. In fact, Sirianni’s offense doesn’t exist. There isn’t one. He has nothing to do with the defense. His entire job as CEO head coach is to be in charge of in-game decisions exactly like this one. And yet, Sirianni has not executed this part of his job well. Undoubtedly, he looked at recent events around the NFL in making the decision to kick it short of the end zone. On September 27 when the Cowboys lost the Ravens on a last second field goal, the Cowboys had just tied the game with a field goal with under 10 seconds left. Dallas kicked the ball into the end zone, giving the Ravens the ball at the 35-yard line. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers with a 27-yard pass and called a timeout with one second remaining. Baltimore then kicked a shocking game-winning field goal, just as Jacksonville did on Sunday. But Baltimore had a timeout remaining. They could throw the ball in the middle of the field and stop the clock. The Jags were out of timeouts, and would have had to force a long completion outside the hash marks and get out of bounds to stop the clock. That’s an enormous difference that Sirianni and Clay should have factored into the equation. They also seemed to ignore the fact they almost gave up a kickoff return for a touchdown earlier in the game, and were undermanned in that unit. These were all thoughts fans were thinking in the moment. Why wasn’t Sirianni? Why wasn’t someone else? New kickoff rules are admittedly making late-game decisions more difficult for head coaches. Touchbacks used to be at the 30-yard line until last year, when they were moved up to the 35 in order to convince more coaches to encourage returns. And now, with kickers allowed access to special kicking balls before the games, we are seeing more field goals of 55+ yards being made throughout the league. It’s no longer necessary to get the ball to the opposing team’s 35-yard line for a realistic shot at a field goal. Most kickers can hit from 55+ with relative ease, and some can go from 60. The league is happy because endings like Sunday’s in London is exactly what the NFL wants. It was exciting, if you weren’t an Eagles fan. But this is the reason Nick Sirianni is still employed by the Eagles. He can’t run an offense. He can’t run a defense. He’s supposed to have mastery over in-game decisions like this. He’s supposed to know when to go for it on fourth down and when not to. And, no, he’s not going to get every decision correct, simply because he’s asking other grown men to execute his decisions for him. Sometimes, they’re going to fail, even if it is the right decision. No one thought this was the right decision. Not in real time and certainly not in hindsight. Sirianni didn’t let us in on his thought process after the game. It would be helpful for us to know why he did what he did, but he is not required to tell us. He owned the decision, and that’s that. The 2026 season is shaping up to be his most difficult and challenging yet, and there is little margin for error. There is not enough talent on this roster to paper over mistakes by the head coach, especially ones that every fan in the Delaware Valley could see as it unfolded in front of them. The Eagles need Nick Sirianni to be a force multiplier. They need him, as CEO, to give them an edge. Too often this season, he’s done the opposite. If he cannot improve in this most important part of his job, it’s going to be difficult to argue he should continue for much longer.
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles-Jaguars snap counts: Darius Cooper played the most of any wide receiver
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Tanner McKee, John Ojukwu INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Marcus Epps, Jonathan Greenard, Lane Johnson, Drew Kendall
full_text: Philadelphia Eagles' Darius Cooper celebrates a touchdown during the NFL London Games match at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 11, 2026. (Photo by Ben Whitley/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Jordan Mailata is the only player on offense who’s played 100% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps this season. Lining up at center, Jake Majors logged his first career start in his first regular season game played. Lining up at left guard, Willie Lampkin made his first career start. Darius Cooper, WR1! In terms of snaps played, at least. But he also led the Eagles in receiving with 71 yards. And this despite only seeing three targets. Safe to say the Eagles should be more intentional about getting him involved. He’s a good player. Dontayvion Wicks ranked second among pass-catchers in snaps played, targets, and receiving yards. Makai Lemon set career highs in snaps played, targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Making some progress. Will Shipley started the game at running back but he left the game due to a foot injury. Dameon Pierce, previously RB4, filled in as RB1. Playing behind a less than stellar offensive line, his 11 carries resulted in just 14 yards. And his five (?!) targets resulted in two catches for negative two yards. That’s 13 total touches for 12 yards. Not great. Tyler Steen missed some snaps due to a shoulder injury but he was able to return to the game. Fred Johnson filled in at right guard during Steen’s absence. Dallas Goedert saw a smaller playing time workload than usual in his first game back from a knee injury. He did log a team-high eight targets, which produced six receptions for 38 yards. Johnny Mundt continues to be TE2. E.J. Jenkins was TE3 … ahead of Zach Ertz, who was TE4. Ertz saw two targets that resulted in zero catches. Ertz’s eight targets over the last three games had produced three receptions for 22 yards. Is he still getting adjusted to the game after coming off last year’s injury? Or might the 35-year-old be cooked at this point? Elijah Moore has yet to see a target this season and he doesn’t contribute on special teams. Wonder if he might be gone if/when DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown get healthy. Seems like they could probably get him back on the practice squad. DEFENSE Another game where the defense had to be on the field a lot because the offense simply can’t sustain drives. This unit logged 7o snaps in Week 1, 72 in Week 3, 84 in Week 4, and 72 once again in Week 5. They’re going to get worn out at this rate. By contrast, the Eagles’ defense only had to play 53 snaps in Week 2. The NFL lead in opponent plays per game last year was 65.5. Vic Fangio’s defense is seeing 70.2 so far. Zack Baun played his normal workload in his first game back from a concussion. Quinyon Mitchell appeared to be banged up after his interception but he did not miss any playing time. Baun revealed that Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. were set to rotate at linebacker in this game. But that plan was obviously scrapped after Trot Jr. got ejected on the opening kickoff that didn’t even actually count due to penalties. Curious to see what this rotation looks like moving forward. Is it a 50/50 split? With Jalyx Hunt leaving the game with ankle/knee injuries that didn’t look so good, Nolan Smith was easily the Eagles’ top edge rusher. Kenny Moore II saw a decent amount of action due to Michael Carter II suffering an abdomen injury that prevented him from returning to the game. Moro Ojomo saw his second-lowest snap count percentage of the season. Arnold Ebiketie became the Eagles’ second edge rusher after Hunt left the game. He logged a team-high four pressures, according to Pro Football Focus charting. He also missed two tackles. Jordan Davis tied his second-highest snap count percentage of the season. He logged his first quarterback hit of the season in this game. It’s his first QB hit since Week 14 last year. Hunt got hurt on the final play of the second quarter. A.J. Epenesa saw some more snaps than usual with Jonathan Greenard out and Hunt getting hurt. Jonathan Jones was the extra defensive back in the Eagles’ dime packages. Ty Robinson has a tiny role on defense each week. SPECIAL TEAMS Carson Steele was limited to special teams duty in his Eagles regular season debut. Could’ve been nice to find him a touch or two after he had some success in the preseason. Especially since he showed more as a pass-catcher than Dameon Pierce, who inexplicably logged five targets. Rookie quarterback Cole Payton, who moved up to QB3 on the depth chart with the Eagles releasing Andy Dalton, made his NFL regular season debut by playing on special teams. He served as the punt protector. Britian Covey had a productive game with 136 total return yards on three kick returns and four punt returns. He was only 96 yards shy of tying the Eagles’ total yards on offense. The Eagles notably went with Fred Johnson instead of Micah Morris at guard when Steen got hurt. The coaching staff doesn’t appear to trust the rookie to play on offense just yet. As previously noted, Trot Jr. was ejected after the opening kickoff that didn’t even count due to penalties. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Tanner McKee, John Ojukwu INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Marcus Epps, Jonathan Greenard, Lane Johnson, Drew Kendall McKee was reportedly promoted to QB2 last week. There’s no doubt that he’s Jalen Hurts’ backup now that Andy Dalton is gone (for now, at least). Ojukwu was temporarily elevated from the practice squad to give the Eagles an eighth offensive lineman but they didn’t need him to play. Brown, Smith, Barkley, Epps, Greenard, and Kendall all missed the game due to injury. At least some of these guys might be able to play in Week 6. Johnson was not announced among the Eagles’ inactives by the team … but he’s included in this game log. In case you missed it, the recently retired Johnson is reportedly set to remain on the Eagles’ roster for the rest of the season . While understandable due to financial implications, it’s not really ideal that the Eagles will now be working with a 52-man roster (instead of the normal 53) the rest of the way in 2026.

title: Eagles News: “It really hasn’t been a good year for Nick Sirianni”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles need more from their head coach. He’s not providing answers on offense and the game management just hasn’t been good. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations as Eagles suffer unimaginable London loss to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles need more from their head coach. He’s not providing answers on offense and the game management just hasn’t been good. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations as Eagles suffer unimaginable London loss to Jaguars – NBCSP One thing about Nick Sirianni. He’s accountable, and after the game he told his players that this loss was entirely on him because he didn’t have Jake Elliott kickoff into the end zone with eight seconds left. “I didn’t make the right decision,” Sirianni said. “Bad job by me. I lost this game for the team. I cost us this game. I put the loss fully on me. I should never have put them in that situation. I take full responsibility for that.” He’s entirely right, and it’s good that he said it but it really hasn’t been a good year for Sirianni. Whether it’s making the wrong calls on some key fourth downs or this decision at the end of the Jaguars game, he’s had a rough time with these basic decisions. When you’re a head coach that doesn’t call plays, you better get the other stuff right, and he just hasn’t. Nick Sirianni: “I lost us that game” – BGN The Eagles struggled throughout Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, but it was their end-of-game management that drew the most criticism. During his post-game press conference, head coach Nick Sirianni took full accountability for the decision-making that led to the loss, and also talked about the team’s continued second-half struggles. Eagles-Jaguars Postgame: Last-Second COLLAPSE Buries Eagles In London – PHLY Eagles Podcast The Eagles lost to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the most gutting way imaginable. Wasting a game-winning drive from Jalen Hurts and a clutch kick from Jake Elliott, the kickoff coverage unit set up a last-second field goal for the Jags that may not send the Eagles season into a spiral. EJ Smith is joined in-studio by Vinny Curry and Brandon Lee Gowton, a well as Anthony Gargano and Bo Wulf LIVE FROM LONDON to break down Jalen Hurts’ performance and everything else from the game. 3 reasons why the Jaguars beat the Eagles – Big Cat Country Let’s get one thing straight: the Jaguars should have lost this game. Not because Philadelphia were particularly impressive, but because Jacksonville seemed determined to sabotage themselves at every available opportunity. There are bad performances, there are frustrating performances, and then there is whatever the hell the Jaguars served up in North London. Thirteen penalties for 100 yards told only part of the story. Jacksonville’s offense repeatedly found ways to turn promising situations into disasters, with questionable playcalling and sloppy execution threatening to undo everything Trevor Lawrence and company had worked for. The most glaring example came in the fourth quarter, when the Jaguars had first-and-goal at the one-yard line. Three procedural penalties later, they had somehow turned a golden opportunity into a turnover on downs. Considering the way the first half ended in similar circumstances, it was enough to test the faith of even the most ardent fan. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Jaguars game – PhillyVoice Ebiketie should have never had a chance to make that mistake. If Nick Sirianni had Elliott kick the ball through the back of the end zone, the Jaguars would have had the ball at their own 35-yard line, and they would have needed to complete a long-ish pass while also getting out of bounds, and do it in seven seconds or fewer since they were out of timeouts. That was the clear strategy. Instead, Sirianni opted to allow a return, despite the Eagles missing several core special teamers (Jeremiah Trotter, Michael Carter, etc.), and in a game in which the Jags had already returned a kickoff for a touchdown (that was called back because of a hold). Sirianni took blame for the loss after the game. “Our guys fought their butts off today,” Sirianni said. “The defense had an outstanding game, keeping us in that game. The offense did enough at the end to go win us that game. Special teams did a nice job of kicking it there. I didn’t make the right decision and I lost us that game, and that’s what I said to our guys. “What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don’t make the decision that I should make at the end of the game, and I cost us that game and I put that fully on me.” Sirianni doesn’t call plays, and it’s not fully his offense anymore. This is the kind of mistake that he cannot afford to make. Oh the Agony – Iggles Blitz Plenty of people are going to scream about firing Sirianni. I certainly get the frustration. That was an ugly finish. Others are simply ready to give up on the season. I get that as well. This team feels like a mess right now. I want to see how this team looks when somewhat healthy. Get Saquon, DeVonta and Drew Kendall back on offense. Get Jonathan Greenard back on defense. Let me see that group for a week or two. If they still stink, then the season is basically over. We saw enough good things on Sunday that I’m still holding out some hope. And remember the three teams that the Birds just played. Wulf: For Jalen Hurts, game management “not his place” as he fights make sure Philadelphia still is – PHLY Eagles “It’s not my place,” he repeated when asked about the end-of-game sequence again. “We’re prepared, I’m prepared as a quarterback to not worry about those things. I’m honoring the playcaller, honoring the things that are coming in the game. When I’m up at night, I might think about, ‘Should I have said something? Should I have took a step back and said, ‘Wait –’’ But ultimately, there’s a commitment to that in going out there and executing. This was one where it did not work in our favor.” Several players in the locker room insisted the nature of “the ultimate team game” means that Sirianni was not alone in blame for Sunday’s loss. The running backs combined for 20 rushing yards on 16 carries. Hurts and Wicks were unable to connect on an uncovered would-be touchdown. Drew Mukuba was left flailing on Parker Washington’s 51-yard touchdown. But all anyone will remember are the game’s final few plays. “That’s gotta be a question for coach,” Elliott said when asked about his final kickoff, later adding: “I always think you want to end the game with a kick there and not have to go out there and try to cover a kick, but that’s not how it played out unfortunately and go back and look at it and learn from it. It didn’t work this time. It sucks. You come all this way. You think you’re in the driver’s seat to win a big game and now we’re feeling pretty down.” Nick Sirianni’s anemic Eagles offense is a bigger problem than his game management – Inquirer But last season was a step back and this one is starting to look like further regression. And a lot of it points back to Sirianni’s inability to maintain continuity on offense. Hurts is part of that equation. General manager Howie Roseman is, as well. And when the Jimmys and Joes aren’t quite what they used to be, the X’s and O’s matter more, and the Eagles just don’t have the schematic answers right now. Sirianni, ultimately, is responsible, and that will decide his team’s fate more than a few game-management blunders. “That’s going to hurt for a while,” Sirianni said, “but I’m going put my chest out, and I’m going to stick my head up, and I’m going to get better from it.” And, doggone it, the Eagles like him. How long will that carry him through? Nick Sirianni took the blame in London. If blunders continue, will he be held responsible? – The Athletic “I don’t even know what that means now,” left tackle Jordan Mailata said. “I…

title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Steelers rebounded well from a Week 4 loss, defeating the Colts in Pittsburgh 34-22 to advance to 3-2 on the 2026 season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers needed a star on offense — and they finally found one When discussing the shortcomings of the Steelers’ offense […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers rebounded well from a Week 4 loss, defeating the Colts in Pittsburgh 34-22 to advance to 3-2 on the 2026 season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers needed a star on offense — and they finally found one When discussing the shortcomings of the Steelers’ offense in recent years, the biggest emphasis has usually been the team’s lack of franchise quarterback. In a league that’s still heavily passer-driven, that’s an accurate takeaway. But recently, I’ve thought that the Steelers have also lacked a true “star” on offense at a skill position over the years — a running back or pass-catcher who could elevate whoever else is on the offense, and single-handedly win a game from time to time. Since the Steelers’ “Killer B” era, there have been some failed attempts to find that player: JuJu Smith-Schuster couldn’t handle the WR1 role, Najee Harris didn’t live up to first-round expectations, and George Pickens didn’t find consistency — something the Steelers’ latest attempt at a star, D.K. Metcalf, has arguably struggled with even more. Some of the team’s struggles on offense over the years have not only been due to a rotating door of quarterbacks and offensive linemen, but also a supporting cast of skill position players who couldn’t be relied upon to consistently provide a spark. And while he’s just had a handful games in a leading role so far this season, Warren has looked the part of that missing star in each one. Despite starting the year in a timeshare with Rico Dowdle, Warren still ranks third in the entire league this season in yards from scrimmage, with gains of at least 20 yards in each of his last four outings. Against the Colts, Warren managed his best game of the season thus far, taking a short pass 80 yards for a score in the second quarter, and later breaking off a 50-yard run for another touchdown in the third. He finished Sunday with 15 carries for 101 yards rushing along with 87 yards and a touchdown as a receiver. With Dowdle due for a return soon, Warren’s workload should decrease in coming weeks. But if the Steelers play their cards right, that could also be a boon for the offense. Warren has earned a clear RB1 workload going forward, but some more rest down the stretch might help his big-play ability stay fresh. 2. Keeanu Benton earns his paycheck The Steelers signed defensive tackle Keeanu Benton to a four-year, $72 million extension this offseason after a breakout 5.5-sack season in 2025. And although Benton certainly hasn’t been bad in 2026, he’s yet to record a single sack through five games in a middle-of-the-pack Steelers defense — failing to make the kind of impact you’d ideally like to see from an $18 million per year defensive tackle. But against the Colts — facing a superstar runner in Jonathan Taylor and without Derrick Harmon on the defensive line — Benton had his best performance of the year. His stat line versus Indianapolis was good, with three tackles, one stuff, and one pass defensed, but the eye test showed a much larger impact. And Taylor was held to just 45 yards on 15 carries. Benton was constantly involved in clogging up Taylor’s running lanes, being one of the biggest reasons why a second-quarter goal-line stand from the Pittsburgh defense nearly succeeded. Benton also recorded a quarterback hit and contributed to several other pressures of Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. Benton gets double-teamed a lot more than most realize, but when he isn’t getting a heavy dose of defensive attention, he remains an above-average pass rusher for his position. How often DTs are double teamed and their grading on those plays pic.twitter.com/OSV04TyAl4 — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) October 8, 2026 With Harmon on injured reserve and Cameron Heyward not getting any younger, Benton’s performance against the Colts was a promising one as his importance to the Steelers defense continues to increase. 3. Cornerback duo shows some fight It’s fair to say this was not the 2026 the Steelers expected when it came to the secondary. Joey Porter Jr. is in Dallas. DeShon Elliott is up to five games missed on injured reserve. And Jamel Dean has struggled with an ankle injury that kept him out against the Colts. But on Sunday, the remaining defensive backs did just enough to secure the win. It wasn’t always pretty. Daniel Jones completed 24 passes for 267 yards, with tight end Tyler Warren having a productive day with seven catches for 83 yards. Four Colts pass-catchers logged 20-plus yard gains. Still, Pittsburgh’s starting duo of boundary cornerbacks in Daylen Everette and Asante Samuel Jr. — neither were supposed to start this year, for what it’s worth — combined for a whopping six passes defensed in a game where they were tested by Jones’ 44 passing attempts. One of those pass deflections, a deep pass where the rookie Everette appeared to get beat badly but did an excellent job of recovering on a clearly underthrown pass, was a microcosm of the group’s performance on Sunday: An imperfect but promising group that won’t always get the Alec Pierce-less Colts as an opponent. “Uh oh… UH OH- ah thank god” -me watching this live pic.twitter.com/QNs1YXUH93 — Chris Ferland 🐝 (@chris_ferland) October 11, 2026 Samuel had a few more highlights, creating a whopping four pass breakups. He’s always been a playmaker at defensive back, with six interceptions and 35 passes defensed through his first three full NFL seasons with the Chargers. He can be a bit of feast or famine player at times, notably struggling with the Bengals’ Tee Higgins in Week 3, but continues to come more into his own after spinal fusion surgery and the resulting rehabilitation kept him off the field for much of 2024 and 2025. Pittsburgh has been a zone-heavy team this season as a result of how shorthanded it is in the secondary — a style of coverage where chemistry and communication can make up for some shortcomings in athleticism and ability. But with Everette’s inexperience and the number of personnel changes so far this season, there have been some expected rough points. Rookie mistake here by Daylen Everette as he trails the post when play the deep third responsibility in the Cover 3, opening up Warren on the out & up route down the sideline. Everette needs to trust that his post safety is gonna take that post and pass this off. #HereWeGo pic.twitter.com/WZw8JPd1rC — Jack Sperry (@jack_sperry) October 12, 2026 With far more high-powered passing offenses looming on the Steelers’ later-season schedule, Pittsburgh certainly has some holes to fix. But Sunday’s performance showed some promise with the usual issues, and Elliott and Dean should return at some point. 4. The Steelers pulled away when it mattered Entering the Steelers-Colts game, I wrote that both teams were fairly evenly-matched. The rosters have some similarities with both franchises straddling the line between flirting with contender status and rebuilding in recent seasons. And as expected, the two teams served up an entertaining game with a number of back and forths despite the two-possession margin at the end. However, the Steelers were able to pull away in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh outscored Indianapolis 10-3 in the final frame, with the defense forcing a red zone field goal and two turnovers on downs on the Colts’ final three drives. We’ve been writing about how the Steelers need to embrace their “ bully ball ” potential to thrive this season, and to do so, they need to be able to bully teams at the end of games. And on Pittsburgh’s final drive, starting with 2:35 left in the game, Warren was able to log six- and five-yard runs to get the team to victory formation and run out the clock. It might not be a performance that falls in the “clutch” category, but Pittsburgh consistently performed the best on Sunday when it mattered the most — including holding the Colts to four-of-15 on third downs. That’s a good sign with plenty of…

title: BTSC Monday Night Football thread: Bills at Rams

title: Mike McCarthy gives Jaylen Warren update every Steelers fan wanted
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is quietly becoming one of the best running backs in the NFL. The league nationally may not be taking notice, but Warren is receiving high praise in Pittsburgh from every facet of the game. The 5-foot-8 running back has been the Steelers’ most impressive offensive weapon over the past […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is quietly becoming one of the best running backs in the NFL. The league nationally may not be taking notice, but Warren is receiving high praise in Pittsburgh from every facet of the game. The 5-foot-8 running back has been the Steelers’ most impressive offensive weapon over the past three weeks, combining for 490 scrimmage yards. He’s taken advantage of and made the most of the opportunity presented to him with Rico Dowdle missing time due to a toe injury. Dowdle is progressing well and is expected back this week. What does it mean for Warren? At his weekly press conference on Monday, Mike McCarthy was asked how the Steelers will utilize the “one-two punch” of Warren and Dowdle moving forward. McCarthy doesn’t necessarily view the duo as a “one-two punch” and shared his confidence level in Warren. “Jaylen’s our featured player right now,” McCarthy said . “Let’s make sure we all recognize that. He’s hot, he’s playing great football for us.” On the second possession against Indianapolis on Sunday, Warren took a quick pass 80 yards to the end zone and was untouched past the 50-yard line. He rushed for 101 yards in the 34-22 victory over the Colts and scored Pittsburgh’s first touchdown on the ground with a 50-yard scamper to the end zone halfway through the third quarter. Warren is on pace for over 2,100 scrimmage yards this season. “It’s important for us as an offense, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays,” McCarthy said. “That won’t change.” Warren recorded a season-high 21 touches after 20 in each of the previous two weeks. The head coach noted the Steelers had the ball offensively for 54 official plays and would like to be in the high 60s and 70s. McCarthy said Dowdle looked good Friday and Saturday and is close to returning on Sundays. Jaylen Warren with the 80-yard touchdown! @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q49IxXTuCP — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 He didn’t want to put a strict number of carries or touches on Warren’s plate and commit to a particular path forward. “I’m not going to pick at numbers; it depends on the game. Who you’re playing and what’s going on in the game,” McCarthy said. “At the end of the day, we want to win the game, so let’s just start there. Whatever it takes to win the game, that will be our approach this week.” Warren owns 410 yards rushing and 230 yards receiving through the first five games of the season. He has played at least 87% of the snaps over the last three weeks in Dowdle’s absence. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: The Steelers’ offense has found its formula
summary: Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers have found their groove offensively. After a slow start in Weeks 1 and 2, Pittsburgh has fielded one of the NFL’s best offenses over the last three weeks. Per Sumer Sports, the Steelers have the fourth-highest EPA per play since Week 3, trailing only the Detroit Lions, Atlanta […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers have found their groove offensively. After a slow start in Weeks 1 and 2, Pittsburgh has fielded one of the NFL’s best offenses over the last three weeks. Per Sumer Sports , the Steelers have the fourth-highest EPA per play since Week 3, trailing only the Detroit Lions, Atlanta Falcons, and Cincinnati Bengals. Aaron Rodgers has stacked solid performances, as well, ranking a respectable 13th in the league in EPA per play (of all QBs with 10 snaps) over this three-week span, ahead of Dak Prescott, Josh Allen, and Matthew Stafford. His nine touchdown passes are the most in the league since Week 3, and his 827 yards rank seventh. Not bad for a quarterback we are constantly told is too old to lead a team to any sort of relevancy. The real takeaway, though, is just how dominant the Steelers have been on the ground in this three-week span. They trail only the Atlanta Falcons in EPA per rush since Week 3, and their 5.58 yards per carry leads the NFL. Which brings us to. the man of the hour, Jaylen Warren, who has almost single-handedly taken the Steelers from a nondescript offense and given them a sense of self. Over the last three games, Warren has shown the Steelers, and the entire league, what he is capable of when he is used as the dual-threat every-down bell cow many have longed for him to be. In that span, Warren is first in total EPA among all running backs to have at least 10 touches. Not Bijan Robinson. Not Jahmyr Gibbs. Not Derrick Henry. Jaylen Warren. Additionally, he is second in total rush EPA, second in rushing yards, second in impact place, second in yards per carry, third in missed tackles forced, and he leads all running backs in receiving yards. The win over the Colts was Warren’s magnum opus, as it was his first with over 100 yards rushing and 50 receiving. Per Zachary Smith , his 87 receiving yards are a new career high, as well. The Steelers have found what works – feed No. 30 in both the run game and short passing game, and allow his efficiency to be what sets up the intermediate passing game. It helps Rodgers stay clean, as teams can’t just pin their ears back and send five or six rushers when Warren is a threat to catch a swing pass on every play, or beat a blitz out of the backfield to bust a long run. It took a few weeks of getting the math right, but Pittsburgh found a formula that works. It’s the morning after game day, and the Steelers offense is capital G Good. Welcome to the show, Germie Bernard The Steelers leaned heavily on Germie Bernard, and he came through when called upon. The rookie caught six passes for 80 yards. His 2.42 yards per route run ranked ahead of Ja’Marr Chase, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Malik Nabers, and Justin Jefferson in Week 5, and his role continues to grow as the season goes on. With both Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson down for multiple weeks, and DK Metcalf’s struggles continuing, Bernard could end up being the Steelers’ top target by season’s end, which could be a big net positive. Pat Freiermuth chasing Steelers history The rebirth of Pat Freiermuth in the Steelers’ offense has been a delight. He is currently on pace for 65 catches and 14 touchdowns – his current career high is seven. Back in June , I wrote about Freiermuth being the biggest beneficiary of the Mike McCarthy hire due to his track record of getting high-level production out of tight ends, and so far that’s been the case. And after his performance on Sunday, Freiermuth passed Bennie Cunningham for second place in franchise history. Freiermuth is back in full form, and the offense has benefited greatly from his resurgence. Quick hitters The offensive line was tremendous. Rodgers had the lowest pressure percentage of all quarterbacks to take at least 10 snaps in Week 5. Secondary still needs work. Jaquan Brisker’s play is concerning. That said, they are out there without Jamel Dean and leaning heavily on rookie Daylen Everette. Hopefully DeShon Elliott returns soon. Lack of pressure from the edge rushers is also a concern. Nick Herbig has zero sacks through five games. Need more from him. Asante Samuel had two big pass breakups in the end zone. He has been far from perfect, but promising plays from No. 22. title: NFC West standings, Week 5: Seahawks stay ahead of Rams after another special teams disaster
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have the odds against them to retain their NFC West title after losing to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but they’re still in better shape than the Los Angeles Rams, who will have to wait at least another two weeks to finally get above .500 on the season. In a […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks may have the odds against them to retain their NFC West title after losing to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but they’re still in better shape than the Los Angeles Rams, who will have to wait at least another two weeks to finally get above .500 on the season. In a Monday Night Football thriller, the Buffalo Bills defeated the preseason odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl by a score of 37-34 in overtime. It was a bit of a slow burner at the beginning but descended into pure chaos and shootout football. When the Bills took the lead at 34-27 inside of two minutes, no soul thought the Bills defense could stop Matthew Stafford in a two-minute drill. Not only did the Rams get the touchdown, they didn’t even need the timeout they still had in their pocket. With five seconds left, the Rams decided to… go for the tie? Play for overtime? The Bills defense wasn’t doing anything to stop the Rams passing attack! RAMS TIE IT UP WITH FIVE SECONDS LEFT! @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ViqY7rqb2Z — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 The Bills had the ball first in overtime, nearly breaking one for a long touchdown when Khalil Shakir was just barely tripped up by Kam Kinchens. It was a heroic play by Kinchens to prevent a Buffalo TD to go up 41-34. On the next play, James Cook, who’d already fumbled once, fumbled again and the Rams recovered. FUMBLE 🚨Nate Landman punches it out and Aaron Donald recovers! @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oUWPBMxS6h — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Game over, right? Nope. McVay bizarrely got ultra conservative when the Rams made it into field goal range, knowing full well that Harrison Mevis had missed a field goal already and has been struggling in recent weeks. From 48 yards for the win… BLOCKED by Greg Rousseau! BLOCKED 🛑 Bills still have a chance! @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EbeYqj6ZgJ — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Josh Allen undressed the Rams vaunted defense and Tyler Bass hit the winning field goal. The Rams started the night giving up a massive kick return, which led to Buffalo’s opening drive field goal, and ended the night with two more missed Mevis field goals to cap off another dismal special teams performance. I guess they were exempt from the “super team” billing. McVay turtled up for no reason at the end of regulation and then trusted his 32nd ranked special teams unit over his MVP quarterback against a bad defense. And he is very much pissed. This is about as upset as I’ve seen Sean McVay after a game. He blames himself for the conservative third and five call in OT and kicking the long field goal. There will likely be special teams changes this week. pic.twitter.com/Y06H3vLON1 — Arash Markazi (@ArashMarkazi) October 13, 2026 Here’s what this result means for the NFC West! NFC West standings, Week 5 San Francisco 49ers (5-0, 3-0 DIV) – Next game: vs. Washington Commanders (MNF) Seattle Seahawks (3-2, 1-1 DIV) – Next game: at Denver Broncos (TNF) Los Angeles Rams (2-3, 0-1 DIV) – Next game: at Arizona Cardinals Arizona Cardinals (1-4, 0-2 DIV) – Next game: vs. Los Angeles Rams We can eliminate the Cardinals, just ‘cuz. This three-team race is looking shaky for Seattle and very shaky for the Rams, but here’s the good news for the Rams: they play the Cardinals next. In fact, the only above .500 team they play until their Week 11 bye is the 3-2 Las Vegas Raiders. They’ll probably still go on a run, but if the 49ers and Seahawks don’t drop off any time soon, the unbeatable squad of superstars may find themselves still in third place by the end of November. And to wrap this late night post up, I hope the NFL finally suspends Alaric Jackson. Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe — ESPN (@espn) October 13, 2026 Thank you, Buffalo!

title: Snap Reactions: Many Seahawks 2024 draftees seeing reduced roles
summary: For the third season in a row, the Seattle Seahawks have opened 3-2, matching the record of each of the previous two seasons through the first five games. Interestingly, and meaningless, the Seahawks are 0-3 in Week 5 under Mike Macdonald, having now lost to the New York Giants, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the […]
full_text: For the third season in a row, the Seattle Seahawks have opened 3-2, matching the record of each of the previous two seasons through the first five games. Interestingly, and meaningless, the Seahawks are 0-3 in Week 5 under Mike Macdonald, having now lost to the New York Giants, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the San Franicsco 49ers in Week 5 during that stretch. Now, of course, the question becomes how Seattle will respond, as in 2024 the team went 1-3 over their next four games, while in 2025 they rattled off four wins in a row. Sunday against the 49ers the biggest issue was, for the second time in three games, turnovers. Of the 32 points the 49ers put on the board, 21 came following a Seahawks turnover, and just like against the Washington Commanders in Week 3, giving the opponent easy points over and over will far too often lead to a loss in the NFL. On the subject of turnovers, the running backs on the roster have struggled mightily with fumbles so far this season. Jadarian Price is on injured reserve, but fumbled twice in three games. Emanuel Wilson has fumbled twice. And George Holani has fumbled twice. There’s not a whole lot to say about that other than that one should expect ball security to be a priority coaching point for the running backs in the coming weeks. To that point, though, it’s worth pointing out that even as the running backs the Seahawks put on the field continue to fumble left and right, Velus Jones has played just two offensive snaps so far this season meaning anyone hoping for a spark from his 4.31 speed may be disappointed. Elsewhere on the offense, the rotation between 2024 third-round pick Christian Haynes and 2026 fifth-round pick Beau Stephens at right guard continued in Week 5, with a 52/48 split. The percentage of snaps Stephens has played has very slowly, but steadily, increased over the four games the Hawks have used the rotation. Week 2: 39% Week 3: 40% Week 4: 42% Week 5: 48% The increase is certainly small, and it could be nothing more than randomness as a result of the combination of small sample sizes and game flow. That said, it’s worth watching in Week 6 to see if Stephens passes Haynes for playing time. At receiver and tight end,, the 2025 draft class continues to lag behind outside additions with Tory Horton and Elijah Arroyo combining for only 31 offensive snaps and a lone target. On the defensive side of things, Ty Okada played 56 snaps in his first action this season, while Rodney Thomas was effectively relegated to special teams after playing all but two defensive snaps over the first four weeks of the season. Elsewhere, a couple of the bigger name free agent acquisitions saw the field sparingly, with Dante Fowler and Trevon Diggs playing just nine and eight snaps, respectively. Meanwhile, in the secondary, 2024 fifth-round selection Nehemiah Pritchett saw his lowest playing time on defense so far this year with just four snaps, while playing the highest percentage of special teams snaps he has logged to this point of the 2026 campaign. Meanwhile, 2024 fourth-round pick Tyrice Knight saw the field for the first time since Week 2 when Drake Thomas briefly left the game with an ankle injury. As for special teams, Brady Russell led the Seahawks with 28 special teams snaps, with Mike Morris and Connor O’Toole coming in just behind at 26 snaps. Rodney Thomas, Patrick O’Connell and Velus Jones rounded out the top five with 21 special teams snaps each. And now it’s on to the Denver Broncos in Week 6.

title: Seahawks Droppings: Seattle practices self-flagellation, falls farther behind 49ers in NFC West
summary: The 2026 Seattle Seahawks are not a great team. At this point last season, neither were the 2025 Seattle Seahawks. This 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers had a similar feeling to last year’s Week 5 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle once again lost a game that they should’ve won, besieged […]
full_text: The 2026 Seattle Seahawks are not a great team. At this point last season, neither were the 2025 Seattle Seahawks. This 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers had a similar feeling to last year’s Week 5 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle once again lost a game that they should’ve won, besieged by turnovers on offense. They had the chance to win it at the end, but couldn’t close the deal. Just like last season, this loss drops the Seahawks to 3-2 with both teams having an early season home loss against the Niners. Seattle went on a huge run after Week 5 last season, going 14-1 over the rest of the year. As much as I would love the Seahawks to do that again, it’s highly unrealistic. Point blank, they have to play better on offense. The score makes it look like the defense got shredded, but anyone who watched it knows that they actually played really well. It was the offensive turnovers that put them in a hole. Three TD drives spanning a total of less than 30 yards will be hard to overcome. Settling for 5 FGs also is usually a recipe for failure. Even one more TD on any of those drives would’ve totally changed the game. You can wish in one hand and take a dump in the other…see which one fills up first. Seahawks Droppings Turnovers are always a factor, and they’re seen by some as lazy analysis . However, it’s a huge factor with the Seahawks under Mike Macdonald. Seattle took excellent care of the ball at the end of the season in 2025 which was a massive reason for their Super Bowl victory. Darnold’s INTs are a problem. The RB fumbles were even more egregious. Honestly, we were spoiled with Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet. Those two just did not cough the ball up. Both Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani fumbled once. Holani tried to fumble another time as he was running down the sideline and just dropped the ball. Seattle won’t be the team they want until they take care of the damn ball. Brace yourselves for a “Sam Darnold Conversation” if he keeps playing like this. Darnold will want an extension in the offseason. John Schneider has made very tough QB decisions in the past. Brian Fleury was brought in to keep Seattle playing “Seahawks Football” which means running the ball and being efficient in the passing game. Might there be another QB out there (or already on the roster) who could play that way at a fraction of the price? Jason Myers made all of his FGs and extra points, which is nice. The fact that they had to rely on him that much is never a good thing. Seattle’s offense needs to find a way to come out with TDs. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is still the only viable threat for the Seahawks offense, with five catches for 102 yards and 1 TD . Sure, he had an uncharacteristic drop on third down in the final drive. Realistically, Seattle wouldn’t have even been in the game without him. Brian Fleury needs to find a way to get others more involved. Please throw the ball to Tory Horton. Seattle’s defense kept them in the game by forcing two turnovers in the third quarter . I just wish they would’ve been able to stop Mike Evans on that 49ers drive that spanned the end of the third quarter and early fourth quarter. He was the only one doing anything for San Francisco, making ridiculous contested catches. The one thing that the defense is still struggling with is limiting teams to FGs when in the red zone. Byron Murphy was great today with two sacks. Nick Emmanwori played well. Ty Okada made impact plays in his first game back. Ernest Jones was effective. Nehemiah Pritchett was a factor again with a great read on his INT. Seattle’s defense has the horses to replicate last season’s success, but it hasn’t all come together. The offensive line got pushed around most of the game, giving up five sacks. They had some push in the run game during the third quarter, but Seattle only ran for 89 yards total. That’s not playing Seahawks football. Mike Macdonald brought up how they’re not playing complementary football in his postgame presser. The run game is a massive part of that. This game was a specific brand of frustrating Seahawks football. On one hand they played like garbage and probably should’ve been blown out. On the other, they were in position to win the game and were in my opinion the better team. I didn’t see anything about the 49ers that screamed NFL Superpower. If the Seahawks don’t step on their own junk, they probably win that game by double digits. As it is, they didn’t win the game and now fall farther behind the 49ers in the NFC West. Seattle needs to get their heads out of there a—es if they have any shot of being competitive in the NFC this year.
author: Ted Zahn

title: Turnovers continue to be the Seahawks’ biggest problem under Mike Macdonald
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have only lost three games dating back to last November; the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders bested Seattle by a combined eight points. You know what else happened? Seattle gave the ball away a lot, namely Sam Darnold, but he’s not the only guilty party. Those three losses […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after an interception against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have only lost three games dating back to last November; the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders bested Seattle by a combined eight points. You know what else happened? Seattle gave the ball away a lot, namely Sam Darnold, but he’s not the only guilty party. Those three losses saw the Seahawks lose the turnover battle by a combined 11-4, with Darnold responsible for eight of those giveaways through his interceptions. But while Darnold deserves his fair share of criticism for his clear issue with ball security, the over-arching story continues to be Seattle’s outright negligence in terms of protecting the football. There have been few consistent weaknesses to point to under Mike Macdonald since he became head coach in 2024. The one thing that has been a problem for almost every portion of the Macdonald Era has been turnovers, particularly in high volume. The Seahawks have turned it over at least twice a whopping 20 times since 2024 I tweeted this stat earlier this afternoon and might as well share it here, because you do not want the Seahawks lumped in with the Cleveland Browns in any negative stat. Today marked the 20th time under Mike Macdonald in which the Seahawks turned it over 2+ times. Only the Cleveland Browns have done that more often since 2024. Week 18 vs SF through Week 1 this year is the ONLY time the Seahawks have gone consecutive games without a TO under MM. — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 12, 2026 (H/T Stathead ) You read that right (you did read it, right?): Seattle has turned it over at least twice in a game a whopping 20 times since 2024. That’s 20 times out of 39 regular season games and obviously 20 out of 42 overall games when you count the playoffs. About half of every game of the Macdonald era has been a multi-giveaway day for the Seahawks, so much so that one of those games was when Riq Woolen fumbled his last Seahawks interception right back to the Minnesota Vikings. But you can get away with turnovers up 26-0; you can’t do what Seattle has done twice already this season. As already noted in the tweet, the Seahawks have not so much as gone consecutive games without a turnover outside of the stretch from Week 18 against the San Francisco 49ers in 2025 through Week 1 against the New England Patriots this season . The five-game run the Seahawks had to win the NFC West, win the Super Bowl, and win on banner-raising night is the outlier, not the new norm under Macdonald. It’s easy to point to Darnold and Geno Smith (0 interceptions through five games playing in the Jets offense, by the way!) as the culprits. Yes, they have/had their turnover woes and are the main catalysts statistically, but I wish it was as simple as blaming the quarterback. The Seahawks cannot stop fumbling The Seahawks led the NFL in fumbles last season, although a lot of that was down to Sam Darnold strip sacks and some botched QB-center exchanges. They've already fumbled six times in four weeks and have been fortunate to only lose two. It's all about the ball! pic.twitter.com/HRmS7ENIhN — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 9, 2026 I wrote this up two days ago and it was prophetic. Three more fumbles, one of which George Holani self-forced, and two were recovered by the 49ers. Seattle has nine fumbles through five games and Darnold doesn’t even have one yet. The running back room has collectively fumbled six times in four games, which is wholly unacceptable. It’s a nice reminder of the airtight ball security Kenneth Walker and Zach Charbonnet showed as a tandem, and we won’t see Charbonnet until Week 7. Rashid Shaheed has fumbled twice on kick returns but been fortunate that neither was lost. Seattle has ranked top 10 in fumbles in each of Macdonald’s seasons, including numero uno in 2025. Fumble recoveries can generally be pinned on luck when you’ve got an oblong ball bouncing crazy directions on the field, but Seattle invites danger by having a high rate of fumbling. And shitty ball security is shitty ball security no matter who’s responsible, and the 2024 Seahawks special teams infamously gave us the duo of Dee Williams and Laviska Shenault Jr, both of whom were axed in December for the single worst display of kick return duties I’ve ever seen. Dee Williams has muffed a couple punts this year but this is first fumble on a kickoff. Regardless, ball security not where it should be for the rookie returner pic.twitter.com/jtgk12P3G2 — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) December 1, 2024 Laviska Shenault Jr with his 3rd fumble on a kickoff. This is the second one he’s lost. pic.twitter.com/OQUcxlgRI3 — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) December 1, 2024 Neither Sam Darnold nor Geno Smith is Russell Wilson in terms of ball security The upside of Russell Wilson’s style of football when he was Seahawks quarterback was a low interception rate. Unfortunately, the trade-off was a perennially high sack rate and those often functioned as turnovers, but when it was time to throw, Wilson usually took exceptional care of the ball. There were sack fumbles and botched exchanges occasionally, but the Seahawks were a low turnover team and he was a low turnover QB. Just as it was unreasonable to think Geno Smith wouldn’t toss a few careless ones away with his gun-slinging style, the same holds for Darnold. These are two reformed draft busts who are willing to take chances in a way Russ generally didn’t, and frankly neither of them has an extensive track record as a high-level quarterback. Every year in which Sam has been a full-time starter he’s thrown double-digit picks. In 2024 and 2025 he made up for it by being insanely productive and a deadly deep passer. We’re not seeing that right now and there are diminishing returns coming alongside those giveaways. Now, is it reasonable to have Sam not lead the league in turnovers again and be closer to his Minnesota Vikings form in terms of a 2.2% interception rate? Absolutely. But even in calmer waters there is probably an acceptance that even the best version of Darnold is not going to be the type of QB who is a low- or even moderate-turnover guy. This means that the environment around him (a competent run game, other players not fumbling, having a great defense to keep scores favorable) must be stronger than it would be for an elite QB in order to keep positively producing. Seattle only has a great defense and isn’t anywhere close on the other two. The Seahawks are not playing complementary football right now, and what figured to be a squashed problem during their postseason performance has returned in terrifying fashion. If the end of last season was the unusual blip in the trend, then the Seahawks are going to be at risk of this season looking a lot more like 2024 than 2025. You can focus your disappointment and ire primarily at Sam Darnold right now, but the turnovers are a team-wide issue that is seemingly getting worse.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 08: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams talks with Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills after the Rams defeated the Bills, 44-42, at SoFi Stadium on December 08, 2024 in Inglewood, California. The 3-1 Buffalo Bills are off their first loss of the season. Buffalo led 26-21 late in the fourth quarter before Drake Maye drove the field to score in less than three minutes and take the lead for good. The Eagles went 1-for-16 on late downs and averaged three yards per play. We’ll go out on a limb and say Josh Allen fares a little bit better than that. But Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford scored 44 against the Bills two years ago. Puka Nacua and Kyren Williams had field days. This iteration of the Bills defense isn’t much better. They’re 29th in rushing and passing success rate. Josh Allen won’t have D.J. Moore. If anything, that should make Joe Brady lean on James Cook and the running game even more. As fun as it is, hero ball against the Rams’ corners probably won’t cut it. It should be high-scoring, full of variance. If these teams are converting their fourth downs, they could score 40.

It’s reasonable to assume we won’t see Deebo until after the Niners’ […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will be down another wide receiver for “at least a couple of weeks”, according to Kyle Shanahan. Shanahan said Samuel “got pretty good” when speaking about his injury. The 49ers face the Commanders and Falcons before their bye week. It’s reasonable to assume we won’t see Deebo until after the Niners’ bye. Ian Rapoport said Deebo pulled his hamstring and is expected to miss “several weeks.” Christian Kirk has yet to return from a preseason injury that happened on the first day. Demarcus Robinson is on the injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain . The Niners will have to get to the bye week with what’s on the roster in-house. On Sunday, Mike Evans led the way with 36 snaps. Deebo and Jacob Cowing played 25 snaps. Brandin Cooks was next at 21, while Jordan Watkins played 20, but ran a team-low nine routes. A trade for a receiver at the deadline feels like the kind of move that cements the Niners as Super Bowl contenders. Linebacker Garret Wallow also has a hamstring injury that’ll sideline him for a bit. The 49ers can’t seem to escape a game without losing meaningful players to injuries. Nick Martin is “getting close” to returning. Shanahan said that is “something we’ll probably look into in these next couple of days” regarding bringing the second-year linebacker back from the injured reserve. There is some good news on the injury front. Nick Bosa “has a chance” to play next Monday night against the Commanders. The same is true for fullback Kyle Juszczyk and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. All three players will be evaluated as the week goes along. They are “all in the same boat.”
