title: Dre Greenlaw was suspended for violating the ‘principles of sportsmanship’
summary: The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for one game after a headbutt on Seattle Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones: According to the league, Greenlaw was in violation of Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” Greenlaw will be eligible […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for one game after a headbutt on Seattle Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones: According to the league, Greenlaw was in violation of Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” Greenlaw will be eligible to return to the 49ers’ active roster on Tuesday, October 20, following the team’s October 19 game against the Washington Commanders. Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, Greenlaw may appeal the suspension. Any appeal will be heard and decided upon by either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash, the hearing officers jointly appointed and compensated by the NFL and NFLPA to decide appeals of on-field player discipline. There was some good back-and-forth about whether there would be any further punishment for Greenlaw. If Greenlaw was a first-time offender, perhaps he would’ve gotten away with it. But that feels like a stretch. His last name and history don’t help Dre in this instance, but it’s hard to imagine anybody else not receiving a similar punishment. So, it’ll be Jaden Dugger and Luke Gifford against Washington. Dugger was great against the Seahawks and played like a player who shouldn’t come off the field. Gifford had some issues playing on the line of scrimmage. If Nick Bosa returns, the 49ers may be able to play their 5-man fronts without Gifford. According to Ian Rapoport, Greenlaw will appeal the suspension.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 3 lessons we learned from the 49ers’ win over Seattle: The bullies are back
summary: The San Francisco 49ers punched, got punched, and punched back on their way to their fifth consecutive victory in 2026 with a hard-fought, message-sending win over the defending Super Bowl champions. From the first play, the 49ers were hell-bent on sending a message: the bullies are still here, and last year was last year. The […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers punched, got punched, and punched back on their way to their fifth consecutive victory in 2026 with a hard-fought, message-sending win over the defending Super Bowl champions. From the first play, the 49ers were hell-bent on sending a message: the bullies are still here, and last year was last year. The team survived a momentum swing in Seattle’s favor and responded with two consecutive scoring drives to take a lead they would not relinquish. The pass rush was ferocious, and with Nick Bosa’s return imminent, this defense feels on the brink of truly breaking out. Here are three takeaways from the 49ers’ massive win over Seattle: Mike Evans is a Hall of Famer Not that his status was ever in doubt for a gold jacket, but the veteran receiver was the best player on the field on Sunday. When the chips were down, Brock Purdy targeted Evans often on a drive punctuated by a Brandin Cooks touchdown grab and a two-point conversion from Evans. Routinely whipping Josh Jobe, Evans made contested catch after catch, and Purdy’s rapport with the veteran looked like a ten-year relationship. Evans leads all wide receivers with 11 first downs on third down. The 49ers needed speed and separators at the receiver position to test Seattle’s secondary. On Sunday, Evans dominated and didn’t even need any separation. Age ain’t nothing but a number! Way to go, Big Mike! The 49ers’ running game sends a message Seattle’s defense is fast and physical and can slow down outside zone runs. What is the answer? The 49ers went back to bully ball and beat up Seattle with their interior offensive line and duo runs. Christian McCaffrey finished with a 6.2 YPA and two runs over ten plus yards. According to Sumer Sports, the 49ers’ run game produced the highest designed rush success rate in any game against a Mike Macdonald defense. They had an 80% success rate on outside zone and had 3.1 yards before contact on those runs. The Seahawks’ previous opponents averaged 0.7 yards before contact on outside zone. The final drive leading to the leading field goal was a complete statement on the ground. The bullies are back, and the 49ers can play any style you like to finish a victory. Renardo Green has arrived The 49ers defense had many stars on Sunday. A monster game from Gracen Halton, another classic Fred Warner performance, and a pass rush highlighted by Keion White, Sebastian Valdez, and the returning Mykel Williams all need to be discussed. Malik Mustapha was physical and flying to the football. Even with Dre Greenlaw’s ejection, the 49ers defense was flying around, and Raheem Morris is doing a fantastic job as the defensive coordinator. It was Renardo Green who may have made the loudest statement on Sunday. Two interceptions and a PBU while allowing two catches for five yards and an NFL QB rating of 8.3 is truly elite play. Even facing the best receiver in the NFL was no issue for Green, as the Florida State cornerback held JSN to one catch for four yards on three targets with an interception and a PBU. Green has three interceptions this season and is blossoming before our eyes.
author: Jason Aponte

title: Brock Purdy shares best odds for MVP with an AFC quarterback
summary: Those of you plotting Brock Purdy’s demise in the media after the 49ers’ 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks, in Seattle, mind you, are going to be disappointed. Or at least you’ll have a hard argument to make. Purdy is currently tied for the best odds to win Most Valuable Player with Buffalo Bills quarterback […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Those of you plotting Brock Purdy’s demise in the media after the 49ers’ 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks, in Seattle, mind you, are going to be disappointed. Or at least you’ll have a hard argument to make. Purdy is currently tied for the best odds to win Most Valuable Player with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. FanDuel Sportsbook has the two at +300 . So while it wasn’t pretty, that performance against one of the best defenses in the league leaves Purdy sharing the best odds to win MVP. At this point, the haters might be gasping for air to point out how “bad” he played. To be fair: Purdy didn’t play his best game Sunday, going 19 for 29 (65 percent completions), with two touchdowns, one interception, and three sacks (his first three of the year). He (finally) posted a sub-100 passer rating in 2026: 92.5. But get this: when he needed to put a drive together that didn’t start on the Seahawks’ side of the field, he delivered: PURDY COOKS SOMETHING UP 👨‍🍳 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/jsWQlTWWPl — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) October 11, 2026 That’s all I keep hearing: can he take the team down the field when needed? Yes, the second drive after this was a stinker, thanks to some really strange playcalling by Kyle Shanahan. Regardless, that’s a good defense, one of the best in the NFL, and Purdy drove down the field to take the lead—and then got a two-point conversion when it mattered most. And his bully-ball defense had his back afterward to put the game away. “I thought Brock did an unbelievable job finding a way there to win at the end,” Kyle Shanahan said following the game . “That’s [Seattle Seahawks] one of the best defenses in the league, one of the best defenses over these last few years.” The fact that this is the Seattle Seahawks, a division rival and one of the league’s best defenses, is key to that drive. There’s no shame in Purdy calling it a day. Especially when he gets flagged for intentional grounding and other “penalties” that could have killed that particular 49ers’ drive. Except here’s Purdy throwing not one, but two touchdown passes to Brandin Cooks (one was nullified due to a last-minute timeout being called), who the 49ers have had for only two weeks. The backhanded compliment you may read is how well Purdy navigated a four-man rush, but that means he’s got eight other guys in coverage to look around and figure out where he can go with the ball. Purdy has just five more pass attempts needed to make the NFL’s all-time career passer rating leaderboard. Even with that sub-100 game, it’s a good guess that when that happens, he’ll be at the top of that leaderboard. If he were going to turn into a pumpkin, it would have happened long before the 1500 pass attempt requirement was fulfilled. “There’s some ups and downs,” Shanahan said. “By no means was everything perfect. But I thought he was really good in the fourth quarter; there are a lot of times when something wasn’t there, and he made some plays. Hell of a game by Brock”
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 49ers unsurprised as defensive youth movement pays huge dividends in Seattle
summary: In the biggest game of the year so far, the 49ers’ defense, stacked with young players in every area, produced its best performance of the season as San Francisco improved to 5-0. A unit that has been so often maligned in recent seasons and in which the 49ers have invested considerable draft capital has shown […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Gracen Halton #93 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after recovering a fumble and scoring a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the biggest game of the year so far, the 49ers’ defense, stacked with young players in every area, produced its best performance of the season as San Francisco improved to 5-0. A unit that has been so often maligned in recent seasons and in which the 49ers have invested considerable draft capital has shown clear signs of promise under new coordinator Raheem Morris. But the level of dominance the defense displayed as the 49ers edged the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a thriller was far from expected. Despite the number of points allowed, the numbers around the Niners’ defensive display make for impressive reading. San Francisco created four turnovers, continually giving the offense short fields with which to work in the first half, sacked Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold five times and registered eight QB hits, and held the Seahawks to just 3.4 yards per rush on the ground. Held to field goals on five of its seven trips into San Francisco territory, Seattle had a success rate of just 30 percent on offense, with that number in large part a product of the joy the 49ers had up front. Indeed, per Sumer Sports , the 49ers registered a 51.4% pressure rate with seven different players recording at least two pressures. Darnold was sacked by five different players, with Jaden Dugger, Keion White, Gracen Halton, Sebastian Valdez and Osa Odighizuwa all getting in on the act. The 49ers defense consistenly got pressure on Darnold and finished when they did get pressure San Francisco had a 97th %ile pressure rate generated. They had 7(!) different players record at least two pressures with Keion White and Gracen Halton leading the way Data:… — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) October 12, 2026 While White and Odighizuwa have plenty of experience, the three other players in that quintet are each just starting their careers. Defensive tackle Valdez has worked his way onto the 53-man roster after spending his rookie year and starting this year on the practice squad. Versatile linebacker Dugger and defensive tackle Halton are each part of a 2026 rookie class that is looking increasingly promising. Halton made one of the most significant plays of the day, forcing and recovering a fumble from Seahawks running back George Holani in the final seconds of the first half to score a touchdown that put the 49ers up 21-13. Dugger, meanwhile, was thrust into more extensive action than planned, moving from playing strong side linebacker on base downs to playing all three downs as the weakside backer following Dre Greenlaw’s second-quarter ejection. In addition to his sack on which the screamed around the edge to bring down Darnold, Dugger also had nine tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit, his performance part of a wider superb effort from a back seven that continues to make significant strides, Renardo Green the standout in the secondary as the third-year corner took his excellent start to the season to new heights with two interceptions. Led by the crucial veteran voice of middle linebacker Fred Warner, the 49ers — boosted by the return of last year’s first-round pick Mykel Williams at defensive end — dictated the line of scrimmage against both the run and the pass, while the secondary continued its ascension, albeit against a Seahawks offense lacking true difference-makers at the pass-catching positions outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. And the significance of the all-round performance of his young defense was not lost on head coach Kyle Shanahan. Shanahan told his postgame press conference: “From what I saw watching, it looked like they stepped it up a number of times. Just the guys you mentioned, I saw them make a number of plays today. If that doesn’t happen, especially when you lose a guy like Dre, and Dugger starting at base, but having to play that much at nickel with Dre going out. Gracen with losing some of the D-linemen we’ve had. Mykel with his first game back. It’s really hard to win a game in that situation if those guys don’t step it up, and they’ve been stepping up huge.” The extent to which the inexperienced members of the defense stepped it up, in a game of such magnitude and — for the most part — without a key player at the second level was stunning. But it was not a surprise to the players on the defense. “When you’re out there it’s your time to play,” Green said when asked about the contributions from the young players. “When you’re out there – I don’t care who’s out there – you’re the guy. So it doesn’t matter if you’re an old guy or a young guy, we all are held to the same standard. That’s how the players hold accountability for each other, and that’s how our coaches also push us. “So, it doesn’t surprise me that young guys are making plays, we do it all the time in practice. We were doing it in camp, and we were doing it in preseason. No matter who’s out there, we’re all held accountable and to the same standard.” #49ers young defenders growing up in a big way in a big game today: DT Gracen Halton – 3 tackles, 2 TFL, 1 sack, 1 FF, 1 FR, 1 TD LB Jaden Dugger – 9 tackles, 1 sack DT Sebastian Valdez – 3 tackles, 1 sack CB Renardo Green – 1 tackle, 2 INT, 3 passes defended DE Romello Height… — Nick Wagoner (@nwagoner) October 11, 2026 Outside of Warner and Greenlaw and with star edge rusher Nick Bosa still, for now, on the sidelines, the 49er defense is lacking in household names. But, as White articulated, there is no shortage of self-belief. “We got the utmost confidence. (Defense) has been going crazy,” White said. “Seabass [Sebastian Valdez], he’s been really stepping up big, making the most of his moment. Yeah, Dugg [Dugger] is a great player in this league. Shout out to John [Lynch] for drafting the really good young guys. And shout out to them for stepping up.” That confidence is reflected by the high-intensity way in which the defense plays the game, which is a crucial reason why 49ers left tackle Trent Williams thinks so highly of the youthful group Morris has at his disposal. “We have a really young defense, but these guys fly around,” explained Williams. We got a young nucleus, a few young players on that side led by Fred. That defense is a sneaky good defense. To keep holding that offense to three [points], that’s what gave us a chance to win.” Asked about the strong performance of the defensive line without Bosa, Williams added: “I can’t say that I saw it coming, but you’ve seen [rookie edge rusher Romello Height], you see him coming on, you see how many plays and how close he is to affecting the game every week. “That line is not a lot of household names so to speak outside of Bosa, but the way they play, they play like their hair is on fire. That’s a very special group.” After the defensive performance in Seattle, more around the NFL are likely to agree with Williams’ assessment. And, with Bosa seemingly set to return in Week 6, a defense few would have necessarily feared coming into the season is set to become an even scarier proposition for opposing offenses.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Gracen Halton shines brightest for the 49ers’ defense against the Seahawks
summary: It might have been the highest-scoring defensive struggle in football history, but the San Francisco 49ers came out of Seattle with a 5-0 record. The 49ers outlasted the Seattle Seahawks to win 32-29. It was a true battle of field position, with 31 of the combined 61 points coming off turnovers, and the two teams […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images It might have been the highest-scoring defensive struggle in football history, but the San Francisco 49ers came out of Seattle with a 5-0 record. The 49ers outlasted the Seattle Seahawks to win 32-29. It was a true battle of field position, with 31 of the combined 61 points coming off turnovers, and the two teams combined for a season-high seven turnovers. But as they did last week against Denver, San Francisco survived to stay undefeated and, most importantly, finished the first leg of their NFC West schedule 3-0. With plenty of players to choose from, these are the three stars from the win on Sunday: 3rd star: CB Renardo Green Entering Week 5, Green was the only 49ers player to have an interception. After Sunday, he’s still the only 49er with an interception, but now with three interceptions on the season. Not even a third into the season, and Green has set a new career-high in interceptions. He actually set it with his first pick of Sam Darnold on Sunday. After the 49ers offense opened the game with a three-and-out, Seattle was faced with the same fate on its opening drive. Facing a third-and-10, Darnold looked to get Jaxon Smith-Njigba going early while converting the third down. Green, however, read it the whole way, and the corner jumped the route, making the interception and abruptly ending the Seattle drive. Four plays later, the 49ers offense opened the scoring, jumping out to a 7-0 lead. With the 49ers scoring right before the half (more on that in a second), Seattle looked to close the eight-point gap to open the second half. This time, it took Green only two plays to strike. Trying to push the ball downfield, Darnold forced a pass to Elijah Arroyo on a route that Green practically ran with him. Green snagged the pass and was given an extra 15 yards after an Arroyo stray peanut-punch attempt caught Green. San Francisco couldn’t capitalize on the second pick, as Eddy Pineiro missed a field goal attempt to push the lead to 11. And to add to his game, when matched up against Smith-Njigba, Green was targeted three times, allowing one catch for four yards, plus an interception and a pass breakup—just a quality game from the third-year corner. 2nd star: WR Mike Evans Just a reminder: Evans is doing all of this despite fracturing his ribs a couple of weeks ago. And despite it, he continues to go up and make some of the most physical catches you have ever seen. All it took was one drive for Evans to make his presence felt on Sunday. Entering the 3:02 mark in the third quarter, when the 49ers took the ball following a field goal to give Seattle a five-point lead, Evans had three receptions for 38 yards with a touchdown. An opening-play offensive pass interference hindered the drive, but Evans wiped it out with a 15-yard reception on the first-and-20. The 49ers would get a new set of downs a few plays later before going back to Evans for a gain of nine. And that’s where Evans turned it on. Facing a third-and-10, Purdy fired a laser over the middle to Evans. Evans got Josh Jobe to lose his balance, then went up to catch the ball in front of Julian Love for a 23-yard gain. The 49ers would lose the following first down on a bogus intentional grounding call, setting up a second-and-21. Again, Evans pressed the button. Purdy gave Evans the perfect back-shoulder throw with Jobe in one-on-one coverage, and Evans went up and got it, with Jobe standing no chance, for a 28-yard gain that put the ball inside the Seattle 10-yard line. The 49ers would score two plays later to go up one and opted to go for two to extend the lead to three. Purdy would roll to his left and find nothing before cutting back to his right. The pressure finally closed in and forced a tight-window pass to Evans, and the receiver caught it to give the 49ers a three-point lead. Evans finished the 74-yard drive with 75 receiving yards (not a typo) to close his day out with seven receptions for 113 yards and a touchdown. 1st star: DT Gracen Halton It felt like the rookie defensive tackle was nearing a breakout game in recent weeks and that breakout came on Sunday. Halton started his day innocently enough, stopping Emanuel Wilson for a run for no gain. He followed with his first-career sack, getting to Darnold late in the second quarter for a loss of eight yards. But it was Halton’s play at the end of the second quarter that earned him Sunday’s No. 1 star. With a Corliss Waitman punt nailing Seattle inside its own 5-yard line with 18 seconds left, Mike MacDonald faced a predicament. San Francisco had all three of its timeouts, so three kneels might not have been enough to get to halftime without having to kick the ball back to the 49ers. Instead of taking the risk of a punt to expire the first half, Macdonald opted to play with some aggression, running the ball out of Seattle’s own endzone. George Holani took the carry, and Halton was instantly there, knocking the ball free. Halton had the wherewithal to stay with the play, jumping on the ball in the end zone for the touchdown. Instead of taking things into the half down one, Macdonald’s play-calling blunder led to Halton’s score, giving the 49ers an eight-point lead. And while Seattle was able to wipe that lead by the end of the third quarter, you’d have to wonder how different the outcome would have been without Halton’s play to close the first half. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 5, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 7 points WR Mike Evans – 5 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points

title: 15 Winners, 5 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers’ statement win over the Seahawks
summary: We witnessed a wild one in Seattle. The San Francisco 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks was the game of the year. You’d think a 61-point contest would feature two offenses that drove downfield against each other. Neither quarterback threw for more than 200 yards. Despite all of the scoring, only two of those […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images We witnessed a wild one in Seattle. The San Francisco 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks was the game of the year. You’d think a 61-point contest would feature two offenses that drove downfield against each other. Neither quarterback threw for more than 200 yards. Despite all of the scoring, only two of those drives traveled over 45 yards. Kyle Shanahan improved to 47-8 after winning the turnover battle. The 49ers needed all four of those turnovers to outlast their rivals on the road. The victory required every hand on deck, as attrition and ejections took a toll on the road team. Here are the winners and losers who tell the story of the 49ers’ action-packed, rollercoaster win that kept them undefeated. Winners Mike Evans You could only marvel at what Mike Evans did against a secondary thought to be among the best in the NFL. No one has had any doubt this season about who Brock Purdy wants to throw the ball to. That didn’t change on Sunday. Evans had more targets than the rest of the receivers combined. On late downs, Purdy targeted him 57.1% of the time. In the red zone, Evans got 40% of the targets. Evans finished with seven receptions on 10 targets for 113 yards. Last year, the 49ers struggled to attack the intermediate portion of the field against the Seahawks. This go-round, Evans’ average depth of target was 15.8 yards. They trusted him to get open downfield, and Evans rewarded Purdy time and time again. Seattle looked shell-shocked that Evans was capable of making the plays he did on a 12-play drive that gave the 49ers the lead into the fourth quarter. Evans kicked off with a first-down reception that beat Seattle’s boundary cornerback. A 15-yarder after taking a shot to the ribs on 1st and 20 erased a Brandin Cooks penalty. The drive looked like it would stall after a four-yard loss on second down. But on third and 10, Evans, who Tom Brady criticized for releasing outside on an in-breaking route, was too big for the defender and picked up 23 yards. Evans tortured Jobe one final time, catching a 28-yard sideline pass on 2nd and 21. It was the most impactful drive by a skill player under Kyle Shanahan that I can remember. Corliss Waitman Renardo Green’s first interception came on a 51-yard punt that was fair caught at the 11. Waitman’s next punt was fair caught, and the ensuing drive went three-and-out. Waitman’s third and fourth punts were fair caught inside the 10. Gracen Halton doesn’t score a touchdown without the punter pinning a kick inside the five. There were a couple of special teams blunders, but the punt team was excellent. Keion White The 49ers are built to defend and stop the pass. The defense is at its best when Keion White is on the field, lining up and down the line of scrimmage. Against Seattle’s offensive line, White had a 21.4% pressure rate. He had six pressures in the game, four against different players. White had a pair of run stops and a couple of tackles for loss. He overwhelmed the Seahawks upfront. Through five games, he looks like a supercharged version of what Charles Omenihu gave the Niners in 2023. Jaden Dugger Without Dre Greenlaw, Garret Wallow was the logical replacement. After all, Wallow rotated with Greenlaw throughout the season. If Week 5 taught us anything, it’s that Dugger shouldn’t come off the field. No player grew up and rose to the occasion as Dugger did against the Seahawks. Dugger already had a tackle for loss while flashing before Greenlaw’s ejection. So maybe Raheem Morris sensed Dugger could match Seattle’s physicality. Dugger finished with seven solo tackles, pressured Sam Darnold twice, and minimized the damage in coverage on three targets; he made Darnold look in different directions multiple times and, above all, looked like he belonged on the field in a playoff atmosphere away from home playing a position he hardly reps during the week. Renardo Green Green intercepted Darnold on the same sideline where he was yanked in a playoff last year. His second interception was a carbon copy of the one Purdy threw last season to Jake Tonges against the Seahawks on a similar route. Green had another pass breakup. On four targets, one completion was allowed for a grand total of one yard. The 49ers haven’t capitalized on quarterback mistakes. The cornerbacks haven’t been in positions to “bait” them. Green The offensive line Purdy had the second-longest average time to throw (3.2 seconds) among any quarterback in the NFL this week. He also had the eighth-slowest average time to pressure (2.69 seconds). There were plenty of dropbacks when Purdy had all day to scan the field. There were times when he was sped up and left the pocket prematurely. He was pressured on 38.2% of his dropbacks. For context, Darnold was pressured on 51.4% of his dropbacks. I don’t think Shanahan thought he’d have as much success running the ball, which is why they didn’t. Christian McCaffrey averaged 3.27 yards before contact. Shanahan would’ve run the ball 50 times if he knew his offensive line would generate the movement they did in the second half. Byron Murphy is a special player. He’s going to get his. He took advantage of Connor Colby. But the offensive line held Leonard Williams and Demarcus Robinson in check and prevented them from disrupting the offense. Aside from Colby, Dominick Puni allowed two pressures on 34 pass-blocking snaps, while Jake Brendel, Colton McKivitz, and Trent Williams each had one. Per Sumer Sports, McKivitz led the way with five impact plays. Colby had four, Brendel had 3, Puni had 2, and Williams had one. Losers Dre Greenlaw Greenlaw lasted 25 snaps before his emotions got the best of him. A late hit on Darnold cost the defense 15 yards. It was bad enough that the penalty occurred on Seattle’s sideline. Instead of leaving the sideline and going back to the huddle, Greenlaw looked like he was hunting for trouble. He found some when he came face to face with Ernest Jones. After headbutting Jones, who didn’t have his helmet on, Greenlaw was ejected. Dre put Dugger in a tough spot. We saw Luke Gifford play in 5-man fronts for the first time all season because Dugger filled in for Greenlaw. The domino effect from the ejection could’ve been disastrous. There’s a script where Gifford gets attacked in coverage, and Dugger looks like most rookies in a road environment. Dugger playing well doesn’t absolve Greenlaw of his actions. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing’s ball security The fear is that Samuel’s hamstring injury could be serious, since he was ruled out right away. The fumble may have been a product of the shock of the injury. Nonetheless, it’s his second in as many weeks. The 49ers weren’t as fortunate to recover this one. Cowing’s fumble was less about ball security and more about decision-making. He needs to feel the gunners or see them out of his peripheral vision. His muffed punt should’ve been a fair catch. Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout Lenoir and Stout combined to allow eight targets to be completed for eight receptions and 125 yards. Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to dominate this matchup. He caught all three receptions for 63 yards and a touchdown — the screen was technically Lenoir’s “man.” Lenoir gave up an out route for a first down to Cooper Kupp on third down in the low red zone. He did not seem confident. Stout also missed a tackle. Eddy Pineiro Was 2025 a mirage? Pineiro missed another kick on Sunday. He’s 31st in the NFL in field-goal percentage and 28th in extra-point percentage this season. This team has Super Bowl aspirations. Games are going to come down to the wire, especially in the postseason. The last thing you want is to trot out a kicker who makes only 2 of 3. IDKs Brock Purdy I’m torn about Purdy’s performance. I thought you could pin at least one sack and a couple of the pressures on the quarterback. He sprayed the ball and missed a couple of receivers. He was late and inaccurate on a throw to Jacob Cowing because he…

title: Future Hogs – Week 6: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: Down went #1 in Week 6 of college football. The Red River Rivalry between #1 Texas and Oklahoma went to the Sooners. full_text: BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 12: Indiana Hoosiers WR Nick Marsh (11) warms up prior to a college football game between the Howard Bison and Indiana Hoosiers on September 12, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Down went #1 in Week 6 of college football. The Red River Rivalry between #1 Texas and Oklahoma went to the Sooners. Although Arch Manning threw for three touchdowns, he also threw a pick-six and a late interception to set up the game-winning field goal. In the matchup between #2 Georgia and #6 Alabama, a controversial no-call on what appeared to be pass interference by the Bulldogs helped them hold on to the lead in Tuscaloosa. With their starting quarterback Dante Moore recovering from a concussion, Oregon’s playoff chances all but faded away against a UCLA team that looks for real but lost it’s starting quarterback for the remainder of the season. Elsewhere in the Big Ten, #7 Indiana needed two fourth quarter touchdowns to survive the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Things will only get tougher for Indiana as they go to Columbus and take on Jeremiah Smith and #4 Ohio State. Texas, now ranked #7, will try to rebound against Florida, while #1 Georgia will take on Auburn. In what is likely their toughest test of the season, #2 Notre Dame will go to Utah to face off against #8 BYU. The SEC will feature a number of ranked-on-ranked matchups: #16 Mississippi State vs. #22 LSU, #13 Missouri vs. #9 Ole Miss, and #6 Alabama vs. #14 Tennessee. Finally, #18 Oklahoma State and their QB Drew Mestemaker, who’s looking more and more like the top quarterback in the draft, will play #20 Houston. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. LaNorris Sellers | QB | RS Junior | South Carolina LaNorris Sellers is a frustrating NFL prospect. He looks the part of an NFL quarterback. He’s 6’3”, 238 pounds, has a big arm, and he’s mobile. When Sellers plays his best, there are the slightest glimpses of Cam Newton. Those glimpses were on full display when the Gamecocks played Florida. Sellers found open receivers and threw the ball with accuracy. He even made some tight window throws downfield. The problem is Sellers is very inconsistent. As an example, he only completed 44% of his passes against Towson earlier this season. He also needs to read defenses more quickly and be more decisive as a playmaker. In the right place, Sellers might develop into a starter, but I think he would be a quality backup at the next level. The Gamecocks beat the Gators, and Sellers went 23 of 35, a completion percentage of 66%, four touchdowns through the air and one on the ground. lanorris sellers vs florida. pic.twitter.com/nv1fpGiIoC — . (@wrldofjordan_) October 12, 2026 Isaac Brown | RB | Junior | Louisville Isaac Brown is a home-run hitter. At 5’9”, 190 lbs, Brown is smaller, but he’s stout. Brown does many of the things an NFL running back must do. He’ll run between the tackles for positive yards and catch the ball out of the backfield. But Brown’s super power is his speed. If he can get in space, it is unlikely anyone will be able to catch him. Where Brown is lacking is that he’s not a particularly creative runner that will make defenders miss in space, and he’s not powerful enough to consistently break tackles and churn out tough yardage. Brown had a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a win over Florida State. Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 6 1 | 21.8 MPH Isaac Brown @isaac6brown_ RB Louisville IGA Score™ : 94.5 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/wRVcC7Wgl3 — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 12, 2026 Nick Marsh | WR | Junior | Indiana The Commanders need a number one receiver and Indiana looks like they have two prospects that can be just that. I discussed Charlie Becker earlier this year, now it’s Nick Marsh’s turn. A transfer from Michigan State, Marsh is every bit of 6’3”, 210 pounds, and he uses that size to bully defensive backs. Yet at that size, he moves like a smaller receiver through the stems of his routes. He looks like he has plenty of speed to run away from defenders after catch. Another thing about Marsh is he will block his behind off. In the discussion for the second receiver to be drafted after Jeremiah Smith, Marsh made a strong case against Nebraska. He made six catches for 187 yards and two touchdowns as the Hoosiers handed the Cornhuskers their first loss. Nick Marsh is playing like a top-20 pick pic.twitter.com/fvyB1yieAJ — James Foster (@NoFlagsFilm) October 10, 2026 Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 6 10 | 20.6 MPH Nick Marsh @TheSticks_11 WR @IndianaFootball IGA Score™ : 86.6 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/nhcOZOJnDR — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 12, 2026 Patrick Overmyer | TE | Senior | Houston One bright spot of the Commanders’ game against the Giants was Chig Okonkwo showing a little of what made him a coveted free agent. Patrick Overmyer is another prospect that is a receiving threat as a tight end. Overmyer stands 6’5” and weighs 240 pounds. Houston mostly uses Overmyer flexed off the line as a big slot receiver. From that spot, he is a mismatch for many defenders: too fast for linebackers and too big for defensive backs. They often line him up in the backfield where he either lead blocks or sneaks out for a pass. If the Commanders want to be creative with their use of a tight end, Overmeyer should be on their list of draft prospects. He had eight receptions for 83 yards and four touchdowns in a win over Kansas State. UTTERLY UNREAL 😱 Patrick Overmyer rakes in 4⃣ TDs in #22 Houston's dominate win Overmyer Highlights vs. K-State 🎬 @UHCougarFB pic.twitter.com/VR4YSyldNN — Big 12 Studios (@big12studios) October 10, 2026 Matt Craycraft | C | Senior | Duke It wasn’t all bad for Lucas Patrick against the Giants, but I saw multiple plays where he was knocked into the backfield by defensive tackles. Matt Craycraft has started at center for the Blue Devils since 2023. He’s a smart player, not because he goes to Duke, but because he’s been named All-ACC Academic 2023-2025. On the field, Craycraft is simply a solid player in the middle of the line. At 6’3”, 305 pounds, Craycraft is athletic enough to play in a zone-blocking scheme and strong enough for a gap-blocking scheme. His awareness in pass protection allows him to identify incoming blitzers, recognize twisting rushers, and block defenders in space. It’d be nice to see him play a little nastier and finish his blocks with authority. Although the Blue Devils did not get the win against Georgia Tech, he helped their running back Nate Sheppard gain almost 100 yards both rushing and receiving. Craycraft is #72. Xavier Gilliam | DT | Junior | Tennessee The Commanders run defense has been one of the best in the NFL. But, it needs more players who can win one-on-one matchups in the pass game. Xavier Gilliam has terrorized offenses this season. He’s a local product that played at Quince Orchard before two seasons at Penn State. The volunteers have unleashed the 6’2”, 305 pound transfer. He is explosive off the line of scrimmage and relentless forcing the issue into the backfield. Gilliam combines his initial quickness with various moves to maneuver past defenders. He is strong enough to bench press blockers and disengage to make a play. Gilliam lines up as a nose for Tennessee, but he’d likely play defensive end for the Commanders, kicking inside in four-man fronts. Gilliam helped Tennessee defeat Arkansas with four tackles, a sack, and a forced fumble that he recovered. #Tennessee DT Xavier Gilliam (2) has been lights out for the Volunteers. He's played like a R1 pick He's up to 22 pressures, six sacks, and 21 run-stop tackles for the season Violence, quickness, and power are the three words I'd use to describe his game pic.twitter.com/mwtXRKcuml — Daniel…

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 5
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 11: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders runs for a touchdown in front of Kayvon Thibodeaux #5 of the New York Giants during the second half of the NFL game at Northwest Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ 27-27 tie in Landover. The defense crumbled in the second half again After effectively limiting Jameis Winston to 7-of-16 for 72 passing yards and 0 TDs in the first half, Daronte Jones’ defense came apart in the second half once again, as Winston went 13-for-17 for 141 passing yards and 2 TDs in the fourth quarter . At one point, Daronte Jones had Daron Payne dropping into coverage. Fans will also note how far off the line of scrimmage the secondary was on the play, and Isiah Likely is given ten free yards in the red zone. The team’s annual struggles to cover tight ends continue, as Isaiah Likely hauled in 11 receptions for 94 yards and two TDs . The team did continue to blitz at times in the second half, but the pressure didn’t get home and Jameis burned the secondary in Cover 0. Ultimately, the Washington Commanders fell just short of allowing their fourth game of 30 or more points in as many weeks. It took multiple missed field goals and some turnovers from the Giants offense to prevent it. This is a fireable and borderline criminal call by Washington DC Daronte Jones. They have a 4th & 7 here to essentially end the game. They bring a blitz and have DT Daron Payne drop back and essentially be responsible for the ENTIRE MIDDLE OF THE FIELD. pic.twitter.com/jPxmFiRSzQ — Gain of Fauci (@DschlopesIsBack) October 11, 2026 The Commanders ran Cover 0 15 times against the Giants. 12 times in the second half. Jameis completed 6-10 vs. Cover 0 and threw 2 TDs. — Jamual (@LetMualTellit) October 12, 2026 The #Commanders ' defense blitzed on 39% of the Giants' dropbacks per NFL Pro, but didn't have as much success. They had just two sacks and a pressure rate of 33.9%. That helped Jameis Winston light up the secondary for 326 yards and 3 TDs. — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) October 12, 2026 The Washington Commanders’ defense once again won the turnover battle, but their inability to stop offenses from scoring in the second half makes this defense one of the worst in the league. The team ranks dead last in second half scoring and red zone defense. The poor defensive performance was underscored by the fact the Giants were starting backup quarterback Jameis Winston behind center. David Blough lacked situational awareness After having some success early, offensive coordinator David Blough failed to adjust as defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson brought increased pressure, coming after Jayden Daniels with blitzes on 62% of his drop backs , the same thing the defensive coordinator did the week before in Arizona. The rookie coordinator continued to call long-developing plays downfield in the face of the rush instead of providing quick options for Daniels to use as outlets. Blough also went away from Bill Merritt, who was successful for much of the game, but finished the day with only 11 rushing attempts and 22 total offensive snaps . Paired with Brandon Coleman’s struggles, the offense sputtered as Blough went with a predictable formula throughout the second half and failed to produce any points in the most critical part of the game. They picked up the blitz. Can’t block 8 people. Have to have a hot option for the QB https://t.co/aQwosODdjh — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) October 11, 2026 The #Commanders couldn’t even get a FG attempt in the final 2 minutes. They had the ball on The 48 yd line with 1:36 in 4th The 50 yd line with 5:00 in OT The 25 yd line with 0:13 in OT Inexcusable! I’m done with having a conservative coach! #RaiseHail — SJM 🪖 (@DMVCommanders) October 11, 2026 Of course, Blough’s awareness could not have been worse than in the final seconds of overtime . The clock showed 55 seconds at the end of the previous play, but the offense showed no urgency to get up to the line before or after the final play. A play that frankly should never have been called. There are still playmakers on the team While the signing was panned by many at the time, Amik Robertson has turned out to be the best free agent addition of the off season thus far. The cornerback continues to get called with questionable penalties, but has been sticky in coverage and shown well as a tackler, which is a key component of Daronte Jones’ scheme. Sam Cosmi also returned to the lineup and immediately made his presence felt as Bill exploded up the interior early for his 33-yard touchdown run. Cosmi also helped clear out one side of the defensive line on Jayden Daniels’ long touchdown run. #Commanders coverage stats of note per NFL Pro: – CB Rasul Douglas: 7 catches, 82 yards, 1 TD – CB Mike Sainristil: 4 catches, 69 yards, 1 TD – LB Sonny Styles: 4 catches, 46 yards, 1 TD – CB Fabian Moreau: 4 catches, 33 yards – CB Amik Robertson: 3 catches, 30 yards — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) October 12, 2026 Amik Robertson is a STRONG tackler for a Corner. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/XIhbWOLK4b — Chad Ryan (@ChadwikoTWW) October 11, 2026 The longest rushing TD of Jayden Daniels’ career: pic.twitter.com/ior8NRqL1C — Ethan Cadeaux (@Ethan_Cadeaux) October 11, 2026 Terry McLaurin was roasted by many fans after turning in limited practices all week but gutted it out in this one and led the team in receiving despite playing about half of the total offensive snaps . The veteran wide receiver made plays when they were needed, including a 2-point conversion and 22-yard catch-and-run in overtime. Sonny Styles was all over the field on Sunday, finishing the day with 13 total tackles, 4 solo, a tackle for a loss . The rookie also teamed up with Daron Payne for a critical forced fumble in overtime. Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels connect for a big chunk of much needed yards. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/RuBN9kfwKl — Chad Ryan (@ChadwikoTWW) October 11, 2026 FUMBLE Sonny Styles forces the Skattebo fumble and this game is still alive. Insane. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/X8Z5S9iB8G — Chad Ryan (@ChadwikoTWW) October 11, 2026 There is no bigger playmaker on the team than their franchise quarterback, and Jayden Daniels was electric running the ball and making pays off script in his return. He did make a critical error on the final play, but was put in a bad position when Chris Paul stepped on his foot yet again. In 13 personnel with his only receiving option to the sideline covered, Daniels was left with only two wide receivers in the middle of the field that weren’t options. Yes, Jayden made a huge mistake by not throwing the ball out of bounds, but there are bigger issues higher up the chain that need to be addressed. Jayden Daniels yesterday: – 91.9 passer rating – 200 passing yards w/ 68% completion rate – 103 rushing yards & 2TDs on 9 rushes – 80.6 QBR I’ll rock with 5 forever #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/q46aEJKhPY — brady (@burgermanders) October 12, 2026 According to #Commanders HC Dan Quinn, the final play of the game was intended to be an outside throw to Ben Sinnott (#82) pic.twitter.com/YXGF0nGE4p — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 12, 2026 The team’s coaching staff needs a hard reboot While Dan Quinn was applauded for making the bold move to hire two rookie coordinators in the offseason, so far the gamble hasn’t paid off and the team is 1-3-1 five weeks into the season. Jones has improved the takeaways, but is failing where it counts when if comes to the box score. While some of it might be personnel related, as…

title: Dan Quinn: “Furious about our execution in the crucial moments in the game.”
summary: The Washington Commanders are the talk of the NFL world, and not for any good reasons. Their blunder in overtime that led to a tie with the Giants is being hailed as an all-time clock management mistake, and has put Dan Quinn firmly on the hot seat. His weekly ‘Tell the Truth Mondays’ media availability […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders are the talk of the NFL world, and not for any good reasons. Their blunder in overtime that led to a tie with the Giants is being hailed as an all-time clock management mistake, and has put Dan Quinn firmly on the hot seat. His weekly ‘Tell the Truth Mondays’ media availability is going to be a lot more interesting with more questions than answers from Sunday’s result. Quinn went over that failed play again, and tried to take the blame for everything that went wrong. He said they wasted too much time, and there were substitutions in the play call that made it take longer to execute the play. Quinn said he was furious at how the big plays in critical moments went down, and they work on situationsl awareness every week. Quinn knows fans are pissed and he’s also pissed. When asked about his own job security, he said he speaks with team owner Josh Harris regularly, and that noone is pleased with this outcome. Furious at the end of game execution: Dan Quinn on talking to the team and explaining the end of game scenario pic.twitter.com/n1uZSfPZKC — Mitchell Tischler (@Mitch_Tischler) October 12, 2026 Dan Quinn time. "Furious about our execution in the crucial moments in the game. We work really hard on these and it didn't look like it yesterday." #Commanders @WTOP — George Wallace (@GWallaceWTOP) October 12, 2026 Dan Quinn addressing the media. Said he was "furious" about the team's execution, players and coaches alike. Said it took "entirely too long" after Rachaad White run to run another play and execute their plan. Added that everyone, including him, feels urgency to get things right — Zach Selby (@ZachSelbyWC) October 12, 2026 Dan Quinn said he was furious after the game. He said, "We've got a lot of shit to clean up." — John Keim (@john_keim) October 12, 2026 Did players know there were no timeouts left?: Quinn when asked if they players knew they were out of timeouts on the final drive: "For each play … we're talking a little bit ahead of the call. 'Hey, on the next one, we're going to clock. The next one's must out of bounds.' full_text: When does a tie feel like a loss? When your head coach is Dan Quinn. This game was a tale of two halves (which I feel like is often the case with the Commanders). Washington scored on their first drive of the game and it felt like something may be clicking with quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. Then, in normal Washington fashion, came the epic second-half collapse — including the mind-blowing overtime! What an emotional rollercoaster for fans and players alike. The good news is no NFC East team won this weekend. The bad news: we most likely have to deal with Dan Quinn and his complete incompetence until the end of the season. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs S Jeremy Reaves leaves everything out on the field. He may not have the most talent, but he has HEART! I thought he played a pretty good overall game against both the run and pass. Revo with the pressure off the blitz. Payne gets the sack 💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/TJS31AHWCA — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 11, 2026 Great play on the ball here by Revo! pic.twitter.com/QgOjFhIo3e — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 11, 2026 LB Sonny Styles – Sonny led the Commanders with 13 total tackles, four solo, a tackle for a loss and a pass defended. He was also in on the play in overtime where Daron Payne forced the fumble on Giants running back Cam Skattebo. Styles TFL! pic.twitter.com/VwAGUtb0G3 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 11, 2026 DL Daron Payne – Payne had a good game. generating multiple pressures and collecting a sack . Tuttle recovers! pic.twitter.com/fwlOs7FifF — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 11, 2026 RG Sam Cosmi – In his first game back from a concussion, Cosmi was rock-solid up front. He made a few really nice blocks — one against Abdul Carter on Jayden’s long touchdown run. He’s playing like a top five guard in the NFL. 38-yard TD run! Jayden Daniels is so back @NYGvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/un8ws01KAe — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Duds Dan Quinn (and David Blough) — Head coach Dan Quinn laid yet another egg , this time with the game hanging in the balance. The clock management, play calling and lack of decision-making has grown old. If Blough was the one who called a pass play in that situation, I don’t know why Quinn didn’t override that. At this point, Quinn is nothing more than an overpaid cheerleader. #Commanders fans booed HC Dan Quinn & GM Adam Peters as they walked off the field (via: @stephenstackzz ) pic.twitter.com/I8WfVuhpzi — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 12, 2026 After digesting this Commanders tie and talking to players in the locker room, my one big thought: This is all on Dan Quinn and the offensive coaches. The clock had stopped. Run the ball one more time and see if you can pick up a few yards – fine, but then you IMMEDIATELY trot out the FG team after that It’s a 42 GD yd kick! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 11, 2026 Rachaad White was tackled at the Giants 24 yard line with 50 seconds left. 50. Seconds. The next play ended the game. You had a full 35 seconds to tell Jayden Daniels ANYTHING productive. You didn't. Inexcusable. Shocking. This falls on Dan Quinn. — District Divided (@DistrictDivided) October 11, 2026 LT Brandon Coleman – Coleman had an absolutely miserable game giving up pressures, sacks and committing penalties. He did play a bit better in the second half, but a traffic cone would have been an upgrade to what he put on film during the first half. summary: The Daily Slop – 12 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders guard Sam Cosmi (76) reacts to the tied game against the New York Giants at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Daily Slop – 12 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles ESPN NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games How devastating was this collapse? This was the worst collapse under coach Dan Quinn. The Commanders are now 1-3-1 and 0-2-1 in a bad NFC East. They could blame other losses on being short-handed or without their starting QB. But not Sunday. They held a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter, and quarterback Jayden Daniels showed his dynamic ability. But it all fell apart. Now, life could get awfully tough with their next games against the 49ers, Eagles and Rams. Washington badly needed a win, especially against an NFC East rival. Having Daniels back will always provide hope, but the defense again struggled to defend the pass. Trend to watch: Washington’s second-half defense continues to struggle. The Commanders allowed a combined 85 points in the past four games combined. That included 17 to the Giants on Sunday, wiping out a two-touchdown lead. The pass rush simply did not bother quarterback Jameis Winston enough, as he threw for 254 yards and two touchdowns after halftime. — John Keim Next game: at 49ers (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET) To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . ESPN Judging overreactions to NFL Week 5 This might be disrespectful to the 3-1-1 Giants, and I apologize if it is. But not having quarterback Jaxson Dart or star edge rusher Brian Burns for the rest of the season is going to be tough to overcome. Their schedule still includes trips to Houston, Philly, Seattle and Detroit, along with home games against the Jaguars and the 49ers. The Cowboys’ defense looks no better than it did last season. Dallas has December road games against the Seahawks and the Rams and home games against the Jaguars and the 49ers. The Eagles are without their top three running backs and are also missing four of their Week 1 starting offensive linemen, and their final four games of the season include a home contest versus Seattle and a game at San Francisco. The Commanders — well, after Sunday, I think we can just say we aren’t going to give them much of a shot. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Ringer The Winners and Losers of the NFL Week 5 It was the worst decision of Daniels’s young career, and what followed was one of the most embarrassing end-of-game sequences in recent NFL history. Daniels went to the ground with eight seconds left, then lounged on the grass for roughly five seconds , seemingly oblivious to the situation he had just created. His teammates scrambled to pull him upright and get the offense lined up for a spike, but by then, it was too late. The clock hit zero before the Commanders could take another snap, and the game ended in a 27-27 tie. A made field goal would have put Washington at 2-3, even with the flailing Eagles and Cowboys and one game behind the Giants. Daniels deserves the largest share of the blame for the final play. A starting quarterback has to know that he cannot go down in bounds there. But Quinn doesn’t get to separate himself from the embarrassment either. Quinn entered 2026 with his seat already warm, and this is the kind of failure that can erode whatever confidence remains in his leadership. Coaches can explain injuries and personnel deficiencies away, but an error of this magnitude is much harder to excuse. And it could end up being the point of no return. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Bad decisions come in threes? If you thought Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles’ curious choice not to kick a chip-shot field goal that would have given his team a three-possession lead in Thursday night’s game against the Dallas Cowboys would be the most scrutinized move of the week — well, it may go down only as the bronze medalist of baffling, thanks to a couple of not-so-smooth moves by men in headsets on Sunday. First came Nicki Sirianni’s decision to pass late in the Eagles’ game against the Jags, with the ensuing incompletion ensuring that Jake Elliott’s eventual go-ahead field goal would leave eight seconds on the clock, rather than zero. Then Sirianni chose to have Elliott kick the ball into the landing zone, setting up Ameer Abdullah’s 53-yard return and Cam Little’s 57-yard walk-off field goal . “I didn’t make the right decision and I lost us that game,” Sirianni said, after Philly (2-3) dropped its third straight. He wasn’t wrong, but given that he came into the game with an NFL-best record of 35-15 in one-score games, we’ll give him a little grace. Besides, embattled Washington coach Dan Quinn later accepted responsibility for an even more egregious collapse: With 12 seconds left, no timeouts and the ball at the Giants’ 24-yard-line, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels inexplicably scrambled and went down inbounds , leaving no time for a field goal attempt. Though Daniels clearly goofed, Quinn, who threw his headset to the ground in disgust, shouldered the blame for taking the risk of running another play, saying, “It falls on me.” Will something else soon fall on Quinn? With a Monday night road game against the undefeated 49ers coming up for the Commanders (1-3-1), followed by a bye week, he has ample reason to be concerned. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) The undefeated NFL teams are exactly as nobody predicted Coach Dan Quinn took the blame , and he’s ultimately responsible for the operation. But the game management coach said this looked like a case of quarterback error. “Decisions made in real time are seldom perfect, but I can assure you of one thing: Dan Quinn and his staff told the quarterback no sack or scramble,” the coach said. “You can’t do that. You throw it away, and if you have eight seconds, throw it away again, get it to four seconds. There are three errors by the quarterback: scrambling, taking the sack and not getting up fast.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Front Office Sports It’s time for NFL Networks to hire ‘clock management’ specialists It was so laughable that ProFootballTalk’s Mike Florio called it a “firing offense.” No wonder, since Washington minority owner Magic Johnson sounded off about the blunder on X/Twitter. “I’m in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today’s overtime game against the Giants,” tweeted Johnson. “All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!” The Magic Man wasn’t alone. Fox play-by-play announcer Chris Myers and color commentator Jonathan Vilma couldn’t believe what they were seeing as the Commanders QB Jayden Daniels danced around with no timeouts instead of clocking the ball and attempting a game-winning field goal inside of 40 yards. “They don’t have a timeout. What are they doing?” asked Myers. “They’ve got to get up and spike this. They’re not going to be able to get this done in time! It’s gonna run out on them! The clock ran out as Daniels ran the ball!…Unbelievable. A comedy of errors late.” Vilma agreed. “Chris, that’s inexcusable!” he said. “It was just supposed to be, you go, you take a knee, set up, clock, and then get out of there.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE…

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 6: Time for Mendoza? Cowboys issues?
summary: Get ready for Week 6 with takes on two QB situations, two teams with defensive issues, two coaches on the hot seat and more.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 6 ? Sure, Bills-Rams just ended like eight hours ago. But the Seahawks and Broncos are playing in another iteration of the Russell Wilson bowl on Thursday ! The Texans' season hangs on the brink against the Jaguars in London on Sunday morning . Caleb Williams should be back for the Bears against the Falcons Sunday afternoon ! And Micah Parsons ... apparently won't play in his revenge game against the Cowboys on Sunday night . Whatever.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with a quarterback change I'm expecting to see soon, touch on a couple of defenses in need of big talent lifts, and anticipate an improvement for an undefeated team. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 6.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 One more start for Cousins? 
 Seahawks need more than Charbonnet? 
 Two head coaches in trouble? 
 Murray, Vikings rounding into form? 
 Cowboys need to sit some vets? 
 Time for the Cards to look at Beck? 
 Massive issues in the Bears' secondary? 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... Kirk Cousins  will get one more start before Fernando Mendoza time 
 Cousins has been totally solid for the Raiders this season. Relative to expectation and contract, there has been nothing disappointing about his play.

 That said, the Patriots went after him Sunday . New England defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr blitzed Cousins on 41.2% of his first-half dropbacks, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and got a 53% pressure rate and two sacks for his trouble. Although Cousins is a wily veteran capable of identifying blitzes and carving them up with hot routes, he's also 38 years old and was not particularly mobile even a decade ago, let alone now.

 The Patriots' game plan was apparent and smart. With starting cornerbacks  Christian Gonzalez  and Carlton Davis III  both unavailable due to injuries and a couple of depth corners also laid up, Kuhr tried to break the Raiders' passing game at the pocket before Cousins could attack his inexperienced cover men. On paper, it didn't work too great -- Cousins was 10-for-15 with 123 yards and a score through two quarters. But it got the Patriots off the field when they needed it.

 Here's a Cover 0 snap on third-and-5 . Cousins can't backpedal fast enough to buy time on the pressure and can't get enough arm into the throw to drive it before the cornerback arrives. Charles Woods , the third-year corner making his first career start, has plenty of time to arrive for the pass breakup.

 

 Here's an extremely similar look on third-and-14 -- already a tough down to handle. Cousins hangs a vertical ball up for Tre Tucker against Kindle Vildor , who was called up from the Pats' practice squad. It's the right read and an open throw, but the ball is uncatchable.

 

 Now, a guy should not be benched for an uncatchable third-and-14 heave against Cover 0. But Kuhr was able to deploy this approach because he knew Cousins couldn't burn him with escapability and play extension. Once Kuhr manufactured the free rusher, he could tell his young corners with total confidence that the ball would come out fast. Drive on the first break. Play aggressive, attack the catch point. Don't worry about eyes in the backfield or long-developing routes -- those won't happen.

 Cousins has 10 dropbacks on the season in which he, at any point, starts to scramble. Only  Michael Penix Jr ., Matthew Stafford and Jordan Love have fewer. He has just three actual scrambles (dropbacks on which he crosses the line of scrimmage to run). Only 7.6% of his throws have come with him on the move (only Stafford and Jared Goff have lower percentages), and his average speed at release of 2.85 mph, per Next Gen Stats, is the lowest of all passers this season.

 Cousins simply does not move. Quarterbacks such as Stafford, Goff and Penix have much bigger arms to get away with this play style, while quarterbacks such as  Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow have their elite processing and accuracy to get away with it. At his age, Cousins doesn't have those cardinal traits. He has enough arm, and he certainly has plus accuracy and processing. But it's not enough to tip the scales back in his favor.

 This has not been a death knell for the Raiders through five weeks, as Cousins is 10th in the league in EPA per pressured dropback and 11th in success rate on pressured dropbacks. He's making do with what he has. But the limitation is apparent, and future opponents will attack it. The Raiders have the Bills in Week 6 , the Rams in Week 7 and the Jets in Week 8 . The Rams and Jets are above average in blitz rate on the season, and the Bills are right around average. They're going to come after Cousins and make the bet Kuhr did -- that eventually the Raiders' lack of a running game will stick them in third-and-long, and those blitzes will create early and errant throws.

 The Raiders might have a solution to this problem: the spry legs of Mendoza that have done little but warm a bench through five weeks.

 I have no doubt that the Raiders will initially be worse against pressures and blitzes when they first deploy Mendoza. He is a rookie and lacks the Spidey-sense that Cousins has honed over a decade-plus of NFL football. Mendoza will take bad sacks and throw the ball into coverage traps because that's what rookies do.

 

 But he'll also move. He will create second-reaction throws that have yet to exist in this offense. He'll allow head coach Klint Kubiak to dust off the rollout sections of his playbook, which were so integral for Sam Darnold in Seattle but have been shelved for Cousins in Vegas. Mendoza is not known as an elite mover, but he's totally functional -- and most importantly, leagues ahead of Cousins.

 To quickly pivot from Cousins to Mendoza might feel like an early abandonment of a well-laid developmental plan. But I would argue that the pivot is justified. The Raiders are currently 3-2 in a suddenly much-more-winnable AFC West than previously believed. Yes, the Chiefs are 4-0 -- but the Raiders went neck-and-neck with them in Week 4, and both the Broncos (3-2) and Chargers (0-5) have been clearly worse than Las Vegas through five weeks. The 1.5 games back should not deter the Raiders from pushing for the division -- and in that effort, potentially landing a wild-card berth regardless.

 I won't be too upset if they keep riding the Cousins train. Like I said, the lack of mobility is a problem but not one that has totally hamstrung an otherwise solid passing attack. The Raiders could defensibly stick with Cousins for another month or two and still prioritize Mendoza's development over anything else. After all, benching Cousins after Week 6 would give Mendoza to the Rams and (presumably)  Myles Garrett in Week 7 -- that's a stiff ask.

 But it's hard to win those first three games ... then lose two ... and not wonder if the team is closer to contention than expected. And then not wonder whether Mendoza's timeline should be accelerated to match.

 

 
 

 I think ... the Seahawks have too many eggs in the Zach Charbonnet basket 
 Last season, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 15.1% of the team's total touches. That was the fourth-highest number for a non-running back leaguewide. His 36% target share was the highest for a single player since 2012 Brandon Marshall. It was incredible to see how successfully the Seahawks built the entire plane, especially in the passing game, out of JSN.

 Because we all thought the Smith-Njigba…

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 6
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 6? We made our 1-32 list and picked the biggest defensive problem for every team.
full_text:
NFL teams are averaging 23.3 points in the 2026 season . Though some of those points have come from defensive touchdowns (but surprisingly no return TDs), it's mostly an indicator that offenses are getting into scoring territory  a lot .

 So why are defenses struggling so much? In addition to our updated 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick out the biggest defensive issue for each team. From secondary depth to third-down defense, what is causing each team to falter?

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Patriots have returned to the top 10 after back-to-back wins over the Bills and Raiders. Sunday's win was catalyzed by another strong performance from quarterback  Drake Maye , who led the team to its most points (45) and yards (536) in a game since 2021. The Patriots could continue their hot streak with matchups against the Jets and Dolphins in two of the next three weeks. 
 The Packers are also climbing back up our list after two losses in their first three games. Green Bay entered Sunday's matchup  against Chicago as 1.5-point underdogs, but it completely dominated to avenge  its wild-card loss last season. Quarterback Jordan Love 's 367 passing yards were the second most by any QB in Bears-Packers series history, per ESPN Research. 
 The bottom three teams in our rankings (Chargers, Titans and Dolphins) are all 0-5. It's the fifth time since the 1970 merger that three teams from the same conference have started a season with that record, per ESPN Research. Los Angeles had the most excruciating loss of the bunch this past weekend, dropping a seven-point lead with nine minutes left against the Broncos . 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week.

 Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3  | Week 4  | Week 5 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (5-0) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Seahawks 32-29 
 Week 5 ranking: 1 

 Biggest issue on defense: Third-down efficiency

 

 Under new coordinator Raheem Morris , the Niners rank fifth in yards per play allowed (4.7) and have limited big plays as well as any team in the league. But they have struggled to get off the field consistently. The Niners rank 20th in third-down defense, giving up a first down on 40.8% of their opportunities. That has led to their defense being on the field for 31 minutes, 12 seconds per game, which ranks 23rd in the NFL. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) 
 Week 5 result: Bye 
 Week 5 ranking: 2 

 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough sacks

 

 The Chiefs can generate pressure on the quarterback, whether it's via Chris Jones , George Karlaftis or rookie R Mason Thomas . But they have one of the biggest statistical anomalies of the 2026 season: zero sacks in the first month. Before their bye week , they couldn't put Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on the turf despite a season-high 21 pressures. If the Chiefs can start collecting sacks, their defense could be a top unit in the second half of the season. -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 3. Buffalo Bills (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Rams 37-34 (OT) 
 Week 5 ranking: 4 

 Biggest issue on defense: Letting offenses off the hook

 

 The Bills haven't had much issue pushing offenses backward on first down. But opponents have had far too much success extending drives in second-and-long and third-and-long situations. Plenty of this has to do with the Bills' dwindling cornerback depth, but that's hardly an excuse for how C.J. Stroud , Jared Goff ,  Drake Maye  and  Matthew Stafford  completed 74.6% of their passes for 558 yards and five touchdowns (80.8 QBR) on second downs against the Bills. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 4. Seattle Seahawks (3-2) 
 Week 5 result: Lost to the 49ers 32-29 
 Week 5 ranking: 3 

 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough stops in the red zone

 

 The biggest problem for the Seahawks' defense might actually be Seattle's offense; the 44 points they've given up off turnovers is tied for most in the NFL. You have to look hard to find a true weakness with a unit that ranks second in both defensive EPA and ESPN's defensive efficiency metric, but the Seahawks are 27th in opponent red zone efficiency (75%) and tied for last in opponent goal-to-go efficiency (100%). Granted, they haven't allowed offenses to get that far down the field often -- only 12 times inside their 20 (tied for fifth fewest) and seven times inside their 10 (tied for seventh fewest). -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Eagles 19-17 
 Week 5 ranking: 5 

 Biggest issue on defense: Finishing with the pass rush

 

 It's nitpicky, considering the Jaguars are No. 1 in run defense and second in scoring defense, but they could do a better job of getting sacks. Their 80 QB pressures are tied for sixth and 11 sacks rank ninth, but edge rushers  Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker only have 3.5 sacks combined. They each had 1.5 sacks in the season opener against the Browns  but a half sack since (Walker last Sunday). Both are a large part of the run defense (63.8 yards per game) by setting the edge, but their sack production needs to increase. -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 6. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Saints 23-13 
 Week 5 ranking: 9 

 Biggest issue on defense: Depth not tested yet

 

 It's not easy to find a negative indicator from a defense that has been the league's best this season, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' expected point average. But because the Vikings have been almost entirely healthy, their depth at multiple positions is untested. In fact, eight defensive players have been on the field for at least 80% of the snaps. That doesn't mean the backups would falter in more prominent roles. It's just hard to judge based on game reps. -- Kevin Seifert 

 
 
 

 7. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Falcons 30-23 (OT) 
 Week 5 ranking: 6 

 Biggest issue on defense: Getting stops on third down

 

 The Ravens are allowing teams to convert 41.5% of their third downs, which ranks 20th in the NFL. It's frustrating because Baltimore seems as if it's winning on the early downs before giving up a big play on third down. Quarterbacks are averaging 8.7 yards per attempt on third down, the fifth highest in the league. The Ravens gave up nine third-down conversions Sunday, which are the most they've given up in a game in two seasons. "It obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win," safety Kyle Hamilton said. "I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better." -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 8. Los Angeles Rams (2-3) 
 Week 5 result: Lost to the Bills 37-34 (OT) 
 Week 5 ranking: 7 

 Biggest issue on defense: Missing Myles Garrett 

 

 The Rams' defense has been inconsistent at times, and it has only eight sacks this season (tied for sixth fewest in the NFL). But Los Angeles should get more sack production once the reigning Defensive Player of the Year is back on the field. Garrett, who had knee surgery in mid-September , is eligible to return to practice this week. Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is unlikely to open Garrett's 21-day practice window this week, but that the pass rusher is making "good progress." -- Sarah Barshop 

 
 

 9. New England Patriots (3-2) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Raiders 45-17 
 Week 5 ranking: 14 

 Biggest issue on defense: Cornerback depth
